children.text: Unnumbered section
smṛteravasthiterupapattiḥ ityalamalīkakalpanākulīkṛtasthitinā kṣaṇabha kalpyate ṅgābhiniveśena ||
children.translated_text: Because memory makes persistence intelligible; thus, enough of the adherence to momentary destruction, a position thrown into confusion by false constructions.

children.text: nāpi ||
children.translated_text: Nor [is that so].

children.text: atha deho'pi parārtha manyase kāya eva ācaitanyāt eva pṛthi cetanātmakaḥ
children.translated_text: Now, if you think that even the body exists for another's sake, then the body itself, because it is insentient like earth and the other elements, is not of the nature of consciousness.

children.text: vyādivaditi tasyāpyānyārthyaṃ pārārthyaṃ suta rāmupapadyate
children.translated_text: Therefore its being directed to another, its being for another's sake, is all the more established.

children.text: tataśca tathāhi dehasya yasminnupacite kṣityādīnāṃ yasyopacayaḥ yadapacaye ca parārthatvātpara ca ātmaivātra apacayaḥ tattadātmakaṃ yuktyupapannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus also, in the body, when it increases there is increase of earth and the other elements, and when it decreases there is decrease; because it is for another, and the other here is precisely the <s>ātman</s> (self), its having that nature is reasonably established.

children.text: yathā vahnayupacayāpa cayayorupacayāpacayāvanugacchedauṣṇyamā yauvana sthāvirabhojanalaṅghanādihetukau ca dehasaṃbānidha ||
children.translated_text: Just as heat follows the increase and decrease of fire, so bodily increase and decrease are connected with causes such as youth, old age, eating, fasting, and the like.

children.text: kiṃcāyamaparo'tra doṣaḥ-yaduta ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, there is this further fault here, namely:

children.text: nanu dehādanyatrayadi caitanyaṃsyāt syādeta devam
children.translated_text: Objection: If consciousness existed somewhere apart from the body, then this would be so.

children.text: pṛthvyādicaturbhūtavikārake prāṇādikā raṇībhūte garbhādau saṃvidudbhavaḥ kiṇvādidravya vikāre madaśaktyutpattivat
children.translated_text: But consciousness arises in an embryo and the like, which are transformations of the four elements beginning with earth and in which breath and the rest have become causal factors, just as the power of intoxication arises in a transformation of substances such as ferment.

children.text: tathāhi kṛśo'haṃ sthūlo'hamiti śarīra evāhaṃpratyayo dṛṣṭaḥ na ca tadvyatirikta ātmā upalabhyate dehe'styā tmā ityasya aśve viṣāṇamityādivat pratya kṣanirākṛtatvāt
children.translated_text: For the notion of 'I' is observed in the body alone, as in 'I am thin' and 'I am stout'; and no <s>ātman</s> distinct from it is apprehended, since the claim 'there is an <s>ātman</s> in the body' is refuted by perception, like 'there is a horn on a horse.'

children.text: atha parārthāścakṣurādayaḥ saṃ ghātatvāt śayanādyaṅgavadityādinā karaṇadināṃ kartṛprayojyatvādinā vā anumānenātmā prasā dhyate na tadyuktaṃ tasyātmāpalāpinaścārvākā npratyasiddheḥ
children.translated_text: If, then, the <s>ātman</s> is to be proved by an inference such as, 'The eye and the other organs are for another's sake, because they are aggregates, like the parts of a bed,' or because instruments and the like must be employed by an agent, that is not reasonable, since it is unestablished for <s>Cārvāka</s> thinkers who deny the <s>ātman</s>.

children.text: nahyeṣāṃpratyakṣādanyatkiṃcitpramāṇaṃ siddhāvapivā anuīyamānasyātmano devadattā divatparatvaṃ prasajyate
children.translated_text: For for them no <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge) other than perception is established; and even if it were established, the inferred <s>ātman</s> would have to be someone else, like <s>Devadatta</s> and the rest.

children.text: yatkila svayaṃ prakāśate sa evātmā tatprakāśyastu para iti vivi ktatayā ātmaparabhāvasya prakāśamānasyaiva saṃka ro'navasthānaṃ ca syāt
children.translated_text: For, they say, whatever shines by itself is the very <s>ātman</s>, while what is illumined by it is other; but when selfhood and otherness are separated in this way in relation to what is appearing, confusion and endless regress would result.

children.text: taduktaṃ ātmā yadi bhavenmayastasya mātā bhavetparaḥ
children.translated_text: It has been said: If the <s>ātman</s> were something to be known, its knower would be another.

children.text: ṃ para ātmā tadānīṃ syātsa paro yastu mīyate ||
children.translated_text: Then the other would be the <s>ātman</s>, and that other which is known would be other still.

children.text: iti
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tathā prakāśate saṃvidekā tadanyatu prakāśyate
children.translated_text: Likewise: Consciousness, being one, shines forth; what is other than it is illumined.

children.text: prakāśyaṃ ca bhavetkarma tacca kartrā vinā katham ||
children.translated_text: And what is illumined would be an object of action; and how could that exist without an agent?

children.text: iti
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tasmānnānumānena dehavyatirikta ātmā upalabhyate apitu caitanyaviśiṣṭaḥ kāya eva vastusannityāśaṅkayāha ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, a body-distinct <s>ātman</s> is not apprehended by inference; rather, the body alone, qualified by consciousness, is really existent. Anticipating this objection, he says:

children.text: Chapter 1
he suvratāḥ parameśvarabhaktiprakarṣaparipoṣitaśobhātiśayatvāt suṣṭhu śobhanaṃ vrataṃ śāstrīyaniyamānuṣṭhānaṃ yeṣāṃ ta eva śrotāraḥ saṃbodhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'O you of good vows': the listeners are addressed as those whose vow, that is, their practice of scriptural restraints, is very good and beautiful because it is splendidly nourished by the fullness of devotion to the Supreme Lord.

children.text: yad vakṣyaty upasaṃhāre bhavatsu śivaśītāṃśujyotsnāpāṇḍuṣv idaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: For in the conclusion he will say, 'This, by me, among you who are whitened by the moonlight of <s>Śiva</s>'s cool-rayed moon...

children.text: tadicchayā mayaivoktam iti ||
children.translated_text: ... was spoken by me alone at his wish.'

children.text: harād indrakramāyātaṃ jñānaṃ śṛṇuta ākarṇayateti sambandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The construction is: 'Listen, hear the knowledge that has come from <s>Hara</s> through the succession of <s>Indra</s>.'

children.text: harati paśubhyaḥ pāśān puṃso 'py ūrdhvaṃ padaṃ tatas tu haraḥ ||
children.translated_text: He removes the bonds from the bound souls and then [leads] the person to a state higher still; therefore he is <s>Hara</s>.

children.text: iti yady api yaugikīyaṃ saṃjñā ananteśādiṣv api sāmānyā tathāpi indraśabdasaṃnidher ihomāpatāv eva haraśabdo jñeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Although this etymological name is common also to <s>Ananteśa</s> and others, nevertheless, because of the proximity of the word <s>Indra</s>, here the word <s>Hara</s> should be understood as referring only to <s>Umāpati</s>.

children.text: yathāhuḥ arthaḥ prakaraṇaṃ liṅgaṃ śabdasyānyasya saṃnidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: As they say: meaning, context, an indicatory mark, and the proximity of another word...

children.text: proktāḥ sāmānyaśabdānāṃ viśeṣasthitihetavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: ... are declared to be the causes that fix a specific sense for general words.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: kuta etad iti ced yasmād aindre asmin kāmikabhede bhagavata umāpater vaktṛtvena indrasya ca śrotṛtvenaiva sambandhaḥ pratītaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If it is asked how this is known: because in this <s>Aindra</s> section of the <s>Kāmika</s>, the relation is understood precisely with the blessed <s>Umāpati</s> as speaker and <s>Indra</s> as hearer.

children.text: tathā hi purastād ihaiva munīnām indro vakṣyati
children.translated_text: For later, in this very text, <s>Indra</s> will say to the sages:

children.text: śivodgīrṇam idaṃ jñānaṃ mantramantreśvareśvaraiḥ
children.translated_text: This knowledge, emitted by <s>Śiva</s>, by the <s>Mantras</s>, <s>Mantreśvaras</s>, and <s>Īśvaras</s>...

children.text: kāmadatvāt kāmiketi pragītaṃ bahuvistaram ||
children.translated_text: ... has been celebrated as <s>Kāmika</s>, because it grants desires, and it is very extensive.

children.text: tebhyo 'vagatya dṛgjyotirjvālālīḍhasmaradrumaḥ
children.translated_text: Having learned it from them, he whose tree of <s>Smara</s> had been licked by the flame of his eye-light...

children.text: dadāv umāpatir mahyam iti ||
children.translated_text: ... <s>Umāpati</s> gave it to me.

children.text: tasmāddharāt śrīkaṇṭhanāthāt indrādikrameṇāyātam iti avatīrṇam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore it has come down from <s>Hara</s>, Lord <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>, through a succession beginning with <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: kiṃ tat ||
children.translated_text: What is that?

children.text: jñāyante anena vidyācaryākriyāyogā iti jñānaṃ śāstram ||
children.translated_text: That by which <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), <s>caryā</s> (conduct), <s>kriyā</s> (ritual action), and <s>yoga</s> are known is 'knowledge,' that is, scripture.

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā śṛṇuta ||
children.translated_text: After doing what should you listen?

children.text: parameśvaraṃ namaskṛtya sṛṣṭisthitisaṃkṣobhaṇādibhiś cidacillakṣaṇaṃ viśvam īṣṭe itīśaḥ īdṛktvaṃ cānanteśādīnām apy astīti paramapadena viśeṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Having bowed to <s>Parameśvara</s>: he is the Lord because he governs the universe, characterized by the conscious and the non-conscious, through creation, maintenance, disturbance, and so on. Since such a status also belongs to <s>Ananteśa</s> and others, he is qualified by the word 'supreme.'

children.text: paramaś cāsāv anyeṣāṃ tadanugrahataḥ śivatvābhivyakteḥ īśaś ca svātantryeṇa sthityādikaraṇāt parameśaḥ taṃ namaskṛtya kāyavāṅmanobhis tasmin prahvībhūya ||
children.translated_text: He is supreme because the <s>Śiva</s>-nature of others becomes manifest through his grace, and he is Lord because he performs maintenance and the like by his own autonomy; thus he is <s>Parameśa</s>. 'Having bowed to him' means having become bowed toward him with body, speech, and mind.

children.text: tat ity anantaraṃ tantrāvatārakaṃ bharadvājam ṛṣim iti ṛ gatāv iti dhātvarthataḥ sarveṣāṃ ca gatyarthānāṃ jñānārthatvād avagataparamārthatayā ṛṣiḥ taṃ namaskṛtya śṛṇuteti śrotṝṇāṃ namaskāropadeśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, immediately afterward, [he refers to] the seer <s>Bharadvāja</s>, who brought down the tantra. Since the root ṛ means 'to go,' and all roots of motion can have the meaning of cognition, he is a <s>ṛṣi</s> because he has understood the supreme truth. Thus 'having bowed to him, listen' is an instruction that the hearers should bow.

children.text: anamaskṛtaparameśvarāṇām apraṇatagurūṇāṃ ca nirvighnasaṃhitādhigamanāsaṃbhavāt ||
children.translated_text: For those who have not bowed to <s>Parameśvara</s> and have not prostrated to the guru cannot obtain the <s>saṃhitā</s> without obstacles.

children.text: yaś ca śrotṛjanam evaṃ śikṣayati so 'rthāt kṛtatathāvidhavidhiḥ pravṛtta iti gamyate ||
children.translated_text: And one who instructs the listeners in this way is understood, by implication, to have begun after performing just such a rite.

children.text: tena yathā parameśvaraṃ guruṃ ca nutvāham upadeṣṭuṃ pravṛttas tathā yūyam api pravartadhvam iti vyavasthitam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the settled meaning is: just as I have begun to teach after praising <s>Parameśvara</s> and the guru, so should you also begin.

children.text: yathā caitad indrasyomāpatinā upadiṣṭaṃ tadgranthaparisamāptau yady api granthe evāsti tathāpi vyākhyānopakrame sambandhāder avaśyābhidheyatvāt kiṃcid ucyate ||
children.translated_text: And although how this was taught to <s>Indra</s> by <s>Umāpati</s> is found at the very end of the text, still, because at the beginning of the exposition the connection and the other preliminaries must necessarily be stated, something is said here.

children.text: kadācid atiruciraratnaprakaravinicitakanakamayakamanīyamahītalamanoharasaptamajaladhitaṭaviharaṇahevākinaṃ nīlopalatviṣaṃ caturbhujaṃ dvikaṃdharādharaṃ mukhadvayena vedādhyayanasurāpānasaṃkarakāriṇam asuranivahaparivṛtaṃ durmadaṃ mahāsuraṃ tridaśapatir apaśyat ||
children.translated_text: Once the lord of the thirty gods saw a proud great <s>asura</s>, surrounded by hosts of asuras, dark as blue sapphire, four-armed, bearing two necks and, with his two mouths, mixing Vedic recitation with drinking liquor; he was intent on wandering along the shore of the seventh ocean, whose charming golden ground was variegated with heaps of very lovely jewels.

children.text: atha tathāvidhadurācāradarśanajanitakopākulitamunigaṇasahitaḥ śatakratur akṣamamāṇo labdhavaratvāt prasabham astrair avadhyatām asya buddhvā phenenāntarnihitavastreṇa asurasya śirodvayaṃ cicheda ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śatakratu</s>, together with the company of sages agitated by anger born from seeing such misconduct, unable to tolerate it, and knowing that because the asura had obtained a boon he could not be violently killed by weapons, cut off the asura's two heads with a weapon hidden inside foam.

children.text: tadvyāpādanataś ca brahmahatyājanitam agham āśaṅkamānas tatpraśāntaye bhagavantam acyutaṃ nāmnāṃ sahasreṇa ṛgyajuḥsāmabhiś cāstauṣīt ||
children.translated_text: From killing him, he feared the evil produced by <s>brahmahatyā</s> (killing a Brahmin); for its pacification he praised blessed <s>Acyuta</s> with a thousand names and with the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: prasannena ca hariṇā navoditabhāsvadbhāsvaraṃ sarvabhūtābhibhāvukaṃ nārasiṃhaṃ kavacaṃ prayacchatā proktam ||
children.translated_text: And pleased <s>Hari</s>, while giving him the <s>Nārasiṃha</s> armor, radiant with the splendor of the newly risen sun and overpowering all beings, said:

children.text: yathaitat saṃnaddhadehas tvam uttarakuruṣu bhagavantaṃ pinākinam ārādhaya varṣasahasrānte ca taṃ dṛṣṭvābhimatam āsādayiṣyasi ity uktvā antarhite surārau sarvaṃ tad indreṇa kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: 'With your body armed with this, worship blessed <s>Pinākin</s> in the <s>Uttarakurus</s>; at the end of a thousand years, having seen him, you will obtain what you desire.' When he had said this and disappeared, <s>Indra</s> did all of that.

children.text: atha pratyakṣībhūte bhagavati pinākini nikhiladuḥkhāntaś cāsya saṃjātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, when blessed <s>Pinākin</s> appeared before him, all his suffering came to an end.

children.text: śrīmatkāmikākhyaṃ cāsmai parameśvara upadideśa ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Parameśvara</s> taught him the revered scripture called <s>Kāmika</s>.

children.text: yataś cendrasya nṛsiṃharūpiṇaḥ samupadiṣṭam idam umāpatinā tato mṛgendrasya śrotṛtvān mṛgendrasaṃjñayā prathitam ||
children.translated_text: And because this was taught by <s>Umāpati</s> to <s>Indra</s> in <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> form, therefore, since <s>Mṛgendra</s> was the hearer, it became known by the name <s>Mṛgendra</s>.

children.text: sambandhas tv atra ṣaṭprakāraḥ parādiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here the connection is sixfold, beginning with the supreme relation.

children.text: tathāhi sargādau parameśvaraḥ ūrdhvaprāgdakṣiṇottarapaścimasrotaḥpañcakabhedabhinnaṃ jñānaṃ svecchānugṛhītavidyeśvarāṣṭakaprabodhanānantaraṃ tad abhivyaktaṃ mantreśvarādibhyo vakṣyamāṇavad ādideśa ||
children.translated_text: For so it is: at the beginning of creation <s>Parameśvara</s>, after awakening the group of eight <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> favored by his own will, manifested the knowledge divided into the five streams of upper, eastern, southern, northern, and western, and taught it, as will be described, to <s>Mantreśvaras</s> and others.

children.text: tathā coktaṃ śrīmatkiraṇe
children.translated_text: So it is also said in the revered <s>Kiraṇa</s>:

children.text: sṛṣṭyanantaram eveśaḥ śivān sṛṣṭvā dṛśātmajān
children.translated_text: Immediately after creation, the Lord, having created the <s>Śivas</s>, sons born from his glance,

children.text: jñānam ekaṃ vibhajyāśu teṣāṃ tatsaṃkhyayāvadata ||
children.translated_text: quickly divided the single knowledge and declared it to them according to their number.

children.text: kāmikaṃ praṇavākhyasya śivākhyasya tu yogajam
children.translated_text: He gave the <s>Kāmika</s> to the one named <s>Praṇava</s>, and the <s>Yogaja</s> to the one named <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: ityādi ||
children.translated_text: and so on.

children.text: atra cātmajān iti ātmanaiva niradhikaraṇenānugraheṇānugṛhītān ity āśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, 'sons of himself' means those who were graced by himself alone, by a grace dependent on no external basis; this is the intention.

children.text: tebhya umāpatiḥ prāpa tasmāc ca śakraḥ tato 'pi bharadvājaḥ tatsakāśāt tu hārītaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Umāpati</s> received it from them; from him <s>Śakra</s>, from him <s>Bharadvāja</s>, and from him <s>Hārīta</s>.

children.text: sa punaḥ svaśiṣyebhyaḥ prāheti purastāt sarvaṃ spaṣṭīkariṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He in turn taught it to his own disciples; all this we shall clarify below.

children.text: abhidheyāś ceha jñānakriyāyogacaryāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The subjects to be taught here are <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>kriyā</s> (ritual action), <s>yoga</s>, and <s>caryā</s> (conduct).

children.text: prayojanaṃ tv atra tattvajñaptiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The purpose here is knowledge of the <s>tattvas</s> (principles of reality).

children.text: tatprayojanam api bhuktimuktī
children.translated_text: The purpose of that, in turn, is enjoyment and liberation.

children.text: parameśvarasadbhāvaprasādhakapramāṇopanyāsas tadbādhakanirākaraṇaṃ ca yady api tatpraṇītāgamaprāmāṇy asādhanāya prathamam evopayujyate tathāpi śāstrakāreṇaiva agre tad vivecitam atas tatraiva vakṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The presentation of proofs establishing the reality of <s>Parameśvara</s> and the refutation of objections to it are indeed useful at the very beginning for establishing the authority of the <s>āgama</s> (scripture) authored by him; nevertheless, since the author of the <s>śāstra</s> himself analyzes that later, we shall discuss it there.

children.text: kevalam etāvad eveha pratijānīmahe ||
children.translated_text: Here we merely state this much.

children.text: yad uktam
children.translated_text: As it has been said:

children.text: āyurvedāc ca gaṇitān mantravādāc ca sasvarāt
children.translated_text: Because of <s>Āyurveda</s>, mathematics, and the doctrine of mantras together with accent,

children.text: rasopaniṣadāṭopād āptaḥ sa parigṛhyate ||
children.translated_text: and because of the elaborate <s>Rasopaniṣad</s>, he is accepted as an <s>āpta</s> (trustworthy authority).

children.text: iti tac cāptatvaṃ sāñjanatvād asarvārthadṛśāṃ darśanāntarapraṇetṝṇāṃ svasvaviṣayam eva nityanirmalaniratiśayasarvārthajñānakriyāśaktes tu sarvadā sarvānugrahapravṛttasya parameśvaratvād eva sarvādhiṣṭhātuḥ sarvaviṣayam ||
children.translated_text: And that trustworthiness belongs only in their own respective fields to the founders of other systems, whose vision is tainted and who do not see all things; but because <s>Parameśvara</s>, the ruler of all, by the very fact of being <s>Parameśvara</s>, possesses eternal, stainless, unsurpassed powers of knowledge and action regarding all objects and is always engaged in favoring all, his trustworthiness extends to every subject.

children.text: evaṃ vividhaviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭasya vaktur vipralambhakatvāsaṃbhavān nāprāmāṇyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, since it is impossible that a speaker qualified by these various attributes should be deceptive, there is no lack of authority.

children.text: etac ca yathāvasaraṃ vakṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And we shall explain this when the occasion arises.

children.text: tad evam īdṛgrūpo bhagavān āgamasya kartā ||
children.translated_text: Thus, then, the blessed one of such a nature is the maker of the <s>āgama</s> (scripture).

children.text: āgamas tu taṃ jñāpayati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>āgama</s> in turn makes him known.

children.text: ataś ca dvayor api visadṛśakriyatvān nātretaretarāśrayadoṣaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: And because the two have dissimilar functions, the fault of mutual dependence does not occur here.

children.text: yathā kaścid evaṃ vakti devadatto 'ham āyāta iti ||
children.translated_text: For example, someone says, 'I, <s>Devadatta</s>, have arrived.'

children.text: tadvākyaśravaṇāc ca tadanye manyante hanta devadatto 'yam āyāta iti ||
children.translated_text: And from hearing that statement, others think, 'Ah, this is <s>Devadatta</s>; he has arrived.'

children.text: na cātra devadattasya tadvākyasya cetaretarāśrayatvaṃ yuktam ||
children.translated_text: Here it is not reasonable that <s>Devadatta</s> and his statement are mutually dependent.

children.text: tadukteṣu ca dṛṣṭārtheṣu viṣabhūtarasavādādiṣu tadāgamasya phalavattvam upalabhyādṛṣṭārthasyāpi tacchāsanasyāvitathatvam anumīyate ity alam anena prakṛtam anusarāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And when the fruitfulness of that <s>āgama</s> is observed in the visible matters taught by him, such as poisons, spirit-afflictions, alchemy, and so on, the unfailing truth of his instruction even in invisible matters is inferred. Enough of this; let us return to the topic.

children.text: tad evaṃ hārītamuniḥ svaśiṣyāṇāṃ jñānopadeśaṃ pratijñāya indrakramāyātatvaṃ darśayitum āha ||
children.translated_text: Thus, after promising instruction in knowledge to his own disciples, the sage <s>Hārīta</s>, in order to show that it came down in the succession from <s>Indra</s>, says:

children.text: Chapter 2
badaryāśramanāmni viṣṇor āśrame tadāśramatvād eva pāvane bharadvājaprabhṛtayo munayas tepur iti sambandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The construction is: in the āśrama of <s>Viṣṇu</s> named <s>Badaryāśrama</s>, holy precisely because it was his āśrama, sages beginning with <s>Bharadvāja</s> practiced austerities.

children.text: bharadvājādīnām ṛṣīṇām advijatvaprasiddhyasaṃbhavāt dvijā iti viśeṣaṇaṃ vāgīśvarīgarbhasaṃyojanasaṃjananādinā kṛtadīkṣātvenotkarṣavattvaṃ na punar upanītatvamātraṃ smārtavad dvijaśabdeneṣṭam adīkṣitānāṃ tantrādiśravaṇānadhikārāt pratyuta pratyavāyaśruteḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because it is impossible that sages such as <s>Bharadvāja</s> could be commonly known as non-<s>dvija</s> (twice-born), the qualifier <s>dvija</s> is intended to mean their excellence through having undergone initiation by rites such as joining with and birth from the womb of <s>Vāgīśvarī</s>, not merely investiture with the sacred thread in the smārta sense; for the uninitiated have no qualification to hear tantras and the like, and on the contrary scripture teaches that there is fault.

children.text: śivaṃ pratiṣṭhāpyeti lohabāṇaliṅgādāv ādhāre sāmānyamantrādinā parameśvarapratiṣṭhāpanaṃ parikalpyety āśayaḥ anyathā yathāvad viditatattadvidhānānāṃ purastāt pratiṣṭhādiviṣayasya praśnasyānupapatteḥ ||
children.translated_text: As for 'having installed <s>Śiva</s>,' the intention is: having conceived the installation of <s>Parameśvara</s> in a support such as a metal or bāṇa-liṅga by means of general mantras and the like. Otherwise a later question about installation and related matters, addressed to people who properly knew those several procedures, would be inappropriate.

children.text: tasminn evaikasminn āhitam ekāgrīkṛtaṃ mānasaṃ yais te tathāvidhāḥ santaḥ tepuḥ śivārādhanalakṣaṇaṃ tapaś cakrur ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those whose mind was placed, that is, concentrated, on that one alone, being such, performed tapas, namely the worship of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: Chapter 3
anantaraṃ ca tān bhāvitān tatraśraddhālūn jñātvā kasmiṃścit kāle munirūpadhārī śakraḥ tadīyam āśramaṃ siṣeve ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s>, having then learned that they were devoted and had faith in that matter, at a certain time assumed the form of a sage and visited their hermitage.

children.text: tataś ca ||
children.translated_text: And then:

children.text: Chapter 4
sa indras tair bharadvājādibhir āśramasamucitenātithisatkāreṇābhyarcitas tān bharadvājādīn pratyekaṃ kuśalaṃ pṛṣṭvābravīt ||
children.translated_text: That <s>Indra</s>, honored by <s>Bharadvāja</s> and the others with the hospitality due to a guest in a hermitage, asked <s>Bharadvāja</s> and the others individually about their welfare and spoke.

children.text: kiṃ tad ity ata āha codanādharmaḥ kim arthaṃ nānuvartyata iti ||
children.translated_text: What was that? To answer this he says: 'Why is the <s>dharma</s> of injunction not followed?'

children.text: codaneti kriyāyāḥ pravartakaṃ vacanam āhuḥ tadāmnāto dharmaḥ kim iti nānuṣṭhīyate codanaiva hi dharme pramāṇaṃ pramāṇam eva codanā ity evam anyayogāyogavyavacchedanena tataḥ pravartamānānām aihikasyāmutrikasya ca phalasyāvisaṃvādāt ||
children.translated_text: They say that <s>codanā</s> (injunction) is a statement that impels an action. Why, then, is the <s>dharma</s> taught by it not practiced? For injunction alone is the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge) for <s>dharma</s>, and the <s>pramāṇa</s> is precisely injunction; by thus excluding any other basis or the absence of that basis, the worldly and otherworldly fruit for those who proceed from it is unfailing.

children.text: tathā coktam
children.translated_text: And accordingly it has been said:

children.text: śrutismṛtyuditaṃ dharmam anutiṣṭhan hi mānavaḥ
children.translated_text: For a human being who practices the <s>dharma</s> taught by <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>

children.text: iha kīrtim avāpnoti pretya cānuttamāṃ gatim iti ||
children.translated_text: obtains fame here and, after death, the unsurpassed state.

children.text: tadviparītaṃ tu trayībāhyaṃ liṅgārādhanādi ca yat tat trayībāhyatvād eva phalguprāyam ||
children.translated_text: But whatever is the opposite of that and outside the threefold Veda, such as liṅga worship, is, precisely because it lies outside the threefold Veda, mostly worthless.

children.text: yad āha bhaṭṭaḥ
children.translated_text: As <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> says:

children.text: tathātikrāntavedoktamaryādāvyavahāriṇām
children.translated_text: Likewise, for those whose conduct transgresses the boundary declared by the Veda,

children.text: saṃvādiṣv api vākyeṣu neṣyate mānahetutā ||
children.translated_text: even statements that correspond with fact are not accepted as grounds of valid knowledge.

children.text: manur api
children.translated_text: <s>Manu</s> too says:

children.text: yā vedabāhyāḥ smṛtayo yāś ca kāścit kudṛṣṭayaḥ
children.translated_text: Those <s>smṛtis</s> that are outside the Veda, and whatever false views there are,

children.text: sarvās tā niṣphalāḥ pretya tamobhūtā hi tāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all of them are fruitless after death, for they are remembered as consisting of darkness.

children.text: ity evaṃ jaiminimatānusāriṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus [he speaks] as one following the doctrine of <s>Jaimini</s>.

children.text: tasya vacaḥ śrutvā ||
children.translated_text: Having heard his words,

children.text: Chapter 5
te bharadvājādayaḥ indraṃ tāpasarūpatvān muniśabdenāmantrya nanv iti prativacanam avocan ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bharadvāja</s> and the others, addressing <s>Indra</s> with the word 'sage' because of his ascetic appearance, gave a reply beginning with 'but surely'.

children.text: yo 'yam asmābhir abhihito rudrākhyadevatāprasādanopāyalakṣaṇo dharmaḥ tapasā samīhitasiddhyartham āsevyate sa codanayaivābhihito vyavasthāpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This <s>dharma</s> that we have described, whose character is a means for propitiating the deity called <s>Rudra</s>, and that is practiced as tapas for accomplishing the desired aim, is stated and established by injunction itself.

children.text: tathā hi codanā nāma liḍloṭtavyadādiśabdavyavasthāpitavidhiniṣedharūpayajanādikriyāpravartakavacanam abhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: For an injunction is said to be a statement that impels actions such as sacrifice, has the form of prescription and prohibition, and is established by optative, imperative, gerundive, and similar verbal forms.

children.text: yathā jyotiṣṭomena yajeta svargakāmaḥ na kalañjaṃ bhakṣayet ityādi ||
children.translated_text: For example, 'One desiring heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>,' 'One should not eat kalañja,' and so on.

children.text: tac ca mukhyatayā śrautaṃ dharmarūpaṃ tanmūlatvāc ca smārtam api ||
children.translated_text: And that <s>dharma</s> is primarily <s>śrauta</s> (grounded in revelation), and, because <s>smārta</s> practice has that as its root, it is <s>smārta</s> as well.

children.text: tathā coktaṃ tasmāc chrutismṛtī eva pramāṇaṃ dharmagocare ||
children.translated_text: Thus it has been said: 'Therefore <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> alone are the <s>pramāṇa</s> in the sphere of <s>dharma</s>.'

children.text: iti tathā ||
children.translated_text: And likewise:

children.text: vedo 'khilo dharmamūlaṃ smṛtiśīle ca tadvidām
children.translated_text: The entire Veda is the root of <s>dharma</s>, along with the <s>smṛti</s> and conduct of those who know it.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tadāsatāṃ tāvad evaṃvidhāḥ śrutyādisadāgamārthāvirodhinyaḥ paurāṇikyaḥ saṃhitāḥ anyāś ca kāścana śrutayo yāsām idaṃ tātparyam ||
children.translated_text: Let that stand for the moment. There are Purāṇic saṃhitās of this kind, not opposed to the meaning of true scriptures such as <s>śruti</s>, and also certain other <s>śrutis</s>, whose purport is this.

children.text: yathā mahābhāratādau
children.translated_text: For example, in the <s>Mahābhārata</s> and similar works:

children.text: ye bhaktā varadaṃ devaṃ śivaṃ rudram umāpatim
children.translated_text: Those devotees who [worship] the boon-giving god <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Umāpati</s>,

children.text: ihaloke sukhaṃ prāpya te yānti paramāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: after gaining happiness in this world, go to the supreme goal.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: sarvarūpaṃ bhavaṃ jñātvā liṅge yo 'rcayati prabhum
children.translated_text: Whoever, knowing <s>Bhava</s> as having every form, worships the Lord in the liṅga,

children.text: tasminn abhyadhikāṃ prītiṃ karoti vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛṣabhadhvaja</s> shows especially great favor toward him.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tathā
children.translated_text: Likewise:

children.text: ādityā vasavo rudrā munayaś ca mahaujasaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Vasus</s>, <s>Rudras</s>, and sages of great power,

children.text: vidhival liṅgam ārādhya padam iṣṭatamaṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: having worshiped the liṅga according to rule, attained the most desired station.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tathā
children.translated_text: Likewise:

children.text: mṛdbhasmagośakṛtpiṣṭaguḍakhaṇḍādiliṅgakam
children.translated_text: A faithful person, after installing a small liṅga made of clay, ash, cow dung, flour, molasses, sugar-candy, and the like,

children.text: sampūjayan pratiṣṭhāpya śraddhāvān adhigacchati ||
children.translated_text: and worshiping it fully, attains [the desired result].

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tatrāprāmāṇyam abhyupagamyāpi brūmaḥ yad abhiprāyeṇedam abhidhīyate bhavadbhiḥ sa tāvat śrutyartha eva smaryatāṃ tatra hi ||
children.translated_text: Even while conceding their non-authoritativeness, we say this: the purport with reference to which this statement is made by you should first be remembered as the very meaning of <s>śruti</s>; for there,

children.text: Chapter 6
rudro devatāsyā iti raudrī saṃhitā ṛgyajuḥsāmalakṣaṇe cātharvaṇe ca vede 'sti
children.translated_text: there is a <s>Raudrī Saṃhitā</s>, so called because <s>Rudra</s> is its deity, in the Veda characterized as Ṛg, Yajus, Sāman, and Atharvan.

children.text: yajurvede hi rudraikādaśinī saṃhitā śrūyate yasyāṃ bhagavanto rudrāḥ sarvābhipretasādhakāḥ paṭhyante
children.translated_text: For in the <s>Yajurveda</s> the <s>Rudraikādaśinī Saṃhitā</s> is heard, in which the blessed <s>Rudras</s>, who accomplish every desired aim, are recited.

children.text: ṛgvede 'pi
children.translated_text: In the <s>Ṛgveda</s> too:

children.text: tryambakaṃ yajāmahe ||
children.translated_text: 'We sacrifice to <s>Tryambaka</s>.'

children.text: imā rudrāya tavase kapardine ||
children.translated_text: 'These [songs] are for mighty <s>Rudra</s>, the matted-haired one.'

children.text: imā rudrāya sthiradhanvane giraḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'These hymns are for <s>Rudra</s> of the firm bow.'

children.text: ityādikā ṛgvidhānāmnātās tattadviśiṣṭavidhānaphalā vidyanta eva
children.translated_text: These and similar passages, taught in the <s>Ṛgvidhāna</s>, with their respective specific rites and fruits, certainly exist.

children.text: sāmavede 'py asti
children.translated_text: There is [such material] in the <s>Sāmaveda</s> as well.

children.text: śrūyate hi sāmnāṃ vidhāne
children.translated_text: For it is heard in the ritual prescription of the Sāmans:

children.text: ā vo rājā tad vo varga ājyadohāni devavratāni caiṣā raudrī nāma saṃhitaitāṃ prayuñjāno rudraṃ prīṇāti ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Ā vo rājā</s>, <s>Tad vo varga</s>, the <s>Ājyadoha</s> chants, and the <s>Devavrata</s> chants: this is the saṃhitā called <s>Raudrī</s>. One who employs it pleases <s>Rudra</s>.'

children.text: iti
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: evam ātharvaṇe 'pi rudrārādhanavidhayaḥ tanmantrasaṃhitāś ca sambhavanti ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, in the Atharvan too, prescriptions for worshiping <s>Rudra</s> and saṃhitās of his mantras are found.

children.text: na ca kevalaṃ saṃhitāmātram evāsti ||
children.translated_text: And it is not the case that only a mere saṃhitā exists.

children.text: tatra tatra rudra eva devatā vācyarūpatayā śrūyate yam uddiśya
children.translated_text: In those passages <s>Rudra</s> alone is heard of as the deity in the form of the intended referent, with reference to whom...

children.text: eṣa te rudra bhāgaḥ saha svasrāmbikayā taṃ juṣasva svāhā
children.translated_text: "This is your portion, O <s>Rudra</s>, together with your sister <s>Ambikā</s>; enjoy it. Svāhā."

children.text: iti śrutiḥ ||
children.translated_text: So says the <s>śruti</s> (revelation).

children.text: na caitāvat yāvatkālpika iti kalpo vedāṅgaṃ tadukto vidhiḥ bhagavataḥ sāṃnidhyakalpanāya śrūyate ||
children.translated_text: Nor is that all, so far as what belongs to the Kalpa is concerned: Kalpa is a <s>Vedāṅga</s>, and a procedure taught by it is heard for establishing the presence of the blessed Lord.

children.text: tathā hi kāṭhake sūtrapariśiṣṭīye rudrakalpe
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Rudrakalpa</s> of the Sūtra appendix in the <s>Kāṭhaka</s>,

children.text: triṣavaṇam udakopasparśanam ity uktvoktaṃ darbheṣv āsīno darbhamuṣṭiṃ dhārayamāṇo rakṣobhyo 'pyavijñeyo bhavati śākayāvakapayobhaikṣabhakṣaḥ ṣaḍbhir māsaiḥ pratyakṣībhavantaṃ bhagavantaṃ paśyati
children.translated_text: after saying, "touching water three times a day," it is said: "Seated on darbha grass and holding a handful of darbha, he becomes unknown even to the demons; eating greens, barley-gruel, milk, and alms, in six months he sees the blessed Lord becoming visible."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: evaṃ ca śraddadhānamanasāṃ jaiminīyacchāyāśrayiṇām api codanāpradarśito 'yam astīva prasiddhaḥ panthāḥ kiṃ punaḥ parameśvaraprakāśanavihatamahāmohatimiratayā vispaṣṭadṛṣṭīnām anyeṣām ||
children.translated_text: And in this way, even for those whose minds have faith and who take shelter in the shadow of <s>Jaimini</s>, this well-known path shown by injunction does indeed exist; how much more, then, for others whose sight is clear because the dense darkness of great delusion has been dispelled by the manifestation of <s>Parameśvara</s>.

children.text: Chapter 7
evam api kathite tadīyaṃ bhaktiprakarṣaṃ jñātum icchur indratvena paramaiśvaryayogāt prabhuḥ prabhavanaśīlaḥ sa tān munīn sasmitam āha ||
children.translated_text: Even when this had been said, he, the Lord, called <s>Indra</s> because he possessed supreme lordship and was powerful by nature, wished to know the excellence of their devotion and said to those sages with a smile:

children.text: kiṃ tat ||
children.translated_text: What was that?

children.text: mithyā jñānaṃ vaḥ yuṣmākaṃ sambandhi yad etalliṅgārcanādiśivārādhanapratipādakaṃ jñānaṃ śāstraṃ tan mithyā na satyaṃ tat praṇetṛtathāvidhadevatānupapatteḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Your knowledge is false: that knowledge, the scripture belonging to you which teaches worship of <s>Śiva</s> through liṅga-worship and the like, is false, not true, because an author of it and such a deity cannot reasonably be established.

children.text: yataḥ karmānuṣṭhānād eva phalaṃ na devatātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the result comes only from the performance of ritual action, not from a deity.

children.text: śabdamātraṃ hi devatā ||
children.translated_text: For the deity is merely a word.

children.text: na khalu vayaṃ pratyakṣetarapramāṇāpahnavapravṛttadurācāracārvākavadasaṃbhavam eva devatāyāḥ pratipadyāmahe ||
children.translated_text: We certainly do not, like wicked <s>Cārvākas</s> intent on rejecting means of knowledge other than perception, accept that a deity is altogether impossible.

children.text: kiṃ tarhi ||
children.translated_text: What, then?

children.text: vidyata eva devatā sā tu śabdān nātiricyate api tu ayogolakavahnivad anupalabhyamānavācyārthapṛthagbhāvaḥ śabda eva teṣu teṣu kriyāviśeṣeṣu aṅgabhāvaṃ gacchan yāgasampradānadevatā viśeṣākhyāṃ labhate ||
children.translated_text: A deity does indeed exist, but it does not go beyond the word; rather, just like fire in an iron ball, the word itself, whose separation from the denoted object is not apprehended, becomes an auxiliary in each particular ritual action and receives the special designation "the deity who is the recipient of the sacrifice."

children.text: tad uktam
children.translated_text: That has been said:

children.text: avinirbhinnaśabdārthaṃ dhyāyed oṃkāram īśvaram
children.translated_text: "One should meditate on <s>Oṃkāra</s>, the Lord, whose word and meaning are not separated."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: na cātra kaścid eka eva viśveśitāstīti niyamaḥ pratijñātuṃ śakyaḥ anekākārasuprasiddhabahutaradevatāviśeṣaśravaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: And here no fixed rule can be asserted that there is one and only one ruler of the universe, because many particular deities, well known in various forms, are heard of.

children.text: tac cedam anupamamahimnaḥ śabdarūpasyaivaṃ vijṛmbhitaṃ yad ekam api sat tat tad devatāviśeṣapratītihetutām ātmapratītihetutāṃ cābhyeti ||
children.translated_text: And this is the expansion of the incomparable greatness of what has the form of word: although it is one, it becomes the cause of cognition of this or that particular deity and also the cause of cognition of itself.

children.text: tathaiva śrutiḥ
children.translated_text: So too the <s>śruti</s> says:

children.text: indraṃ mitraṃ varuṇam agnim āhur atho divyaḥ sa suparṇo garutmān
children.translated_text: "They call him <s>Indra</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Agni</s>; and he is also the heavenly, fair-winged <s>Garutmān</s>.

children.text: ekaṃ sadviprā bahudhā vadanty agniṃ yamaṃ mātariśvānam āhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: What exists is one; sages speak of it in many ways. They call it <s>Agni</s>, <s>Yama</s>, and <s>Mātariśvan</s>."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tat saṃsthitam etac chabdātmikā devateti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore this is established: the deity is word by nature.

children.text: evam anvayenābhidhāya vyatirekeṇāmum evārthaṃ draḍhayitum āha ||
children.translated_text: Having stated this same meaning positively, he now states it negatively in order to make it firm.

children.text: Chapter 8
śabdavyatiriktā hi yadi devatā vidyate kiṃ vigrahavatī avigrahā ubhayarūpānubhayarūpā vā ||
children.translated_text: For if a deity exists apart from word, is it embodied, disembodied, both of these, or neither?

children.text: anubhayarūpatve viruddhadharmādhyāsaḥ svasiddhāntaviruddhānekāntavādābhyupagamaḥ vyastapakṣadvayodbhāvitadoṣaprasaṅgaś ca ||
children.translated_text: If it has neither form, there is the attribution of contradictory properties, the acceptance of a doctrine of non-one-sidedness that contradicts one's own position, and the consequence of the faults raised against each of the two alternatives taken separately.

children.text: avigrahatve śabdenaiva kim aparāddham ||
children.translated_text: If it is disembodied, what fault has been committed by the word alone?

children.text: vigrahavattve tu bhinnadeśāvasthiteṣu yugapat prārabdhayāgeṣu yajvasu mūrtatvāt tasyāḥ sāṃnidhyānupapattiḥ ||
children.translated_text: But if it is embodied, then, since it has a body, its presence is impossible among sacrificers who have begun sacrifices simultaneously in different places.

children.text: nanu mūrtatve saty api sāṃnidhyaṃ parasparavidūradeśasthopasthātṛjanopahṛtasaparyayor arkendubimbayor dṛṣṭam ity anaikāntikaṃ mūrtatvam ||
children.translated_text: Objection: Even when they are embodied, the disks of the sun and moon are seen to be present for worship offered by attendants located in mutually distant places; therefore embodiment is inconclusive.

children.text: nānaikāntikam arkendubimbayoḥ svaprabhābhāsvarayor uccataratvena sakaladeśopalakṣyasthānamātrasthayor bahujanopalambhayogyadeśāvasthānam eva sāṃnidhyaṃ bhavatāṃ pratibhāti na vāstavam ||
children.translated_text: Reply: It is not inconclusive. In the case of the disks of the sun and moon, bright with their own radiance and very high, located only in a place visible from every region, what appears to you as presence is merely their being situated in a place fit to be perceived by many people, not a real presence.

children.text: tathā cātyuttuṅgaraṅgotsaṅgavartinī nartakī vidūradeśavartibhir bhūyobhiḥ prekṣakaiḥ prekṣyamāṇā naikaikaṃ prati prākāmyaśaktyā sāṃnidhyaṃ bhajate ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, a dancer standing on the top of a very high stage, though seen by many spectators situated far away, does not by the power of free attainment become present to each one individually.

children.text: tasmāt samakālam anekagṛhabhojanopanimantritānāṃ yathāsmākam anekagṛhabhojanaṃ na dṛṣṭam evaṃ devatāyās tulyakālaṃ bhinnadeśasthayāgasāṃnidhyaṃ mūrtatvān na saṃbhāvyam iti śabdamātratvam evāsyāḥ sādhīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, just as we do not see people invited at the same time to meals in many houses eating in many houses, so too a deity's simultaneous presence at sacrifices situated in different places cannot be supposed if it is embodied; hence it is better that it be merely word.

children.text: kiṃca ||
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: Chapter 9
na kila tathāvidhavyatyayadaśāvirahitaparamaparokṣavapuṣaḥ prakṛṣṭātiśayaiśvaryopapannajñānānantamahimno devatāviśeṣasya sādhakaṃ kim api pramāṇaṃ pratibhāti ||
children.translated_text: No means of knowledge appears to establish any particular deity with a supremely immediate body free from such states of alteration and endowed with knowledge, infinite greatness, and exceedingly surpassing lordly power.

children.text: tathā hi aparokṣatvena sakalapramāṇajyeṣṭhasya pratyakṣasya tāvan nāsau gocaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: For, to begin with, that deity is not within the range of perception, which, because it is immediate, is the foremost of all means of knowledge.

children.text: na hy atīndriyaviṣayagrahaṇakṣamatvaṃ pratyakṣasya sambhavati ||
children.translated_text: For perception cannot have the capacity to apprehend supersensible objects.

children.text: atha vyavahitaviprakṛṣṭārthaviṣayaṃ yogipratyakṣaṃ tat sattāniścāyakam iti cet tan na yasmād asmadādyatīndriyārthadarśino yoginaḥ sūkṣmādiviṣayas tatpratyakṣaṃ tena ceśaḥ sākṣātkriyate ity etat sarvam anupapannaṃ pramāṇābhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: Now, if it is said that <s>yogipratyakṣa</s> (yogic perception), whose objects are things remote and separated, ascertains that [Lord's] existence, that is not so. For all this is untenable for lack of a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge): that there are yogins who see objects beyond the senses of people like us, that their perception has subtle things and the like as its objects, and that by it <s>Īśa</s> is directly realized.

children.text: atīndriyo 'tīndriyārthadarśī ca kaścit sādhayitum iṣṭas tasya tathāvidhapuruṣapratyakṣeṇāsiddhena sādhanaṃ prāmāṇikasyāpi bhavataḥ kim iti na trapāvaham ||
children.translated_text: You want to prove that some person is supersensible and sees supersensible objects. For you, even though you are a defender of <s>pramāṇa</s>, why is it not shameful to establish him by the perception of such a person, when that perception itself is unestablished?

children.text: nanv asty atrānupahatasāmarthyam anumānaṃ tathā hi jagad idam urvīparvatasaritsamudrādi dharmi kāryam iti sādhyo dharmaḥ sāvayavatvāt yad yat sāvayavaṃ tat tat kāryaṃ yathā valabhiprākārapuṣkariṇyādi ||
children.translated_text: Objection: But there is here an inference whose capacity is unobstructed. To explain: this world, with earth, mountains, rivers, oceans, and so on as the subject, has the property to be proved, namely that it is an effect, because it possesses parts. Whatever possesses parts is an effect, as mansions, ramparts, reservoirs, and the like are.

children.text: vipakṣavyāvṛttaś cāyaṃ hetur yatra kilātmādau kāryatvaṃ nāsti tatra sāvayavatvam api nāstīti ||
children.translated_text: And this <s>hetu</s> (reason) is excluded from the contrary class: wherever effecthood is absent, as in the <s>ātman</s> and the like, there possession of parts too is absent.

children.text: na cāsya hetor īśvaraśarīreṇānaikāntikatvaṃ yathāhur jaiminīyāḥ
children.translated_text: Nor is this reason inconclusive because of <s>Īśvara</s>'s body, as the <s>Jaiminīyas</s> say:

children.text: anekāntaś ca hetus te taccharīrādinā bhavet
children.translated_text: 'And your reason would become inconclusive because of his body and the like.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tasyāpi tadicchākāryatvena asmābhir iṣyamāṇatvād iti ||
children.translated_text: For we hold that that too is an effect of his will.

children.text: siddhe ca jagataḥ kāryatve 'pi yad yat kāryaṃ tat tad viśiṣṭajñānakriyopapannakartṛkāvinābhāvi ghaṭapaṭādivat ||
children.translated_text: And once the world has been established as an effect, [one may argue:] whatever is an effect is invariably connected with a maker endowed with distinctive knowledge and action, as pots, cloths, and the like are.

children.text: kāryaṃ cedaṃ jagat ||
children.translated_text: And this world is an effect.

children.text: tasmād idam api niratiśayajñatvakartṛtvasampannaṃ nirmātāraṃ gamayati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore this too indicates a maker possessed of unsurpassed knowledge and agency.

children.text: yaś cātra nirmātā sa kaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And who is the maker here?

children.text: īśvara iti ||
children.translated_text: It is <s>Īśvara</s>.

children.text: kim etan na pramāṇaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Would this not be a means of proof?

children.text: etad yady abādhitaṃ syāt yāvatā paramāṇvindriyāder jagadbhāgasyāsiddhaṃ sāvayavatvam iti bhāgāsiddho 'yaṃ hetuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Reply: It would be, if it were uncontradicted. But possession of parts is not established for part of the world, namely atoms, sense faculties, and the like; so this <s>hetu</s> (reason) is unestablished in part of the subject.

children.text: paramāṇūnām ācaitanye sati anekatvād ghaṭādivat kāryatvam avyabhicāri iti kila bhavatām abhyupagamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Indeed your own admission, it seems, is that atoms, because they are many while insentient, are invariably effects, as pots and the like are.

children.text: yad apy etat dṛṣṭāntīkṛtaṃ valabhiprākārapuṣkariṇyādi tad gatam upādānasahakārikāraṇādyānuguṇyavaiguṇyāt nirvṛttasadasatsaṃniveśaṃ sāvayavatvam ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, what was presented as an example, mansions, ramparts, reservoirs, and so forth, has possession of parts in the form of a well or badly completed arrangement, according to the fitness or unfitness of material causes, auxiliary causes, and so on.

children.text: tadanyad eva tattatsaṃniveśasadṛśam ||
children.translated_text: That is something quite different, though it resembles those particular arrangements.

children.text: itarad eva hi mahīmahīdharādigataṃ sāvayavatvaṃ vastusādṛśyāvalambanapūrvavyāptidarśanāhitasaṃskārā ca tadanuguṇasādhyasādhanārthaṃ prāmāṇikam iti pravartata iti yuktaṃ na punaḥ sāvayavatvaśabdamātrasāmānyāśrayeṇa ||
children.translated_text: For the possession of parts found in earth, mountains, and the like is entirely different. A competent reasoner proceeds in order to establish a matching probandum and proof on the basis of similarity in real things and on the impression produced by previous observation of pervasion; that is reasonable, but not on the basis of the mere shared word 'possessing parts.'

children.text: yad āha dharmakīrtiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Dharmakīrti</s> says:

children.text: siddhaṃ yādṛg adhiṣṭhātṛbhāvābhāvānuvṛttimat
children.translated_text: An arrangement and the like of such a kind as is established to follow the presence and absence of a superintendent

children.text: saṃniveśādi tad yuktaṃ tasmād yad anumīyate ||
children.translated_text: is a proper basis for whatever is inferred from it.

children.text: vastubhede prasiddhe 'pi śabdasāmyād abhedinaḥ
children.translated_text: Even when the difference of things is well known, because of sameness of word,

children.text: na yuktānumitiḥ pāṇḍudravyād iva hutāśane ||
children.translated_text: it is not proper to infer identity, as one would not infer fire from a pale substance.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: api ca valabhyādīnāṃ pakṣāntarbhāve dṛṣṭāntābhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, if mansions and the like are included in the subject, there is no example.

children.text: na cetaratrāntarbhāvaḥ tadā īśvarasya sarvakartṛtvahāniḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nor can they be included elsewhere; in that case <s>Īśvara</s>'s being the maker of everything would be lost.

children.text: sthapatyādyanvayavyatirekānuvidhāyinau bhāvābhāvau valabhyādīnāṃ dṛṣṭau ||
children.translated_text: The existence and nonexistence of mansions and the like are observed to follow the positive and negative concomitance of architects and other craftsmen.

children.text: na ca dṛṣṭaṃ kāraṇam apahāya kāraṇāntaraṃ tadīśvarākhyaṃ kalpayitum upapannam ||
children.translated_text: And it is not reasonable, abandoning an observed cause, to posit another cause called <s>Īśvara</s> for those things.

children.text: evaṃ hi sati sarvatra kāryakāraṇabhāvo viplaveta ||
children.translated_text: For if this were so, the relation of effect and cause would be thrown into disorder everywhere.

children.text: tad uktam
children.translated_text: That has been said:

children.text: yasmin sati bhavaty eva yat tato 'nyasya kalpane
children.translated_text: When, given the existence of one thing, another thing certainly comes about, if one imagines something else as its cause,

children.text: taddhetutvena sarvatra hetūnām anavasthitiḥ ||
children.translated_text: then everywhere causes would fail to be fixed as causes.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: kiṃ ca na tāvad aśarīrajagannirmātṛdevatāviśeṣābhyupagamo yuktaḥ tasya jagallakṣaṇakāryasampādanāsaṃbhavāt ||
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the acceptance of a particular deity who is a bodiless maker of the world is not reasonable, because it is impossible for him to accomplish an effect characterized as the world.

children.text: yad āha
children.translated_text: As it says:

children.text: kāryaṃ śarīrayuktena kartrā vyāptaṃ sadaiva yat
children.translated_text: Whatever is an effect is always pervaded by an agent who has a body;

children.text: kāryatvāt tena jagataḥ kartā dehī prasajyate ||
children.translated_text: therefore, because the world is an effect, its maker would have to be embodied.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tataś ca dharmisvarūpaviparītasādhakaḥ kāryahetuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Consequently the <s>hetu</s> (reason) 'being an effect' proves the opposite of the subject's own nature.

children.text: śarīravattve tv asmadādivad utpattipralayayogitvam ||
children.translated_text: But if he has a body, then, like people such as ourselves, he would be subject to origination and dissolution.

children.text: tac cāsya śarīraṃ svanirmitaṃ kartrantaranirmitaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: And that body of his is either made by himself or made by another agent.

children.text: svanirmitatve kim asau tatsargakāle saśarīraḥ śarīrarahito vā ||
children.translated_text: If it is self-made, then at the time of creating it was he possessed of a body or without a body?

children.text: dehendriyarahitasya na kvacit kiṃcit kāryaṃ dṛṣṭam ity uktam ||
children.translated_text: It has already been said that no action at all is seen anywhere for one who lacks body and senses.

children.text: śarīravāṃś cet śarīraṃ sṛjati tarhi tad apy asya śarīraṃ kiṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: But if, while having a body, he creates a body, then was that body of his also made?

children.text: svakṛtatve 'nyakṛtatve vānavasthety evamādibādhakasadbhāvāt sādhakaṃ pramāṇaṃ na kiṃcid upapadyate ||
children.translated_text: Whether made by himself or made by another, there is regress. Thus, because such defeaters exist, no proving <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge) is reasonable at all.

children.text: athocyate vākyam āgamalakṣaṇaṃ pramāṇam asti yad atyantātīndriyārthaniścāyakaṃ tataḥ pravartamānasyābhipretasampatter dṛṣṭatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Now it may be said: there is a <s>pramāṇa</s>, a statement characterized as <s>āgama</s> (scripture), which determines an utterly supersensible object, since one who acts on it is seen to attain the desired result.

children.text: tad āhuḥ akṣaliṅgātigo hy arthaḥ puṃsaḥ śāstreṇa darśyate
children.translated_text: They say: 'For an object beyond perception and inferential sign is shown to a person by scripture,'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: thus.

children.text: etad eva nirākartum āha ||
children.translated_text: To refute just this, he says:

children.text: Chapter 10
vākyam āgamalakṣaṇaṃ purāṇetihāsādigītam ||
children.translated_text: A statement characterized as <s>āgama</s>, sung in <s>Purāṇa</s>s, <s>Itihāsa</s>s, and the like,

children.text: yathāha mahābhāratādau bhagavān vyāsamuniḥ
children.translated_text: as, for example, the blessed sage <s>Vyāsa</s> says in the <s>Mahābhārata</s> and similar works:

children.text: sa śivas tāta tejasvī prasādād yāti te 'grataḥ
children.translated_text: 'That radiant <s>Śiva</s>, dear one, goes before you through his grace;

children.text: sendrādiṣu ca deveṣu tasyaivaiśvaryam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: and among the gods beginning with <s>Indra</s>, his lordship alone is proclaimed.

children.text: taṃ gaccha śaraṇaṃ devadevādiṃ bhuvaneśvaram
children.translated_text: Go to him for refuge, the origin of the gods of gods, the Lord of the worlds,'

children.text: ityādi ||
children.translated_text: and so on.

children.text: śrutāv api
children.translated_text: In the śruti too:

children.text: yo rudro 'gnau yo 'psu ya oṣadhīṣu yo vanaspatiṣu
children.translated_text: That <s>Rudra</s> who is in fire, who is in the waters, who is in the plants, who is in the forest trees,

children.text: yo rudro viśvā bhuvanā viveśa tasmai rudrāya namo 'stu ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Rudra</s> who has entered all the worlds: homage to that <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: tathā
children.translated_text: Likewise:

children.text: tryambakaṃ yajāmahe
children.translated_text: We worship <s>Tryambaka</s>...

children.text: ityādi ||
children.translated_text: and so on.

children.text: tad etad anyathāsiddham atra hi paurvāparyaparyālocanānirākṛto yathāśrutaśrutisamutpādito vākyārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But this is accounted for otherwise. For here the sentence-meaning produced from the śruti just as it is heard is rejected by examining what precedes and follows.

children.text: ato naiva pratītimātrāvipralabdhabuddhayas tatheti pratipattiṃ bhāvayanti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore those whose minds are not deceived by mere appearance do not cultivate the conviction that it is so.

children.text: tathā kila viṣaṃ bhakṣaya mā cāsya gṛhe bhuṅkthāḥ ity atra viṣabhakṣaṇe 'bhyanujñānaṃ śrūyamāṇam api na vākyārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, in the sentence, "Eat poison, but do not eat in his house," although permission to eat poison is heard, that is not the sentence-meaning.

children.text: kiṃ tarhi ||
children.translated_text: What then?

children.text: pratikūlagṛhabhojananiṣedha eva tātparyam ||
children.translated_text: The intended point is only the prohibition against eating in a hostile person's house.

children.text: evaṃ bhāratādāv upākhyānadvāreṇa sodyogasya vijigīṣor dviṣadupaśamo nirvighnaḥ kṣatriyāṇāṃ ca svadharmānuṣṭhānam abhyudayāyety evam arthaḥ stutivādaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, in the <s>Bhārata</s> and similar works, through narratives, the meaning is that the suppression of enemies is unobstructed for an energetic would-be conqueror, and that the performance of their own <s>dharma</s> by kṣatriyas leads to prosperity; such a meaning is a <s>stutivāda</s> (eulogistic statement).

children.text: śrutau tu mantrārthavādapadānāṃ kāryātiśayāvedanaṃ vinā puruṣāpravṛtteḥ śraddhāvahavividhābhyudayajñānopajananapratītyaṅgatvaṃ na svarūpayāthārthyam ity aṅgatvam iti na taduktimātrād viśiṣṭadevatāsadbhāvāvedakatvam ||
children.translated_text: But in śruti, since a person does not act without being informed of the special excellence of what is to be done, the words of <s>mantra</s> and <s>arthavāda</s> are auxiliary to the cognition that gives rise to faith-bearing knowledge of various prosperities; their auxiliary status is not due to the literal truth of their own form. Thus, merely from their utterance, they do not indicate the existence of particular deities.

children.text: tathā cāhuḥ
children.translated_text: And so they say:

children.text: stutivādakṛtaś caiṣa janānāṃ mativibhramaḥ
children.translated_text: This confusion in people's understanding is produced by <s>stutivāda</s>;

children.text: paurvāparyāparāmṛṣṭaḥ śabdo 'nyāṃ kurute mitim ||
children.translated_text: a word not considered with what precedes and follows creates a different cognition.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: atha sakalalokasiddhā prasiddhir anapahnavanīyā vidyate yat sarvo hy ayam āvidvadaṅganābālo janaḥ parameśvarasyecchāvidhipreritaḥ pravartate daivam evātra kāraṇam iti bruvāṇo dṛśyate ca upākhyānāni ca dakṣamakhamathanakāladamanakāmadāhāndhakavadhatrailokyākramaṇādyuparacitāni bahuśaḥ paṭhantaḥ kathayantaḥ śṛṇvantaś copalabhyante taduddeśena cārthaviniyoganiyamajapatapaḥprabhṛtikleśakāriṇīm api karmapaddhatim anutiṣṭhanto 'smān avagamayanti yad uta santi devatāviśeṣā ity āha ||
children.translated_text: Now, if it is said that there is an undeniable public reputation, established among all people, namely, that all these people, from learned men to women and children, are seen to act as impelled by the command of <s>Parameśvara</s>'s will, saying, "The divine alone is the cause here"; and that many are found reciting, telling, and hearing stories composed about the destruction of <s>Dakṣa</s>'s sacrifice, the subduing of <s>Kāla</s>, the burning of <s>Kāma</s>, the killing of <s>Andhaka</s>, the overrunning of the three worlds, and the like; and that, with reference to him, by undertaking even a hardship-producing course of action such as dedication of wealth, vows, recitation, and austerity, they make us understand that particular deities do exist, he says:

children.text: Chapter 11
aparyālocitapaurvāparyagatānugatamūrkhajanapravartitāt pravādamātrād asakṛddṛṣṭavyabhicārād vastusiddhim icchan aho bata vṛthaiva dainyāspadatām upayāto 'si ||
children.translated_text: If you seek to establish a real entity from mere report, set in motion by foolish people who follow along without examining what precedes and follows, and repeatedly observed to be unreliable, then alas, you have quite uselessly fallen into a pitiable condition.

children.text: atha pratyayitapuruṣapravartitaḥ pravādaḥ tarhi āgama evāsau ||
children.translated_text: But if the report was set in motion by a trustworthy person, then it is itself an <s>āgama</s> (authoritative tradition).

children.text: pratyayitatvaṃ ca tasya katamena pramāṇena siddhaṃ tatpravartitād āgamaprāmāṇyāc ca tatsiddhiḥ tatsiddhyā ca āgamaprāmāṇyam itītaretarāśrayadoṣaḥ nityatve tv āgamasya kārya evārthe prāmāṇyaṃ na siddhe iti na yuṣmadabhimatadevatāviśeṣaḥ katham api sidhyatīti ||
children.translated_text: And by what <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge) is his trustworthiness established? If that is established from the authority of the <s>āgama</s> set in motion by him, and the authority of the <s>āgama</s> from the establishment of that trustworthiness, there is the fault of mutual dependence. But if the <s>āgama</s> is eternal, its authority concerns only what is to be done, not an already established fact; therefore the particular deity accepted by you is not proved in any way.

children.text: evaṃ śakroktim abhidhāya hārītamuniḥ svoktyā svaśiṣyān āha ||
children.translated_text: Having thus stated <s>Śakra</s>'s speech, the sage <s>Hārīta</s> addresses his own disciples in his own words.

children.text: Chapter 12

ity anenoktena krameṇa īśvaranirākaraṇavacanāny eva nimnamārgānusaraṇād vārīṇi teṣāṃ velā samullāso jalavṛddhir iti yāvat tayā nunnaḥ prerito 'py eṣāṃ bharadvājādīnāṃ sambandhī matiparvataḥ sāravattvāt gurutvāc ca hetoḥ na cacāla na cakampe
children.translated_text: By this stated sequence, the very statements that refute <s>Īśvara</s>, because they follow a downward course, are the waters; their "shore-surge" means a swelling of water. Even though driven and impelled by that, the mountain of thought belonging to these men such as <s>Bharadvāja</s> did not move, did not tremble, because of its substantiality and weight.

children.text: kena nunna ity āha abdhineva śakreṇa
children.translated_text: By what was it driven? He says: by <s>Śakra</s>, as by the ocean.

children.text: yathā kila velācalaḥ samudrajalataraṃgadṛḍhāhataḥ svāvaṣṭambhān na calati evaṃ munimatis tīkṣṇāgratvādisādharmyāt parvatena rūpakīkṛtā ca svasthairyān na vyacalat ||
children.translated_text: For just as a shore-mountain, firmly struck by waves of ocean water, does not move because of its own support, so the sages' thought, metaphorically made into a mountain because of similarities such as sharp-peakedness, did not move from its own stability.

children.text: tataś cendraṃ prati te punar idam abhyadadhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then they again said this to <s>Indra</s>:

children.text: Chapter 13

vibhūtiyogatāratamyam asmadādilocanagocaracāri sāmānyapuruṣamātrāśrayaṃ dṛṣṭam adṛṣṭavigrahasya devatāviśeṣasya aṇimādyaiśvaryasampattim anumāpayati tat kathaṃ prākāmyaśaktijanitaṃ yugapad anekadeśamātrasaṃnidhimātram asaṃbhāvyaṃ manyase ||
children.translated_text: The observed gradation in the possession of supernormal power, moving within the range of sight of people like us and resting merely in ordinary persons, leads us to infer the possession of lordly powers such as <s>aṇimā</s> by a particular deity whose form is unseen. So how can you regard as impossible even mere simultaneous presence in many places, produced by the power of <s>prākāmya</s>?

children.text: na hi kadācid asmadādiśarīravat devatāmūrtiḥ kleśakarmavipākāśayayoginy avyāpikā vā icchāmātreṇāsmadādisṛṣṭisthitidhvaṃsakaraṇakṣamaviśiṣṭaiśvaryasampannatvāt ||
children.translated_text: For a deity's form is never like a body such as ours, joined with afflictions, karma, karmic fruition, and latent deposits, nor is it non-pervasive, since it is endowed with a distinctive lordly power capable, by mere will, of causing the creation, maintenance, and destruction of beings such as ourselves.

children.text: mūrchitāṇutrāṇāddhi mūrtitvam asmadādimūrtitvavilakṣaṇaṃ cāsyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For its having a form is for the protection of benumbed <s>aṇus</s> (finite souls), and this formhood is unlike the formhood of beings such as ourselves.

children.text: tataś ca yugapad anekadeśasaṃnidhinirākaraṇāyopāttasya mūrtitvākhyasya hetor aprayojakatvam ||
children.translated_text: Consequently, the reason called "having a form," adopted in order to refute simultaneous presence in many places, is irrelevant to what is to be proved.

children.text: dṛṣṭāntaś cānupapannaḥ sādhyadharmāsiddhatvāt ||
children.translated_text: And the example is untenable, because the property to be proved is not established in it.

children.text: sādhyo hi dharmas tulyakālam anekadeśāsaṃnidhilakṣaṇo 'tra sarvātmanā nāsti yasmād asmadādimadhyavartināṃ mūrtimatāṃ satām apy aṇimādisiddhiprakarṣayogināṃ yogināṃ yugapad anekadeśasaṃnidhir adyatve 'pi nāsaṃbhāvyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the property to be proved here, defined as non-presence in many places at the same time, is not present in every respect, since even today simultaneous presence in many places is not impossible for embodied <s>yogins</s> among people like us who possess an excellence of accomplishments such as <s>aṇimā</s>.

children.text: na ca niratiśayasakalotkarṣayoginaḥ parameśvarasya svadarśanābhiniveśibhiḥ kumbhakārādinidarśanakaluṣīkriyamāṇajagannirmāṇasya kiṃkāyaḥ kimāśrayaḥ kimupakaraṇa ity ādyasadvikalpaviplavo 'nupraviśati ||
children.translated_text: Nor does the turmoil of false conjectures such as, "What body does he have? what support? what instruments?" enter into <s>Parameśvara</s>'s creation of the world, which those attached to their own doctrine sully with examples such as a potter; for he possesses unsurpassed excellence in every respect.

children.text: tathā coktaṃ siddhacūḍāmaṇinā
children.translated_text: And so it has been said by <s>Siddhacūḍāmaṇi</s>:

children.text: kim īhaḥ kiṃkāyaḥ sa khalu kim upāyas tribhuvanaṃ kim ādhāro dhātā sṛjati kimupādāna iti ca
children.translated_text: "What is his effort? what is his body? what indeed is his means? On what basis does the creator create the three worlds, and what is the material cause?"

children.text: atarkyaiśvarye tvayy anavasaraduḥstho hatadhiyaḥ kutarko 'yaṃ kāṃścin mukharayati mohāya jagatām ||
children.translated_text: This wretched sophistry, out of place with regard to you whose lordly power is beyond reasoning, makes some witless people noisy, to the bewilderment of the worlds.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: yathā cāśarīradevatāviśeṣasambhavo 'saṃbhavadbādhas tatheśvarasiddhiprakaraṇe vakṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And we shall explain in the section on the proof of the Lord how the possibility of a particular disembodied deity is not subject to any impossible refutation.

children.text: sa tu tathā tathā pratipādyamāno 'pi na tannirākaraṇapravaṇānāṃ prayojanahetur bhaviṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: But although he is demonstrated in various ways, he will not become a cause of benefit for those who are intent on denying him.

children.text: atra daivopahatatvam evāparādhyati ||
children.translated_text: Here only ill-fatedness is to blame.

children.text: yathāha rājānaka utpaladevaḥ
children.translated_text: As <s>Rājānaka Utpaladeva</s> says:

children.text: samujjvalannyāyasahasrasādhito 'py upaiti siddhiṃ na vimūḍhacetasām ||
children.translated_text: "Though established by thousands of brilliantly shining arguments, he does not become established for people of bewildered mind.

children.text: maheśvaraḥ pāṇitale sthito 'pi san palāyate daivahatasya sanmaṇiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one struck down by fate, even a true jewel resting in the palm of the hand slips away."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: īdṛśābhyāṃ ca hetudṛṣṭāntābhyāṃ sādhyasiddhyupagame 'nyatrāpy ayam eva nyāyaḥ prasajyata ity āha ||
children.translated_text: And he says that, if the establishment of the probandum were accepted on the basis of such a reason and example, this same reasoning would follow in other cases too.

children.text: Chapter 14
bhavatā kila śabdamātraṃ hi devatā iti pratijñātam ataḥ śabdavyatiriktadevatānabhyupagame saty etad āpatitaṃ yad uta vācakavyatiriktavācyārthāsambhavaḥ
children.translated_text: You, after all, have asserted the thesis, "The deity is merely a word." Therefore, when one does not accept a deity apart from the word, this follows: a denoted object apart from the denoting word is impossible.

children.text: indrādiśabdānāṃ nānyo vācyo 'rtho vidyate
children.translated_text: For words such as "<s>Indra</s>" have no other denoted object.

children.text: evaṃ śabdatvāviśeṣāt ghaṭādāv api ayam eva nyāyo 'stu na caitad yuktam anubhavavirodhāt ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, since there is no difference in their being words, let this very reasoning apply also to a pot and the like. But this is not reasonable, because it contradicts experience.

children.text: tathā hi ||
children.translated_text: For example:

children.text: Chapter 15

ghaṭate ceṣṭate arthakriyām iti ghaṭaḥ candati hlādayati dīpyate ceti candra ity evaṃvidhayā śabdavyutpattyā śabdavyatiriktavācyārthāsaṃbhavato ghaṭaśabdasyaivodakāharaṇaṃ candraśabdasyaiva cāhlādanādi prāptaṃ na cānayos tad asti api tu tadvācyayoḥ pṛthubudhnodarādyākārabhāsvarabimbasvarūpayos tattadarthakriyākaraṇakṣamatvaṃ dṛṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: By such derivations as "a pot is so called because it exerts itself and performs a practical function" and "the moon is so called because it delights and shines," if a denoted object apart from the word were impossible, then bringing water would belong to the word "pot" itself, and delighting and so on to the word "moon" itself. But those capacities are not present in these two words; rather, the ability to perform those respective functions is seen in the things denoted by them, whose forms are a broad base and belly and the like, and a shining disk.

children.text: tato na vācyavācakayor aikyam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the denoted object and the denoting word are not identical.

children.text: tataś ca na śabdamātraṃ devatā kiṃ tarhi tadvācyaiveti siddham ||
children.translated_text: And therefore the deity is not merely a word. Rather, it is precisely what that word denotes; this is established.

children.text: idānīṃ vākyaṃ tadanyathāsiddham iti paramatam anusaṃdhāya dūṣayati ||
children.translated_text: Now, taking up the opponent's view that the sentence is otherwise accounted for, he refutes it.

children.text: Chapter 16

indro vajrī hiraṇmayaḥ ityādīni vākyāni śakrādidevatāliṅgāni mantrārthavādaparāṇi tv eṣāṃ svarūpayāthārthyam iti yad bhavadbhir abhihitaṃ tat tathāstu svārthapratipādanaparāṇāṃ tu śrūyamāṇānāṃ karmarūpādiśabdānāṃ katham arthavattvaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: You have said that sentences such as "<s>Indra</s>, wielder of the thunderbolt, golden" are marks of deities such as <s>Śakra</s> and are concerned with mantras and eulogistic passages, and that for these their truth lies in their own verbal form. Let that be so. But how could action words, color words, and the like, which are heard as intent on conveying their own meanings, be meaningful?

children.text: tatra karmaśabdāḥ kriyābhidhāyinaḥ vrīhīn avahanti ityādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among these, action words are those that express actions, such as "he pounds the rice-grains."

children.text: evaṃ rūpaśabdāḥ jātyādiśabdāś ca ||
children.translated_text: So too there are color words, class words, and the like.

children.text: yathā śvetaṃ chāgam ālabheta ity atra śvetaśabdasya rūpābhidhāyinaḥ chāgaśabdasya ca jātivācinaḥ śakrādiśabdavat śabdatvāviśeṣāt svarūpayāthārthyāsaṃbhave saty ānarthakyaṃ tataś ca codanāvākyānām akiṃcitkaratvam ||
children.translated_text: For example, in "one should sacrifice a white goat," if, because there is no difference in their being words, the color-denoting word "white" and the class-denoting word "goat," like words such as "<s>Śakra</s>," cannot be true to their own referents, then they are meaningless; and consequently injunction-sentences would accomplish nothing.

children.text: yad vā śakrādivācakasya vākyasyānyaviṣayatve kalpyamāne tadviṣayāṇām indro vṛtram avadhīt ityādīnāṃ karmaśabdānāṃ sahasradṛgvajrapāṇyādīnāṃ ca rūpādyabhidhāyināṃ śabdānāṃ katham arthavattvaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: Or, if a sentence that denotes <s>Śakra</s> and the like is imagined to have another subject matter, how would action words such as "<s>Indra</s> slew <s>Vṛtra</s>," and words denoting form and the like, such as "thousand-eyed" and "thunderbolt-handed," whose subject matter is that same deity, be meaningful?

children.text: na cārghajaratīyanyāya upapādayituṃ śakyo yena vidhiśabdānām eva svarūpayāthārthyaṃ nendrādiśabdānām iti syāt ||
children.translated_text: Nor can one justify the <s>ardhajaratīya-nyāya</s> (the half-old-woman maxim), by which there would be truth to their own form only for injunctive words and not for words such as "<s>Indra</s>."

children.text: yad apy uktaṃ lokavādāḥ kva sādhavaḥ iti tad ayuktam ||
children.translated_text: And what was also said, "Where are popular sayings trustworthy?" is unreasonable.

children.text: yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: For:

children.text: Chapter 17
nadyās tīre guḍaśakaṭaṃ paryastam ityāder nirmūlasyāpi pravādasya ekāntena na mithyātvaṃ kadācit saṃvāditatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Even a baseless report such as "a cart of jaggery has overturned on the riverbank" is not absolutely false, because it sometimes agrees with fact.

children.text: tataś ca sarvapravādo na satya ity etan na yuktimat na pramāṇopapannam iti yāvat samūlatve sati mithyātvāsiddheḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the claim that no popular report is true is not reasonable, that is, it is not supported by a means of knowledge, since when a basis exists its falsity is not established.

children.text: mūlaṃ cāsyāgamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the basis of this is <s>āgama</s> (authoritative tradition).

children.text: tathā cāhuḥ
children.translated_text: And so they say:

children.text: prasiddhim āgamaḥ prāpto loka ity abhidhīyate
children.translated_text: "An <s>āgama</s> (authoritative tradition) that has reached common renown is called <s>loka</s> (popular usage)."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: atha nirmūlo yaḥ pravādaḥ sa cen mithyārūpaḥ tad apy ayuktaṃ yasmād evaṃ kalpyamāne bhūtānāṃ sarvāḥ pravṛttayo vyāhanyeran ||
children.translated_text: Now, if a report that is baseless is false in nature, that too is unreasonable, because if this were assumed, all the activities of beings would be obstructed.

children.text: sarvo hi hitaprepsur ahitajihāsur vā na pramāṇaghaṭanāṃ kṛtvā tāṃ puraskṛtya lokavyavahāre dṛṣṭaphale sevākṛṣyādāv adṛṣṭaphale veṣṭāpūrtādau pravartate kiṃ tu prāyaśo gatānugatikapravādamātrādhivāsitamatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For everyone who desires benefit or wishes to avoid harm does not engage in worldly dealings, such as service and agriculture whose results are seen, or in acts such as <s>iṣṭāpūrta</s> whose results are unseen, after first constructing a proof and placing it before himself. Rather, for the most part, his mind is conditioned merely by a report followed by those who came before.

children.text: kīdṛśaṃ ca bhavatā pravādasya mūlam anveṣṭavyam ||
children.translated_text: And what sort of basis for a report is to be sought by you?

children.text: yadi cirakālapravṛttatvena bahujanoddhoṣsthayamāṇatvaṃ tad yuktam eva ||
children.translated_text: If it is its having been current for a long time and being proclaimed by many people, that is indeed reasonable.

children.text: anyathā pravāda eva nāsau tathā ca sati nāsya mithyātvam ||
children.translated_text: Otherwise, it is not a report at all; and if that is so, its falsity does not apply.

children.text: cirataram anekajanaprathitatve 'pi kuto 'syodbhava ity evaṃ vidhimūlaṃ parīkṣyate tarhy āgamaparīkṣaiveyaṃ na lokavādavicāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: But if, even though it has long been widely known among many people, one examines its source, asking, "From where did this arise?", then this is simply an examination of <s>āgama</s> (authoritative tradition), not an inquiry into public report.

children.text: na caitad evaṃ yato bhavadbhir api śrutirūpād āgamād anya eva sajjanasevito vyavahāraḥ śiṣṭācārākhyo dharmamūlatvenābhyupagata ity alaṃ pradveṣeṇa ||
children.translated_text: And this is not so, since even by you a practice distinct from <s>āgama</s> in the form of <s>śruti</s>, followed by good people and called <s>śiṣṭācāra</s> (the conduct of the learned), is accepted as a root of <s>dharma</s> (normative order). Enough with hostility.

children.text: tad evaṃ samūlena lokapravādeneśvarākhyaviśiṣṭadevatāsaṃbhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by a public tradition that has a genuine source, the existence of the particular deity called <s>Īśvara</s> is possible.

children.text: tathā hi ||
children.translated_text: For so it is.

children.text: Chapter 18
kiṃ na nāmākhilajanapratītam etad yan munir upamanyuḥ parameśvareṇa varapradāne nānugṛhītaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Surely this is known to all people: the sage <s>Upamanyu</s> was favored by <s>Parameśvara</s> in the granting of boons.

children.text: tathā ca mahābhārate ānuśāsanike parvaṇi bhagavadvyāsamuninopamanyuvākyaṃ pradarśitam
children.translated_text: And so, in the <s>Ānuśāsanika Parvan</s> of the <s>Mahābhārata</s>, the blessed sage <s>Vyāsa</s> has set forth the words of <s>Upamanyu</s>:

children.text: āha māṃ bhagavān īśaḥ prahasann iva śaṃkaraḥ
children.translated_text: "The blessed Lord, <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, said to me, as though smiling:

children.text: vatsopamanyo prīto 'smi paśya māṃ munipuṃgava ||
children.translated_text: 'Child <s>Upamanyu</s>, I am pleased. Behold me, foremost of sages.

children.text: dṛḍhabhakto 'si viprarṣe mayā jijñāsitas tv asi
children.translated_text: You are firm in devotion, O Brahmin-sage; you have been tested by me.

children.text: anayā vatsa sadbhaktyā te 'tyarthaṃ prītavān aham ||
children.translated_text: By this true devotion of yours, child, I have been exceedingly pleased.

children.text: tasmāt sarvān pradāsyāmi varān ye manasi sthitāḥ
