children.translated_text: Therefore I shall grant all the boons that are present in your mind.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus."

children.text: athocyate mithyaitad upamanyunātmaprabhāvakathanāyoktam atra hi kiṃ pramāṇaṃ yad evam asau bhagavatānugṛhīta iti
children.translated_text: Now it is said: "This is false, spoken by <s>Upamanyu</s> in order to proclaim his own greatness. For what <s>pramāṇa</s> (proof) is there here that he was thus favored by the Blessed One?"

children.text: tad asad yasmāt ||
children.translated_text: That is unsound, because:

children.text: Chapter 19
yasya kila sakalamunijanapratyakṣaparidṛśyamānaḥ kṣīrābdhiḥ svādhīnaḥ tasya vacasaḥ kiṃ nāma mithyātvam
children.translated_text: How indeed could the statement of one be false when the milk-ocean, directly seen by the whole company of sages, was under his control?

children.text: ayam āśayaḥ parameśvarāt prāptavaro 'ham ity anṛtavāditvaṃ tadānīṃ tasya bhavet yadi dugdhodadhivaśīkāraḥ pracuramunijanapratyakṣo na syāt
children.translated_text: The idea is this: he would then have been speaking falsely in saying, "I received a boon from <s>Parameśvara</s>," if his mastery over the ocean of milk had not been directly witnessed by many sages.

children.text: yadi ca saṃvādīny api vacāṃsi mithyā tarhi na kiṃcit satyavacanam
children.translated_text: And if even statements that are corroborated are false, then there is no true statement at all.

children.text: praśāntarāgadveṣāṇāṃ sākṣātkṛtabhūtabhaviṣyadarthānāṃ munīnām api mithyāvāditvābhyupagame manvādayo 'pi dattadakṣiṇās tvayety aho svadarśanakauśalam ||
children.translated_text: If false speech is admitted even for sages whose passion and hatred are pacified and who directly know past and future realities, then <s>Manu</s> and the others too must, one supposes, have received a fee from you. Ah, what skill in your own doctrine!

children.text: kiṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: Chapter 20

viṣānalārciḥparamparākṣepabhīṣaṇenāśīviṣapāśena vivaśīkṛtaḥ śvetaḥ pātīti patis tena patyā trāṇaśīlena parameśvareṇa huṃkāramātraṃ kṛtvā krodhāgninā bhasmīkṛtya mocitaḥ iti ghanair aviralair bhūyobhir janair asmatsajātīyair muniprabhṛtibhiś ca dṛṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śveta</s>, made helpless by the noose of a venomous serpent, fearsome because it hurled forth successive flames of poisonous fire, was seen by many dense and unbroken crowds of people of our own kind, and by sages and others, to have been released by the Lord, the protecting <s>Pati</s>, <s>Parameśvara</s>, who merely made a huṃkāra and burned it to ashes with the fire of anger.

children.text: atrāpi trikāladarśibhir devaiś ca pravartite pravāde yady asamāśvāsas tarhi āgamam eva na sahata iti vaktavyaṃ tathā ca sati śrutir api asahanasya bhavataḥ prāmāṇyalābhe dainyena bhītabhītā mukham anvīkṣata iti tadanukampayā saṃrakṣyatām atisāhasam ||
children.translated_text: If even here, in a tradition set in motion by seers of the three times and by gods, you have no trust, then it must be said that you simply cannot tolerate <s>āgama</s>. And if that is so, even <s>śruti</s>, seeking to obtain authority for you who cannot tolerate it, looks anxiously at your face in pitiable fear; therefore, out of compassion for it, restrain this excessive rashness.

children.text: nanu mithyātvahetūnāṃ doṣāṇāṃ kartrāśrayatvād akṛtakatvena nityatvāt śrutes tasyāḥ prāmāṇyāya ko 'yam upahāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But, it may be objected, since the defects that cause falsity reside in an author, and since <s>śruti</s> is unmade and therefore eternal, what is this ridicule concerning its authority?

children.text: na kaścit kiṃ tu kartrabhāvaniścaye pramāṇaṃ notpaśyāmaḥ pratyuta svayaṃbhuve namaskṛtya ityādivākyavat racanāvattvāt kartṛvyāpārāvivanābhāvitvam utprekṣāmaha ity alam anena ||
children.translated_text: None at all. But we see no <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge) for determining the absence of an author; rather, because it has composition, as in sentences such as "having bowed to <s>Svayambhū</s>," we conjecture that it is inseparably connected with the activity of an author. Enough of this.

children.text: prakṛtam anusarāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let us return to the matter at hand.

children.text: Chapter 21
uktavaddevatāstitvaprastāvāyāyātaparameśvarapraśaṃsāharṣapravṛttānandāśruvaśād avispaṣṭagirastān bharadvājādīn dṛṣṭvā indras tān prati paraṃ tutoṣa ity evaṃ hārītamuniḥ svaśiṣyān āha ||
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Bharadvāja</s> and the others whose words were indistinct because of tears of joy, which had begun from delight at the praise of <s>Parameśvara</s> that had arisen in the discussion of the existence of deity as stated, <s>Indra</s> was exceedingly pleased with them. Thus the sage <s>Hārīta</s> spoke to his own disciples.

children.text: Chapter 22
pratyagrārkabhāsvaraṃ devair gaṇaiś ca stūyamānam ātmīyaṃ rūpaṃ vajrapāṇir devaḥ śatakratuḥ prakaṭīcakāra
children.translated_text: The god <s>Śatakratu</s>, holding the thunderbolt in his hand, revealed his own form, shining like a newly risen sun and praised by gods and gaṇas.

children.text: tejo'tiśayayogasya hetutayā śatakratur vajrīti ca viśeṣaṇadvayam
children.translated_text: The two epithets <s>Śatakratu</s> and <s>Vajrin</s> state the cause of his possessing surpassing splendor.

children.text: kuliśasya svabhāva evāyaṃ yad adbhutaprabhābhāsvaratvaṃ śatakratutvāc ca tajjanitapuṇyaprabhāvād adbhutabhūrimahaḥsamūhatvam iti ||
children.translated_text: For it is the very nature of the thunderbolt to shine with wondrous radiance; and because he is <s>Śatakratu</s>, through the power of the merit produced by that, he possesses a wondrous mass of abundant splendor.

children.text: Chapter 23
te bharadvājādayas taṃ pratyakṣīkṛtasvasvarūpam indraṃ ṛgyajuḥsāmabhiḥ prahvāḥ santas tuṣṭuvuḥ
children.translated_text: Those sages beginning with <s>Bharadvāja</s>, having directly seen <s>Indra</s> in his own true form, bowed down and praised him with <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s> verses.

children.text: sa ca sarvajagatpravaro varo bhavadbhir abhyarthyatām iti tān āha
children.translated_text: And he said to them, "Let a boon, the best in all the world, be requested by you."

children.text: te tadaivam uktāḥ pārameśvaraṃ jñānaṃ śāstraṃ vṛtavantaḥ
children.translated_text: When they had been addressed in this way, they chose the <s>śāstra</s> (teaching), the knowledge concerning <s>Parameśvara</s>.

children.text: sa tu tadabhyarthitaṃ jñānopadeśaṃ dātuṃ tān prativacanaṃ śrūyatām ity āha kiṃ tu mamaika eva bhavatāṃ madhyāt sakalaśrotṛjanābhimato yathāvasaram anuktavastunaḥ praṣṭā bhavatu sarvaiś caiva bhavadbhiḥ śrūyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: But he, in order to give the instruction in knowledge requested by them, said in reply to them, "Let my answer be heard. Yet let just one among you, approved by all the listeners, be my questioner at the proper occasions about matters not yet stated, and let it be heard by all of you."

children.text: evaṃ bhagavatā śakreṇokte sati ||
children.translated_text: When the blessed <s>Śakra</s> had spoken thus,

children.text: Chapter 24

athānantaraṃ teṣāṃ madhyād aiśvaryādiguṇayogāt bhagavān vividhaśāstrābhyāsādhivāsapraśasyavāgyuktatvāc ca vāgmī praṣṭavyāvasareṣu akauśalāpratipattyādyayogāt pragalbhaś ca bharadvājo munir nyāyata iti nyāyena śiṣyocitayā nītyā yuktyupapannapūrvapakṣakaraṇena vā indram apṛcchad iti ||
children.translated_text: then, immediately afterward, from among them, the sage <s>Bharadvāja</s>--called blessed because he possessed qualities such as lordly power, eloquent because he had praiseworthy speech formed by practice in various <s>śāstra</s>s, and bold because he was not subject to lack of skill, failure of understanding, and the like on occasions for questioning--asked <s>Indra</s> according to <s>nyāya</s>, that is, by a method proper for a disciple, or by setting forth a prima facie objection supported by reasoning.

children.text: āha ||
children.translated_text: He said:

children.text: Chapter 25
yad etad bhagavatā asmabhyam upadeṣṭum ārabdham itarebhyo jñānebhyaḥ sātiśayaphalatvāc chreṣṭhatamaṃ jñānaṃ tat kathaṃ maheśvarāt praśāntasvarūpān niṣkalāc chivāt prasṛtam ||
children.translated_text: How did this knowledge, which the blessed one has begun to teach us, the very best among other knowledges because its fruit is unsurpassed, issue forth from <s>Maheśvara</s>, from <s>Śiva</s> who is partless and whose nature is wholly tranquil?

children.text: jñānaṃ hi dvirūpam avabodharūpaṃ śabdarūpaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: For knowledge is twofold: it has the form of understanding and the form of words.

children.text: tad avabodharūpaṃ śabdarūpārūḍhaṃ sarveṣu pravartate ||
children.translated_text: That knowledge in the form of understanding, mounted upon the form of words, comes into operation among all.

children.text: tatrāditaḥ parameśvarād avabodharūpam eva tāvat kathaṃ prāptaṃ kathaṃ ca śabdarūpatām etya bahubhedabhinnaṃ sampannam ||
children.translated_text: In that case, first, how was it obtained from <s>Parameśvara</s> in the form of understanding, and how, having entered the form of words, did it become divided into many distinctions?

children.text: kiṃ cākalayya bhagavān idam akarot ||
children.translated_text: And with what in view did the blessed one do this?

children.text: na hy anabhisaṃhitaprayojanaḥ kaścit kartā kiṃcit kāryaṃ kurvan dṛṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For no agent is ever seen to perform any action without having intended a purpose.

children.text: tasya ca bhagavata etat karaṇe kiṃ kāraṇam ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is: what cause did that blessed one have in doing this?

children.text: athātra prativacanam ||
children.translated_text: Now here is the reply.

children.text: Chapter 26

sargaprārambhe parameśvareṇa puruṣārthasya bhuktimuktyātmanaḥ sampattyarthaṃ vimalam ity avabodhātmano nādarūpatvena prathamaṃ prasṛtatvād agṛhītopādhibhedaṃ paratas tūrdhvaprāgdakṣiṇapaścimottarasrotaḥpañcakenābhitaḥ samantāt prasṛtatvena lakṣitam iti sadāśivarūpeṇa darśanātmatāṃ prāpitaṃ jñānaṃ nirmitam iti kramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the beginning of creation, for the attainment of the human goal consisting of enjoyment and liberation, <s>Parameśvara</s> produced knowledge: because, as understanding, it first issued forth in the form of <s>nāda</s> (resonant sound), it was stainless and had not assumed distinctions of limiting adjuncts; and afterwards, because it issued forth everywhere through the five streams upward, eastward, southward, westward, and northward, it was marked out and, in the form of <s>Sadāśiva</s>, brought to the state of revelation. This is the sequence.

children.text: prayojanaṃ ca pūrvapraśnitam upavarṇitam ||
children.translated_text: And the purpose asked about earlier has been described.

children.text: kiṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: Chapter 27

mantroddhāraprakaraṇābhidhāsyamānajñānamadhyavartino vācakavrātasya mantragaṇasya ye vācyā anantādayo 'ṣṭau vidyeśās tāṃs tathā māyīyasyāśuddhasyādhvanas tatkālam anāvirbhāvāc chuddhavidyābhuvane kṛtasthitīn saptakoṭisaṃkhyātān mantrān parameśvaro vidhatta iti pūrveṇa sambandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is connected with the preceding statement: <s>Parameśvara</s> appoints the eight <s>Vidyeśa</s>s beginning with <s>Ananta</s>, who are denoted by the multitude of mantras, the set of denoting expressions situated within the knowledge that will be taught in the section on mantra-extraction; and likewise he appoints the mantras numbering seven crores, established in the realm of pure <s>vidyā</s> because at that time the impure <s>adhvan</s> belonging to <s>Māyā</s> had not yet become manifest.

children.text: kālasāmānye 'pi prathamalakārasya spaṣṭatvāt sṛṣṭikāle vyadhād ity arthaḥ pratisargakālaṃ vā tathā karotīti vartamānataiva ||
children.translated_text: Although the time-reference is general, because the first tense-form is explicit, the meaning is that he arranged them at the time of creation; or else, since he does so at each re-creation, the present-tense sense itself is appropriate.

children.text: tatra vidyeśvarāṇāṃ vāmādiśaktiyogitvena svasamaprabhāvāvirbhāvanaṃ nāma karaṇaṃ mantrāṇāṃ tv āgamāpagamāt prakaṭīkṛtadṛkkriyatvam ||
children.translated_text: There, in the case of the <s>Vidyeśvara</s>s, their creation means the manifestation of a power equal to his own through their union with the powers beginning with <s>Vāmā</s>; but in the case of the mantras, it means that their vision and action have been made manifest through approach and withdrawal.

children.text: ubhayeṣām apy eṣāṃ parameśvarāj jñānakriyāśaktyor uddīpanaṃ jñeyam na punar muktāṇuvan nirmalīkaraṇam adhikāramalenāparatvān mukter asyā iti vakṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For both of these, this should be understood as a kindling, from <s>Parameśvara</s>, of the powers of knowledge and action, not as a purification like that of liberated <s>aṇu</s>s (finite souls); for this state is lower than liberation because it contains the impurity of office, as we shall explain.

children.text: tad evaṃ mantramaheśvarān mantrāṃś coktvā mantreśvarān vaktum āha ||
children.translated_text: Thus, after speaking of the <s>Mantramaheśvara</s>s and the mantras, in order to speak of the <s>Mantreśvara</s>s he says:

children.text: Chapter 28
māyāyām adhikāriṇo māyādhikāriṇas teṣām uparitanaśuddhādhvavartividyeśvarasamānadhāmnām aṣṭādaśādhikaṃ śataṃ vidhatta iti pūrveṇaiva sambandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those who hold office in <s>Māyā</s> are <s>Māyādhikārin</s>s. The connection is again with the preceding statement: he appoints one hundred and eighteen of them, whose station is equal to that of the <s>Vidyeśvara</s>s dwelling in the higher pure <s>adhvan</s>.

children.text: tatra maṇḍalino 'ṣṭau vakṣyamāṇāḥ krodhādyāś cāṣṭāv eva rudrāṇāṃ ca brahmāṇḍadhārakāṇāṃ śataṃ śrīkaṇṭhavīrabhadrau cety evam aṣṭādaśottaraṃ śataṃ prāgvan mantreśvaratve śivena niyuktam ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among them are the eight <s>Maṇḍalin</s>s who will be mentioned later, likewise the eight <s>Rudra</s>s beginning with <s>Krodha</s>, the hundred <s>Rudra</s>s who support the cosmic eggs, and <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> and <s>Vīrabhadra</s>. Thus the sense is that, as before, the one hundred and eighteen were appointed by <s>Śiva</s> to the state of <s>Mantreśvara</s>s.

children.text: Chapter 29
teṣv anantādiṣu mantramaheśvareṣu maṇḍalyādiṣu ca mantreśvareṣv abhivyakto deva idam ity anantaropakrāntaṃ jñānaṃ prakāśayati
children.translated_text: Manifest in those <s>Mantramaheśvara</s>s beginning with <s>Ananta</s> and in the <s>Mantreśvara</s>s beginning with the <s>Maṇḍalin</s>s, the god reveals this knowledge that was just introduced by the word "this."

children.text: kasmin viṣaye kim arthaṃ prakāśayatīty āha yogyeṣu siddhaye paripakvāñjanatvān niratiśayaśreyaḥprepsuṣu bhuktyarthaṃ muktyarthaṃ ca vaktīty arthaḥ
children.translated_text: In what sphere and for what purpose does he reveal it? He says: among those who are fit, for accomplishment. The meaning is that he teaches it to those who, being mature persons, desire unsurpassed welfare, for the sake of enjoyment and for the sake of liberation.

children.text: ato 'nyeṣv iti etacchāstrārhebhyo ye 'nye aparipakvāñjanatayā paśuśāstrānuvartinas teṣu viṣayeṣu yaḥ kāpilapāñcarātrādi prāpyo 'rthaḥ samyag iti taduktayogyatānusāreṇopapadyate anuguṇo bhavati taṃ prakāśayati
children.translated_text: "Among others than these" means: among those other than persons qualified for this scripture, who, because they are immature persons, follow the scriptures for bound souls. In their case he reveals the object attainable through systems such as <s>Kāpila</s> and <s>Pāñcarātra</s>; "properly" means that it is made intelligible, that is, it becomes suitable, in accordance with the qualification taught there.

children.text: paśuśāstrapraṇetṝn adhiṣṭhāya tattacchāstraprakāśanam api pāramparyeṇa kuruta iti yāvat ||
children.translated_text: That is, he also brings about, indirectly, the manifestation of each of those scriptures by presiding over the propounders of the scriptures for bound souls.

children.text: athāsya jñānasyāsmabhyam abhidhīyamānasya kim abhidhānam ity āha ||
children.translated_text: Now he asks: what is the name of this knowledge that is being taught to us?

children.text: Chapter 30

parameśvarāt proktena krameṇa prasṛtam etaj jñānaṃ śāstraṃ skandasya devyās tad anyeṣāṃ ca pṛthak pṛthak śrotṝṇāṃ bahutvād bahubhedatvena vistaram abhimatakāmadatvāt kāmikatvenopadeṣṭṛbhir mantrāṇāṃ mantreśvarāṇāṃ ceśvarair mantramaheśvarair anantādibhir upadiṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: This knowledge, this scripture, having issued from <s>Parameśvara</s> in the stated sequence, became extensive in many divisions because of the multitude of separate hearers, <s>Skanda</s>, <s>Devī</s>, and the others; because it grants the desired aims, it is <s>Kāmika</s>. It was taught by the <s>Mantramaheśvara</s>s beginning with <s>Ananta</s>, the lords who instruct the mantras and the <s>Mantreśvara</s>s.

children.text: tebhya āgamayya kasmai kiyatā granthena ko dattavān ity āha ||
children.translated_text: Having received it from them, who gave it, to whom, and in how large a work? He says:

children.text: Chapter 31
tebhyo 'nanteśādibhyas tṛtīyanetrāgniśikhānirdagdhasmaratarur bhagavān umāpatir adhigamya bhavasaṃkhyair ekādaśabhiḥ sahasraiḥ saṃkṣipya mahyam adāt ||
children.translated_text: Having learned it from those beginning with <s>Ananteśa</s>, the blessed <s>Umāpati</s>, who had burned <s>Smara</s>'s body with a flame of fire from his third eye, condensed it into eleven thousand verses, the number indicated by <s>Bhava</s>, and gave it to me.

children.text: so 'ham idānīm ||
children.translated_text: I, then, now,

children.text: Chapter 32

tatrāpi arthavādānuvādarūpaṃ vistaraṃ tyaktvā sārārthābhidhāyibhir bāhulyena kvacit taduktaiḥ kvacic cātmīyair nirākulaṃ kramaṃ jñānaṃ śāstram abhidhāsye itīndro munīn āheti hārītaḥ svaśiṣyān brūte ||
children.translated_text: even within that, setting aside the expansion consisting of <s>arthavāda</s> (eulogy) and <s>anuvāda</s> (restatement), shall explain the knowledge, the scripture, in an orderly sequence free from confusion, mostly through words expressing the essential meaning, sometimes in words stated there and sometimes in my own. Thus <s>Indra</s> says to the sages, and <s>Hārīta</s> tells his own disciples.

children.text: Chapter 33
sambandhābhidheyaprayojanāni prathamam eva vivecitāni ||
children.translated_text: The relation, the subject matter, and the purpose have already been distinguished at the very beginning.

children.text: athety ānuṣaṅgikasambandhādikathanād anantaraṃ vidyākhyaḥ pādaḥ prakramyate ||
children.translated_text: After the statement of the incidental connection and the like, the section called <s>Vidyā</s> is now begun.

children.text: atra ca śāstre patipaśupāśākhyās trayaḥ padārthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And in this śāstra there are three categories called <s>pati</s> (Lord), <s>paśu</s> (bound soul), and <s>pāśa</s> (bond).

children.text: paśūnām asvātantryāt pāśānām ācaitanyāt tadvilakṣaṇasya patyuḥ pañcavidhakṛtyakāritvam tatkārakāṇi svaśaktirūpāṇi māyādīni ca kriyā ca dīkṣādyā tatphalaṃ ca paśūnām anugrahākhyena karmaṇā parakaivalyāsādanam ityādi abhidhāsyamānam ||
children.translated_text: Because the <s>paśu</s>s lack independence and the <s>pāśa</s>s lack consciousness, what is to be taught is the capacity of the <s>pati</s>, who is distinct from them, to perform the fivefold act; also the agents of that act, namely <s>māyā</s> and the others in the form of his own powers; and action such as <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation); and its result, namely the bringing of the <s>paśu</s>s to supreme <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation) through the act called grace.

children.text: tadgarbhīkāreṇedaṃ mūlasūtram ||
children.translated_text: With these included within it, this is the root sūtra.

children.text: anādimalāpeta iti ||
children.translated_text: The phrase is: 'free from beginningless <s>mala</s>.'

children.text: anādiśabdaḥ kriyāviśeṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: The word <s>anādi</s>, 'beginningless,' qualifies the action.

children.text: anādi kṛtvā malāpetaḥ svabhāvanirmalaḥ parameśvaraḥ tathā anādiś cāsau malāpetaś ca tatprasādāt pradhvastasamastamalo muktāṇuvargaḥ kiṃ ca anāder malād apetaḥ svābhāvikamalavidāraṇāt parameśvareṇa prakaṭīkṛtadṛkkriyaḥ kiṃcid avaśeṣitatvād ādimatā adhikāramalena yukto mantramantreśvaramantramaheśvaravarga ity evaṃ samāsatrayakaraṇāt muktāṇubhir vidyeśvarādibhiś ca sahitaḥ patipadārthaḥ atra sūcitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by making three compounds, it is indicated here that the category of <s>pati</s> includes the Supreme Lord, naturally pure and free from <s>mala</s> from beginningless time; likewise the class of liberated <s>aṇu</s>s, beginningless and free from <s>mala</s>, whose entire impurity has been destroyed by his grace; and further the classes of <s>mantra</s>s, <s>mantreśvara</s>s, and <s>mantramaheśvara</s>s, who are removed from beginningless <s>mala</s>, whose cognition and action have been made manifest by the Supreme Lord through the splitting of innate impurity, but who, because something remains, are joined with a beginningful <s>mala</s> of office; that category is thus shown together with liberated <s>aṇu</s>s and with <s>Vidyeśvara</s>s and the rest.

children.text: tasya ca trividhasyāpi sarvajñatā sarvakartṛtvaṃ ca vidyate muktātmanāṃ tu saty api sarvārthadṛkkriyatve pāśajālāpohanasāmarthyam asti na tv apohanakartṛtvam ||
children.translated_text: And omniscience and the power to do all things belong to all three kinds of it; but, for liberated selves, although cognition and action toward all objects are present, there is the capacity for removing the mesh of bonds, not actual agency in removing it.

children.text: yatas te karaṇīyasyābhāvāt na pravartante ataḥ svātmany eva śreyoyogāc chivatvam eteṣāṃ vidyeśvarāṇāṃ śivapadaprāptihetutvāt bhagavatas tu sarvānugrahapravṛttatvāt ||
children.translated_text: For, since they have nothing to do, they do not act. Therefore these have Śiva-hood only because blessedness is joined to their own self; the <s>Vidyeśvara</s>s have it because they are causes of attaining the state of Śiva; but the Blessed One has it because he is engaged in grace toward all.

children.text: tathā ca muktātmanām apravṛttatvāt vidyeśvarāṇāṃ ca parameśvarapāratantryāt svatantraḥ sa bhagavān ||
children.translated_text: Accordingly, because the liberated selves do not act, and because the <s>Vidyeśvara</s>s are dependent on <s>Parameśvara</s>, that Blessed One is independent.

children.text: kiṃ karotīty āha pūrvavyatyāsitasyāṇoḥ ||
children.translated_text: What does he do? He says: 'of the <s>aṇu</s> that has previously been inverted.'

children.text: pāśajālaṃ vyapohatīti aṇor iti vijñānākalapralayākalasakalatvena trirūpasya tathā vijñānākalapralayākalātmanor viparyavasitamaleśvaraśaktyadhikāratadanyathābhāvabhedāt pratyekaṃ dvividhayoḥ sakalasyāpi tribandhanabaddhasya kutaścid upāyāt prakṣīṇakarmatayā kevalakalādiyuktasya ca evaṃ dviprakārasyāsyaiva ca pratyekaṃ videhasadehabhedāt pratibhedaṃ ca malādyadhikāravirahiṇas tadyuktasya cety aṣṭaprakārasya ittham anekabhedabhinnasyātmanaḥ parameśvaraḥ pāśajālaṃ yathāsaṃbhavam apohatīti saṃbandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He removes the mesh of bonds. The word 'of the <s>aṇu</s>' refers to the self as divided in many ways: as threefold, being <s>vijñānākala</s>, <s>pralayākala</s>, and <s>sakala</s>; again, as twofold in each case for the <s>vijñānākala</s> and <s>pralayākala</s> selves, according to the difference between the settled states of <s>mala</s>, the Lord's power, and office, and their being otherwise; also as twofold for the <s>sakala</s>, whether bound by the three bonds or, because karma has been exhausted by some means, furnished only with <s>kalā</s> and the rest; and each of these two is further distinguished as bodiless or embodied, and in each subdivision again as lacking or possessing office connected with <s>mala</s> and the like. Thus, in relation to this self, divided into eight kinds and further many subdivisions, the connection is that <s>Parameśvara</s> removes the mesh of bonds as appropriate.

children.text: yasya ca yathā cāpohati tat sarvaṃ yathāvasaram agre vakṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whose bonds he removes, and in what way, we shall state all of that later, at the proper occasion.

children.text: kīdṛśasyāṇor ity āha pūrvavyatyāsitasyeti pūrvair anādikālīnair malakarmamāyāparameśvaranirodhaśaktyākhyair yathāsaṃbhavaṃ hetutayā sthitair vyatyāsitasya parameśvarād vaisādṛśyaṃ prāpitasya tatpreryasya bandhāntarayoginaś ca ||
children.translated_text: Of what sort is the <s>aṇu</s>? He says, 'previously inverted': it has been made dissimilar to <s>Parameśvara</s> by prior causes, beginningless in time, called <s>mala</s>, karma, <s>māyā</s>, and <s>Parameśvara</s>'s restraining power, which stand as causes as far as possible; it is impelled by him and is connected with further bonds.

children.text: ayam arthaḥ maleneśvaranirodhaśaktyā karmabhiś ca sadbhir aṇor aśivatvaṃ tataś ca bandhāntarayogaḥ tadapohane tu śivatvam ||
children.translated_text: This is the meaning: when <s>mala</s>, the Lord's restraining power, and karmas are present, the <s>aṇu</s> lacks Śiva-hood, and from that follows connection with other bonds; but when they are removed, it has Śiva-hood.

children.text: evaṃ ca śivavaisādṛśye ta evānādayo hetavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus those same beginningless factors are the causes of dissimilarity to Śiva.

children.text: śivas tv apratibaddhaniratiśayasarvārthadṛkkriyāśaktiḥ teṣāṃ yogyatām apekṣya anugrahe pravṛttaḥ pāśavrātam apohati nirasyati ||
children.translated_text: Śiva, however, whose power of cognition and action toward all objects is unobstructed and unsurpassed, undertakes grace in consideration of their fitness and removes, that is, casts away, the multitude of bonds.

children.text: upasargād asyatyūhyor vā vacanam ity apohatipadam ||
children.translated_text: The word <s>apohati</s> is justified by the grammatical statement that, after a prefix, forms from <s>asyati</s> or <s>ūhati</s> may be taught.

children.text: tad evam akhilatantrārthasūcanād etan mūlasūtram ||
children.translated_text: Thus, since it indicates the meaning of all the tantras, this is the root sūtra.

children.text: tathā cehaiva vyākhyānāvasare vakṣyati yatra bīja ivārūḍho mahātantrārthapādapaḥ ābhāti mūlasūtraṃ tad athaśabdādyalaṃkṛtam iti ||
children.translated_text: And accordingly, on this very occasion of explanation, he will say: 'Where the tree of the meaning of the great tantra has grown as from a seed, that root sūtra, adorned with the word <s>atha</s> and the like, shines.'

children.text: Chapter 34

pāśasadbhāve hy ātmanāṃ janmasthitidhvaṃsatirobhāvānugrahakṛt bhagavān bhavatīti patipaśupāśātmavyatiriktaṃ na kiṃcit padārthāntaraṃ prayojanavad eṣv evānyeṣām antarbhāvād iti tripadārthatvam uktam ||
children.translated_text: For when the bonds exist, the Blessed One becomes the agent of the birth, maintenance, destruction, concealment, and grace of the selves. Therefore there is no useful separate category apart from <s>pati</s>, <s>paśu</s>, and <s>pāśa</s>, since other things are included within these. Thus the threefold set of categories has been stated.

children.text: kiṃ ca pāśajālam apohatīty apohatikriyākṣiptāḥ kriyācaryāyogapādāḥ patipaśupāśoktyākṣiptaś ca vidyāpāda iti pādacatuṣṭayopakṣepaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, the sections on <s>Kriyā</s>, <s>Caryā</s>, and <s>Yoga</s> are implied by the action of removing, which is supplied by the statement 'he removes the mesh of bonds'; and the <s>Vidyā</s> section is implied by the statement of <s>pati</s>, <s>paśu</s>, and <s>pāśa</s>. Thus the four sections have been introduced.

children.text: mahātantram iti darśanāntarebhyo 'dhikaphalatvāc chivabhedakatvena paratvād vā mahat tantritatattatprameyatvāc ca tantram ||
children.translated_text: It is called the Great Tantra because its result is superior to those of other systems, or because it is supreme in that it distinguishes Śiva; and it is a tantra because the various objects of knowledge, the principles and the rest, are systematized in it.

children.text: ekenaivāmunā sūtreṇa saṃhṛtya saṃgṛhya punar vistareṇaitad eva prameyaṃ jagatpatiḥ śrīkaṇṭhanāthaḥ prāha ||
children.translated_text: With this one sūtra alone, after condensing and collecting the matter, the Lord of the world, <s>Śrīkaṇṭhanātha</s>, again taught this very object of knowledge in detail.

children.text: mūlasūtrāt sarvakṛt sarvavid iti viśeṣaṇadvayaṃ vyācaṣṭe ||
children.translated_text: From the root sūtra he explains the two qualifiers, 'maker of all' and 'knower of all.'

children.text: Chapter 35

jagato janmavaj jantucakrasya bhogopayogiparikarasahitasya paunaḥpunyena tattadvividhayoniṣu udbhāvanaṃ janma sthitis tadicchāniruddhasya sarvalokasya svagocare niyogaḥ sthāpanaṃ dhvaṃsa ādānaṃ jagadyonāv upasaṃhāraḥ tirobhāvo yathānurūpād bhogād apracyāvaḥ saṃrakṣaṇākhyayāny atroktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As for the birth of the world, "birth" is the repeated bringing forth of the cycle of beings, together with the equipment useful for experience, in each of the various wombs; "persistence" is the assigning or establishing of the whole world, restrained by his will, within its own sphere; "destruction" is taking it back, its withdrawal into the womb of the world; and "concealment," here spoken of under the name "protection," is not being made to fall away from the experience appropriate to each.

children.text: yad āha vārttikakāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the author of the <s>Vārttika</s> says:

children.text: svasaṃskārocitād bhogād apracyāvaḥ śarīriṇām ||
children.translated_text: The non-falling-away of embodied beings from the experience suited to their own <s>saṃskāra</s>s

children.text: proktaṃ saṃrakṣaṇaṃ nāma nyāyena parikalpanam iti ||
children.translated_text: is said to be called protection: an arranging according to proper rule.

children.text: vimuktiśabdenātrānudhyānarūpo 'nugraha ity etat parameśvarasya saṃbandhi pañcavidhaṃ kṛtyaṃ kārakaiḥ śaktyādibhiḥ phalena ca bhuktimuktyātmanā sahitaṃ jñeyam avaboddhavyam ||
children.translated_text: By the word "liberation" here is meant grace in the form of <s>anudhyāna</s> (attentive contemplation). This fivefold activity belonging to <s>Parameśvara</s>, together with the causal factors such as <s>śakti</s> and with its result in the form of enjoyment and liberation, is to be known and understood.

children.text: etac ca na māyādibhiḥ karmabhir vā nirvartayituṃ śakyam ācaitanyāt nāpi puruṣeṇāsya malaniruddhaśaktitvāt ||
children.translated_text: And this cannot be accomplished by entities such as <s>māyā</s> or by karmas, because they are insentient; nor by a <s>puruṣa</s>, because his power is obstructed by <s>mala</s> (impurity).

children.text: na cānīśvaro 'tra kartā yuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nor is it reasonable that a non-lord should be the agent here.

children.text: yaś caitat sṛṣṭyādi kartuṃ śaknoti so 'vaśyaṃ tadviṣayajñaḥ cikīrṣitakāryaviṣayāṇāṃ jñānaviśeṣāṇām aṃśenāpi vaikalye tattatkāryāniṣpatteḥ ||
children.translated_text: And whoever is able to perform this creation and the rest must necessarily know those objects, since if the specific cognitions whose objects are the acts he intends to perform are deficient even in part, the respective acts are not accomplished.

children.text: ataś ca sarvakartrā sarvajñena tena ca svabhāvasiddhena jagataḥ kartrā bhavitavyam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the maker of the world must be that maker of all, omniscient, and established by nature.

children.text: arvāg iti ādimattvena siddhe tasminn abhyupagamyamāne yadi kāraṇāt kutaścit tasyāsāv anugrahas tasyāpi kāraṇaṃ tatkāraṇasyāpi kāraṇāntaraṃ mṛgyam ity anavasthā ||
children.translated_text: If he is accepted as "later," that is, once he has been established as having a beginning, and if this grace of his comes from some cause, then a cause of that too, and another cause of that cause, must be sought; thus there is infinite regress.

children.text: athāsya vinaiva kāraṇaṃ svata eva tathāvidham aiśvaryaṃ tad akasmāj jātaṃ tarhy eṣa nirhetuko mokṣo 'nyān apekṣaṇāt sarvasyaiva syāt tasyāpi vā na syāt ||
children.translated_text: But if, without any cause, such sovereignty belongs to him simply of itself, and has arisen accidentally, then this liberation, being causeless and not dependent on anything else, would belong to everyone, or else it would not belong even to him.

children.text: yad āhuḥ
children.translated_text: As they say:

children.text: nityaṃ sattvam asattvaṃ vā hetor anyān apekṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: A thing would be permanently existent or permanently nonexistent when it does not depend on a cause;

children.text: apekṣāto hi bhāvānāṃ kādācitkatvasaṃbhavaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: for the possibility that things occur only at certain times comes precisely from dependence.

children.text: tasmāt svabhāvasiddhanityaniratiśayanirmalasarvārthadṛkkriyaḥ patipadārthaḥ pūrvam uddiṣṭo 'nena lakṣitaḥ parīkṣyate purastāt ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the category of <s>pati</s> (Lord), whose cognition and action toward all objects are innate, eternal, unsurpassed, and pure, has been indicated earlier, is characterized by this, and will be examined below.

children.text: idānīṃ paśupadārthaṃ lakṣayitum āha ||
children.translated_text: Now, in order to characterize the category of <s>paśu</s> (bound soul), he says:

children.text: Chapter 36
jñānakriyātmakaṃ yac caitanyaṃ tad ātmany asti na tu śarīrasamavetam iti cārvākanirākaraṇe vakṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The consciousness whose nature is knowledge and action exists in the self, not as something inhering in the body; this we shall state in the refutation of the <s>Cārvāka</s>s.

children.text: tac ca sarvadaivāsti na tu muktāv eva ||
children.translated_text: And it exists always, not only in liberation.

children.text: muktau tu saṃvittyabhāvo yathā vaiśeṣikair iṣṭaḥ tathāvidhāyā moharūpāyā mukter nirākariṣyamāṇatvāt ||
children.translated_text: For the kind of liberation that is delusion in form, in which the absence of cognition in liberation is accepted by the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>s, is going to be refuted.

children.text: tac cātmanaś caitanyaṃ jñānakriyātmakaṃ sarvatomukham asti na tu kṣapaṇakānām iva dehapramāṇakatvaniyamād avyāpi paśupadārthaprakaraṇe vyāpakatvasya vakṣyamāṇatvāt ||
children.translated_text: And that consciousness of the self, consisting of knowledge and action, exists as <s>sarvatomukha</s> (facing every direction); it is not non-pervasive, as the <s>Kṣapaṇaka</s>s hold because of a fixed rule that it is the size of the body, since its pervasiveness will be stated in the section on the category of <s>paśu</s>.

children.text: atra hetum āha yato muktau śrūyate sarvatomukhaṃ muktātmanāṃ sarvatomukhasya caitanyasya śravaṇād ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here he gives the reason: "because in liberation it is heard to be facing every direction." The meaning is: because a consciousness facing every direction is heard of in the liberated selves.

children.text: na ca teṣāṃ tadānīm eva tad utpadyate iti vācyaṃ sadutpatteḥ satkāryavādaprakaraṇe 'bhidhāsyamānatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Nor may it be said that it is produced in them only at that time, since the production of an existent thing will be explained in the section on <s>satkāryavāda</s> (the doctrine that the effect preexists).

children.text: atha muktāv eva tathāvidhacaitanyaśruteḥ pūrvaṃ ca tadanupalambhād anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ saṃsārāvasthāyāṃ sarvatomukhatvaṃ caitanyasya kuta ity āśaṅkānirāsāyāha sad apy abhāsamānatvād ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Now, if because such consciousness is taught only in liberation and because it is not apprehended before then, someone doubts, by positive and negative concomitance, "How can consciousness be facing every direction in the state of <s>saṃsāra</s>?", to dispel that suspicion he says, "though existent, because it is not manifest," and so on.

children.text: satyam anupalambhaḥ saṃsārāvasthāyāṃ tathāvidhasya caitanyasya ||
children.translated_text: It is true that in the state of <s>saṃsāra</s> such consciousness is not apprehended.

children.text: sa tv anyathāsiddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But that is accounted for otherwise.

children.text: vyañcakābhāvakṛto hi yo 'nupalambhaḥ sa nābhāvasādhakaḥ api tu asati vyañjake yaś cāyam anupalambhaḥ sa vyañjakābhāvakṛtaḥ ataś ca nāsattvaṃ sādhayati ||
children.translated_text: For a non-apprehension caused by the absence of a manifester does not prove absence. Rather, when the manifester is absent, this non-apprehension is caused by the absence of the manifester; therefore it does not prove non-existence.

children.text: tac ca sarvatomukhatvaṃ sad api yasmān na prathate tataḥ kenāpi pratibaddham ity avasīyate ||
children.translated_text: And since that facing-every-directionness, though existent, does not appear, it is ascertained that it is obstructed by something.

children.text: asmāc ca hetor anāvṛtanijasāmarthyasya mukteḥ purā sa ātmā vaśya iti ||
children.translated_text: And for this reason, before the liberation in which its own capacity is uncovered, that self is subject to control.

children.text: Chapter 37
prāvṛṇoti prakarṣeṇācchādayati ātmanāṃ dṛkkriye iti prāvṛtiḥ svābhāviky aśuddhir mala ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That which covers, that is, powerfully obscures, the seeing and action of selves is <s>prāvṛti</s>; it is natural impurity, meaning <s>mala</s>.

children.text: īṣṭe svātantryeṇetīśaḥ tadīyaṃ balaṃ rodhaśaktir dvitīyaḥ pāśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He rules by his own autonomy, thus he is the <s>īśa</s>; his power, the power of obstruction, is the second <s>pāśa</s> (bond).

children.text: tathā hy agre vakṣyati tāsāṃ māheśvarī śaktiḥ sarvānugrāhikā śivā dharmānuvartanād eva pāśa ity upacaryate iti ||
children.translated_text: For accordingly he will say later: "Their auspicious <s>Māheśvarī Śakti</s>, which bestows grace on all, is spoken of metaphorically as a <s>pāśa</s> only because it follows <s>dharma</s> (the proper order)."

children.text: kriyate tattatphalārthibhir iti karma tasya cānāditvam ādyakoṭer anupalabhyamānatvāt yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: What is performed by those seeking their respective results is <s>karma</s>; and its beginninglessness follows because an initial limit is not apprehended.

children.text: śarīravataḥ karma karaṇaṃ tac ca śarīraṃ karmārabdhaṃ tānyapi śarīrāntareṇa kṛtāni tac ca karmajam iti so 'yaṃ tṛtīyaḥ pāśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For an embodied one, there is the performance of <s>karma</s>; that body is produced by <s>karma</s>; those karmas too were done through another body; and that body was born from <s>karma</s>. Thus this is the third <s>pāśa</s>.

children.text: mātyasyāṃ śaktyātmanā pralaye sarvaṃ jagat sṛṣṭau vyaktiṃ yātīti māyā ||
children.translated_text: Because, at dissolution, the entire world, in the form of power, is contained in this, and at creation comes to manifestation, it is <s>māyā</s>.

children.text: yathoktaṃ śrīmatsaurabheye
children.translated_text: As is said in the revered <s>Saurabheya</s>:

children.text: śaktirūpeṇa kāryāṇi tallīnāni mahākṣaye vikṛtau vyaktim āyānti iti ||
children.translated_text: At the great dissolution the effects, absorbed in that, exist in the form of power; at transformation they come to manifestation.

children.text: svakāryeṇa kalādinā sahiteyam apy anādikālīnā caturthaḥ pāśa iti ||
children.translated_text: This too, together with its own effects such as <s>kalā</s>, is beginningless and is the fourth <s>pāśa</s>.

children.text: etad ātmanāṃ sahajasāmarthyapratibandhakatvāt pāśānāṃ jālam iva jālaṃ samāsataḥ saṃkṣepād uktam ||
children.translated_text: This, because the <s>pāśa</s>s obstruct the innate capacities of the selves, has briefly been called a "mesh," like a net.

children.text: yeṣāṃ ca ye dharmā vyāpārās te nāmnaiva pradarśitāḥ anvarthena svābhidhānena sūcitās tathāpi yathāvasaraṃ vakṣyante ||
children.translated_text: And the particular properties, that is, activities, belonging to each of them have been shown by their very names, indicated by their own meaningful designations. Nevertheless, they will be explained at the proper occasion.

children.text: atha padārthatrayopasaṃhāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now comes the summing up of the three categories.

children.text: Chapter 38
ittham asyaiva padārthatrayasya vidyāpāde sthitasya caryādipādatrayeṇa viniyogo vibhajanam abhidhāsyate vakṣyate ||
children.translated_text: Thus the application, that is, the distribution, of this very triad of categories established in the <s>Vidyā</s> section will be explained by means of the three sections beginning with <s>Caryā</s>.

children.text: evaṃvidhena vidhinā patiḥ pāśopaśamanaṃ kṛtvā paśūnāṃ kaivalyado bhavati ātmanām iti pratipadam eṣām eva praviveko 'bhidhāsyata ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By a procedure of this kind, the <s>pati</s> (Lord), having pacified the <s>pāśa</s>s (bonds), becomes the giver of <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation) to the <s>paśu</s>s, that is, to the selves. The meaning is that the precise discrimination of these very things will be explained step by step.

children.text: tatphalakathanāyāha ||
children.translated_text: To state its result, he says:

children.text: Chapter 39
tasya ca viniyogasya vibhajanasya muktiḥ phalam anuṣaṅgataḥ anuniṣpannatayā muktir api vakṣyamāṇā bhautikadīkṣādibhiḥ samabhilaṣitabhogopabhogāt parataḥ parakaivalyāvirbhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the result of that application, that distribution, is liberation. Liberation too, which is to be described as arising consequentially and being completed afterward, is the manifestation of supreme <s>kaivalya</s> after the enjoyment of the desired pleasures through <s>bhautika-dīkṣā</s> and the like.

children.text: tathā coktaṃ rurusaṃhitāyām ||
children.translated_text: And accordingly it is said in the <s>Rurusaṃhitā</s>:

children.text: dīkṣāpūtā gaṇapatiguror maṇḍale janmavantaḥ siddhā mantrais taruṇadinakṛnmaṇḍalodbhāsidehāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Purified by initiation, born in the circle of the <s>Gaṇapati</s>-guru, perfected by mantras, their bodies shining like the disk of the young sun,

children.text: bhuktvā bhogān suciram amarastrīnikāyair upetāḥ srastotkaṇṭhāḥ śivapadaparaiśvaryabhājo bhavantīti ||
children.translated_text: having enjoyed pleasures for a long time in the company of hosts of heavenly women, with longing fallen away, they become possessors of the supreme sovereignty of the state of <s>Śiva</s>."

children.text: tena bhuktimuktī parāparavibhāgena bahudhā bhidyete ||
children.translated_text: Therefore enjoyment and liberation are divided in many ways according to the distinction between higher and lower.

children.text: tatra parā muktiḥ pātālādikalāntādhvavartivicitraiśvaryasampannatattadbhuvanādhipatyaṃ tattadbhuvanavāsitvamātraṃ cāparā ||
children.translated_text: Among these, higher liberation is lordship over each particular world, endowed with varied powers and situated on the path from <s>Pātāla</s> up to <s>Kalā</s>; lower liberation is merely residence in those respective worlds.

children.text: evaṃ parā muktiḥ parameśvarasāmyam aparā tu mantramantreśvaratvam ||
children.translated_text: In this way, higher liberation is equality with <s>Parameśvara</s>, while lower liberation is the state of being a <s>mantra</s> or a <s>mantreśvara</s>.

children.text: āsāṃ ca yathā bahubhedatvaṃ tathāgre vakṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And we shall explain later how these have many subdivisions.

children.text: athānyebhyo darśanebhyaḥ ko 'sya pārameśvarasya jñānasya viśeṣa iti muniḥ praṣṭum āha ||
children.translated_text: Now, in order to ask what distinction this knowledge belonging to <s>Parameśvara</s> has from other systems, the sage says:

children.text: Chapter 40

vedāntavidāṃ mateṣūpaniṣadādiśāstreṣu ṣaṣṭitantrādiṣu sadasadvādinām arhatāṃ ca mateṣv akalaṅkatritayaprasūtiṣu dravyādipadārthavādikāṇādādiśāstreṣu ādigrahaṇāt saugatādimateṣv api yato muktis tatsādhanāni ca śrūyante tataḥ ko 'sau śivāgame viśeṣaḥ iti viśeṣajijñāsayā tadvyavasitasya muneḥ praśnaḥ na saṃdigdhatvenādāv eva viśeṣasambhāvanāniścayataḥ śrotuṃ pravṛttatvāt nāpi viparyastatvena te vavrire śivajñānam ity abhyarthanāpravṛttatvena darśanāntarānabhiniviṣṭatvapratīteḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since liberation and its means are heard of in the views of the knowers of <s>Vedānta</s>, in scriptures such as the <s>Upaniṣad</s>s, in works such as the <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s>, in the views of the <s>Arhat</s>s who teach being and non-being and arise from the triad of <s>Akalaṅka</s>, in the treatises of <s>Kaṇāda</s> and others that teach categories such as substance, and, by the word "and so on," also in the views of the <s>Saugata</s>s and others, therefore the sage asks, from a desire to know the distinction, "What is that special feature in the <s>Śivāgama</s>?" He is resolved upon that distinction. His question is not due to doubt, because from the very beginning he has set out to hear with certainty that a special feature is possible; nor is it due to misconception, because, from the request "they chose the knowledge of <s>Śiva</s>," it is understood that he is not attached to other systems.

children.text: tattadāgamaśrutā muktis tatsādhanāni ca purastāt teṣu teṣv avasareṣu granthakṛtaivānubhāṣya dūṣayiṣyanta iti nāsmābhiḥ pṛthak prayatnena darśyante ||
children.translated_text: The liberations and the means to them that are heard in each of those scriptures will later, on their respective occasions, be restated and refuted by the author of the treatise himself. Therefore we do not show them separately by our own effort.

children.text: atra siddhāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here is the established conclusion.

children.text: Chapter 41
praṇetāro hiraṇyagarbhādyāḥ kaṇādapatañjalikapilaprabhṛtayaś ca te cāsarvajñāḥ aparatvenābhimatāḥ svaprameyād ūrdhvavartino yuktyāgamopapannasya prameyajātasya tair anavagamāt ||
children.translated_text: The promulgators, such as <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, and those beginning with <s>Kaṇāda</s>, <s>Patañjali</s>, and <s>Kapila</s>, are not omniscient and are regarded as lower, because they do not comprehend the class of knowable objects, established by reasoning and scripture, that lies beyond their own objects of knowledge.

children.text: tad uktaṃ svabhāvapuruṣāvyaktakarmakālātmavādibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: That has been said with reference to those who teach nature, <s>puruṣa</s>, the unmanifest, karma, time, and the self:

children.text: parameśam adṛṣṭvaiva muktir mithyaiva kalpitā iti ||
children.translated_text: "Without having seen <s>Parameśa</s>, liberation is simply falsely imagined."

children.text: tathā sugato yadi sarvaśaḥ kapilo neti kā pramā ||
children.translated_text: Likewise: "If <s>Sugata</s> is omniscient in every respect and <s>Kapila</s> is not, what is the proof?

children.text: athobhāv api sarvajñau mitibhedas tayoḥ katham iti ||
children.translated_text: But if both are omniscient, how can there be a difference between their cognitions?"

children.text: tair yataḥ praṇītāni śāstrāṇi ata evaiteṣu vastusaṃgraho 'py asphuṭaḥ puṃspratibaddhāpavargajñānam aspaṣṭam ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since the treatises were composed by them, for that very reason even the enumeration of reality in them is indistinct; the meaning is that their knowledge of liberation as connected with the individual self is unclear.

children.text: ye cātropāyāḥ puṃsprakṛtivivekajñānabrahmādvaitābhyāsaṣoḍaśapadārthajñānādayaḥ phalāni ca svargāpavargalakṣaṇāni tat sarvaṃ tadvad aspaṣṭam eva tathātathāvakṣyamāṇanirvāhāsahatvāt ||
children.translated_text: And the means taught in these systems, such as knowledge discriminating the self from <s>prakṛti</s>, practice of the non-duality of <s>brahman</s>, and knowledge of the sixteen categories, and also the results characterized as heaven and liberation, are all similarly unclear, because they cannot withstand the explanations that will be given in the respective ways.

children.text: tasmāt tebhyo 'syāyaṃ viśeṣaḥ yad iha sarvaṃ prakṛṣṭaṃ yataḥ paśupāśātītaniratiśayasarvārthajñānakriyātmanā parameśvareṇedam ādiṣṭam iti praṇetṛgataṃ paratvam upāyānām api dīkṣādīnāṃ paridṛṣṭasaṃvāditatvāt paratvam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore this is the special feature of this teaching in comparison with those systems: here everything is excellent, because this was taught by <s>Parameśvara</s>, whose nature is unsurpassed knowledge and action with respect to all things and who transcends <s>paśu</s> and <s>pāśa</s>. Thus there is superiority in the teacher; and the means also, such as <s>dīkṣā</s>, are superior because their effectiveness is directly observed.

children.text: tathāhi saddīkṣādinā brahmahatyādimahāpātakayogino 'py apetapātakatvaṃ dṛṣṭam ity ato viṣasya māraṇātmakaśaktyapaharaṇavat pāśānāṃ bandhakatvavyapagamaḥ siddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For it is seen that even one connected with great sins such as killing a Brahmin becomes free from sin through true <s>dīkṣā</s> and the like. Therefore, just as the death-dealing power of poison is removed, the disappearance of the binding capacity of the <s>pāśa</s>s is established.

children.text: tad śuddhiṃ vrajati uktaṃ
children.translated_text: That reaches purity. It has been said:

children.text: tulāyāṃ dīkṣāto brahmahetyato mukhyāt ||
children.translated_text: "After initiation, from the indication of the balance, even in the principal case of <s>brahmahatyā</s>,

children.text: pratyayato jānīyād bandhanavigamaṃ viṣakṣayavat iti ||
children.translated_text: one should know by direct proof the disappearance of bondage, as with the wasting away of poison."

children.text: phalaṃ cehānyasarvadarśanadṛṣṭād bhogāpavargalakṣaṇāt phalāt prakṛṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: And the result here is superior to the result seen in all other systems, which is characterized as enjoyment and liberation.

children.text: uktaṃ hi śrīmanmataṃgake agnihotrādibhiḥ pūtās tathā cāndrāyaṇādibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For it has been said in the venerable <s>Mataṅga</s>: "Purified by <s>agnihotra</s> and the like, and likewise by <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> observances and the like,

children.text: lokatraye 'pi modante vimānasthā yaśasvinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: famous and seated in aerial palaces, they rejoice throughout the three worlds.

children.text: athāpnuyuḥ padaṃ śākram iṣṭvā kratuśataṃ vidheḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, having performed a hundred sacrifices according to rule, they may attain the station of <s>Śakra</s>.

children.text: yā gatiḥ śivabhaktānāṃ śāṭhyenāpi mahātmanām ||
children.translated_text: But the destiny that belongs to the great-souled devotees of <s>Śiva</s>, even through guile,

children.text: na sā yajñasahasreṇa prāpyate munipuṃgaveti ||
children.translated_text: that is not attained by a thousand sacrifices, O best of sages."

children.text: apavargo 'py asmin darśane sarvāṇy āgamāgocaratvāt paraḥ tattadāgamapraṇetṝṇāṃ sāñjanatvenāsarvajñatvāt tadupadiṣṭāyā mukter muktyābhāsatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Even <s>apavarga</s> (release), in this system, is higher than all [others], because those [other forms of release] are outside the range of authoritative <s>āgama</s>, because the promulgators of those respective <s>āgama</s>s are stained and therefore not omniscient, and because the liberation taught by them is only a semblance of liberation.

children.text: uktaṃ ca śrīmadbhārgavottare
children.translated_text: And it is said in the venerable <s>Bhārgavottara</s>:

children.text: anyatantreṣu ye muktā dharmādharmakṣayān narāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Those men who are liberated in other tantras through the exhaustion of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>,

children.text: te 'tra rudrāṇavaḥ proktā guṇatrayavivarjitāḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: they are taught here as <s>Rudrāṇavas</s>, devoid of the three <s>guṇa</s>s."

children.text: atha kiṃ tadanyadarśanānām asphuṭatvam ity āha ||
children.translated_text: Now, asking what the indistinctness of the other doctrines is, he says:

children.text: Chapter 42
ātmaivedaṃ jagat sarvaṃ neha nānāsti kiṃcana ||
children.translated_text: "This whole world is just the self; there is no multiplicity here at all.

children.text: tathaiko vaśī sarvabhūtāntarātmā ekaṃ viśvaṃ bahudhā yaḥ karoti ||
children.translated_text: Likewise: 'The one ruler, the inner self of all beings, who makes the one universe manifold ...'

children.text: ityādi śrutibhiḥ paramātmaiva sakalacidacidbhāvāvirbhāvatirobhāvaprakṛtisūtaḥ paripūrṇaṣāḍguṇyavaibhavasvatantraḥ eko 'pi san saṃsṛṣṭyarthaṃ tattadvividhamanolakṣaṇopādhibhedena svabhāvāntarānuvidhāyī yathāvad avagato 'bhyudayāya bhavatīti vedāntavidaḥ pratipannāḥ ||
children.translated_text: By śruti-passages such as these, the knowers of Vedānta have accepted that the <s>paramātman</s> alone, the cause of the manifestation and withdrawal of all conscious and unconscious states, independent in the majesty of the six qualities in their fullness, though one, conforms to different natures through the difference of <s>upādhi</s>s (limiting adjuncts) characterized by the various minds of each being, for the sake of worldly manifestation, and, when understood as it really is, becomes conducive to attainment.

children.text: sa eva hi sattvātmani śānta upādhau śānta iva rajobahule tu bhagavān ivājñānātmake ca tamasi mugdha ivāste na tu tato 'nyat pṛthak kiṃcid avatiṣṭhate tasyaiva tathā tathā vaicitryeṇāvasthiteḥ satyatvāt dvaitapratibhāsasya dvicandrādijñānavat bhrāntatvāt ||
children.translated_text: For that very one, in a peaceful <s>upādhi</s> whose nature is <s>sattva</s>, remains as if peaceful; in one abounding in <s>rajas</s>, as if lordly; and in <s>tamas</s> whose nature is ignorance, as if deluded. But nothing other than it exists separately, because it alone is truly established in such and such varied forms, while the appearance of duality is erroneous, like the cognition of two moons and the like.

children.text: tathā cāha tatrabhavān bhartṛhariḥ ||
children.translated_text: And so the venerable <s>Bhartṛhari</s> says in that connection:

children.text: yathā viśuddham ākāśaṃ timiropapluto janaḥ
children.translated_text: "Just as a person afflicted by eye disease

children.text: saṃkīrṇam iva mātrābhiś citrābhir abhimanyate ||
children.translated_text: imagines the pure sky to be as if mixed with various colored forms,

children.text: tathedam amṛtaṃ brahma nirvikāram avidyayā
children.translated_text: so this immortal <s>brahman</s>, changeless,

children.text: kaluṣatvam ivāpannaṃ bhedarūpe pravartate iti ||
children.translated_text: as if made turbid by ignorance, proceeds in the form of difference."

children.text: evaṃ cābhinnam evedaṃ paraṃ brahma paramātmalakṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Thus this supreme <s>brahman</s>, characterized as the <s>paramātman</s>, is simply non-different.

children.text: manasāṃ hi saṃsāradharmaiḥ sukhaduḥkhādibhir yogaḥ paramātmā tu sūrya ivāmbhaḥpratibimbabhedair upādhibhir abhinno 'pi bhinna iva pratibhāti ||
children.translated_text: For minds are connected with the properties of saṃsāra, such as pleasure and pain; but the <s>paramātman</s>, like the sun through differences among its reflections in water, though not divided by <s>upādhi</s>s, appears as if divided.

children.text: tathā ca śrutiḥ
children.translated_text: And so the śruti says:

children.text: yathā hy ayaṃ jyotirātmā vivasvān apo bhinnā bahudhaiko 'nugacchan
children.translated_text: "For just as this luminous self, the sun, though one, follows many different waters,

children.text: upādhinā kriyate bhedarūpo devaḥ kṣetreṣv evam ajñas tathātmeti ||
children.translated_text: and is made by an <s>upādhi</s> to have the form of difference, so is the unborn self, the god, in the fields."

children.text: Chapter 43
om ity upapattyanupapattiparyālocanaparihāreṇa yady etad aṅgīkriyate kāmam avatiṣṭhatāṃ na tu prāmāṇikarītyā ||
children.translated_text: If this is accepted with the words "Om, yes," while dismissing examination of what is tenable and untenable, then let it stand as one wishes; but it does not stand by a method grounded in <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition).

children.text: yasmāt pratijñāmātram evaitat na tv atra hetudṛṣṭāntādisaṃbhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For this is merely an assertion; no reason, example, and the like are possible here.

children.text: tadabhāvān niścayaḥ kiṃnibandhanaḥ kimāśrayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In their absence, what is the basis of certainty, and on what does it rest?

children.text: pramāṇanibandhano hi niścayas tattatprameyavyavasthāpanasamartho bhavati nānyathā ||
children.translated_text: Certainty based on a <s>pramāṇa</s> is capable of establishing the respective object to be known, not otherwise.

children.text: nanv atra pramāṇam āgamas tāvac chrutirūpaḥ pradarśita evety āha ||
children.translated_text: If one says, "But here an <s>āgama</s> as <s>pramāṇa</s>, namely the śruti, has already been shown," he replies:

children.text: Chapter 44
yadi pramāṇam asatyarūpaṃ paramārthataḥ paramātmana eva satyatvāt tathāvidhena pramāṇenaitat pramīyamāṇaṃ manor nimitena pradīpena san tamasāvasthitapadārthapravivecanaprāyam ||
children.translated_text: If the <s>pramāṇa</s> is unreal in nature, since in ultimate reality only the <s>paramātman</s> is real, then this being known by such a <s>pramāṇa</s> is almost like distinguishing objects located in dense darkness by means of a lamp produced by the mind.

children.text: atha satyam eva pramāṇam evaṃ tarhi sa paramātmā prameyatvena sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But if the <s>pramāṇa</s> itself is real, then in that case that <s>paramātman</s> stands as a <s>prameya</s> (object of knowledge).

children.text: pramāṇaṃ hi prameyaṃ paricchindat pramāṇatām āsādayati itarathā pramāṇataivāsya na syāt ||
children.translated_text: For a <s>pramāṇa</s> attains the status of <s>pramāṇa</s> by delimiting a <s>prameya</s>; otherwise it would not itself be a <s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text: kiṃca ataḥ ||
children.translated_text: And what follows from this?

children.text: kim anyad yatraitad dvitayaṃ pramāṇaprameyalakṣaṇaṃ tatra pramātṛpramityātmakam anyad api dvayam anyonyasattvavyapekṣatvāt sthitam eva ||
children.translated_text: What else? Where this pair characterized as <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>prameya</s> exists, there another pair too, consisting of <s>pramātṛ</s> (knower) and <s>pramiti</s> (cognition), is certainly established, because they depend on one another for their existence.

children.text: na hi pramātāraṃ kartāram antareṇa pramāṇaprameyayoḥ kvacit kiṃcitkaratvaṃ karaṇakarmaṇoḥ kriyāsiddhau kartrāśrayatvāt ||
children.translated_text: For without a <s>pramātṛ</s>, the agent, <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>prameya</s> cannot accomplish anything anywhere, since instrument and object depend on an agent for the accomplishment of an action.

children.text: pramitir api kriyārūpo vyāpāras tebhyaḥ pṛthag evānvayavyatirekābhyām upalabhyata iti catuṣṭayam avaśyaṃbhāvi ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pramiti</s> too is an operation in the form of an action, and it is perceived as distinct from those by agreement and difference; therefore a fourfold set necessarily follows.

children.text: yad āha ākṣapādaḥ
children.translated_text: As <s>Ākṣapāda</s> says:

children.text: catasṛṣu caivaṃvidhāsu sarvo 'pi vyavahāraḥ parisamāpyata iti ||
children.translated_text: "All practical activity is completed within just these four such members."

children.text: kiṃ cāta ity ata āha ||
children.translated_text: What follows from this? He replies:

children.text: Chapter 46
pramāṇaprameyavyavahārāṅgīkaraṇe sati advaitahānir ataḥ svābhyupagamavirodhaḥ tadapahnave tu niṣpramāṇakatvam kiṃca bhogasāmyam avimokṣaś cātmavādibhir anabhyupagatau doṣau prasajyete ||
children.translated_text: If the transaction involving <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>prameya</s> is accepted, non-dualism is lost; therefore there is contradiction of one's own accepted position. But if that transaction is denied, the doctrine lacks any <s>pramāṇa</s>. Moreover, for those who teach the self, two faults that they do not accept would follow: sameness of experience and non-liberation.

children.text: sarvair evātmavādibhiḥ pratyakṣavirodhabhīrubhir dṛśyamānaṃ bhogavaicitryam avaśyābhyupeyam ātmanāṃ ca muktir eṣṭavyā niḥśreyasahetutayaiva śāstrāṇāṃ pravṛtteḥ ||
children.translated_text: All teachers of the self, fearing contradiction of direct perception, must accept the visible variety of experience; and liberation of selves must be desired, since the scriptures operate precisely as the cause of the highest good.

children.text: tad iha
children.translated_text: Here [the opponent cites]:

children.text: nādatte kasyacit pāpaṃ na caiva sukṛtaṃ vibhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: "The all-pervading one takes on neither anyone's sin nor merit."

children.text: tathā na kartṛtvaṃ na karmāṇīty abhyupagamāt vicitraphaladāyināṃ pratiniyatajantukṛtatvena bhogapratiniyamakāriṇāṃ karmaṇām evābhāvād bhogasāmyaprasaṅgo durnivāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, because they accept "not agency, nor actions," since there would be no <s>karma</s>s that give varied results and regulate experience by being performed by specifically determined beings, the consequence of sameness of experience is hard to avoid.

children.text: ātmanānātve hi kaścit duḥkhitaḥ kaścit sukhita iti bhogavaicitryam upapannaṃ nānyathā ||
children.translated_text: For only if selves are many is variety of experience, such as "one is suffering, another is happy," intelligible; not otherwise.

children.text: yata eva saṃsāritāyāḥ prabhavas tatraiva niraṃśe paramātmani yadi layo mokṣas tat punar api tata eva prādurbhāvaḥ punaś ca mokṣa iti seyaṃ gatānugatikā na tu mokṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If liberation is dissolution in that very partless <s>Paramātman</s> from which transmigratory existence arises, then from that very source there would again be manifestation, and again liberation. Thus this would be a following of the same coming and going, not liberation.

children.text: tathāha tatrabhavān avadhūtācāryaḥ
children.translated_text: Accordingly the venerable <s>Avadhūtācārya</s> says:

children.text: tvanmateśvaravijñānaniṣpannā api muktayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even the liberations that, in your view, are accomplished through knowledge of <s>Īśvara</s>

children.text: bhajante nāvisaṃvādam āmbhasā iva kṛṣṭayaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: do not attain freedom from contradiction, like cultivated fields with water.

children.text: tataś ca mokṣābhāvāt tadupāyānām ātmā vā are jñātavyaḥ śrotavyo mantavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And therefore, because there is no liberation, the means to it, such as 'The self, dear one, is to be known, to be heard, and to be reflected upon,'

children.text: ityādīnām ānarthakyam ||
children.translated_text: and the like, are purposeless.

children.text: api cāsya paramātmanaś cetanācetanaviśvotpattihetutve cetanācetanatvaṃ prāptaṃ kāryāṇāṃ kāraṇasvabhāvānvayāt ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, if this <s>Paramātman</s> is the cause of the production of the conscious and unconscious universe, then it follows that it is both conscious and unconscious, since effects inherit the nature of their cause.

children.text: yad āhuḥ
children.translated_text: As they say:

children.text: tadatadrūpiṇo bhāvās tadatadrūpahetujāḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: Entities having such and contrary forms are born from causes having such and contrary forms.

children.text: tataś ca viruddhayor anyonyābhibhavenaivātmalābhād bhāvābhāvayor ivaikasmin kāle cetanācetanasvabhāvayoḥ paramātmani avasthānaṃ nopapadyate ||
children.translated_text: And since two opposed things come to have their own being only through overcoming each other, like being and non-being, the simultaneous presence in the <s>Paramātman</s> of conscious and unconscious natures is not possible.

children.text: yathāha tatrabhavān kheṭakanandanaḥ
children.translated_text: As the venerable <s>Kheṭakanandana</s> says:

children.text: viruddhāv ekakālasthau dharmāv ekāśrayaṃ gatau ||
children.translated_text: When two opposed properties, existing at one time, have come to a single substrate,

children.text: itaretaranāśāt tau kuruto lopam ātmanaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: they bring about the loss of their own being through mutual destruction.

children.text: na cāsyānaṅgatvāt kenacid aṅgena cetanatvaṃ kenacic cācetanatvaṃ yuktaṃ sāṅgatvābhyupagame tu kusūlādivat kāryatvāt paramakāraṇatāhāniḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nor, since it has no parts, is it proper that by one part it should be conscious and by another part unconscious. But if possession of parts is admitted, then, like a granary and the like, because it is an effect, its status as supreme cause is lost.

children.text: yathā kiṃca yad yad upādānakāraṇaṃ tat tad acetanaṃ yathā mṛdādi acetanaś cāyaṃ tattad acetanaṃ paramātmopādānakāraṇatvāt cetanatve nāsyopādānakāraṇatvam ||
children.translated_text: Furthermore, whatever is a material cause is unconscious, as clay and the like are. This too would be unconscious, because the <s>Paramātman</s> is the material cause of those things; if it were conscious, it would not be their material cause.

children.text: astv acetanaḥ ko doṣa iti cet cetanānāṃ kāraṇaṃ svayam acetana iti vicitreyam uktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: If one says, 'Let it be unconscious; what fault is there?' this is a strange statement: that the cause of conscious beings is itself unconscious.

children.text: ācaitanyābhyupagame cāsya buddhimatkartranadhiṣṭhitasya mṛtpiṇḍāder iva na svakāryajanane sāmarthyam ||
children.translated_text: And if unconsciousness is admitted for it, then, being ungoverned by an intelligent agent, it has no capacity to produce its own effect, like a lump of clay and the like.

children.text: ye 'pi ca grāhakatvena svasaṃvedanasiddhā ātmāno bhoktāras tata utpannā ity ucyante te 'py utpādyatvāt ghaṭādivad acetanāḥ prasajyanta ity anekadoṣāśrayasya paramātmādvaitasyānupapattiḥ ||
children.translated_text: And as for the selves, the experiencers, established by self-awareness as apprehenders, who are said to be produced from it, they too, because they are produced, would absurdly be unconscious like pots and the like. Thus the non-dualism of <s>Paramātman</s>, which is the locus of many faults, is untenable.

children.text: athaivaṃ vedāntavādināṃ mate nirākṛte kāpiloktāt prakṛtipuruṣavivekajñānān niḥśreyasāvāptir bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Now, when the view of the <s>Vedāntavādin</s>s has been refuted in this way, one might think that the highest good will be attained through the knowledge of the distinction between <s>prakṛti</s> and <s>puruṣa</s> taught by the <s>Kāpila</s>s.

children.text: yathā cāhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: As they also say:

children.text: evaṃ tattvābhyāsān nāsmi na me nāham ity apariśeṣāt ||
children.translated_text: Thus, through repeated practice of the principles, there arises without remainder: 'I am not; nothing is mine; I am not this.'

children.text: ekāntikam ātyantikam ubhayaṃ kaivalyam āpnotīti ||
children.translated_text: One obtains <s>kaivalya</s>, both certain and absolute.

children.text: śrutir apy āha ajām ekāṃ lohitaśuklakṛṣṇāṃ bahvīḥ prajā janayantīṃ sarūpāḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>śruti</s> too says: 'One unborn female, red, white, and black, giving birth to many offspring like herself;

children.text: ajo hy eko juṣamāṇo 'nuśete jahāty enāṃ bhuktabhogām ajo 'nya iti ||
children.translated_text: for one unborn male lies beside her, enjoying her, while another unborn one abandons her after her pleasures have been enjoyed.'

children.text: etad api nirākartum āha ||
children.translated_text: To refute this as well, he says:

children.text: Chapter 47

sāṃkhyajñāne 'py etad asamyaktvaṃ yat kārye māyodbhūtakalājanite pradhāne kāraṇabuddhiḥ paramakāraṇatābhramaḥ mūlaprakṛtir avikṛtir iti hi teṣām abhyupagamaḥ kalādīnāṃ tattvānāṃ pṛthakpṛthagupalabhyamānaprayojanānāṃ kāraṇabhūtasya jagannidhibhūtasya māyātmano 'navagamāt ||
children.translated_text: Even in <s>Sāṃkhya</s> knowledge there is this incorrectness: with regard to <s>pradhāna</s>, which is an effect produced by <s>kalā</s> arisen from <s>māyā</s>, there is the notion of a cause, the delusion that it is the supreme cause. For their accepted doctrine is that root-<s>prakṛti</s> is unevolved, because they do not understand the reality of <s>māyā</s>, which is the cause of the principles such as <s>kalā</s>, whose distinct purposes are observed separately, and which is the repository of the world.

children.text: uktaṃ ca kvacid guṇatattvordhvabhogyasya karmaṇo 'nupalabdhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And it is said somewhere: 'Because no karma is observed whose experience lies above the <s>guṇa</s>-principle,

children.text: kaivalyam api sāṃkhyānāṃ naiva yuktam asaṃkṣayād iti ||
children.translated_text: even the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>s' <s>kaivalya</s> is certainly not possible, because there is no complete exhaustion.'

children.text: tad ayam arthaḥ yeyaṃ kāpilaiḥ paramakāraṇatayā parikalpitā sattvarajastamolakṣaṇaguṇatrayasāmyātmikā prakṛtiḥ tasyās tāvan na guṇebhyo 'nyatvam ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is this: this <s>prakṛti</s>, imagined by the <s>Kāpila</s>s as the supreme cause, whose nature is the equilibrium of the three <s>guṇa</s>s characterized as <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>, is first of all not different from the <s>guṇa</s>s.

children.text: guṇā eva prakṛtir iti hi te pratijānate guṇebhyo 'nanyatve cāvaśyam anekatvam asyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For they assert that the <s>guṇa</s>s themselves are <s>prakṛti</s>; and if it is not different from the <s>guṇa</s>s, it must necessarily be multiple.

children.text: yac cācaitanye saty anekaṃ tatkāraṇāntarapūrvakaṃ yathā tantavo mṛtpiṇḍā vā sati ca kāraṇāntarapūrvakatve na paramakāraṇatā ||
children.translated_text: And whatever, while unconscious, is multiple is preceded by another cause, like threads or lumps of clay. And if it is preceded by another cause, it is not the supreme cause.

children.text: idaṃ ca te praṣṭavyāḥ draṣṭṛdṛśyayoḥ saṃyogaḥ saṃsārahetus tatpūrvakaś ca viyogo 'pavargakāraṇam iti yad ucyate tatra saṃyogas tāvat puṃspradhānayor draṣṭṛdṛśyalakṣaṇa eva na parasparāśleṣarūpaḥ ubhayor apy amūrtatvena tādṛśasyānupapatteḥ ||
children.translated_text: And they should be asked this: when it is said that the conjunction of seer and seen is the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and that a disjunction preceded by that is the cause of liberation, then the conjunction of <s>puruṣa</s> and <s>pradhāna</s> is only one characterized as seer and seen, not one in the form of mutual contact, since both are formless and such contact is impossible.

children.text: pradhānaṃ ca na svato dṛśyam apratyakṣatvena tasyeṣṭatvāt ||
children.translated_text: And <s>pradhāna</s> is not visible in itself, since they accept it as imperceptible.

children.text: na ca mahadahaṃkārādirūpeṇa pariṇateḥ draṣṭā tad draṣṭuṃ śaknoti ||
children.translated_text: Nor can the seer see it through its transformation into the form of <s>mahat</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, and so on.

children.text: tataś ca katham anayor ādyaḥ saṃyogaḥ tadabhāvāc ca kathaṃ tatpūrvako viyogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore how can there be an initial conjunction of the two? And in the absence of that, how can there be a disjunction preceded by it?

children.text: evaṃ ca saṃyogaviyogānupapatter akāraṇatvam eva puruṣārthaṃ prati pradhānasya ||
children.translated_text: Thus, since conjunction and disjunction are not possible, <s>pradhāna</s> is simply not a cause with respect to the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s>.

children.text: itaś ca mithyātvam etadīyasya jñānasya ||
children.translated_text: For this reason too, the falsity of their knowledge is shown.

children.text: kuta ity āha ||
children.translated_text: Why? He says:

children.text: Chapter 48
abhoktuḥ puruṣasya bhogāyatanena dehena bhogasādhanair indriyair bhoktavyair indriyārthair bhogena ca sukhaduḥkhavedanātmanā phalena kiṃ prayojanam ||
children.translated_text: What use does a non-experiencing <s>puruṣa</s> have for a body, the abode of experience; for the senses, the instruments of experience; for sense objects to be experienced; and for the result, experience itself, whose nature is the feeling of pleasure and pain?

children.text: yataś cāsya bhogas tadadhikaraṇatatsādhanasahito 'sti ato bhoktṛtvam apahnotum aśakyam ||
children.translated_text: And since this <s>puruṣa</s> has experience together with its locus and its instruments, its being an experiencer cannot be denied.

children.text: yaś ca bhoktā sa katham akartā akartari kāraṇādisambandhasya nirarthakatvāt ||
children.translated_text: And how can the one who is an enjoyer be a non-agent? For, when there is no agent, connection with instruments and the like is purposeless.

children.text: dṛkkriyātmakatvam eva svarūpaṃ caitanyasya tataś ca kartṛtvanirāsāt jñatvam api nirastaṃ saṃvedanasyāpi kriyātmanaḥ kartṛtvānapagamāt ||
children.translated_text: The very nature of consciousness is being an activity of seeing; therefore, if agency is denied, knowing too is denied, since agency cannot be removed even from awareness, which is itself an activity.

children.text: na hi akartuḥ saṃvedanaṃ cāpy upapannam ||
children.translated_text: For awareness is not possible for a non-agent either.

children.text: itaś ca sāṃkhyajñānasya mithyātvam āha ||
children.translated_text: For the following reason too he states that <s>Sāṃkhya</s> knowledge is false.

children.text: Chapter 49
acetanam api pradhānaṃ buddhimat kartṛpreraṇaṃ vinā svātantryeṇa kathaṃ kāryakaraṇe pravartate ||
children.translated_text: How can the unconscious <s>pradhāna</s>, without the prompting of an intelligent agent, independently set itself to producing an effect?

children.text: na hy anusaṃdhānaśūnyasya buddhimato 'pi ghuṇakīṭasyevākṣaralekhane pravṛttir yuktā kiṃ punaḥ pariṇāmino jaḍasya ||
children.translated_text: For even an intelligent being who lacks purposive reflection cannot reasonably be engaged in writing letters, like a wood-boring insect; how much less can something inert and subject to transformation be so engaged?

children.text: yaś cātra cetanaḥ puruṣaḥ sa tadadhīno na karteti prakṛtisthānāṃ neyam uktir ucitā ||
children.translated_text: And the claim of those who stand by <s>prakṛti</s>, that the conscious <s>puruṣa</s> here is dependent on it and is not an agent, is not appropriate.

children.text: idānīm anekāntavādinirākaraṇāya saṃkhyātas tanmataṃ pūrvapakṣayitum ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Now, in order to refute the proponents of <s>anekāntavāda</s>, their view is stated in summary as the prima facie position.

children.text: Chapter 50
tatra tāvat jīvapadārthas tattantrarītyā jīvāstikāyasaṃjñayā paribhāṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, first, the category of <s>jīva</s>, according to the method of that system, is defined by the designation <s>jīvāstikāya</s>.

children.text: trividhaś cāsau anādisiddhamuktabaddhabhedāt ||
children.translated_text: And it is threefold, through the distinction between what is beginninglessly perfected, liberated, and bound.

children.text: atrānādisiddho 'rhan jīvāstikāyākhyaḥ vyapetamohādibandho muktaḥ tadāvṛtas tu baddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here the beginninglessly perfected one is the <s>Arhat</s>, called <s>jīvāstikāya</s>; the liberated one is free from bonds such as delusion, while the bound one is covered by them.

children.text: ajīvapadārtho 'pi pudgalākāśadharmādharmāstikāyaiś caturbhedair bhinnaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The category of <s>ajīva</s> too is divided into four divisions: <s>pudgalāstikāya</s>, <s>ākāśāstikāya</s>, <s>dharmāstikāya</s>, and <s>adharmāstikāya</s>.

children.text: atrāpi pṛthivyādimahābhūtāni catvāri tṛṇagulmādilatādirūpaṃ sthāvaraṃ jarāyujāṇḍajasvedajodbhijjabhedabhinnaṃ jaṅgamaṃ ceti ṣaṭprakāro 'yaṃ pudgalāstikāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here too this <s>pudgalāstikāya</s> is sixfold: the four great elements beginning with earth, the stationary realm in the form of grasses, shrubs, creepers, and the like, and the moving realm divided into womb-born, egg-born, sweat-born, and earth-born beings.

children.text: ākāśāstikāyo dvirūpaḥ lokākāśāstikāyo 'lokākāśāstikāyaś ceti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>ākāśāstikāya</s> is twofold: <s>lokākāśāstikāya</s> and <s>alokākāśāstikāya</s>.

children.text: lokānām antarākāśaṃ lokākāśam iti smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: The space within the worlds is remembered as <s>lokākāśa</s>.

children.text: alokākāśāstikāyo bahis teṣāṃ sa kīrtitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>alokākāśāstikāya</s> is said to be outside them.

children.text: dharmāstikāyaḥ pudgalāstikāyād anyo 'bhyudayahetuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>dharmāstikāya</s>, distinct from the <s>pudgalāstikāya</s>, is the cause of movement or ascent.

children.text: adharmāstikāyo 'pi tatpratibandhakṛd ity ayam asāv ajīvapadārthaś catuṣprakāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>adharmāstikāya</s>, by contrast, produces obstruction to that. Thus this category of <s>ajīva</s> is fourfold.

children.text: āsravaś cakṣurādīndriyapañcakasya yathāsvaṃ pravṛttiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Āsrava</s> is the respective activity of the five senses beginning with the eye.

children.text: tathā cāhuḥ vṛttiḥ pañcavikalpā dhruvādhruvā cakṣurādivargasya ||
children.translated_text: And accordingly they say: the activity of the group beginning with the eye is fivefold, permanent and impermanent;

children.text: yaiṣā sravaty ajasraṃ yatas tato 'sāv ihāsravaḥ proktaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: because this flows continually from whatever source, it is here called <s>āsrava</s>.

children.text: indriyasaṃyamalabdhapratiṣṭhaṃ dhyānam āsravanirodhātmakatvāt saṃvṛṇoty āsravam iti saṃvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Meditation, made firm by restraint of the senses, since it consists in stopping <s>āsrava</s>, blocks the influx; hence it is <s>saṃvara</s>.

children.text: taptaśilāśayanakeśolluñcanāditapaḥsaṃcayanirjīrṇavīryaṃ karma nirjaraśabdenocyate ||
children.translated_text: Karma whose force has been worn away by the accumulation of austerities such as lying on heated stones and pulling out the hair is called by the word <s>nirjarā</s>.

children.text: nānānirayasaṃsaraṇakāraṇaṃ mohādir aṣṭavidho gaṇaḥ svātantryavighātahetutvāt bandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The eightfold group beginning with delusion, the cause of wandering through many hells, is bondage, because it causes the obstruction of independence.

children.text: uktaṃ ca mohādiko gaṇaś caiṣa bandho jīvasya kalpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And it has been said: this group beginning with delusion is conceived as the bondage of the <s>jīva</s>.

children.text: lohapañjarasambaddhaṃ yathā kṣiptaṃ jalāśaye ||
