children.translated_text: Just as a bottle-gourd, fastened in an iron cage and thrown into a reservoir,

children.text: alābukam adho yāti tadvaj jīvaḥ sabandhana iti ||
children.translated_text: goes downward, so too the <s>jīva</s> goes downward when it is bound.

children.text: prakṣīṇasarvāvaraṇatvāt svātantryasamprāptau ūrdhvapadāsādanaṃ mokṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When independence is attained because all coverings have been exhausted, the attainment of the upper state is <s>mokṣa</s>.

children.text: yad āhuḥ lohapañjaravicchedāt plavate 'lābukaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: As they say: just as a bottle-gourd floats upward when the iron cage is cut away,

children.text: ārohati tathā mokṣaṃ jīvo mohādisaṃkṣayāt ||
children.translated_text: so the <s>jīva</s> ascends to liberation through the destruction of delusion and the rest,

children.text: nityabodhasukhādyaiś ca dharmair yuktaḥ sa tiṣṭhati iti ||
children.translated_text: and it remains endowed with qualities such as eternal knowledge and bliss.

children.text: ete ca sapta padārthāḥ syādvādānugatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And these seven categories follow <s>syādvāda</s>.

children.text: tathā hi dehagrahaṇāt pūrvaṃ jīvaḥ kim asti uta neti yaḥ paryanuyuṅkte taṃ pratyanekāntavādo 'bhyupagantavyam ||
children.translated_text: For example, when someone asks whether the <s>jīva</s> exists before the assumption of a body or not, <s>anekāntavāda</s> must be accepted in reply to him.

children.text: syād asti syān nāsti syād asti ca nāsti ca syād avaktavyaṃ syād asti cāvaktavyaṃ syān nāsti cāvaktavyaṃ ca syād asti ca nāsti cāvaktavyaṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: In some respect it exists; in some respect it does not exist; in some respect it both exists and does not exist; in some respect it is inexpressible; in some respect it exists and is inexpressible; in some respect it does not exist and is inexpressible; and in some respect it exists, does not exist, and is inexpressible.

children.text: atra hi yadyat paryanuyojyaṃ tattat sadasat tathā samādheyam ||
children.translated_text: For here, whatever is to be questioned about must be answered in that way, as existent and non-existent.

children.text: tatra vācyatayāvācyatayāpi ca virodhahānis tu ghaṭanīyeti ||
children.translated_text: And there the removal of contradiction must also be arranged through its being expressible and also inexpressible.

children.text: saptabhaṅgyamoghabrahmāstravatām ajeyam iha kiṃ tat ||
children.translated_text: What is there, in this world, that is unconquerable for those who possess the unfailing Brahmā-weapon of the sevenfold predication?

children.text: yat syād asti syān nāsti syād iti pudgalibhir bhrāmyate jagat sarvam iti ||
children.translated_text: For the whole world is made to reel by the <s>pudgalin</s>s with their formula, 'in some respect it exists, in some respect it does not exist, in some respect ...'.

children.text: nanu cānekāntavādinā tāvad ekāntānabhyupagamān niyamenānekāntavādo 'bhyupagantavyaḥ tathā ca svasiddhānta evaikānta iti kutaḥ sarvatra saptabhaṅgī naiṣa doṣaḥ anekāntavāde 'py ekāntānabhyupagamāt yataḥ syād anekāntaḥ syād ekāntaḥ syād anekāntaś caikāntaś ca syād avaktavyaḥ syād anekāntaś cāvaktavyaś ca syād ekāntaś cāvaktavyaś ca syād ekāntaś cānekāntaś cāvaktavyaś ceti ||
children.translated_text: Objection: Surely, since the proponent of <s>anekāntavāda</s> does not accept one-sidedness, he must necessarily accept <s>anekāntavāda</s>; and thus his own doctrine itself is one-sided. How, then, can the sevenfold predication apply everywhere? Reply: This is no fault, because one-sidedness is not accepted even with regard to <s>anekāntavāda</s>. For in some respect it is non-one-sided; in some respect it is one-sided; in some respect it is both non-one-sided and one-sided; in some respect it is inexpressible; in some respect it is non-one-sided and inexpressible; in some respect it is one-sided and inexpressible; and in some respect it is one-sided, non-one-sided, and inexpressible.

children.text: tad etal leśato dūṣayitum āha ||
children.translated_text: To criticize this briefly, he says:

children.text: Chapter 51
syād asti syān nāsti ceti yad uktaṃ tad asaṃgatam ||
children.translated_text: The statement, 'in some respect it exists and in some respect it does not exist,' is incoherent.

children.text: na hi yadyad eva vastu arthakriyākāritayā sattvenāvagamyate tat tadānīm evāsattvenaikāntataḥ kaścid apy avaiti ||
children.translated_text: For no one at all understands the very same entity, which is apprehended as existent because it is capable of causal efficacy, to be absolutely non-existent at that very moment.

children.text: kaḥ kilānudbhrāntamatiḥ puraḥprasphuradrūpe sad iti pratyayakāriṇi ghaṭādau nāyam astīti buddhiṃ kuryād asati ca tasmin prakhyopākhyāvirahiṇi sattāṃ niścinuyāt vidhiniṣedharūpayor bhāvābhāvayoḥ parasparaparihāreṇaivātmalābhāt ||
children.translated_text: For what person of unconfused mind would, with regard to a pot and the like whose form shines before him and which produces the cognition 'it exists,' form the idea 'this does not exist'; and, when that thing is absent, bereft of appearance and designation, determine that it has existence? For positive being and non-being, in the forms of affirmation and negation, obtain their own nature only by excluding one another.

children.text: abhāvo hi tadasaṃbhavalabdhajanmāpi yadi tenaiva bhāvena sahitaḥ syāt tadānīm abhāva eva na syāt tadupamardanenaiva tasya svarūpasiddheḥ ||
children.translated_text: For non-being, even though it comes into existence from the impossibility of that thing, if it were accompanied by that very being, would then not be non-being at all, since its own nature is established only by suppressing that.

children.text: evaṃ bhāvo 'pi yadi svapratipakṣeṇābhāvenāvyatirikto bhavet tarhi bhāva eva na bhavet ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, if being too were not distinct from its opposite, non-being, then it would not be being at all.

children.text: nanu ghaṭarūpeṇa svātmanāsti ghaṭaḥ parātmanā paṭarūpeṇa nāstīti sadasattvam uktam ||
children.translated_text: Objection: The pot exists by its own nature, in the form of a pot, and it does not exist by another's nature, in the form of a cloth; thus both existence and nonexistence have been stated.

children.text: na tu tad yuktam ||
children.translated_text: But that is not appropriate.

children.text: kiṃ kilaitāvatā pratipāditaṃ syāt ghaṭaḥ paṭātmanā na bhavati ghaṭe vā paṭo nāsti ||
children.translated_text: What indeed would be established by so much: that the pot does not become the nature of a cloth, or that cloth is not present in the pot?

children.text: tad etad abhimatam evātadātmakatvena tatrāvidyamānatvāt ||
children.translated_text: But this is precisely what is accepted, because, being not of that nature, it is absent there.

children.text: paṭād bhidyamāno 'yaṃ ghaṭo 'nya eveti siddhaṃ sādhyate ||
children.translated_text: What is already established is being proved: this pot, being different from cloth, is simply other.

children.text: tad āha ||
children.translated_text: He states this.

children.text: Chapter 52

nanu svātmanā yathā ghaṭaḥ svasāmarthyakriyāṃ karoti evaṃ paṭātmanāpi tatkāryaṃ kuryāt na ca karoty ataḥ paṭātmanā nāsti yadi svātmanāpi parātmavan na syāt tadā svakāryam api na kuryāt tasmād asti ca nāsti cety uktam ||
children.translated_text: Objection: just as a pot, by its own nature, performs the action belonging to its own capacity, so too, by the nature of cloth, it should perform that effect; but it does not perform it, and therefore it does not exist as cloth. If, by its own nature too, it did not exist, just as it does not exist by another's nature, then it would not perform even its own effect. Therefore it has been said that it both exists and does not exist.

children.text: tathaitad ghaṭatvam aghaṭatvaṃ ca parasparam abhinnam ||
children.translated_text: So too, this potness and non-potness would be mutually non-different.

children.text: bhede hi tadbuddhyabhidhānānuvṛttir na syāt ghaṭaś cāghaṭaś ceti sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ ca na bhavet ||
children.translated_text: For if there were difference, the continued occurrence of the corresponding cognition and designation would not occur, nor would there be co-reference in saying 'it is a pot and a non-pot.'

children.text: asti caitat tasmād ubhayātmako 'sau krameṇa tacchabdābhidheyatām udvahan syāt ghaṭaś cāghaṭaś cety avirodhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And this does occur. Therefore that object, possessing both natures and bearing, in sequence, denotability by those words, may be both pot and non-pot; there is no contradiction.

children.text: etad apy ayuktaṃ yato nāsti kaścid abhedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This too is unreasonable, because there is no such non-difference.

children.text: tathā hi aghaṭaśabde ghaṭo na bhavatīti prasajyapratiṣedho vā syāt ghaṭād anyaḥ paṭādir iti vā paryudāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For in the word 'non-pot,' either there is <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s> (direct negation), meaning 'it is not a pot,' or there is <s>paryudāsa</s> (exclusion), meaning 'something other than a pot, such as cloth and the like.'

children.text: ādye pakṣe ghaṭaś cāghaṭaś ca syād ity ukte ghaṭāghaṭayor avyatirekād ghaṭasyābhāva eva ghaṭa ity abhipretam ||
children.translated_text: On the first alternative, when it is said 'it would be both pot and non-pot,' since pot and non-pot are not distinct, what is intended is that the very absence of the pot is the pot.

children.text: evaṃ ceṣyamāṇe sarpābhāve 'pi sarpa eva syāt ||
children.translated_text: And if this is accepted, then even where there is an absence of a snake there would be a snake itself.

children.text: tathā ca sati sarpādivat tadabhāvād api bhayaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: And if that were so, there would be fear even from the absence of it, just as from snakes and the like.

children.text: sasarpaniḥsarpadeśayoḥ sama evopalambho bhavet ||
children.translated_text: There would be exactly the same perception of places with snakes and places without snakes.

children.text: paryudāsapakṣe 'pi ghaṭatvād anyad aghaṭatvaṃ bhinnam eva paṭatvādikaṃ kathyate ||
children.translated_text: On the exclusionary alternative too, non-potness, as something other than potness, is said to be quite different, namely clothness and the like.

children.text: tac ca ghaṭatvād bhinnam ||
children.translated_text: And that is distinct from potness.

children.text: abhede hi ghaṭādiṣv api paṭabuddhyabhidhānānuvṛttir na syāt ||
children.translated_text: For if there were non-difference, one could not avoid the recurrence, even in pots and the like, of the cognition and designation 'cloth.'

children.text: ghaṭādāv api spaṣṭe ghaṭapratyayaś ca na syāt ||
children.translated_text: And even with regard to a clearly present pot and the like, the cognition 'pot' would not occur.

children.text: tasmān na ghaṭāghaṭayor abheda iti na sadasator ekāśrayatvam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore there is no non-difference between pot and non-pot, and so there is no single locus for existent and nonexistent.

children.text: kiṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: Chapter 53
yad api sadasacchabdābhidheyaṃ śreṣṭhāśreṣṭharūpaṃ vastu tad api tadvido naikatrābhidadhati tasyāpi bhinnaviṣayatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Furthermore, that thing which is denoted by the words existent and nonexistent in the sense of superior and inferior is not described by those who know it as occurring in one and the same locus, because it too has distinct objects.

children.text: na hi yad evāśreṣṭhaṃ tad eva śreṣṭham iti vaktuṃ śakyam ||
children.translated_text: For it is not possible to say that the very same thing which is inferior is superior.

children.text: ayam eva hi bhāvānāṃ bhedaḥ yad viruddhadharmādhyāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For precisely this is the difference among entities: the attribution of contradictory properties.

children.text: atha mataṃ yat tac chreṣṭhāśreṣṭhatvaṃ tad ekatra sambhavaty eva apekṣāvaśāt ||
children.translated_text: Now if it is thought that that superiority and inferiority can indeed occur in one thing because of dependence on a comparison,

children.text: yathāyaṃ devadatto yajñadattasakāśād abhirūpaḥ caitrāpekṣayā tu nīrūpa iti ||
children.translated_text: as, for example, this <s>Devadatta</s> is handsome in comparison with <s>Yajñadatta</s>, but ugly in relation to <s>Caitra</s>,

children.text: evaṃ tarhi yajñadattasyāśreṣṭhatvaṃ caitrasya ca śreṣṭhatvam ity ubhayaṃ tata ity apekṣātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then in that case both the inferiority of <s>Yajñadatta</s> and the superiority of <s>Caitra</s> come from that, that is, from comparison.

children.text: evaṃ bhinnaṃ labdhaṃ yad api dvayaṃ tadāpekṣikatvād asatyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus even the pair that is obtained as distinct is unreal, because it is relative.

children.text: apekṣā hi nāma na vāstavī ||
children.translated_text: For what is called <s>apekṣā</s> (dependence on comparison) is not real.

children.text: tasyāḥ kila vastunaḥ sati sadbhāve kiṃ prayojanaṃ siddhasattākatvenānapekṣatvāt ||
children.translated_text: For when a thing has real existence, what use does it have for that? Since its existence is already established, it is independent.

children.text: tathā cāhuḥ saṃś ca sarvo nirāśaṃso bhāvaḥ katham apekṣate ||
children.translated_text: And accordingly they say: How can every existent entity, being without dependence, depend on anything?

children.text: na cālabdhasattāke vastuny apekṣāyāḥ kim api karaṇīyam asti tasyāsattvād eva tadapekṣānupapatteḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nor, in an object whose existence has not been obtained, is there anything at all for dependence to do; precisely because it does not exist, dependence upon it is impossible.

children.text: tad idam uktam apekṣā na satāṃ siddher asiddher api nāsatām iti ||
children.translated_text: This is what was said: dependence is not for the establishment of things that exist, nor, because they are unestablished, for things that do not exist.

children.text: tad evaṃ na kathaṃcid api sadasator abhedopapattiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in no way at all is there any possibility of non-difference between existent and nonexistent.

children.text: Chapter 54
tasya dehāt pūrvaṃ sadasattvenābhimatasya vyāpakatvāt pudgalāntaraiḥ saha karmasaṃkaraḥ śaṅkyate ||
children.translated_text: Since that self, which is accepted as both existent and nonexistent before the body, would be pervasive, an admixture of karma with other <s>pudgala</s>s is suspected.

children.text: vyāpakatve hi viprakīrṇānāṃ karmaṇāṃ bhoktṛn prati niyamaḥ kiṃkṛtaḥ avyāpakānāṃ tu teṣāṃ pratyekaṃ vyavasthito mohādibandhapadārtha eva tanniyāmaka iti karmasaṃkarabhayād avyāpakatvam acetasaḥ durbuddhayaḥ jagur ūcuḥ ||
children.translated_text: For if it were pervasive, what would account for the restriction of scattered karmas to their respective experiencers? But if they are non-pervasive, then for each of them the established bondage-factor, beginning with delusion, is what regulates them. Therefore, out of fear of karmic admixture, those senseless, dull-minded people declared that it is non-pervasive.

children.text: kuta eṣāṃ mandabuddhitvam ity āha sāmānyetarasaṃbandhajñānābhāvāt samānyenānādikālīnenātmano vyāpakatvena yaḥ saṃbandhaḥ sarvakālabhāvitvena sādhāraṇyam asya itareṇa ca muktāv eva saṃjātatvāt tathārūpeṇa tayor jñānaṃ samyagavabodhas teṣāṃ pudgalavādināṃ nāsti ||
children.translated_text: Why are they dull-minded? He says: because of the absence of knowledge of the relation to the universal and to what is other than it. The <s>Pudgalavādin</s>s lack correct understanding of the two: the relation of the self to pervasiveness as a universal, beginningless factor, common because it exists at all times, and its relation to the other aspect, which arises as such only in liberation.

children.text: yadi hi tadavabodha eṣāṃ syāt tadā naivam ayuktam eva kalpayeyur mohādipāśāvaruddhasahajavyāpakasvabhāvasyātmanaḥ svabhāvata evāvyāpakatvābhyupagamo yas tasya viruddhatvāt ||
children.translated_text: For if they understood that, they would not imagine this plainly unreasonable thing: the acceptance that the <s>ātman</s> (self), whose innate, pervasive nature is obstructed by the bonds (<s>pāśa</s>) beginning with delusion, is by its very nature non-pervasive; for that is contradictory.

children.text: Chapter 55
prāk pūrvaṃ saṃsārāvasthāyām avyāpako yaḥ sa kathaṃ mokṣe vyāpakaḥ vyāpakatvaṃ ca tadānīm apy abhyupagantum ayuktam ||
children.translated_text: How could that which earlier, in the state of <s>saṃsāra</s>, was non-pervasive be pervasive in <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation)? Nor is it proper to accept that it was pervasive even then.

children.text: evaṃ hi saṃsāramuktyor aviśeṣaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: For in that case there would be no distinction between <s>saṃsāra</s> and liberation.

children.text: atha tathāvidhadharmasya vikāsasaṃkocadharmitvam abhyupagamyate yad uta saṃsṛtau saṃkocam eti muktau tu vikasati iti tato vipariṇāmitvajaḍatvādyanekadoṣasantatiḥ prasajyata iti na kathaṃcid api sadasadvādimatam upasthāpayituṃ śakyam ||
children.translated_text: But if one accepts that a property of that kind has the nature of expansion and contraction, namely, that it contracts in transmigration but expands in liberation, then a series of many faults, such as transformability and inertness, would follow. Thus the doctrine of the proponents of existence-and-nonexistence cannot be established in any way.

children.text: idānīṃ pādārthikadarśanapradarśitamuktinirākaraṇāyāha ||
children.translated_text: Now, in order to refute the liberation presented by the <s>Pādārthika</s> system, he says:

children.text: Chapter 56

dravyaguṇakarmasāmānyaviśeṣasamavāyānāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ padārthānāṃ sādharmyavaidharmyatattvajñānaṃ niḥśreyasahetur ity abhyupagamāt dravyādipadārthaṣaṭkasya yathāvaj jñānād ajñānanivṛttau ragādidoṣopaśame buddhisukhaduḥkhecchādveṣaprayatnadharmādharmasaṃskārāṇāṃ navānām ātmaguṇānāṃ dehasaṃyogajatvāt krameṇa nivṛttau yā muktiḥ sā buddhyādyuparame sati ātmanas tadvinākṛtasya kiṃcijjñatvoparamāj jaḍatārūpāṅgīkriyate tataḥ śavo 'pi kiṃ na muktaḥ kalpyate tasyāpi buddhyādiguṇāviraheṇecchājñānādivinākṛtatvād iti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because they accept that true knowledge of the similarity and dissimilarity of the six categories, substance, quality, action, universal, particularity, and inherence, is the cause of the highest good, ignorance ceases through correct knowledge of the six categories beginning with substance; when faults such as passion subside and, because they arise from connection with the body, the nine qualities of the <s>ātman</s> (self), cognition, pleasure, pain, desire, aversion, effort, <s>dharma</s> (merit), <s>adharma</s> (demerit), and impression, cease in sequence, the liberation that remains when cognition and the rest have ceased is accepted as a form of inertness, since the self bereft of them has ceased to know anything at all. Hence, why should even a corpse not be imagined to be liberated, since it too lacks qualities such as cognition and is devoid of desire, knowledge, and the like? This is the purport.

children.text: atha saugatamuktinirācikīrṣayā tanmatam anubhāṣya dūṣayati ||
children.translated_text: Then, wishing to refute <s>Saugata</s> liberation, he restates their doctrine and criticizes it.

children.text: Chapter 57
cijjñānaṃ grahītṛrūpaṃ saṃvedanam ||
children.translated_text: Conscious cognition is <s>saṃvedana</s> (awareness) in the form of an apprehender.

children.text: sā cit vyañjakasya vyaktihetoḥ karmaṇo vyāpārasya yogasaṃgrahaṇāder yadi vā karmaṇo grāhyasya ghaṭapaṭāder ādigrahaṇāt karaṇasya cakṣurādeḥ sahakāriṇa ālokādeś cānatisthairyāt pratikṣaṇam utpadyamānaiva vyajyate prakaṭībhavati ||
children.translated_text: This consciousness, because the manifesting factor, the cause of manifestation, is unstable, whether that factor is an activity such as conjunction and grasping, or the object to be grasped, such as a pot or a cloth, with the instrument such as the eye and an auxiliary such as light included under the expression 'and so on', becomes manifested, that is, evident, only as something produced at every moment.

children.text: ayam arthaḥ vakṣcamāṇasatkāryavādadṛśā abhivyaktitirobhāvabhājāṃ bhāvānāṃ vyāpārabhedena avasthādeśakālādibhedena cānatisthairyāt tajjñānam api tattadupādhibhedān muhurmuhur vyajyamānaṃ kṣaṇikaṃ tad eva ca pramaṇam iti pare manyante ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is this: according to the standpoint of <s>satkāryavāda</s> that will be stated, entities undergo manifestation and disappearance; because they are not stable, owing to differences in activity and in condition, place, time, and so on, cognition of them too, repeatedly manifested through the difference of each limiting condition, is momentary, and that very cognition is <s>pramāṇa</s> (a means of knowledge). So the opponents think.

children.text: tad āhuḥ nityaṃ pramāṇaṃ naivāsti prāmāṇyād vastusaṃgateḥ ||
children.translated_text: They say: There is no permanent <s>pramāṇa</s> at all, since validity depends on connection with a real object;

children.text: jñeyānityatayā tasyā adhrauvyāt kramajanmanaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: because, owing to the impermanence of what is knowable, that connection is unstable and arises successively.

children.text: cid eva hi kṣaṇikā tattadarthaprakāśarūpānubhavasiddhā na tv etātirikta ātmā vidyate saṃvedanavyatiriktasya bhedenāpratibhāsanāt ||
children.translated_text: For consciousness alone is momentary, established by experience as the illumination of each particular object; but no <s>ātman</s> distinct from it exists, since something apart from awareness does not appear as separate.

children.text: yathāhuḥ ekam evedaṃ saṃvidrūpaṃ harṣaviṣādādyanekākāravivartaṃ paśyāmaḥ tatra yatheṣṭhaṃ saṃjñāḥ kriyantām iti ||
children.translated_text: As they have said: We see this one thing alone, whose form is consciousness, undergoing transformation into many forms such as joy and sorrow; let names be assigned there however one likes.

children.text: saṃvedana eva kṣaṇike jaladhārāpravāhavat sadṛśaparāparotpattibhramād vikalpena sthairyam adhyāropyata ity avidyājanitā seyam ātmadṛṣṭiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Upon momentary <s>saṃvedana</s> alone, as upon a stream of water, stability is superimposed by conceptual construction because of the illusion of similar earlier and later arisings. Thus this view of a self is produced by ignorance.

children.text: tad uktaṃ mithyādhyāropahānārthaṃ yatno 'saty api bhoktari iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus it has been said: Effort is made for abandoning false superimposition, even though there is no enjoyer.

children.text: ātmagrahe hi sati tad anyatra paratvābhimānāt svaparabhedaḥ tataś ca rāgadveṣādyanarthodbhavādātmagraho bandha iti bhagavatā sugatena nairātmyabhāvanopadiṣṭā ||
children.translated_text: For when there is grasping of a self, the notion that what is other than it is alien produces the division between self and other; and since evils such as passion and aversion arise from that, grasping a self is bondage. Therefore the blessed <s>Sugata</s> taught meditation on no-self.

children.text: yad uktam ātmani sati parasaṃjñā svaparavibhāgāt parigrahadveṣau ||
children.translated_text: As has been said: When there is a self, there is the notion of another; from the division between self and other arise appropriation and aversion;

children.text: anayoḥ saṃpratibaddhāḥ sarve doṣāḥ prajāyanta iti ||
children.translated_text: bound up with these two, all faults arise.

children.text: na cābhyupagatasyāpy ātmano nityatvaṃ ghaṭate yat sat tat sarvaṃ kṣaṇikam akṣaṇikasya kramayaugapadyābhyām arthakriyānupapatteḥ sattāyā evāsiddhatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Nor, even for a self that has been admitted, does permanence make sense. Whatever exists is momentary; for in the case of a non-momentary thing, causal efficacy is impossible either successively or simultaneously, and so its very existence is unproved.

children.text: tad āhuḥ arthakriyāsamarthaṃ yat tad atra paramārthasat ||
children.translated_text: They say: Whatever is capable of causal efficacy is ultimately real here;

children.text: asanto 'kṣaṇikās tasmāt kramākramavirodhataḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: therefore non-momentary things are unreal, because of incompatibility with succession and simultaneity.

children.text: tathā hi nityo bhāvaḥ krameṇa vārthakriyāṃ kuryād yugapad vā ||
children.translated_text: For example, a permanent entity would perform causal efficacy either successively or all at once.

children.text: na tasya tāvat krameṇa karaṇam upapadyate yasmād ayam apracyuto 'nutpannasthiraikasvabhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: First, its acting successively is not possible, because it has one fixed nature, unchanging and not newly produced.

children.text: sa ca kālāntaranirvartyām arthakriyāṃ tadānīm eva kiṃ na karoti na hy asāv avasarāntarakaraṇīyaṃ svabhāvāntareṇa kuryāt svabhāvasyaikarūpatvāt svabhāvānyathābhāve hi tadvato 'pi tadavyatirekād vināśas tataś cānityatvam ||
children.translated_text: Why, then, does it not perform right then the causal activity that is to be accomplished at another time? For it would not perform, by means of another nature, what is to be done on a different occasion, since its nature is uniform. If its nature became otherwise, then, because the possessor of that nature is not distinct from it, that possessor too would perish; and consequently it would be impermanent.

children.text: athocyate sa padārtho 'rthakriyāṃ karoty eva yadi sahakāriṇo 'sya saṃnihitāḥ syuḥ tadasaṃnidhānād akurvāṇasya nāsyopālambhayogyatvam iti ||
children.translated_text: If it is said: That entity does indeed perform causal efficacy if its auxiliaries are present; because they are absent, when it does not act it is not liable to reproach.

children.text: naivaṃ sahakāriṇo 'syākiṃcitkarāś cet kim arthaṃ tān apekṣate ||
children.translated_text: Not so. If its auxiliaries do nothing for it, why does it depend on them?

children.text: kiṃcitkaratve tu yat tat kiṃcit kurvanti tat tato 'vyatiriktaṃ vyatiriktaṃ vā vyatiriktakaraṇe kiṃ tasya tadapekṣayā tadavyatiriktakaraṇe sa eva sahakāribhiḥ kriyata ity āyātam ||
children.translated_text: But if [the auxiliaries] do something, then whatever that something is which they do: is it non-different from that [thing], or different? If what is made is different, what dependence does that [thing] have on it? If what is made is non-different from it, it follows that that very thing is made by the auxiliaries.

children.text: na cāsthirasya karaṇam upapannaṃ tatsvabhāvasya sataḥ svahetubhya evotpatteḥ kṛtasya ca kartum aśakyatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Nor is the making of something unstable tenable, because when it has that nature it arises from its own causes alone, and because what has already been made cannot be made [again].

children.text: atha sthirasvabhāvasyāsya sahakāriṇo 'tiśayādhānaṃ kurvanti yena kālāntare 'rthakriyāṃ karotīti ||
children.translated_text: If, then, the auxiliaries impart some special capacity to this thing whose nature is stable, by which it performs <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy) at a later time, [we reply:]

children.text: etad apy asad yasmād anāhitātiśayāt svabhāvād āhitātiśayo 'nya eveti sthiraikasvabhāvataiva truṭyati ||
children.translated_text: This too is unsound, since a nature without an imparted special capacity and one with an imparted special capacity are simply different; thus its being one stable nature breaks down.

children.text: tathā hi sahakāribhyo 'tiśayotpattau sa pūrvotpannānāhitātiśayasva bhāvaḥ svata eva vinaṣṭo 'bhyupagantavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For when a special capacity arises from the auxiliaries, that nature, previously arisen and lacking the imparted special capacity, must be admitted to have perished by itself.

children.text: tasyānaśvarasvabhāvatvena nāśahetor api tatrākiṃcitkaratvāt vinaśvarodbhavasvabhāvatve vā vaiyarthyāt tasya ca svabhāvasyāviśeṣāt pratikṣaṇam iti kṣaṇikatā ||
children.translated_text: Because it has a non-perishing nature, even a cause of destruction can do nothing to it there; or, if its nature is to arise as perishable, [a cause of destruction] is useless. And since that nature is undifferentiated at every instant, this is <s>kṣaṇikatva</s> (momentariness).

children.text: tad evaṃ na nityasya krameṇārthakriyā ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in this way, an eternal thing has no successive <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy).

children.text: nāpi yugapat karaṇam upapadyate yasmād yaugapadyena nirvartitārthakriyo 'pi tasmāt svabhāvān na viramet sthiraikasvabhāvatvāt svabhāvaviratau svabhāvahāniḥ kṣaṇikatvam eva ||
children.translated_text: Nor is simultaneous action tenable, because even after it has completed its causal efficacy simultaneously, it would not cease from that nature, since it has one stable nature. If it ceases from its nature, there is loss of nature, which is simply momentariness.

children.text: atha nāsya svabhāvāntarayogaḥ kiṃtu na karoty evāyaṃ kāryasya tv ayaṃ vipākaḥ kṛtasya yat kartum aśakyatvam eva ||
children.translated_text: If [you say], 'There is no connection with another nature in it; rather, it simply does not act, since this is the consequence in the case of an effect: what has been made simply cannot be made [again],'

children.text: tad apy ayuktaṃ tasya tāvad arthakriyām akurvato 'syaiva sattāyā eva durlabhatvāt arthakriyāsamarthaṃ yat tad atra paramārthasat ity uktatvāt ||
children.translated_text: that too is unreasonable, because, so long as it does not perform causal efficacy, even its very existence is hard to establish; for it has been said here that whatever is capable of causal efficacy is ultimately real.

children.text: arthakriyākaraṇalakṣaṇāt svabhāvāt tadakaraṇātmakasvabhāvo 'nya eveti katham asya na svabhāvāntarayogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A nature whose defining mark is performing causal efficacy is one thing, and a nature whose essence is not performing it is another; how, then, is there no connection with another nature in it?

children.text: yadi ca yaugapad yenāpi kurvann anavarataṃ karoti tadā svabhāvāviśeṣāt sarvadā sarvārthakriyākaraṇaprasaṅga iti kṣaṇikam evedaṃ saṃvedanaṃ yuktaṃ na tu tadvyatiriktanityātmasiddhir iti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And if, even while acting simultaneously, it acts without interruption, then, because there is no difference in its nature, the consequence follows that it performs every causal efficacy at all times. Therefore this <s>saṃvedana</s> (conscious awareness) is properly momentary alone, while an eternal self distinct from it is not established. This is the prima facie position.

children.text: Chapter 58
siddhāntas tu tad etat kṣaṇikatvaṃ saṃvedanasya nairātmyabhāvanābhyupagamanaṃ ca na yuktaṃ svasaṃvedanasiddhasya sthirarūpasyāparokṣasyātmanaḥ prakāśanāt ||
children.translated_text: But the established conclusion is this: that momentariness of <s>saṃvedana</s> and the acceptance of <s>nairātmyabhāvanā</s> (contemplation of no-self) are not justified, because the immediate <s>ātmā</s> (self), of stable form and established by <s>svasaṃvedana</s> (self-awareness), shines forth.

children.text: nanu sadṛśaparāparakṣaṇotpattivipralabdhatvāt sthairyam asyāropitam ity uktam ||
children.translated_text: Objection: It has been said that stability is superimposed on it because one is deceived by the arising of preceding and succeeding moments that are similar.

children.text: tad ayuktaṃ svātmani kriyāvirodhād adhyāropānupapatteḥ ||
children.translated_text: That is unreasonable, because superimposition is impossible, since an action directed at one's own self is contradictory.

children.text: yad api kṣaṇabhaṅgasādhanārtham akṣaṇikasya kramayaugapadyābhyām arthakriyāvirodhāt sattāyā evāsiddhatvād yat sat tatkṣaṇikam ity anumāpanaghaṭanaṃ kṛtaṃ tatsvasaṃvedanalakṣaṇapramāṇabādhitatvād ayuktam akṣaṇikasya sataḥ sarvasya svasaṃvedanasyānubhavasiddhatvāt anaikāntikaṃ ca sarvasya sataḥ kṣaṇikatvena vyāptipradarśane sati akṣaṇikasya paramārthasato vaidharmyadṛṣṭāntasyāsaṃbhavād vipakṣavyāvṛttyadarśanena hetoḥ kevalānvayino gamakatvābhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, the construction of an inference made to prove momentary destruction, namely, 'because a non-momentary thing is incompatible with causal efficacy successively and simultaneously, its very existence is not established; whatever exists is momentary,' is unreasonable, since it is contradicted by the <s>pramāṇa</s> whose character is self-awareness. For the whole of self-awareness, existent and non-momentary, is established by experience. It is also inconclusive: when the pervasion that everything existent is momentary is set forth, there can be no dissimilar example that is non-momentary and ultimately real; and since exclusion from the counter-instance is not seen, a reason that is merely positively concomitant has no probative force.

children.text: viruddhaś cāyam asattvākhyo hetuḥ sādhyaviparyayeṇākṣaṇikatvena sarvārthakriyākāriṇi ghaṭādau siddhavyāptikatvāt ||
children.translated_text: And this reason called 'non-existence' is contradictory, because its pervasion is established with the opposite of what is to be proved, namely non-momentariness, in things such as a pot, which perform every causal function.

children.text: yad apy etad vyāptisādhanārthaṃ nityasya kramayaugapadyābhyām arthakriyāvirodhād iti hetvantaraṃ tad apy āśrayāsiddhatvād ayuktam ||
children.translated_text: And the further reason meant to establish the pervasion, 'because an eternal thing is incompatible with causal efficacy successively and simultaneously,' is also unreasonable, since its locus is unestablished.

children.text: na hi nityaḥ kaścid artho bhavadbhir abhyupagato yatrāyaṃ hetuḥ siddhaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: For no eternal entity is accepted by you in which this reason could be established.

children.text: na cānityasyāpi maṇyāder arthasya krameṇānekadeśasthāṃs tāṃs tān bhāvān prakāśayato yugapac caikagṛhagatān ghaṭapaṭādīn avabhāsayataḥ kaścid virodhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nor is there any contradiction even in the case of an impermanent object such as a jewel, when it successively illuminates various things situated in many places and simultaneously makes visible pots, cloths, and the like located in one house.

children.text: api ca na tāvat kṣaṇikaṃ saṃvedanam anekakṣaṇanirvartyārthakriyānuṣṭhānasamartham utpattyanantaraṃ dhvaṃsinas tadupapattyayogāt ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, momentary <s>saṃvedana</s> is certainly not capable of carrying out causal efficacy that is completed over many moments, because, since it perishes immediately after arising, that performance is impossible.

children.text: na cāropitaṃ sthairyaṃ tattadvyāpāranirvartanakṣamaṃ tasya ca svātmany adhyāropānupapatter ity uktatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Nor can an imputed stability be capable of accomplishing those various operations, because, as was said, superimposition upon its own self is impossible.

children.text: āropyasya cāvastutvenārthakriyānuṣṭhānam asaṃbaddham ||
children.translated_text: And since what is superimposed is unreal, its carrying out causal efficacy is incoherent.

children.text: vastutve ca sthirasyāvabodhasyātmarūpatvenāsmābhir abhyupagamān nāsti bhedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But if it is real, there is no difference [between us], since we accept stable awareness as the nature of the self.

children.text: kṣaṇavyatiriktaś ca sattāsantāno na kathaṃcid upalabhyate tasmāt karmānuṣṭhānadarśanānyathānupapattyā vastusiddham evāsya cidātmanaḥ sthairyam ||
children.translated_text: And no continuum of existence apart from the moments is perceived in any way. Therefore, because the observed performance of action cannot otherwise be accounted for, the stability of this conscious self is established as a real thing.

children.text: itaś caitat kṣaṇikatvam ayuktaṃ karmaṇo bhogāt ||
children.translated_text: For this reason too, this momentariness is unreasonable: because <s>karma</s> is experienced.

children.text: kṣaṇāntarānanvayini vijñāne karmabhogo 'nupapannaḥ yenaiva hi dṛṣṭaṃ sevākṛṣyādi karma kṛtaṃ tam eva tasya bhoktāram upalabhāmahe ||
children.translated_text: When cognition does not continue into another moment, the experience of <s>karma</s> is impossible; for we observe that the very person by whom a visible action such as service or plowing was performed is the experiencer of its result.

children.text: dṛṣṭavac cādṛṣṭakalpanā yuktimatī ||
children.translated_text: And it is reasonable to infer the unseen on the model of what is seen.

children.text: yady ubhayajanmani śarīrādibhede 'py abhinna eka eva bhoktābhyupagamyate tadā hi karmaphalabhogo nirbādho bhavati ||
children.translated_text: For if, despite the difference of body and so on in the two births, one and the same undivided experiencer is accepted, then the experience of the fruit of karma is unobstructed.

children.text: atha caityavandanākhyaṃ karmānyena kṛtam anyasyaiva tatphalena svargādinā yoga ity akṛtābhyāgamakṛtavipraṇāśaprasaṅgo durnivāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: But if the action called veneration of a shrine is done by one person, while another alone is connected with its fruit, such as heaven, then the consequence that what was not done arrives and what was done is lost is hard to avoid.

children.text: uktaṃ ca śrīmataṅge kṛtam ekena yat karma tadvipākaṃ paraḥ katham ||
children.translated_text: And it is said in the venerable <s>Mataṅga</s>: How can another obtain the ripening of an action

children.text: prāpnoti yuktidaurbalyād iti ||
children.translated_text: which was done by one person? It is because of weakness in reasoning.

children.text: nanu nāyaṃ doṣaḥ aihikasya karmaṇo labdhaśarīreṇa jñānasantānena paratra bhogopapatteḥ ||
children.translated_text: Objection: This is no fault, since the experience of the fruit of karma done in this world can occur in the next world through a continuum of cognition that has obtained a body.

children.text: tad ayuktam aśarīrasya jñānasantānasya sadbhāve pramāṇābhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: That is not right, because there is no means of proof for the existence of a bodiless continuum of cognition.

children.text: karmaphalabhogānyathānupapattyā vijñānasantānasiddhis tatsiddhyā ca karmaphalabhoga ity anupapannam asthairyaṃ saṃvedanasya ||
children.translated_text: It is untenable to say that the continuum of cognition is established because otherwise the experience of karmic fruit would not be possible, and that the experience of karmic fruit follows once that is established, since consciousness is unstable.

children.text: itaś ca kṣaṇikaṃ saṃvedanam ity asat ||
children.translated_text: For this reason too, the claim that consciousness is momentary is false.

children.text: kuta ity āha atītānubhavasmṛteḥ atītaḥ samatikrānto yasyānubhavas tasya smaraṇāt ||
children.translated_text: Why? He says: because of memory of past experience, that is, because one remembers an experience that has gone by and passed away.

children.text: yadā hi sthirasva bhāva ubhayakālānusaṃdhātā ātmābhyupagamyate tanubhūtaviṣayāsaṃpramoṣarūpaṃ smaraṇam upapadyate na tu kṣaṇikatve ||
children.translated_text: For when a self of stable nature, connecting both times, is accepted, memory, whose form is the non-loss of the object experienced by that same one, is possible; but it is not possible under momentariness.

children.text: na hi prāktanakṣaṇānubhūtasukhaduḥkhādisaṃvedanaṃ vartamānena kālāntarabhāvinā vā kṣaṇena smartuṃ śakyaṃ tasyānyatvāt yathā na devadattānubhūtaṃ tatputraḥ smarati ||
children.translated_text: For the awareness of pleasure, pain, and the like experienced by a prior moment cannot be remembered by the present moment or by a moment occurring at another time, because it is different, just as Devadatta's son does not remember what <s>Devadatta</s> experienced.

children.text: dṛśyate ca śaiśavādyanubhūtaṃ yauvanasthāvirādyavasthāsu smaryamāṇam ||
children.translated_text: And what was experienced in childhood and the like is seen to be remembered in the states of youth, old age, and so on.

children.text: sāceyam atītānubhavasmṛtiḥ kṣaṇikatāṃ vijñānasya nirasyati na tu sthirasvabhāvam ātmānam anumāpayati tasya svasaṃvedanasiddhasya svānubhūtyekapramāṇatvāt ||
children.translated_text: This very memory of past experience refutes the momentariness of cognition; it does not, however, make one infer a self of stable nature, because that self is established by self-awareness and has one's own experience alone as its means of proof.

children.text: tad evaṃ karmopabhogād atītānubhavasmṛteś ca na kṣaṇikatvam upapadyate citaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, from the experience of karma and from memory of past experience, the momentariness of consciousness is not established.

children.text: tad āha ||
children.translated_text: Therefore he says:

children.text: Chapter 59

sūcyagranipatatsarṣapavadanavasthāyitvādaviśramyaiva vinaśyatsu vijñānakṣaṇeṣu proktavan na smṛter avasthiter upapattiḥ kalpyate nāpi karmaṇa ity alam alīkakalpanākulīkṛtasthitinā kṣaṇabhaṅgābhiniveśena ||
children.translated_text: As cognition-moments, which do not remain any more than mustard seeds falling on the tip of a needle, perish without even pausing, no possibility can be conceived, as stated, for the continuance of memory, nor for that of karma. Enough with this attachment to momentariness, whose position is confused by false suppositions.

children.text: Chapter 60
śuddhacitsaṃtatisamutpādo bhavatāṃ mokṣaḥ syāt yadi vā pradīpanirvāṇarūpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For you, <s>mokṣa</s> would either be the arising of a pure stream of consciousness, or else it would have the form of the extinction of a lamp.

children.text: ādye pakṣe svaparikalpitasya pratikṣaṇavināśitvalakṣaṇasyopaplavasya muktāv apy anupaśamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the first alternative, even in liberation there is no cessation of the calamity imagined by you, whose mark is destruction at every moment.

children.text: dvitīye tu pradīpanirvāṇarūpatvāt saṃvedanāsaṃbhavataḥ kaścid apy anubhavo nāstīti tathāvidhāt saṃvedanavināśātmakāt kāṣṭhakuḍyādīnām api sulabhān mokṣāt saṃsārāvasthā varaṃ saugatānām iti kṛtam evaṃvidhamokṣalipsayā ||
children.translated_text: But in the second, since, because it has the form of a lamp's extinction, consciousness is impossible, there is no experience at all. Since even pieces of wood, walls, and the like can easily obtain a <s>mokṣa</s> of that sort, consisting in the destruction of consciousness, the state of <s>saṃsāra</s> is better for the <s>Saugata</s>s; enough with the desire for such liberation.

children.text: tadiyatā vedāntasāṃkhyasadasatpādārthikādimateṣu asarvadarśipraṇetṛtvād vastusaṃgrahasyāsphuṭatvam asaṃbaddhatāṃ codbhāvya darśanāntarāṇām apy eṣaiva vārteti tattadabhiniveśināṃ na niratiśayaniḥśreyasayoga iti vaktum āha ||
children.translated_text: Thus, having to this extent pointed out, in the doctrines of the <s>Vedānta</s>s, <s>Sāṃkhya</s>s, proponents of real and unreal categories, and others, the obscurity and incoherence of their account of reality, because their founders were not omniscient, he says the following to state that the same is also the case with other systems and that those attached to each of them do not attain unsurpassed final good.

children.text: Chapter 61

śivaśaktividyeśvarādāv upādeyasatattve malakarmamāyādau ca heyaparamārthe yeṣāṃ nāsty avabodhaḥ teṣām ajñānamūḍhānāṃ darśanāntarapraṇetṝṇāṃ saṃbandhi mataṃ śāstram āśrityākuśalamatayo ye muktim icchanti te khadyotād agnyabhyarthinaḥ kīṭamaṇer vahniṃ lipsavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those of poor understanding who rely on doctrines and scriptures belonging to the founders of other systems, who are deluded by ignorance and have no understanding of the true principles to be adopted, such as <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śakti</s>, and <s>Vidyeśvara</s>, or of the ultimate realities to be rejected, such as <s>mala</s>, <s>karma</s>, and <s>māyā</s>, and who desire liberation, are like people asking a firefly for fire, desiring fire from a luminous insect-gem.

children.text: te yathā vyarthaśramās tathā te viphalakleśā bhavantīty arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that, just as those people make effort in vain, so these people undergo fruitless trouble.

children.text: tathā hi ||
children.translated_text: For thus:

children.text: Chapter 62

yad etat kapilakalpitaṃ puṃsprakṛtyor vivekāt kaivalyaṃ yā ca sarvaṃ khalv idaṃ brahmeti matvā dvaitavikalpaprahāṇe sati brahmaprāptiḥ yāś ca pāśajanyāḥ kāścit pāñcarātrādibhir muktayo 'bhyupagatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: This <s>kaivalya</s> imagined by <s>Kapila</s> from the discrimination of <s>puruṣa</s> and <s>prakṛti</s>, and the attainment of <s>Brahman</s> when, after thinking 'all this indeed is <s>Brahman</s>,' the construction of duality has been abandoned, and whatever liberations born of bonds are accepted by the <s>Pāñcarātra</s>s and others:

children.text: yathāhuḥ īśās tu te samabhavan prakṛteḥ parasyāḥ kṛṣṇāniruddhamakaradhvajarauhiṇeyāḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: as they say, Those lords came forth from the higher <s>prakṛti</s>: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Aniruddha</s>, <s>Makaradhvaja</s>, and <s>Rauhiṇeya</s>;

children.text: yathā vā kālaikavādināṃ kālaḥ sṛjati bhūtāni kālaḥ saṃharati prajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: or as among those who maintain time alone: Time creates beings; time destroys creatures.

children.text: kālaḥ supteṣu jagarti kālo hi duratikrama iti ||
children.translated_text: Time wakes among those who sleep; time indeed is hard to overcome.

children.text: yathā vā keṣāṃcit cittam eva hi saṃsāro rāgādikleśadūṣitam ||
children.translated_text: Or as some say: Mind itself is <s>saṃsāra</s>, defiled by afflictions such as passion.

children.text: tad eva tadvinirmuktaṃ mokṣa ity abhidhīyata iti ||
children.translated_text: That very same mind, when freed from them, is called <s>mokṣa</s>.

children.text: etāḥ kila prakṛtikālabuddhyādīnāṃ bandhakatvena pāśarūpatvāt pāśajanyā muktayaḥ sargārambhe bhedam āyānti vinaśyantīty arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: These, to be sure, are liberations born of bonds, because <s>prakṛti</s>, time, intellect, and the like, being binders, have the nature of bonds; the meaning is that at the beginning of creation they undergo differentiation and perish.

children.text: yad uktaṃ śrīmanmataṅge tasmāt pradhānaśabdena tattvam uktam acetanam ||
children.translated_text: As is said in the venerable <s>Mataṅga</s>: Therefore, by the word <s>pradhāna</s>, an unconscious <s>tattva</s> is stated.

children.text: tasmāt paraṃ nāsty aparaṃ yeṣāṃ bhāvaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those whose conviction is fixed that there is nothing higher than that and nothing other than that

children.text: na te muktā munivyāghra punar āyānty adhogatim iti ||
children.translated_text: are not liberated, O tiger among sages; they return again to a lower state.

children.text: tathā upādāneṣu līnānāṃ punar āvartanaṃ dhruvam iti ||
children.translated_text: Likewise: For those dissolved into the material causes, return is certain.

children.text: teṣāṃ tu tathāvidhamithyādhyāsabhājāṃ na nirantaram ajñānadhvāntasantatir antaḥkaraṇam āvṛṇoti api tu te krameṇa vivekaprathanāt parameśvarānugrahāspadatāṃ kasmiṃścid api kāle yāsyanti ||
children.translated_text: But for those who are subject to such false superimposition, the continuous mass of the darkness of ignorance does not cover the inner organ forever; rather, through the gradual manifestation of discrimination, at some time or another they will become a fit recipient of the Supreme Lord's grace.

children.text: tathā coktaṃ śrīmatpauṣkarapārameśvare na mokṣaṃ yāti puruṣaḥ svasāmarthyāt kadācana ||
children.translated_text: And so it has been said in the venerable <s>Pauṣkarapārameśvara</s>: A person never attains liberation by his own power at any time,

children.text: muktvā prasādaṃ devasya śivasyāśivahāriṇa iti ||
children.translated_text: apart from the grace of the god <s>Śiva</s>, the remover of what is inauspicious.

children.text: athaivaṃ matāntaroktāyā mukteḥ prāguktavad asatyatve tataḥ kiṃ tadvailakṣaṇyamihatyayoḥ siddhimuktyor ity āha ||
children.translated_text: Now, if the liberation taught by other systems is unreal, as stated before, then what is the distinction between the <s>siddhi</s> and liberation taught here? He states it.

children.text: Chapter 63
iha śāstre yaḥ siddhaḥ sa vividhabhuvanopapannavicitraiśvaryasaṃpāditatattadbhogabhāk sarvottkarṣaśālī bhavati ||
children.translated_text: In this scripture, one who is perfected becomes endowed with unsurpassed excellence, enjoying each of the enjoyments produced by the varied lordly powers found in manifold worlds.

children.text: tathā coktaṃ bṛhaspatipādaiḥ yan māhātmyaṃ bhagavati paramaśive 'nupamam avyayam acintyam ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Bṛhaspatipāda</s> has said: Whatever greatness in the blessed supreme <s>Śiva</s> is incomparable, imperishable, and inconceivable,

children.text: tan māhātmyaṃ siddhe hatabandhanamaṇḍale bhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: that greatness exists in the perfected one whose whole circle of bonds has been destroyed.

children.text: na ca darśanāntarapratipannabrahmalayasaṃvidvināśaprakṛtipuruṣavivekādyātmano mokṣasyaivaṃguṇatvam ity uktam ||
children.translated_text: And it has been stated that liberation as accepted in other systems, whose nature is dissolution in <s>brahman</s>, destruction of consciousness, discrimination between <s>prakṛti</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>, and the like, does not possess such qualities.

children.text: yas tv asmin darśane muktaḥ sa bandhakāraṇānāṃ malakarmamāyāparameśvaranirodhaśaktīnām uparatādhikāratvāt punaḥ sargaprārambhe nādho 'bhyeti na saṃsārī bhavatīty arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But one who is liberated in this system, because the authority of the causes of bondage, namely <s>mala</s> (impurity), <s>karma</s>, <s>māyā</s>, and the restraining power of the Supreme Lord, has ceased, does not descend again when creation begins; that is, he does not become a transmigrating being.

children.text: kiṃ tarhi sa karotīty āha viśvān arthān iti āvirbhūtaniratiśayasarvārthajñatvakartṛtvataḥ śivasamānamahimatvāt svatejasā samadhiṣṭhitasarvārtho 'pi san muktātmā na kiṃcit karoti karaṇīyābhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: What, then, does he do? He says: all objects. Since unsurpassed knowledge and agency with regard to all objects have become manifest, and since his greatness is equal to that of <s>Śiva</s>, the liberated self, though he has all objects established under his own radiance, does nothing, because there is nothing to be done.

children.text: evaṃ cen mukteḥ pūrvam akiṃcitkaro 'bhūt muktaś ca tadrūpa eveti ko 'sya muktau viśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If this is so, before liberation he did nothing, and when liberated he is of just the same nature. What distinction, then, does liberation make for him?

children.text: ayaṃ viśeṣaḥ yat sarveśānena parameśvareṇānīśitaḥ apreritas tadānīm asau bhavati ||
children.translated_text: This is the distinction: at that time he is not ruled, not impelled, by the Supreme Lord, the Lord of all.

children.text: kiṃ kiṃcid eva kālam apreryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Is he not impelled only for some limited time?

children.text: nety āha sarvadeti sarvakālaṃ taṃ pratyaprerakaḥ śivabhaṭṭārako bhavatīty arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: No. He says: always. The venerable <s>Śiva</s> is at all times not an impeller with regard to him; this is the meaning.

children.text: Chapter 64
athaśabdo'dhikārārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The word <s>atha</s> indicates the opening of a topic.

children.text: atra hi patipadārthaparīkṣādhikriyata ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For here the examination of the category <s>pati</s> (lord) is being undertaken.

children.text: atra ca tanukaraṇabhuvanādīnāṃ bhāvānāṃ saṃniveśaviśiṣṭatvena kāryatvaṃ buddhvā anumānenaiṣāṃ buddhimatkartṛpūrvakatvaṃ pratīyata iti tātparyam ||
children.translated_text: And here the purport is this: when one has understood that entities such as bodies, instruments, and worlds are effects because they possess a particular arrangement, it is known by inference that they are preceded by an intelligent maker.

children.text: nanu dehasyaiva tāvatkāryatvam asiddhaṃ nahi kvacit kadācid dehaḥ kenacit kriyamāṇo dṛṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Objection: To begin with, the very effectedness of the body is not established, for nowhere, at any time, is a body seen being made by anyone.

children.text: satyaṃ kenacit kriyamāṇatvaṃ dehasya na dṛṣṭam iti kartṛdarśanāpahnavo na yuktaḥ tasyānumeyatvena darśanāviṣayatvāt ||
children.translated_text: True, the body's being made by someone is not seen; nevertheless, denying the perception of a maker is not proper, because that maker is inferable and therefore not an object of perception.

children.text: dehasya tu kriyamāṇatvaṃ kathaṃ na dṛṣṭam abhūtvā bhāvitvam eva hi kāryatvaṃ tac ca dehasyopalabhyata eva ||
children.translated_text: But how is the body's being made not seen? Being something that comes to be after not having existed is precisely being an effect, and that is indeed observed in the body.

children.text: tathā hi śukraśoṇitakalalādyupādānāt diha upacaye iti dhātvarthagatyā pratimāsopacīyamāno garbhastho dehaḥ pratīyate iti katham eṣa kāryatvam atikrāmet ||
children.translated_text: For, from the material cause consisting of semen, blood, the embryonic mass, and so on, and by understanding the verbal root <s>dih</s> in the sense of increase, the body in the womb is observed to increase month by month. How, then, can it escape being an effect?

children.text: kiṃ ca saṃniveśaviśeṣavattvād vinaśvaratvāc ca dehādeḥ kāryatvam apahnotum aśakyam ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, because the body and so forth possess a specific arrangement and are perishable, it is impossible to deny that they are effects.

children.text: yad yat saṃniveśaviśeṣavad vinaśvaraṃ tat tat kāryaṃ yathā ghaṭādi ||
children.translated_text: Whatever possesses a specific arrangement and is perishable is an effect, as a pot and the like are.

children.text: tathā caite dehādayaḥ padārthāḥ tasmād ete'pi kāryāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And these entities, the body and the rest, are of that kind; therefore these too are effects.

children.text: evaṃ ca sati dehādi vastujātaṃ dharmi buddhimatkartṛpūrvakam iti sādhyo dharmaḥ kāryatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Thus, when this is so, the class of things such as the body is the subject; the property to be proved is that it is preceded by an intelligent maker, because it is an effect.

children.text: yad yat kāryaṃ tat tad buddhimatkartṛpūrvakaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yathā rathādi ||
children.translated_text: Whatever is an effect is seen to be preceded by an intelligent maker, as a chariot and the like are.

children.text: yat tu naivaṃvidhaṃ na tat kāryaṃ yathātmādi ||
children.translated_text: But whatever is not of this kind is not an effect, as the self and the like are.

children.text: nanu ghuṇākṣare kārye 'pi na buddhimatkartṛpūrvakatvam astīty anaikāntikaḥ kāryatvahetuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Objection: In an insect-made letter, although it is an effect, there is no being preceded by an intelligent maker; therefore the reason, being an effect, is inconclusive.

children.text: naivaṃ tatra kāryatāyā evānanvayāt ||
children.translated_text: Not so, because in that case there is no positive connection with being an effect itself.

children.text: yatheṣṭasaṃcāramātra eva kila ghuṇasya kartṛtā nanu viśiṣṭasaṃniveśākṣaranirmitau ||
children.translated_text: For the agency of the wood-boring insect is merely its moving about as it likes, is it not? Objection: surely it has agency in producing letters with a particular arrangement.

children.text: sa tu saṃniveśas tathā anyathāsya parisarpataḥ svabhāvata evopapadyate ||
children.translated_text: But that arrangement arises naturally as it crawls in this way and that.

children.text: nanu tadbhāve bhāvāt tadabhāve cābhāvāt ghuṇakartṛkam evākṣaram ||
children.translated_text: Objection: Since the letter exists when that exists and is absent when that is absent, the letter is indeed made by the insect.

children.text: yadyevaṃ tat tathācāritve bhāvāt atathācāritve cākṣarasyānabhivyakter avyavadhānena ghuṇākṣarasya buddhimatkartṛpūrvakatvam astīti kutaḥ kāryatvahetor anaikāntikatvam ||
children.translated_text: If this is so, since the letter exists when the insect behaves in that way, and since it does not manifest when the insect does not behave in that way, the insect-made letter is immediately preceded by an intelligent maker. How, then, could the reason, being an effect, be inconclusive?

children.text: na cāyam akṛṣṭajātaiḥ śālyādibhir vanadrumādibhir vānaikāntikaḥ teṣu kartrabhāvasyāniścayāt teṣāṃ ca pakṣībhūtatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Nor is this reason inconclusive because of rice plants and the like born without ploughing, or because of forest trees and the like; for the absence of a maker in those cases is uncertain, and they are included in the subject under discussion.

children.text: nanvasiddhavyāptikasya pakṣīkaraṇamātreṇa yadi hetvābhāsānāṃ nirāsastarhi na kecana hetavo hetvābhāsāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Objection: If fallacies of reasons are removed merely by making into the subject what has an unestablished pervasion, then no reasons at all would be fallacious.

children.text: bhaved etad yadyayaṃ kāryatvahetur asiddhavyāptikaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: That would be so if this reason, being an effect, had an unestablished pervasion.

children.text: yāvatā dṛṣṭāntīkṛtadṛṣṭakartṛkaghaṭādivyatiriktās trailokyodaravartinas tanukaraṇabhuvanādayo bhāvā dharmiṇaḥ kartṛpūrvakāḥ kāryatvād upalabhyamānakartṛkaghaṭādivad ityanumāne kriyamāṇe kim anyad avaśiṣyate yatra kāryatvasya vyāptirna siddhā syāt ||
children.translated_text: Since, when the inference is made, 'The subject-entities, such as bodies, instruments, and worlds existing within the three worlds and distinct from pots and the like, whose observed makers have been made the examples, are preceded by a maker, because they are effects, like pots and the like whose makers are observed,' what else remains in which the pervasion of effecthood would not be established?

children.text: nanu cātrānumāne ya eva ghaṭādir dṛṣṭānte dharmī sa dṛṣṭakartṛkatvān na tāvat siṣādhīyaṣiteśvaranirvartyaḥ tasya tu kumbhakārakāryatveneśasyāsarvakartṛtvam atheśvarakartṛtvaṃ dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇo ghaṭāderiṣṭaṃ tatsādhyabhraṣṭo dṛṣṭāntaḥ pratītibādhaśca ||
children.translated_text: Objection: But in this inference, the very pot and so on that is the subject in the example, since it has a seen maker, cannot be something produced by the <s>Īśvara</s> whom you wish to establish. If it is the work of a potter, then <s>Īśvara</s> would not be the maker of everything; but if the pot and so on, the subject of the example, is intended to have <s>Īśvara</s> as maker, then the example lacks the probandum and is contradicted by ordinary cognition.

children.text: na hi ghaṭādikam arthaṃ kulālādyanvayavyatirekānuvidhāyinam īśvarakartṛkatvena kaścid apyavaiti ||
children.translated_text: For no one at all understands an object such as a pot, which follows the presence and absence of a potter and the like, as made by <s>Īśvara</s>.

children.text: viruddhaścāyaṃ hetuḥ yādṛśo hi ghaṭādeḥ kartā kulālādiḥ kleśādibhāg anīśo vinaśvaraśca tādṛk jagato'pi kartā prāpnoti ||
children.translated_text: And this reason is contradictory: for whatever sort of maker a pot and the like has, namely a potter and so on, one subject to afflictions, non-sovereign, and perishable, just such a maker would also follow for the world.

children.text: tad uktaṃ jaiminīyaiḥ
children.translated_text: This has been said by the <s>Jaiminīya</s>s:

children.text: kumbhakārādyadhiṣṭhānaṃ ghaṭādau yadi ceṣyate
children.translated_text: If, in the case of a pot and the like, superintendence by a potter and others is accepted,

children.text: neśvarādhiṣṭhitatvaṃ syād asti cet sādhyahīnatā ||
children.translated_text: there would be no superintendence by <s>Īśvara</s>; but if there is, the example lacks what is to be proved.

children.text: tathā siddhe ca dṛṣṭānte bhaveddhetor viruddhatā
children.translated_text: And when the example has been established in that way, the reason would become contradictory;

children.text: anīśvaravināśyādikartṛkatvaṃ prasajyate ||
children.translated_text: it would follow that the maker is non-sovereign, perishable, and so forth.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: So they say.

children.text: syād eṣa sarvadoṣāvakāśo yady asmābhir asarvaviṣayam īśvarādhiṣṭhānam upagamyate yāvatā ye 'pi tu kumbhādīnāṃ kartāraḥ kulālādayas te 'pi tatpratyavekṣaṇānugṛhītaśaktayas tattatkāryanirvartanasamarthā bhavantīti brūmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This room for all these faults would exist if we accepted <s>Īśvara</s>'s superintendence as not extending to everything. But what we say is that even the makers of pots and the like, potters and others, become capable of producing their respective effects because their powers are assisted by his oversight.

children.text: nanu kutraitat dṛṣṭaṃ yat kulālatantuvāyādisadbhāve bhāvāt tadabhāve cābhāvād api ghaṭādi kāryajātam īśvarādhiṣṭhitamiti ||
children.translated_text: Objection: Where is this observed, that a class of effects such as pots, even though it exists when potters, weavers, and the like exist and is absent when they are absent, is superintended by <s>Īśvara</s>?

children.text: kutra vā na dṛṣṭaṃ kiṃ na śrutaṃ bhagavatā svayam ādiṣṭaṃ sarvajanaprasiddheṣvapi śāstreṣūdghuṣyamāṇaṃ bhavadbhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Reply: Or where is it not observed? Have you not heard it taught by the <s>Bhagavat</s> himself and proclaimed in scriptures famous among all people?

children.text: gāmāviśya ca bhūtāni dhārayāmy aham ojasā
children.translated_text: 'Entering the earth, I support beings by my power;

children.text: puṣṇāmi cauṣadhīḥ sarvāḥ somo bhūtvā rasātmakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, becoming <s>Soma</s>, whose nature is sap, I nourish all plants.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: na tadasti vinā yatsyānmayā bhūtaṃ carācaram ||
children.translated_text: 'There is no moving or unmoving being that could exist without me.'

children.text: iti śrutāv api ||
children.translated_text: And also in the śruti:

children.text: yo rudro 'gnau yo 'psu ya oṣadhīṣu yo rudro viśvā bhuvanāviveśa
children.translated_text: 'That <s>Rudra</s> who is in fire, who is in the waters, who is in the plants, that <s>Rudra</s> who has entered all the worlds,'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: thus.

children.text: ata eva bhavadudbhāvitaḥ pratītivirodho'pi nirastaḥ ajño janturanīśo'yamātmanaḥ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: For this very reason the contradiction with cognition raised by you is also refuted, since, on the contrary, such a cognition is established: 'This ignorant creature is not master over his own pleasures and pains;

children.text: īśvaraprerito gacchetsvargaṃ vā śvabhrameva vā ||
children.translated_text: impelled by <s>Īśvara</s>, he goes either to heaven or to a pit.'

children.text: ityevaṃvidhāyāḥ pratyuta pratīteḥ siddhatvāt ||
children.translated_text: because, rather, a cognition of this kind is established.

children.text: na cāyaṃ viruddho hetur viparyayavyāptyabhāvāt dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇi ghaṭādau svasādhyena buddhimatkartṛpūrvakatvena vyāpteḥ siddhatvāt buddhimatkartṛpūrvakatvavirahiṇo vipakṣād ātmāder vyāvṛttatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Nor is this reason contradictory, because there is no pervasion by the opposite. In the example-subject, the pot and the like, pervasion by its own probandum, being preceded by an intelligent maker, is established, since the reason is excluded from the dissimilar case, such as the self, which lacks being preceded by an intelligent maker.

children.text: sa viruddha ucyate yaḥ sapakṣanivṛtto'pi vipakṣameva vyāpnoti yathā nityaḥ śabdaḥ kṛtakatvāditi ||
children.translated_text: That is called contradictory which, though absent from the similar case, pervades only the dissimilar case, as in, 'Sound is eternal, because it is produced.'

children.text: buddhimatkartṛpūrvakatvaṃ ca ghaṭasya kumbhakārakāryatvāt siddhamiti kā sādhyabhraṣṭatā ||
children.translated_text: And a pot's being preceded by an intelligent maker is established from its being the work of a potter; so how is there any falling away from the probandum?

children.text: na ca sarva eva dṛṣṭāntadharmāḥ sādhyadharmiṇi kvāpyanumāne bhavanti yenānīśvaravināśyādikartṛkatvaprasaṅgaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: Nor, in any inference, do all the properties of the example occur in the subject to be proved, such that the consequence would follow that the maker is non-sovereign, perishable, and so on.

children.text: tathā hi nityaḥ śabdaḥ kṛtakatvāt ghaṭādivad ityatrāpi śabdasya kumbhakārakāryatvarauhityapārivartulyādayo ghaṭadharmāḥ kimiti na bhavantīti bhavadbhirvaktavyamiti na kiṃcidetat ||
children.translated_text: For example, even in the inference, 'Sound is eternal because it is produced, like a pot and the like,' you must explain why pot-properties such as being the work of a potter, redness, and roundness do not belong to sound. Therefore this objection is nothing at all.

children.text: nanvete kāryatvasaṃniveśādimattvādayo hetavaḥ kāryasyānekakartṛtāmapi sādhayantīti dharmisvarūpaviparītasādhanatvād viruddhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Objection: But these reasons, such as being an effect and possessing arrangement, prove that an effect may have many makers as well; therefore, because they prove the opposite of the subject's own nature, they are contradictory.

children.text: tathā ca maṇḍanaḥ
children.translated_text: And so <s>Maṇḍana</s> says:

children.text: saṃniveśādimat sarvaṃ buddhimaddhetumadyadi
children.translated_text: 'If everything possessing arrangement and the like has an intelligent cause,

children.text: prasiddhasaṃniveśāder ekakāraṇatā kutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whence comes the single-cause character of things such as the familiar arrangements?

children.text: rathādyavayavā nānātakṣanirmāpitā api
children.translated_text: The parts of chariots and the like, although made by many carpenters,

children.text: dṛśyante jagati prāya upakāryopakārakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: are commonly seen in the world as mutually assisted and assisting.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tad apyayuktaṃ rathādīnāṃ kāryāṇām anekatakṣaviracitānāmapi ekasthapatīcchānuvartanaṃ vinā niṣpattyadarśanāt ||
children.translated_text: That too is unreasonable, because products such as chariots, although fashioned by many carpenters, are not seen to come to completion without following the will of a single master-builder.

children.text: tadevaṃ kāryatvahetunā jagato buddhimatkartṛpūrvakatvasiddhau yo 'sau tattadvaicitryasampādikecchājñānakriyāśaktiyuktaḥ kartā sa ity asmadādikāryavilakṣaṇakṣityādikāryaviśeṣajanakakāraṇaviśeṣāvagamo yuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, when it is established by the reason of effecthood that the world is preceded by an intelligent maker, it is reasonable to understand a distinctive cause: that maker endowed with the powers of will, knowledge, and action that bring about each particular variety, the special producing cause of particular effects such as earth that are unlike effects made by people such as ourselves.

children.text: na caitad aprasiddhaṃ yasmādvaiśiṣṭyaṃ kāryavaiśiṣṭyād dṛṣṭaṃ lokasthitāv api lokavyavahāre'pi viśiṣṭaṃ kāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā viśiṣṭameva kāraṇam anumīyate yayā vicitrabhāvanādivastucitralepādikalākalāpasyāmukhyatāṃ madhyatvam anupamasaundaryasampadaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā tattatkarturapi tadgatavailakṣaṇyād vaiśiṣṭyamavasīyate ||
children.translated_text: And this is not unestablished, because distinctiveness is observed from distinctiveness in the effect even in ordinary worldly practice. In worldly dealings too, after seeing a distinctive effect, one infers a distinctive cause; just as, after seeing the inferiority, middling status, or incomparable beauty of a collection of arts such as variegated designs, objects, paintings, and the like, one ascertains the distinctiveness of each maker from the distinctive qualities present in those works.

children.text: ataśca ||
children.translated_text: And therefore:

children.text: Chapter 65

yat kāryaṃ dhūmādi yatheti yena prakāreṇa giriguhāgatatvena tadutsaṅgavartitayā tadaparapārśvavartitvena copalabdhaṃ yādṛśaṃ ca tārṇapārṇādinā svarūpeṇa viśiṣṭaṃ yāvatparimāṇaṃ tanutararekhākāram ambudanivahabahalaṃ vā tatkāraṇaṃ vahnilakṣaṇaṃ tatheti parvatotsaṅgasthaṃ vā tacchikharaniviṣṭaṃ vā tatpaścādbhāgagataṃ vā tādṛśaṃ ca tāvat pramāṇakaṃ vālpatvabahutvena yathānumīyate ||
children.translated_text: Just as, in the case of an effect such as smoke, in whatever manner it is perceived, whether as having entered a mountain cave, as being on its slope, or as being on the far side of it, and whatever its particular form, such as being made of grass, leaves, and the like, and whatever its extent, whether shaped like a very thin line or thick as a mass of clouds, its cause, namely fire, is inferred accordingly as being on the slope of the mountain, fixed on its summit, or located behind it, and as being of that kind and of that measure, whether small or abundant.

children.text: evaṃ jagallakṣaṇakāryasya tattatprakārākāravaicitryam upalabhya tattadviśeṣaviṣayaniratiśayajñānakriyāśaktiyuktaṃ kāraṇamanumīyate ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, after observing the variety of particular modes and forms in the effect characterized as the world, one infers a cause endowed with unsurpassed powers of knowledge and action concerning each of those particulars.

children.text: tac ca ||
children.translated_text: And that [cause] is as follows.

children.text: Chapter 66
yasyābhūtvā bhavanaṃ bhūtvā cābhavanaṃ tasya kālenāvacchedād anityatvam ||
children.translated_text: That which comes into being after not having existed, and ceases to be after having existed, is impermanent, because it is delimited by time.

children.text: yattu pūrvāparakoṭidvayavirahāt kālānavacchinnaṃ tan nityam ||
children.translated_text: But that which, because it lacks both a prior and a posterior limit, is not delimited by time is eternal.

children.text: kiṃ ca na tat kvacid avasthitam api tu vaitatyān mahattvād digdeśānavacchinnatvāt sarvagaṃ sarvatra tatkāryopalabdheśca vibhu tathā kramayaugapadyābhyāṃ tanukaraṇādikāryasyotpādanāt krameṇa yugapac cotpādikayā śaktyā yuktam ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, it is not situated in any particular place; rather, because of its extension, greatness, non-delimitation by direction and place, and because its effects are perceived everywhere, it is all-pervading and present everywhere. Likewise, because it produces effects such as bodies and instruments both successively and simultaneously, it is endowed with a power that produces successively and simultaneously.

children.text: nanu jagatsṛṣṭisthityādikā tatkriyā nākaraṇikā kriyātvāt chidikriyāvat atastasyāpi karaṇena bhavitavyamityāha ||
children.translated_text: Objection: The activity consisting in the creation, maintenance, and so on of the world is not without an instrument, because it is an action, like the action of cutting. Therefore he too must have an instrument. He answers this.

children.text: Chapter 67
yasmādakaraṇikā kriyā na sambhavati atastasya bhagavataḥ kimapyavaśyaṃ karaṇamasti ||
children.translated_text: Since an action without an instrument is impossible, that blessed Lord must necessarily have some instrument.

children.text: tac ca kṛtyasya sargāder anāditvenāvasthānād anāgāmi anāgantukam ||
children.translated_text: And because the task, creation and the like, exists beginninglessly, that [instrument] is not something future and not something adventitious.

children.text: atha kiṃ tatkaraṇamityucyate ||
children.translated_text: Now, what is that instrument? This is stated.

children.text: Chapter 68
śaktirevāsya viśveśituḥ karaṇaṃ tayaitatkriyāniṣpādanāt sā cec chādirūpeti vakṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The power itself of this Lord of the universe is his instrument, because this activity is accomplished through it; and that power has the form of will and the like, as we shall explain.

children.text: uktaṃ ca śrīmatkiraṇe ||
children.translated_text: And it is said in the venerable <s>Kiraṇa</s>:

children.text: icchaiva karaṇaṃ tasya yathā sadyogino matā
children.translated_text: Will alone is considered his instrument, as in the case of a true yogin,

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: thus.

children.text: śaktiśca cetanarūpā nahi citsvabhāvasyācidrūpā śaktirbhavati ||
children.translated_text: And power is conscious in nature; for one whose own nature is consciousness does not have a power that is unconscious in form.

children.text: yac caitac chaktyātmakaṃ karaṇam ||
children.translated_text: And this instrument, whose essence is power, is such:

children.text: Chapter 69
yasya jñeyānāṃ karaṇīyānāṃ cānantyaṃ tasya karaṇair apyanantair bhavitavyam ||
children.translated_text: One whose objects to be known and tasks to be done are infinite must also have infinite instruments.

children.text: aparimitaviṣayaṃ ca parameśvarasya jñānaṃ kṛtyaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: And the knowledge and task of <s>Parameśvara</s> have limitless objects.

children.text: yad vakṣyati
children.translated_text: As he will say:

children.text: śāṃkaram jñānam ||
children.translated_text: the knowledge belonging to <s>Śaṅkara</s>,

children.text: iti prakramya
children.translated_text: having begun in this way,

children.text: tad ekaṃ viṣayānantyād bhedānantyaṃ prapadyate
children.translated_text: that one [knowledge], because of the infinity of its objects, comes to possess infinite differentiation;

children.text: kartṛtvaṃ tadabhinnatvāt tadvad evopacārataḥ ||
children.translated_text: agency, because it is not different from that, is likewise [infinitely differentiated], by figurative usage.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tasmādviṣayasya jñeyasya karaṇīyasya cāniyatatvād anavacchinnatvād ekamapi tacchaktirūpaṃ karaṇaṃ bodhaviṣaye kṛtyaviṣaye ca tathetyanavacchinnam anantam evetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, because the object to be known and the task to be done are indefinite and unbounded, that single instrument whose form is power is, in the same way, unbounded in the sphere of cognition and in the sphere of action; the meaning is that it is indeed infinite.

children.text: atha matāntaraniranubhāṣaṇeneśvarāstitvam eva draḍhayati ||
children.translated_text: Now, by rehearsing and refuting other doctrines, he strengthens the very existence of the Lord.

children.text: Chapter 70
nanu kimatra karaṇāpekṣeṇeśvareṇa kalpitena tasmin karmanairapekṣyeṇa kartṛtvānabhyupagamāt taccaritāni karmāṇyeva sṛṣṭisthityādikāraṇatayā bhavantviti jaiminīyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Objection, according to the <s>Jaiminīya</s>s: Why posit a Lord here in connection with the need for an instrument? Since agency is not admitted in him as independent of karma, let the karmas performed by them alone be the causes of creation, maintenance, and so on.

children.text: yadāhuḥ
children.translated_text: For they say:

children.text: kasyaciddhetumātrasya yadyadhiṣṭhātṛteṣyate
children.translated_text: If superintendence is desired for some mere cause,

children.text: karmabhiḥ sarvajīvānāṃ tatsiddheḥ siddhasādhanam ||
children.translated_text: then, since that is established by the karmas of all living beings, it is proving what is already proved.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: yadvā bījam ivāṅkurādīnāṃ kalādikāryāṇām upādānaṃ māyaivānyānapekṣiṇī sṛṣṭyādikṛd bhavatu prakṛtireva vāvyaktā etatkartṛtve nāstu yāṃ vinā tasyeśvarasyāpi tatkāryāniṣpattir upalabhyate kṣityādyātmanā pārārthyapravṛttā anyānapekṣiṇī prakṛtireva ataḥ kim īśvareṇeti kāpilāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or else, just as a seed is the material cause of sprouts and the like, let <s>māyā</s> alone, independent of anything else, be the material cause of effects such as the <s>kalā</s>s and the maker of creation and the like; or let unmanifest <s>prakṛti</s> itself be the agent of this. There need be no Lord, since without [prakṛti] even his, the Lord's, accomplishment of those effects is not observed. <s>Prakṛti</s> alone, proceeding for the sake of another in the form of earth and the like and depending on nothing else, should suffice; therefore what need is there of a Lord? So say the <s>Kāpila</s>s.

children.text: tathā hi
children.translated_text: For thus:

children.text: yad yathā pariṇāmaikasvabhāvaṃ tatra tat tataḥ
children.translated_text: Where something has transformation in such-and-such a way as its sole nature, in that case that [effect] arises from that [cause],

children.text: anyānapekṣi bījādisāmagrī yadvad aṅkure ||
children.translated_text: independent of anything else, just as the aggregate beginning with the seed does in the case of a sprout.

children.text: mahadādivikāraughapariṇāmasvabhāvakam
children.translated_text: And <s>pradhāna</s>, whose nature is transformation into the mass of evolutes beginning with <s>mahat</s>,

children.text: triguṇātma pradhānaṃ ca tena sāṃkhyam anīśvaram ||
children.translated_text: is constituted by the three <s>guṇa</s>s; therefore the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> system is without a Lord.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: yadi vā puruṣa evedaṃ sarvaṃ yadbhūtaṃ yac ca bhavyam ||
children.translated_text: Or else, '<s>puruṣa</s> alone is all this, whatever has been and whatever will be';

children.text: iti aṇoḥ puruṣād eva vivartatayā cidacillakṣaṇaviśvaprādurbhāvādi bhaviṣyati kimīśvareṇeti ||
children.translated_text: thus, from the minute <s>puruṣa</s> alone, through apparent transformation, there will be the manifestation and so forth of the universe characterized by conscious and unconscious entities. What need is there of a Lord?

children.text: tadasad bahirbījabhūtānāṃ karmaṇāṃ māyādīnāṃ cācetanānāṃ buddhimadadhiṣṭhitānāṃ sṛṣṭyādi kṛtyam upapannam ityuktatvāt ||
children.translated_text: That is unsound, because it has been said that acts such as creation are intelligible for unconscious things such as karmas, <s>māyā</s>, and the rest, which serve as external seed-causes, only when they are superintended by an intelligent being.

children.text: prakṛterapyautsukyanivṛttyarthaṃ kāryeṣu pravṛttir nitarāmayuktā tasyā ācaitanyād autsukyasya ca cetanadharmatvāt ||
children.translated_text: It is still more unreasonable that <s>prakṛti</s> should act with respect to effects for the sake of removing eagerness, because it is unconscious and because eagerness is a property of consciousness.

children.text: puruṣasyāpi pariṇāmitvādyanekadoṣopanipātāt svatantrasya cābhirucitahāner aniṣṭopanipātasya cānupapatter asvavaśatvāt sthitijanmapralayakartṛtvanirāse sati pāriśeṣyān maheśvarasyaivaitat sthitijanmādi kāryamiti pāriśeṣyānumānam anavadyamiti gamakametat ||
