children.translated_text: And for <s>puruṣa</s> too, since many faults would follow, such as being subject to transformation, and since for an independent being the loss of what he desires and the occurrence of what he does not desire are not intelligible, because that would mean he was not under his own control, once agency in maintenance, birth, and dissolution has been ruled out [for those alternatives], by elimination this effect, maintenance, birth, and the like, belongs to <s>Maheśvara</s> alone. Thus this inference by elimination is faultless; this is the proof.

children.text: idamidānīṃ vivicyate yadi tāvat parameśvaraḥ kāruṇyāt saṃsārijanojjihīrṣayā jagatāṃ sthitijanmādau pravartate tatkimarthaṃ pratyuta sāṃsārikeṣu duḥkheṣu varākānimān prāṇino niyojayati atha tasyaivaṃvidha eva svabhāvaḥ tanmuktamapi jantuṃ kiṃ na saṃsārayatītyāha muktasya śiva eva saḥ satyaṃ kāruṇyādeva bhagavān prāṇino'nugrahītuṃ pravartate ||
children.translated_text: This is now being examined. If, first, the Supreme Lord acts out of compassion, wishing to lift up transmigrating beings, in the maintenance, birth, and so on of the worlds, then for what purpose does he, on the contrary, place these poor creatures in worldly sufferings? If that alone is his nature, then why does he not make even a liberated being transmigrate? He answers: For one who is liberated, he is <s>Śiva</s> himself. True: the Lord acts out of compassion alone in order to favor living beings.

children.text: yattu duḥkhamohādinā nirayādyupabhogena vā tān saṃyojayati tannijakarmānurūpyavaśāt ||
children.translated_text: But the suffering, delusion, and so on, or the experience of hell and the like, with which he connects them, occurs because of conformity to their own <s>karma</s>.

children.text: na ca karmāpekṣitayeśvarasya svātantryahānir ityāśaṅkanīyaṃ karaṇāpekṣayā kartuḥ svātantryavyāghātādarśanāt bhāṇḍāgārikāpekṣasya rājñaḥ prasādādidānavat ||
children.translated_text: Nor should one suspect that the Lord loses his independence because he has regard for <s>karma</s>, since no impairment of an agent's independence is seen when he depends on instruments, as when a king who depends on a treasurer gives favors and gifts.

children.text: yaduktaṃ siddhagurubhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: As has been said by the perfected teachers:

children.text: svatantrānyāprayojyatvaṃ karaṇādiprayoktṛtā
children.translated_text: Not being set in motion by another independent being, and being the mover of instruments and the like:

children.text: kartuḥ svātantryametaddhi na karmādyanapekṣitā ||
children.translated_text: this indeed is the agent's independence, not non-dependence on <s>karma</s> and the rest.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: na cābhuktasya karmaṇaḥ kṣayo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: And there is no destruction of <s>karma</s> that has not been experienced.

children.text: tattadyoniśarīropabhogabhuktavicitrakarmakṣayatas tatsāmyād vā atyutkaṭamalaparipākavaśapravṛttaśaktipātāpasāritamalasyāvāptānugrahasya jantor nirastasamastapāśatvād āvirbhūtasarvārthatattvakartṛkasya muktātmanaḥ saṃsāryatāhetoḥ paśutvasyābhāvāc chivasvarūpa eva bhagavān bhavati na tu paśorivāsya kutsitabhavabhogopabhogahetur bhavatīti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Through the exhaustion of the manifold <s>karma</s>s experienced by undergoing the experiences belonging to bodies in each respective womb, or through the equalization of those <s>karma</s>s, and because <s>mala</s> has been removed by a <s>śaktipāta</s> (descent of power) proceeding from the ripening of an extremely intense <s>mala</s>, the being has received grace. Since all his <s>pāśa</s>s (bonds) have been destroyed, since omniscience and agency with regard to all realities have become manifest, and since <s>paśutva</s> (the state of a bound soul), the cause of transmigration, is absent, the liberated self simply becomes the Lord whose nature is <s>Śiva</s>. He does not become, as in the case of a bound soul, the cause of its experiencing the enjoyments of a wretched existence; this is the sense.

children.text: punar apīśvarakartṛkatvam eva jagato ghaṭayitum anumānaṃ pratisamādhātum ākṣipati ||
children.translated_text: Again, in order to establish that the world has the Lord as its maker, he raises an objection so as to settle the inference.

children.text: Chapter 71

nanv asya sthitijanmādeḥ kāryasyāvinābhāvalakṣaṇasambandho yadi kadācij jagatkartrā saha kenacidapi gṛhītaḥ syāt tadaitad anumānaṃ sidhyet sambandhasyaiva tu agrahaṇāt kathaṃ nāsya bādheti yadi kasyacin mataṃ syāt tadidam apyasau pratyanuyojya ityāha ||
children.translated_text: Now, if the relation, characterized by invariable concomitance, of this effect consisting of maintenance, birth, and the like with some maker of the world had ever been apprehended by anyone, then this inference would be established. But since the relation itself has not been apprehended, how is there no defeat of it? If this should be someone's view, that very person too is to be counter-questioned; so he says:

children.text: Chapter 72
saiṣā bādhā sarvasyāpy anumānavādinaḥ prasaktā ||
children.translated_text: This defeat would apply to every proponent of inference.

children.text: tathā hi mahānasādigatānāṃ viśiṣṭadeśakālākārāṇām eva dhūmāgnivyaktīnāṃ sambandhagrahaṇe dhūmamātrāc ca parvatādau vahnimātrānumānam ityagṛhītasambandhaiva dhūmavyaktiḥ kathaṃ tathāvidhavahnivyaktiṃ gamayediti sambandhagrahaparyanuyogaḥ samānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For example, when the relation of individual smokes and fires in kitchens and the like, each marked by particular place, time, and form, has been apprehended, and yet fire in general is inferred from smoke in general on a mountain and so forth, how can an individual smoke whose relation has not been apprehended indicate such an individual fire? The demand that the relation be apprehended is the same.

children.text: tataśca
children.translated_text: And therefore:

children.text: yatra syād ubhayordoṣaḥ parihāraśca vā samaḥ
children.translated_text: Where there would be a fault common to both parties, and the remedy too would be the same,

children.text: naikaḥ paryanuyoktavyas tādṛgarthaviniścaye ||
children.translated_text: one side alone should not be pressed with a counter-question in deciding such a matter.

children.text: iti naitad asmākameva codyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus this objection is not directed at us alone.

children.text: atha dhūmamātrasyaiva vahnimātrāvinābhāvalakṣaṇaḥ sambandho gṛhītaḥ tad ihāpi kāryamātrāt kartṛmātrānumānamaduṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: But if the relation characterized by invariable concomitance of smoke in general with fire in general has been apprehended, then here too the inference from effect in general to maker in general is free from fault.

children.text: anyathā sarvānumānoccheda eva syāt ||
children.translated_text: Otherwise there would be the abolition of all inference.

children.text: taduktam
children.translated_text: That has been said:

children.text: sādhyasādhanasāmānyenāvinābhāvaniścayāt
children.translated_text: Because invariable concomitance is determined through the generality of what is to be proved and what proves it,

children.text: pravṛttiranumānasya tadabhāvas tadanyathā ||
children.translated_text: inference proceeds; if that were otherwise, inference would be absent.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: itthaṃ ca vicitratattatkarmāśayādhivāsitabhoktṛbhogatatsādhanatadupādānādiviśeṣajñaḥ kartā anumānāntareṇānumīyata iti na kaściddoṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And in this way, by another inference, a maker is inferred who knows the specific details of enjoyers, enjoyments, their means, their material causes, and so on, all conditioned by the various deposits of <s>karma</s>; so there is no fault.

children.text: tadidam uktaṃ tatrabhavadbṛhaspatipādaiḥ
children.translated_text: This was said by the venerable <s>Bṛhaspatipāda</s>:

children.text: bhavabhoktṛbhogasādhanatadupādānādi yo vijānāti
children.translated_text: He who knows worldly existence, the enjoyers, the enjoyments, their means, their material causes, and the like:

children.text: tamṛte bhaven nahīdaṃ puṃskarmāśayavipākajñam ||
children.translated_text: without him, this world, whose existence depends on knowledge of the maturation of human deposits of <s>karma</s>, would surely not be.

children.text: iti astu tarhi īśvaraḥ kartā sa tu na tāvadaśarīraḥ pratyetavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then let <s>Īśvara</s> be the maker. But he is certainly not to be understood as bodiless,

children.text: kāryaṃ śarīrayuktena kartrā vyāptaṃ sadaiva yat ||
children.translated_text: because an effect is always pervaded by a maker endowed with a body,

children.text: ityādinā dehavirahiṇaḥ kartṛtvāyogasyoktatvāt ||
children.translated_text: and by such statements the impossibility of agency for one devoid of a body has been stated.

children.text: tathāhi ||
children.translated_text: For so it is:

children.text: Chapter 73
ghaṭapaṭādi kāryaṃ śarīravataiva kriyamāṇaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ nāśarīreṇeti ||
children.translated_text: An effect such as a pot or a cloth is seen to be produced only by one possessing a body, not by one without a body.

children.text: kiṃcātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And what follows from this?

children.text: Chapter 74
evaṃ ca sati asmadādivatkleśādiyukto'sarvajñaḥ parimitaśaktir deśādyavacchinnaḥ so 'pīśvaraḥ śarīritvāt prāpnotīti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In that case, because he would possess a body, that <s>Īśvara</s> too, like ourselves and others, would turn out to be connected with afflictions and the like, not omniscient, limited in power, and bounded by place and so forth. This is the prima facie view.

children.text: siddhāntastu ||
children.translated_text: But the established conclusion is as follows:

children.text: Chapter 75
aśarīrasyāpi tāvat svadehaspandādau kartṛtvaṃ dṛṣṭamiti ||
children.translated_text: To begin with, agency is observed even for the bodiless self in the motion of its own body and the like.

children.text: kāryaṃ śarīrayuktena kartrā vyāptam ity uktam abhyupagamyāpi brūmaḥ śarīravattve'pi bhagavato na prāguktadoṣaprasaṅgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even while accepting the statement that an effect is pervaded by a maker endowed with a body, we say: even if the Lord possesses a body, the faults stated earlier do not follow.

children.text: kuta ityāha mūlādyasaṃbhavād iti mūlaṃ malaḥ sarvānarthamūlatvāt avidyāvṛtirugglānipāpamūlakṣayādibhiḥ paryāyair vakṣyamāṇatvāc ca ādigrahaṇāt karmāṇi rodhaśaktiśca tadasaṃbhavāt ||
children.translated_text: Why? He says: because the root and so on are impossible. The root is <s>mala</s>, because it is the root of all misfortune, and because it will be described by synonymous terms such as ignorance, covering, sickness, weariness, sin, root, and decay. By the word 'and so on' are included <s>karma</s>s and the power of obstruction; because these are impossible in him.

children.text: na hi parameśvarasya malakarmādi pāśajālaṃ sambhavati yannimittaṃ prākṛtaṃ vapuḥ kalpyate api tu śāktamiti śaktisvarūpaiḥ sadyojātādibhiḥ pañcabhirmantraiḥ svecchāvinirmitamaparimitasāmarthyam adigdeśakālākāravyavacchinnam anupamamahima taccharīraṃ na tv asmadādiśarīrasadṛśam ||
children.translated_text: For in the Supreme Lord there is no net of bonds such as <s>mala</s> and <s>karma</s> on account of which a material body would be imagined. Rather, his body is <s>śākta</s> (made of power): created by his own will from the five mantras, <s>Sadyojāta</s> and the others, whose nature is power; endowed with limitless capacity; not delimited by direction, place, time, or form; and of incomparable greatness. It is not like the bodies of ourselves and others.

children.text: ata eva hi ||
children.translated_text: Precisely for this reason:

children.text: Chapter 76
yathākramam anugrahatirobhāvādānarakṣaṇotpattilakṣaṇakṛtyapañcake 'vaśyam upayogo yeṣāṃ tair īśānādibhiḥ pañcabhir mantraistat mūrdhādi vapuḥ devasyocyate ityadhyāhāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: It should be supplied as follows: those five <s>mantra</s>s beginning with <s>Īśāna</s>, whose use is necessarily required in the five functions characterized respectively by grace, concealment, withdrawal, protection, and production, are said to be the god's body, beginning with the head.

children.text: varaiḥpuṣṇāti dhyāyinaḥ iti vapuḥśabdasyānvarthatā bhaktānugrahaṇāya tattadākāragrahaṇasyāgameṣūpadiṣṭatvāt ||
children.translated_text: The word 'body' is meaningful because it nourishes meditators with boons, since the taking on of each particular form for the grace of devotees is taught in the <s>āgama</s>s.

children.text: tathā coktaṃ śrīmatpauṣkare
children.translated_text: And so it is said in the venerable <s>Pauṣkara</s>:

children.text: sādhakasya tu lakṣyārthaṃ tasya rūpamidaṃ smṛtam iti ||
children.translated_text: 'But this form of his is remembered for the sake of the practitioner's object of meditation.'

children.text: atha kathaṃ bhagavata īśānamūrdhatvam ityāha ||
children.translated_text: Now he says how the Blessed One has <s>Īśāna</s> as his head.

children.text: Chapter 77

yena guṇena mantreṇa sarvasroto'nusrotasā mūrdhvasthitatvāt sarvānugrahahetutvādvā uparivartinā jagaccidacidātmakaṃ viśvamīṣṭe sa uttamāṅgavat sarvordhvasthitatvān mūrdheva mūrdhā na paramārthato dehāvayavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The quality, the <s>mantra</s>, by which, moving above as it follows every stream, or because it is situated above and is the cause of grace to all, he rules the world, the whole universe made of conscious and unconscious, is the head: like the chief limb, it is as it were a head because it is situated above all, but it is not, in the ultimate sense, a bodily member.

children.text: tatpuruṣavaktraṃ vyācaṣṭe ||
children.translated_text: He explains the <s>Tatpuruṣa</s> face.

children.text: Chapter 78
tasya tasya amaranarāderyā pūḥ purī tanustasyāṃ puri yajamānasvarūpeṇādhiṣṭhānabhāvenoṣitas tatpuruṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is <s>Tatpuruṣa</s> because he dwells in each city, that is, in the body belonging to each god, human, and so on, in the form of the sacrificer and as the indwelling foundation.

children.text: taduktam ||
children.translated_text: This has been stated:

children.text: svātmaivāyaṃ vasati sakalaprāṇinām īśvaro'ntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'This Lord himself, as one's own self, dwells within all living beings.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tatpuruṣa iti yasmād vyanakti jñānakriye trāyate janmādibhayāt tatastatpuruṣavaktraḥ vyañjanatrāṇarūpatvād vaktram ityabhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: Because as <s>Tatpuruṣa</s> he manifests knowledge and action and protects from the fear of birth and the like, he therefore has the <s>Tatpuruṣa</s> face; it is called a face because it has the nature of manifestation and protection.

children.text: iti śruteḥ ||
children.translated_text: So says the śruti.

children.text: aghorahṛdayatvaṃ vaktum āha ||
children.translated_text: To state his being <s>Aghora</s> as heart, he says:

children.text: Chapter 79
hṛdayamāśayo bodha iti paryāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Heart,' 'seat,' and 'cognition' are synonyms.

children.text: śivo bodho yasmād bhagavatas tasmādaghorahṛdayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since the Blessed One is auspicious cognition, he therefore has <s>Aghora</s> as heart.

children.text: nanu ghoram aśreyorūpaṃ yaducyate tadghorarūpatā kathaṃ devasyetyāha parigrahasya ghoratvād iti ||
children.translated_text: Objection: What is called <s>ghora</s>, terrible, has the form of what is inauspicious; how can such terribleness belong to the deity? He answers: because the retinue is terrible.

children.text: yeyaṃ parameśvarasya ghorarūpoktiḥ sā na vāstavī kiṃtu parigrahasya svaśaktyuttejitasāmarthyasyāśuddhādhvādhikārinikurambasya ghoratvād ghoraśaktirdeva upacārāducyate ||
children.translated_text: This statement that the Supreme Lord has a terrible form is not literal. Rather, because the retinue, the mass of authorities over the impure path whose capacities are stimulated by his own power, is terrible, the god is figuratively called one whose power is terrible.

children.text: tathā coktam
children.translated_text: And so it has been said:

children.text: viṣayeṣveva saṃlīnān adho'dhaḥ pātayanty aṇūn
children.translated_text: 'Those powers which, embracing the atomic souls completely absorbed in sense objects, cast them lower and lower,

children.text: rudrāṇūn yāḥ samāliṅgya ghorataryo 'parāstu tāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and those other, more terrible powers which embrace the <s>Rudra</s>-souls, are these.'

children.text: vāmadevaguhyatvam abhidhatte ||
children.translated_text: He explains <s>Vāmadeva</s> as the secret.

children.text: Chapter 80
dharmārthakāmalakṣaṇena trivargeṇa pralobhya vamati adho nikṣipatīti vāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is <s>Vāma</s> because, having enticed beings with the <s>trivarga</s> (three aims) characterized by <s>dharma</s> (normative order), <s>artha</s> (material aim), and <s>kāma</s> (desire), he vomits them out, that is, casts them downward.

children.text: svabhāvena rahasyo guhyo bhāvaḥ kathyate ||
children.translated_text: A state that is hidden by nature is called <s>guhya</s>, secret.

children.text: itthaṃ pṛthag anayoḥ padayorarthaṃ pradarśya vigrahaṃ karoti vāmaṃ dhāmeti ||
children.translated_text: Having shown the meanings of these two words separately in this way, he forms the compound: 'the <s>Vāma</s> radiance.'

children.text: diverdhātor dyutyarthatvād devaśabdena tejo'bhimatam ||
children.translated_text: Since the root div has the meaning 'to shine,' radiance is intended by the word <s>deva</s>.

children.text: tena vāmam adhastane'dhvani vamanaśīlaṃ yattejas tadguhyam aprakaṭamasyeti vāmadevaguhyaḥ parameśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus the Supreme Lord is <s>Vāmadevaguhya</s>: the radiance that has the habit of casting downward in the lower path is his secret, unmanifest aspect.

children.text: Chapter 81
patyuricchayā hi karmaprakṣayāya kṣipram evātmanāṃ tāstā mūrtayo jātā iti sadyojātamūrtir devaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the Lord's will, those forms were born at once for the exhaustion of the souls' karma; therefore the god has the <s>Sadyojāta</s> form.

children.text: yadvakṣyati dīkṣāprakaraṇe
children.translated_text: As he will say in the section on initiation:

children.text: sadyena janayetsadyo nānāniṣpannavigraham
children.translated_text: 'By the <s>Sadya</s> he should immediately generate a body manifested in many forms.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: yadvā yogināṃ tattatsamādhibhājāṃ sadyastatkṣaṇaṃ mūrtīrvidhatte proktavanmantramayasvamūrtisadṛśīṃ tanuṃ sampādayatīti acirāt svaramatābhivyañjakatvāt sadyomūrtitvaṃ na tu śīghrasaṃjātasvadehatvād ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or, for yogins who have attained their respective <s>samādhi</s>s, he fashions forms immediately, at that very instant; as stated, he produces a body similar to his own <s>mantra</s>-made form. The meaning is that his being immediately formed is due to his manifesting his own intention without delay, not because his own body has been quickly born.

children.text: etadeva draḍhayati ||
children.translated_text: He confirms this very point.

children.text: Chapter 82
paramārthataḥ parameśvarasyāśarīratvāc chaktireva dehakāryaṃ kurvatī dehākhyayoktā ||
children.translated_text: In ultimate reality, because the Supreme Lord is bodiless, it is power alone, performing the function of a body, that is spoken of by the name 'body.'

children.text: tasyāścaikasyā api kṛtyabhedād vāmādibhedabhinnatvam ||
children.translated_text: And although that power is single, it is differentiated into distinctions such as <s>Vāmā</s> because its functions differ.

children.text: yathā vahniśakter dāhyaprakāśyārthaviṣaye dāhaprakāśaprakaraṇād gauṇam anekatvaṃ vastuta ekatvāt tasyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Just as the power of fire, with respect to objects to be burned and illuminated, has a figurative multiplicity because of the procedures of burning and illuminating, though in reality that power is one.

children.text: Chapter 83
ittham ityanenoktaprakāreṇa mantrātmako vigraho yasya sa bhagavān itthaṃvigrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the manner stated by the word 'thus,' the Blessed One whose form is <s>mantra</s>-made is one whose form is thus.

children.text: aneneti
children.translated_text: 'By this' means:

children.text: karaṇaṃ ca na śaktyanyat ||
children.translated_text: 'And the instrument is nothing other than power.'

children.text: iti prāguktenātmanā apratihatasāmarthyena karaṇena sthityādikāryajātaṃ sarvakālaṃ sarvaṃ nirvartayati ||
children.translated_text: By the previously stated self, the instrument whose capacity is unobstructed, he accomplishes the whole class of works, such as maintenance, at all times and in every way.

children.text: na paraṃ yugapatkaroti yāvadyadā yadupapadyate tattadā karoti krameṇāpi sarvaṃ kāryaṃ karotītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He does not, however, do them simultaneously; rather, whatever is possible whenever, he does then. The meaning is that he performs every work even in sequence.

children.text: taduktaṃ prāk
children.translated_text: As was said earlier:

children.text: kramākramasamutpatteḥ kramādyutpattiśaktimat ||
children.translated_text: 'Because ordered and unordered productions arise, it possesses the power of producing sequence and the rest.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: atha prathamataḥ parameśvaraḥ kiṃ karotītyāha ||
children.translated_text: Now, what does the Supreme Lord do first? He says:

children.text: Chapter 84
tatrety evaṃ sthite sati ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'There' means: when the situation is thus.

children.text: ekasyā eva śakter vāmādikṛtyavaśād vāmādibhedabhinnatvam ityuktam ||
children.translated_text: It has been said that the one power itself is differentiated into distinctions such as <s>Vāmā</s> because of the functions such as <s>Vāmā</s>.

children.text: sā ca śaktiḥ sarvajñānakriyārūpā śivavat sarvāṇūnāṃ vidyata eva teṣāṃ cānādyavidyāruddhatvāc chivānugrahaṃ vinā na tatsamānā bhavatīti prakṣīṇakārmamāyīyabandhānāṃ vijñānakevalānām añjanaparipākādyanusāreṇa tatpadayogyānām aṣṭakaṃ mantrakoṭisaptakaparivāraṃ vāmādiśaktinavakayuktaṃ ca karoti ||
children.translated_text: And that power, whose nature is all knowledge and action, exists indeed in all atomic souls, just as in <s>Śiva</s>; but because they are obstructed by beginningless ignorance, it does not become equal to his without the grace of <s>Śiva</s>. Therefore, according to the ripening of their <s>añjana</s> and so on, he makes the <s>vijñānakevala</s>s whose karmic and māyic bonds have been exhausted and who are fit for that station into an octad, attended by a retinue of seven crores of <s>mantra</s>s and endowed with the nine powers beginning with <s>Vāmā</s>.

children.text: anyeṣāmapi saptakoṭisaṃkhyātānāṃ mantrāṇām ananteśādaya evāṣṭāv īśitāra iti vaktumārabhate ||
children.translated_text: He begins to state that <s>Ananteśa</s> and the others are the eight lords even of the other <s>mantra</s>s, whose number is seven crores.

children.text: Chapter 85
rājāno lokeśā indrādayaḥ teṣāṃ rājānaḥ śatarudrāḥ tadīśvarāṇāṃ maṇḍaliprabhṛtīnāmapyeta īśvarāḥ prabhavaḥ vidyāmaheśvarā iti yāvat ||
children.translated_text: The kings are the world-lords, <s>Indra</s> and the others; their kings are the hundred <s>Rudra</s>s. And over those lords, beginning with the <s>Maṇḍalins</s>, these lords are the sources of power, that is to say, the <s>Vidyāmaheśvaras</s>.

children.text: ete ca ||
children.translated_text: And these also:

children.text: Chapter 86
adhikāramalāṃśāvaśeṣāt kiṃcidanavāptaparameśvarasāmyā ityasyaite preryāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because only a remnant portion of the impurity belonging to their office remains, they have not quite attained equality with the Supreme Lord. These are the ones impelled by him.

children.text: athaiṣāmaṣṭānāmapi sarvajñatvasarvakartṛtvasambhavāt kiṃsvid abhinnarūpatvamuta kaścidviśeṣa ityāha ||
children.translated_text: Now, since omniscience and universal agency are possible for all eight of these, is their nature perhaps undifferentiated, or is there some distinction? He states this.

children.text: Chapter 87

yadyapi sarve sarvārthadṛkkriyāḥ tathāpyekaikasya svasvādhovartino niyojyā iti preryatālakṣaṇamalāṃśāvaśeṣād adho'vasthitānām eṣām ūrdhvasthamavekṣya kalayā kartṛtvasya nyūnatvamiti parasparaviśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Although all have knowledge and agency with regard to all objects, nevertheless each one has as his appointees those below him. Therefore, because of the remnant portion of <s>mala</s> characterized by being impellable, these who stand below, when considered in relation to the one above, have a deficiency of agency by one <s>kalā</s>; this is their mutual distinction.

children.text: taduktam
children.translated_text: That has been said:

children.text: yo hi yasmādguṇotkṛṣṭaḥ sa tasmād ūrdhvam iṣyate
children.translated_text: For whoever is superior to another in qualities is held to be above him.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: na kevalameta eva viśiṣyante yāvat tadadhovartino mantrā apyevameva parasparaviśeṣabhājaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Not only these alone are distinguished; rather, the <s>mantra</s>s who stand below them also possess mutual distinctions in just this same way.

children.text: tāneva mantrān viśinaṣṭi ||
children.translated_text: He specifies those very <s>mantra</s>s.

children.text: Chapter 88
te ca mantrāḥ parāparamantreśvaravyaktayā śivaśaktyā vyāpāritā yogyatānurūpyeṇa kadācitkeṣāṃcidanugrahaṃ kurvanti na tu yogyatānapekṣam atiprasaṅgāt ||
children.translated_text: And those <s>mantra</s>s, set in operation by the power of <s>Śiva</s> manifest as the higher and lower <s>Mantreśvara</s>, sometimes bestow grace on certain persons in accordance with their fitness, but not without regard to fitness, since that would lead to overextension.

children.text: Chapter 89

teṣāṃ saptakoṭisaṃkhyātānāṃ mantrāṇāmardhaṃ prayoktṝṇām anugrahītṝṇāṃ dehaṃ śarīram āśrayatvenāpekṣamāṇam īśvaramapekṣata iti tatsāpekṣam ācāryādhikaraṇeśvarāpekṣam akhile māyīye'dhvani svamadhikāram anugrāhyānugrahalakṣaṇaṃ nirvartya sthitikālasyānte māyīyasyādhvano'pyuparamasamaye seśvaramiti mantreśvaraiḥ sahitaṃ śivasāyujyaṃ gacchati ||
children.translated_text: Of those <s>mantra</s>s, whose number is seven crores, half requires as its support a body, the body of officiants who bestow grace, and depends on an <s>Īśvara</s>; therefore it is dependent on that, namely dependent on the <s>Īśvara</s> who is the authority of the teacher. Having fulfilled its own office throughout the whole <s>māyīya adhvan</s>, characterized as bestowing grace on those to be graced, at the end of the period of maintenance, when the <s>māyīya adhvan</s> too ceases, that half goes, together with its <s>Īśvara</s> and along with the <s>Mantreśvara</s>s, to union with <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: aparasyārdhasya kā vārttetyāha ||
children.translated_text: What is the case with the other half? He says.

children.text: Chapter 90

anyad aparam ardhamīśeṣṭamiti yatra yatra parameśvarasyānugrahecchā tatra tatra tadicchayaiva vinādhikaraṇenety ācāryalakṣaṇam adhikaraṇam anapekṣyaiva pradhānā cāsau vikṛtiśceti pradhānavikṛtiḥ śuddhavidyā asyā adhaḥ sarvatra māyīye cādhvani svamadhikāraṃ kṛtvā svasyādhvano'nugrahamārgasya saṃhṛtau samāptau apaiti apavṛjyate ||
children.translated_text: The other, remaining half is held to be desired by the Lord. Wherever the Supreme Lord has the wish to bestow grace, there, by that wish alone and without an authority, that is, without depending on the authority characterized as a teacher, it performs its own office everywhere below <s>Śuddhavidyā</s>, the principal evolute, and also in the <s>māyīya adhvan</s>. When its own path, the path of grace, is withdrawn and completed, it departs, that is, it is released.

children.text: taduktaṃ tatrabhavadbhiḥ sadyojyotiḥpādaiḥ
children.translated_text: That has been said there by the venerable <s>Sadyojyotis</s>pāda:

children.text: jagati kṛte tatrārdhaṃ mantrāṇāṃ śivasamāhṛtān puṃsaḥ
children.translated_text: When the world has been made, there half of the <s>mantra</s>s, [approaching] the souls gathered by <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: anugṛhya yāti hi vinā daiśikamūrtiṃ prayuktamīśena ||
children.translated_text: having bestowed grace on them, departs, employed by the Lord without the form of a teacher.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: itthaṃ mantrānuktvā mantreśvarānvaktum āha ||
children.translated_text: Having spoken in this way about the <s>mantra</s>s, he says this in order to speak about the <s>Mantreśvara</s>s.

children.text: Chapter 91
tac ca sātmakamākramya viśramāyāvatiṣṭhate ||
children.translated_text: And having occupied that which contains selves, it remains until repose.

children.text: iti antarviśrāntāṇusaṃghātaṃ māyātattvaṃ vakṣyamāṇaṃ tasmād granthitattvatas tadgarbhādhikāriṇāṃ kalādyārabdhaśarīrāṇāṃ maṇḍalyādīnāṃ patīnāmaṣṭādaśādhikaṃ śatam ananteśādyabhivyaktaḥ parameśvaraḥ karoti kalādyārabdhadehatvam eṣāṃ karotītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This means: from the <s>māyātattva</s> to be described, which is an aggregate of souls resting within it, and according to the principle stated in the treatise, the Supreme Lord, manifest as <s>Ananteśa</s> and the others, produces one hundred and eighteen lords beginning with the <s>Maṇḍalins</s>, who hold office within its womb and whose bodies begin with <s>kalā</s> and the rest. The meaning is that he gives them bodies beginning with <s>kalā</s> and the rest.

children.text: nanu ca
children.translated_text: But, it may be objected,

children.text: aṣṭādaśādhikaṃ cānyacchataṃ māyādhikāriṇām
children.translated_text: 'And another hundred and eighteen who hold office in <s>māyā</s>,

children.text: vidyeśvarāṇām ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Vidyeśvara</s>s,'

children.text: ityādinā sākṣāt parameśvarānugṛhītatvam eṣāmuktam iha tv anantādyabhivyaktasya bhagavatas tatkaraṇamucyata iti virodhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by this and the following words it has been said that these are directly graced by the Supreme Lord. But here the production of them is said to belong to the Blessed One manifest as <s>Ananta</s> and the others. Thus there is a contradiction.

children.text: naivaṃ yato'nantādīnāmeva kalādiyogakaraṇe kartṛtvaṃ natu parameśvarasya
children.translated_text: Not so, because agency in bringing about conjunction with <s>kalā</s> and the rest belongs to <s>Ananta</s> and the others themselves, not to the Supreme Lord.

children.text: śuddhe'dhvani śivaḥ kartā prokto'nanto'site prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: For scripture says, '<s>Śiva</s> is declared the agent in the pure path; <s>Ananta</s> is lord in the impure one,'

children.text: iti śruteḥ ||
children.translated_text: because of this scriptural statement.

children.text: sa tu kalādiyogino bhogabhujastān sākṣādanugṛhṇātīti na kaściddoṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But he directly bestows grace on those enjoyers who are joined with <s>kalā</s> and the rest; therefore there is no fault at all.

children.text: te 'pyanyeṣāṃ viniyoktāra ityāha ||
children.translated_text: That they too appoint others, he says.

children.text: Chapter 92
tānapi maṇḍaliprabhṛtīn aṣṭāv adhiṣṭhāya sa parameśvaro'nyānapi brahmaprabhṛtīn samalān bhuvaneśān uttejitadṛkkriyāśaktīn karotīti pūrveṇaiva sambandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having presided over those eight, beginning with the <s>Maṇḍalins</s>, that Supreme Lord also makes other world-lords beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, who still possess <s>mala</s>, into beings whose powers of knowledge and action have been stimulated; this is to be connected with the preceding statement.

children.text: kiṃvidhān ityāha yebhyaḥ sarvamidaṃ jagat sthāvarajaṅgamalakṣaṇam āvirbhavatīti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What kind of world-lords? He says: those from whom this whole world, characterized by stationary and moving beings, comes forth. This is the remainder to be supplied.

children.text: yeṣāṃ śaktiḥ karmanibandhanā karmapāśo yeṣām uparodhakatvān na nivṛttaḥ sakalānāmevaiṣāṃ parameśvarād anugraho yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Their power is bound by karma; the bond of karma has not ceased for them, because it obstructs them. For all these, who are still <s>sakala</s> beings, grace comes from the Supreme Lord.

children.text: na parametāneva karoti yāvat ||
children.translated_text: He produces not only these alone, but also:

children.text: Chapter 93

paśuśāstrāṇām ārhatasāṃkhyapāñcarātrādīnāṃ praṇetṝn arhatkapilaprabhṛtīṃs tadanuṣṭhātṝṃśca paśūn svasādhyena tattacchāstropadiṣṭena phalena tatsādhanahetubhiḥ kārakaiśca yuktān kālāgnibhuvanāntaṃ yāvatkarotīti pūrveṇaiva sambandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The construction continues from the preceding statement: he produces, as far as the world of <s>Kālāgni</s>, the founders of the <s>paśuśāstra</s>s, the scriptures of bound beings, such as the <s>Ārhata</s>, <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, and <s>Pāñcarātra</s> systems, beginning with <s>Arhat</s> and <s>Kapila</s>, and also the <s>paśu</s>s, the bound souls who practice them, endowed with the goal to be achieved by them, namely the fruit taught in each of those scriptures, and with the instruments that are causes for accomplishing it.

children.text: athaitānsṛṣṭvā devaḥ kiṃ karotītyāha ||
children.translated_text: Now, having created these, what does the god do? He says.

children.text: Chapter 94

etān kārakair bhogasādhanais tattvabhāvabhuvanādibhir yuktān svatejasā nijecchāśaktyā samyagadhiṣṭhāya svārthasiddhyartham ityātmīyasya vyāpārasya sampattaye yadvā svairātmabhir arthyata ityartho bhogāpavargalakṣaṇaḥ puruṣārthaḥ tasya niṣpattyarthaṃ niyojayati na tūnmattavat nāpy aprayojanaṃ prayojanānuddeśena mandasyāpyapravṛtteḥ naca krīḍārthaṃ rāgādivirahiṇas tadasaṃbhavāt nāpyātmanimittaṃ paripūrṇatvāt ||
children.translated_text: After fully superintending these beings, who are furnished with causal instruments and with means of experience such as tattvas, states, and worlds, by his own radiance, namely by his own power of will, he appoints them for the accomplishment of their own goal. That is, he does so for the fulfillment of his own activity; or, the meaning is that he appoints them for the realization of the human aim, characterized by enjoyment and liberation, which is desired by the selves themselves. He does not act like a madman, nor without a purpose, since even a dull person does not act without intending a purpose; nor for play, since that is impossible for one free from passion and the like; nor for his own sake, because he is complete.

children.text: bhūtaiḥ prāṇibhiravidyāvaśādaviditataddṛkkriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here 'beings' means living creatures, for whom, because they are under the sway of ignorance, his seeing and action are not known.

children.text: tadiyatā sṛṣṭisthitī uktvā saṃhāraṃ vaktum āha ||
children.translated_text: Having thus stated creation and maintenance, he says the following in order to describe dissolution.

children.text: Chapter 95

ityante bhogasādhanaṃ tanukaraṇabhuvanādi upasaṃhṛtya kāraṇe māyākhye līnaṃ kṛtvā tac ca māyākhyaṃ kāraṇam antarnihitātmavrātamadhiṣṭhāya saṃsāriṇāṃ bhavādhvabhramaṇaśrāntānāṃ viśramārtham avatiṣṭhate niruddhavyāpārāṃs tāṃs tān karotītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the end, having withdrawn the means of experience, such as bodies, instruments, and worlds, and made them dissolve in the cause called <s>māyā</s>, and having superintended that cause called <s>māyā</s>, within which the host of selves is concealed, he remains for the sake of rest for transmigrating beings exhausted by wandering along the path of becoming. The meaning is that he makes each of them cease from activity.

children.text: kuta ityāha sarvabhūtahito yataḥ yasmāt sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ hitāya pravṛttaḥ parameśvaraḥ khedāpanodāya viśrāntiṃ svāpalakṣaṇāmeṣāṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: Why? He says: because he benefits all beings. Since <s>Parameśvara</s> is engaged for the welfare of all beings, he gives them rest, in the form of sleep, in order to remove their fatigue.

children.text: tatastu ||
children.translated_text: Then, however,

children.text: Chapter 96
vakṣyamāṇakālaparimāṇasya svāpasyānte bhūyaḥ pūrvavad aharmukhe parameśvaraśceṣṭate ||
children.translated_text: at the end of the sleep whose measure of time will be stated, <s>Parameśvara</s> again acts as before at the beginning of the day.

children.text: tatsvāpe'pi kriyādiśaktayas tattatkāryaniṣpādanodyuktā bhavantītyāha ||
children.translated_text: He says that even during that sleep the powers, beginning with the power of action, are intent on accomplishing their respective effects.

children.text: Chapter 97

jāgradavasthāyāmiva svāpāvasthāyāmapi malaparipākatāratamyāpekṣayā bodhanārhān bodhayan rodhanārhān rodhanaśaktyārundhan karmiṇāṃ karmāṇi pariṇāmayan māyāśaktīśca prasavābhimukhīḥ kurvan sarvaṃ cidacittattvabhāvabhūtabhuvanātmakaṃ yathāvadavalokayannāste ||
children.translated_text: As in the waking state, so also in the state of sleep, he remains: awakening those who are fit to be awakened according to the gradations in the maturity of <s>mala</s>, restraining through the power of restraint those who are fit to be restrained, bringing the deeds of karmic agents to fruition, making the powers of <s>māyā</s> ready for production, and observing everything as it really is, whether it consists of conscious or unconscious tattvas, states, beings, or worlds.

children.text: yadyatheti na tv asmadādivat ayathāvastvavabhāso 'pyasya bhavatīti vakṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The expression 'as it really is' means that, unlike us and others, he does not have even an appearance of things otherwise than they are; we shall explain this.

children.text: tadiyatā jagatsṛṣṭisthitidhvaṃsalakṣaṇaṃ kṛtyatrayamihoktamiti prakaraṇopasaṃhāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus this is the conclusion of the topic: by this much the threefold act consisting of the world's creation, maintenance, and destruction has been stated here.

children.text: Chapter 98
tamaso malasya śakteśca bhagavatsambandhinyā vāmākhyāyā yo 'sāv adhikāro nyagbhāvanavyāpṛtatvaṃ tasya nivṛttervirāmāt yāsau paricyutiḥ kaivalyābhimukhībhāvaḥ tathā coktaṃ śrīmatsvāyambhuve
children.translated_text: The falling away in question is a turning toward <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation-liberation), due to the cessation, the stopping, of that authority of darkness, that is, <s>mala</s>, and of the Lord's power called <s>Vāmā</s>, whose activity is making beings lower. Thus it is said in the venerable <s>Svāyambhuva</s>:

children.text: kṣīṇe tasminyathā sā syātparaṃ niḥśreyasaṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: When that has waned, she turns toward supreme blessedness.

children.text: iti tasyāṃ tatparicyutau satyāṃ jagaduddharaṇapravaṇaḥ parameśvaro dṛkkriyānantyamaṇorātmanaḥ prakaṭīkaroti ||
children.translated_text: Thus, when that falling away has occurred, <s>Parameśvara</s>, inclined to raise up the world, manifests the infinitude of knowledge and action belonging to the atomic self.

children.text: satyorevānantayor dṛkkriyayor malāvacchannatvād āvṛtānantyayos tatpariṇaterāvaraṇāpagamādabhivyaktiḥ kriyate na tv apūrvotpāda ityuktaṃ vakṣyāmaśca satkāryavāde ||
children.translated_text: The infinitude of knowledge and action is manifested because those two are truly infinite already but have their infinitude covered by <s>mala</s>, and because their covering is removed through its maturation; it is not the production of something previously non-existent. This has been stated, and we shall state it again in connection with <s>satkāryavāda</s> (the doctrine that the effect already exists).

children.text: Chapter 99
svāpāvasthitān yānparameśvaro'nugṛhṇāti te tu tatkāla eva śivāḥ sampadyante na tv adhikāriṇo bhavanti teṣāṃ malāṃśān avaśeṣato'preryatvena śivatvayogāt tadānīṃ cādhikāriṇāmanupayogāt ||
children.translated_text: But those in the state of sleep whom <s>Parameśvara</s> favors attain the state of <s>Śiva</s> at that very time; they do not become office-bearers, because, since the remaining portions of their <s>mala</s> are no longer impelled, they are joined to the state of <s>Śiva</s>, and because at that time office-bearers have no function.

children.text: kiṃca saṃhāre sṛṣṭau vā yānvimocayati te 'pi sadya eva śivāḥ sampadyante na vyatirekeṇa ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, those whom he liberates at dissolution or at creation also attain the state of <s>Śiva</s> immediately, and not in some distinct way.

children.text: athaveti anayoḥ sṛṣṭisaṃhārakālayor añjanaparipākavailakṣaṇyatas tatkṣaṇaṃ śivatvavyaktyā niradhikāramūrtibhājaḥ sādhikārāḥ patitvayogino vā ātmāno bhavantītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Alternatively, the meaning is this: at these two times, creation and dissolution, because of differences in the maturation of the stain, selves either possess forms without office, or possess office and are fit for lordship, through the manifestation of the state of <s>Śiva</s> at that very moment.

children.text: tatra saṃhāre yeṣām adhikāravān anugrahaste tadānīṃ rudrāṇavaḥ sṛṣṭau tv adhikāriṇo bhavitāraḥ sargārambhe tu sādhikārānugrahānugṛhītāḥ pataya iti parāparavidyeśvarādyadhikārabhājo bhavantīti ||
children.translated_text: Among these, at dissolution, those whose grace is accompanied by office are then <s>Rudrāṇu</s>s; at creation they are to become office-bearers; and at the beginning of creation those favored by grace that carries office become lords, that is, holders of offices such as those of the <s>Parāpara Vidyeśvara</s>s.

children.text: atha sṛṣṭisaṃhārakālayor aśrutamapi kathamanugrāhyāṇāṃ śivatvaṃ labhyata iti cet labhyata eva malaparipākasya parameśvarānugrahasya cāniyatakālatvāt ||
children.translated_text: If one asks how the state of <s>Śiva</s> can be obtained by those who are to receive grace, even though this is not heard of at the times of creation and dissolution, it is indeed obtained, because the maturation of <s>mala</s> and the grace of <s>Parameśvara</s> are not fixed to a particular time.

children.text: athaivaṃ sargasaṃhārasvāpakāleṣu anugṛhītānāṃ muktiviśeṣamuktvā sthitikālānugṛhītānāṃ tadviśeṣamāha ||
children.translated_text: Now, having in this way stated the particular form of liberation for those favored at the times of creation, dissolution, and sleep, he states that particular form for those favored during the period of maintenance.

children.text: Chapter 100

gurvadhikaraṇaḥ parameśvaraḥ sthitikāle cidvata iti tadanudhyānavaśāt parāparaniḥśreyasaviṣayayā praśasyayā citā yuktānyānaṇūnanugṛhṇāti te mandatīvrādiśaktisampātavailakṣaṇyāt pañcāṣṭakādirudrāṇāṃ saptakoṭisaṃkhyātānāṃ mantrāṇāṃ tatpatīnāṃ ca vidyeśvarāṇām īśānasya ceśvarasadāśivāntalakṣaṇasya sambandhi padaṃ bhajanta iti tatpadabhājas tatsālokyādipadayogino bhavatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: During the period of maintenance, <s>Parameśvara</s>, whose locus is the guru, favors those atomic selves that are endowed, by force of contemplation of him, with a praiseworthy consciousness directed toward supreme and non-supreme liberation. Because of distinctions in the descent of power, mild, intense, and so on, they attain ranks connected with the <s>Rudra</s>s beginning with the groups of five and eight, with the mantras numbered at seven crores, with their lords the <s>Vidyeśvara</s>s, and with <s>Īśāna</s>, whose range extends through <s>Īśvara</s> and <s>Sadāśiva</s>. The meaning is that they become possessors of those ranks and are fit for states such as <s>sālokya</s> (dwelling in the same world).

children.text: nanu śaktipātaviśeṣāt tattatpadabhāktvaṃ cet tarhi tadviśeṣaḥ kathaṃ jñeyaḥ ityāha ||
children.translated_text: Objection: If the attaining of each rank results from a particular <s>śaktipāta</s> (descent of power), then how is that particularity known? He says:

children.text: Chapter 101

aśarīriṇāṃ tāvadgurubhiḥ śaktipātasya durlakṣatvāc charīravatāṃ yeṣāṃ pārameśvarī śaktirapunarāvirbhāvāya patati teṣāṃ tatpāte muktyutkaṇṭhā saṃsāradveṣaḥ parameśvarabhaktipareṣu bhaktiḥ tacchāsake śāstre śraddhā ceti liṅgaṃ cihnam ||
children.translated_text: For in the case of beings without bodies, <s>śaktipāta</s> (descent of power) is hard for teachers to discern. But for embodied beings upon whom the Supreme Lord's power descends so that there will be no reappearance, the sign or mark at its descent is longing for liberation, aversion to <s>saṃsāra</s>, devotion toward those devoted to the Supreme Lord, and faith in the scripture that teaches him.

children.text: anenaiva cihnenāprakarṣavatā avaśiṣṭasya saṃsārasthitihetoḥ pāśajālasyāsūkṣmabuddhīnām apyanumānam
children.translated_text: By this very sign, even when it lacks intensity, even people whose intellects are not subtle can infer the remaining network of bonds that causes continued existence in <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: pūrvoktānāṃ cihnānāmeva mandatve sati paśoḥ pāśaśaithilyamāndyaṃ mandamatayo 'pyanuminvanti iti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that, when the signs mentioned earlier are weak, even dull-minded people infer that the loosening of the bound soul's bonds is weak.

children.text: nanu kimanenātyantāpūrveṇa śaktipātaniścayena sakaladarśanaprasiddhaṃ tāvadidaṃ kaivalyaprāptikāraṇaṃ liṅgatvena kiṃ na niścīyate ||
children.translated_text: But, one may object: what need is there for this determination of <s>śaktipāta</s>, which is utterly unprecedented? Why is this cause for attaining <s>kaivalya</s>, well known in all systems, not determined as the sign?

children.text: yaduktam
children.translated_text: As has been said:

children.text: na hṛṣyatyupakāreṇa nāpakāreṇa kupyati
children.translated_text: He is not delighted by assistance, nor angered by injury;

children.text: yaḥ samaḥ sarvabhūteṣu jīvanmuktaḥ sa iṣyate ||
children.translated_text: one who is equal toward all beings is accepted as a <s>jīvanmukta</s> (liberated while living).

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tatrāha ||
children.translated_text: To this he replies:

children.text: Chapter 102

paśudṛgbhiḥ pāśavair jñānaistaduktena ca patañjaliprabhṛtipraṇītena yogena ye siddhāḥ sattvaguṇaprasādān mādhyasthyaṃ prāptāsteṣāṃ yatkarmabhyām upakārāpakārarūpābhyāṃ ceṣṭābhyāṃ prasādakrodhalakṣaṇaṃ vyaktidvayaṃ samamiti nāpakāriṇi krodhavyaktir nāpyupakāriṇi prītivyaktir mādhyasthyād evaitadbhavatu nāsmābhir niṣidhyate ||
children.translated_text: Those who are perfected by knowledges belonging to bound beings and marked by the viewpoint of bound beings, and by the yoga taught in them and composed by <s>Patañjali</s> and others, have attained neutrality through the clarity of the <s>sattva</s> quality. In their case, let the two manifestations characterized as pleasure and anger, with regard to the two actions consisting of benefit and harm, be equal: there is no manifestation of anger toward one who harms, nor any manifestation of affection toward one who helps. Let this arise from neutrality; we do not deny it.

children.text: iha punarayaṃ viśeṣaḥ yadadhikāravatīṣu muktiṣu viṣayeṣūpāyasya dīkṣādeḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, however, this is the distinction: in regard to liberations that carry office, the means, such as <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation),

children.text: lokadharmamayī dīkṣā śivadharmamayī tathā ||
children.translated_text: 'There is <s>dīkṣā</s> made of worldly <s>dharma</s>, and likewise one made of <s>Śiva</s>-<s>dharma</s>,'

children.text: ityādinā vakṣyamāṇād vaiśiṣṭyād ādarasya ca tattatpadaprāptiprītiśraddhātmanovailakṣaṇyāt yathoktaṃ śrīmatsūkṣmasvāyambhuve
children.translated_text: and so on, have a special character that will be stated later; and reverence differs because its nature is joy and faith in attaining each particular station. As is said in the venerable <s>Sūkṣmasvāyambhuva</s>:

children.text: yo yatrābhilaṣed bhogānsa tatraiva niyojitaḥ
children.translated_text: Wherever a person desires enjoyments, he is appointed just there,

children.text: siddhibhāṅmantrasāmarthyāt ||
children.translated_text: and becomes a possessor of accomplishment through the power of <s>mantra</s>.

children.text: iti tasmād upāyādaravailakṣaṇyān mantramaheśvarādipadaprāptilakṣaṇajyeṣṭhaphalayogyatāṃ mantreśvarapadaśaktyātmakaphalārhatvaṃ pañcāṣṭakādyaparādhikāri padayojanāyogyatāṃ ca niścetuṃ karmavyaktitrayaṃ mṛgyate anviṣyate ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, because reverence for the means differs, the threefold manifestation of conduct is sought out and investigated in order to determine fitness for the highest fruit, characterized as attainment of the station of <s>Mantramaheśvara</s> and the like; eligibility for a fruit whose nature is the power of the station of a <s>Mantreśvara</s>; and fitness for assignment to lower offices such as the <s>pañcāṣṭaka</s>.

children.text: bhaktiśraddhābhivyaktitāratamyād utkṛṣṭamadhyamāpakṛṣṭarūpasādhikārāpavargapadabhāja ityanugrāhyā bhavantītyāśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The intention is that, because of gradations in the manifestation of devotion and faith, those to be graced become sharers in liberating stations with office, in superior, middling, and inferior forms.

children.text: yac caitat sādhikāramuktitrayaṃ darśitam tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: And since this threefold liberation with office has been shown, therefore:

children.text: Chapter 103
madhyamāpakṛṣṭayor muktyor uparyadhovartinaḥ padasya prāpyatayā svasmāt padāt cyutisambhavena ca kaścidvyaktikaro'ntarāyaḥ natv anantaram evāpavargasya prāptiḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the middling and inferior liberations, because there remains a higher or lower station to be attained and because falling from one's own station is possible, there is some impediment that produces manifestation; liberation is not attained immediately afterward.

children.text: tṛtīyasyāṃ tu tatpadādhikārasamāptisamanantareṇaiva tallābhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But in the third case, it is attained immediately after the office belonging to that station is completed.

children.text: atha kiṃnimittam etac cihnavaicitryaṃ yadvaśāttritvaṃ sādhikārāyā mukterityāha ||
children.translated_text: Now he says what causes this variety of signs, under whose influence liberation with office is threefold:

children.text: Chapter 104
tamaḥpateḥ kriyādṛṅniroddhur vāmadevanāthasya yadrodhakatvaṃ tasmin kiṃcin nivṛtte manāg avaśiṣṭe ca sati etac cihnatāratamyaṃ śarīriṇāṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: When the obstructive power of <s>Vāmadevanātha</s>, the lord of darkness who restrains action and vision, has partly ceased while remaining only slightly, this gradation of signs occurs in embodied beings.

children.text: ata eva ||
children.translated_text: For just this reason:

children.text: Chapter 105
etadyogyatātrayam anapekṣyaiva svāpe'ṇumanugṛhṇāti aṇumiti jātāvekavacanam yogyatāvaicitryeṇānugrahavaicitryamaṇūnāṃ tadānīṃ na karotīti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Without taking account of this threefold eligibility, he bestows grace on the <s>aṇu</s> (atomic soul) during repose. The word <s>aṇu</s> is singular with reference to the class; the meaning is that at that time he does not create variety in the grace given to souls on account of variety in eligibility.

children.text: atraiva hetumāha sādhikāramidaṃ yataḥ yasmādyogyatātrayamadhikārāpekṣam ||
children.translated_text: Here he states the reason: 'because this is with office'; that is, because the threefold eligibility depends upon office.

children.text: na ca tadānīmadhikāropayogaḥ tasmān nāpekṣate ||
children.translated_text: And at that time office has no use; therefore he does not take it into account.

children.text: Chapter 106
bhaviṣyati sargārambhe saṃhāropānte vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇāyāṃ tṛtīyasyāṃ ca bhūtasaṃhṛtau yānanugṛhṇāti te śivāḥ sampadyante svāpāvasthānugṛhītāṇuvat ||
children.translated_text: In the future, at the beginning of creation, at the end of dissolution, and in the third withdrawal of the elements whose definition will be stated later, those whom he graces become <s>Śiva</s>s, like the <s>aṇu</s>s graced in the state of repose.

children.text: svāpe'ṇumanugṛhṇātīti yatprāguktaṃ tato'ṇuśabdaṃ lakṣayitum āha ||
children.translated_text: With regard to the earlier statement, 'he bestows grace on the <s>aṇu</s> during repose,' he now speaks in order to clarify the word <s>aṇu</s>.

children.text: Chapter 107
sa ityanantaroktaḥ sargādau tṛtīye ca bhūtasaṃhāre svāpe ca yo 'nugrāhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The pronoun 'he' refers to the one just mentioned: the one who is to be graced at the beginning of creation, in the third withdrawal of the elements, and in repose.

children.text: yo yad vyapāsyāpanīya tādṛgvidhaḥ kriyate abhivyaktaśivabhāvaḥ sampadyate so 'ṇuśabdavācyo jñeyaḥ aṇuḥ sann apavṛjyata iti yāvat ||
children.translated_text: The one who, after whatever is to be removed has been removed, is made to be of that kind, that is, becomes one whose <s>Śiva</s>-nature is manifest, should be known as what is denoted by the word <s>aṇu</s>; in other words, while still an <s>aṇu</s>, he is released.

children.text: tadevaṃ bodhayanbodhayogyān iti yatprāguktaṃ taddṛkkriyānantyavyaktyā pradarśitam ||
children.translated_text: Thus the earlier statement, 'awakening those fit to be awakened,' has been illustrated by the manifestation of the infinitude of vision and action.

children.text: yadapi rodhyānrundhan ityādi sūcitaṃ tat yānvimocayati svāpe ityanena keṣāṃcideva tathāvidhānugrahabhāktve sati anyeṣām arthākṣipto rodha itikṛtvā na vipañcitam ||
children.translated_text: And what was indicated by 'obstructing those to be obstructed' and the like has not been elaborated, because, by the phrase 'whom he releases in repose,' when only some are recipients of such grace, the obstruction of the others is implied by force of meaning.

children.text: idānīṃ tu pācayankarmikarma ityuktaṃ nirvarṇayitum āha ||
children.translated_text: Now, in order to explain the statement, 'ripening karma belonging to the karmic agents,' he says:

children.text: Chapter 108
bhagavataḥ śaktayaḥ sarvakāryeṣu prasṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One's powers extend into all activities.

children.text: tābhiḥ śarīrendriyajātyāyurbhogakāraṇaṃ karma dehabhājāṃ tatsvāpe pācayati phaladānonmukhamāpādayati ||
children.translated_text: Through them, during their repose, he ripens the karma of embodied beings, the cause of body, senses, birth, lifespan, and experience, making it ready to give its fruit.

children.text: yasmāt ||
children.translated_text: Because:

children.text: Chapter 109
yogyatāyā arhatvasyāṅgaṃ sampādakaṃ pākākhyaṃ saṃskāram abhajad anāsevyamānaṃ tat karma sadyastatkṣaṇaṃ harītakyādyauṣadhamiva na syān na bhavetphaladamiti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If that karma did not obtain the conditioning called ripening, which is an auxiliary that produces eligibility or fitness, then, like a medicine such as <s>harītakī</s> when it has not been taken, it would not at once, at that very moment, become fruit-giving; 'fruit-giving' is to be supplied.

children.text: yadāhuḥ aprāptapākaṃ harītakyādidravyaṃ sadapi svakāryasampādanāśaktaṃ yogyatāṅgasya pākasyānāsādanāditi ||
children.translated_text: As they say: a substance such as harītakī, though existent, if it has not reached maturation, is unable to accomplish its own function, because it has not attained maturation, the factor of fitness.

children.text: evaṃ sadapi karmāpakvaṃ tatphaladānāśaktam ataḥ pākāpekṣaṃ pākaścāsya na svataḥ sambhavatītyāha ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, <s>karma</s>, though existent, is unable to give its fruit while unripe. Therefore it depends on maturation; and since its maturation does not occur by itself, he says:

children.text: Chapter 110
pākayogyamapi tat svayamātmānamātmanā na pācayitum īśam ||
children.translated_text: Even though it is fit to be matured, it cannot mature itself by itself.

children.text: sarvasyaiva hi pariṇāmino vastunaḥ kṣīrāderivāyaṃ sādhāraṇo dharmaḥ yatkimapyapekṣya pariṇāmitvaṃ nānyathā pariṇāmitvāc ca karmaṇo'pyanyāpekṣo vipākaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For every object that undergoes transformation, such as milk, has this common property: it transforms only in dependence on something, not otherwise. And because <s>karma</s> too undergoes transformation, its ripening depends on another.

children.text: anena māyāśaktīrvyaktiyogyāḥ prakurvan ityetadapi prakāśitaṃ tasyāpi pariṇāmitvāt ||
children.translated_text: By this, the statement that he makes the powers of <s>māyā</s> fit for manifestation has also been clarified, since that too undergoes transformation.

children.text: na caiṣāṃ malamāyākarmaṇāṃ pariṇāmakatvamanīśena suśakamityuktam ||
children.translated_text: And it has been said that for these, namely <s>mala</s>, <s>māyā</s>, and <s>karma</s>, the role of transformer is not readily possible for one who is not Lord.

children.text: īśatīty aduṣṭam īśa ivācarati iti sarvaprātipadikebhya ityeke iti kvipaḥ smaraṇāt ||
children.translated_text: The expression īśati, 'he rules,' is unobjectionable: it means 'he acts like an īśa,' and the affix kvip is remembered under the rule, according to some, that it applies after all nominal stems.

children.text: tadiyatā tāvatsarvakartṛtvaṃ parameśvarasya pratipāditam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by just this much, the universal agency of the Supreme Lord has been established.

children.text: ata eva cāsya sarvajñatvaṃ sidhyatītyāha ||
children.translated_text: And from this very fact his omniscience is established, he says:

children.text: Chapter 111
sarvakartṛtvād eveśvarasya sarvajñatvaṃ sarvaviṣayajñānaṃ vinā sarvakartṛtānupapatteḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because of the Lord's universal agency alone, the Lord's omniscience is established, since universal agency is impossible without knowledge whose object is everything.

children.text: yo hi yadyatkriyāsiddhiṃ tadaṅgāni tatphalāni ca jānāti tasyaiva vicitratattatkārakopayogābhisaṃdhānavatas tattatkartṛtvaṃ ghaṭate kuvindāderiva paṭādikṛtau ||
children.translated_text: For only one who knows the accomplishment of each action, its auxiliaries, and its fruits, and who intends the employment of the various relevant factors, can be the agent of those respective things, as a weaver is in making cloth and the like.

children.text: ato yastu tatrājñaḥ sa tatkāryakaraṇāya nālaṃ bāliśa iva nyāyavidyādyupanyāsa ityetatsusthitamityavyabhicārīti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore someone who is ignorant of that is not capable of producing that effect, just as a simple-minded person is not fit to expound logic and the like. Thus this is well established as invariable.

children.text: Chapter 112
śivasya tat sarvajñatvam anādyāvaraṇaśūnyatvān na vyañjakāpekṣam nāpi saṃsāriṇa iva saṃśayaviparyayānadhyavasāyayuktam ata eva hetoḥ ||
children.translated_text: That omniscience of <s>Śiva</s>, since it is free from beginningless covering, does not depend on a manifesting condition; nor, like the cognition of a transmigrating being, is it accompanied by doubt, error, or failure of ascertainment, for this same reason.

children.text: tathāhi ||
children.translated_text: For so it is:

children.text: Chapter 113
yāni kila jñānāni malaśaktyāvṛtatvādbhoganiṣpādanāya vyañjakaṃ kalādyapekṣante tāni vyañjakasya kalādeḥ svalpaprakāśakaraṇāt tathāvidhavyañjanabhāji jñeyaviṣaye vyāghātavantyapi bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Those cognitions which, because they are covered by the power of <s>mala</s>, depend on a manifestor such as <s>kalā</s> for the production of experience, may also be subject to obstruction with regard to the knowable object that receives such manifestation, since the manifestor such as <s>kalā</s> produces only a slight illumination.

children.text: na caiśvaraṃ jñānamevaṃvidhaṃ pūrvoktādevāvṛtiśūnyatvāt kāraṇāt ||
children.translated_text: But the Lord's knowledge is not of this kind, because, for the reason already stated, it is free from covering.

children.text: tathā coktaṃ śrīkiraṇe
children.translated_text: And so it is said in the <s>Śrīkiraṇa</s>:

children.text: anādimalamuktatvāt sarvajño 'sau tataḥ śivaḥ
children.translated_text: "Because he is free from beginningless <s>mala</s>, therefore that <s>Śiva</s> is omniscient."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: yataścaivamataḥ ||
children.translated_text: And since this is so, therefore:

children.text: Chapter 114
akṣasavyapekṣaṃ hi jñānaṃ pratyakṣamakṣavyāpāraṇāt tadabhāve'bhāvāt tadbhāve bhāvānuvidhāyitvāc ca vyāhatamapi syāt ||
children.translated_text: Knowledge that depends on the sense faculties is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception), because it operates through the senses, because it is absent when they are absent, and because its occurrence follows their presence; and it can even be obstructed.

children.text: na caivaṃ śāmbhavaṃ jñānamato na pratyakṣam nāpyānumānikaṃ tasya pratyakṣādhīnavṛttitvāt śābdatvaṃ tu dūrāpāstam atyantaparokṣārthaviṣayatvāt tasya ||
children.translated_text: But <s>Śambhu</s>'s knowledge is not like this. Therefore it is not <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception), nor is it inferential, since inference functions in dependence on perception. Verbal testimony is still farther removed, because its object is something extremely remote.

children.text: na ca kiṃcidbhagavataḥ parokṣamataḥ sarvaviṣayaṃ tasya jñānaṃ prakāśate ||
children.translated_text: And nothing is remote from the Blessed Lord; therefore his knowledge shines upon every object.

children.text: nanu
children.translated_text: But, one may object:

children.text: pañcavaktrastripañcadṛk
children.translated_text: "Five-faced and fifteen-eyed,"

children.text: ityādinā śrūyata evāgameṣvīśvarasya śarīrendriyayogaḥ tatsadbhāve'pi kasmān na tatsavyapekṣe īśvarasya jñānakriye ||
children.translated_text: by such passages in the <s>āgama</s>s the Lord is indeed heard to be connected with body and sense organs. Even if these exist, why do the Lord's knowledge and action not depend on them?

children.text: nāsya jñānakriyopayogī śarīrendriyayogaḥ svabhāvata eva sarvārthakriyā śaktimattvādicchāmātreṇaiva sargasthityādikaraṇakṣamatvāt ||
children.translated_text: His connection with body and sense organs is not useful for his knowledge and action, because by nature he possesses the power to act with regard to all things and is capable of creation, maintenance, and the rest by mere desire alone.

children.text: bhaktānugrahaṇārthaṃ cākāragrahaṇamanyathā nirākāre dhyānapūjādyayogāt ||
children.translated_text: And his taking on form is for the sake of favoring devotees; otherwise meditation, worship, and so forth would be impossible with respect to one who is formless.

children.text: yaduktaṃ śrīmatpauṣkare
children.translated_text: As stated in the venerable <s>Pauṣkara</s>:

children.text: sādhakasya tu lakṣyārthaṃ tasya rūpamidaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: "But for the practitioner, this form of his is remembered for the purpose of having an object of focus;

children.text: sarvataḥ pāṇipādaṃ tatsarvato 'kṣiśiromukham ||
children.translated_text: it has hands and feet everywhere, eyes, heads, and faces everywhere."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: Chapter 115
yathāvasthitavastvavabhāsātmanas tāvattadīyasyaikasya jñānasya jñeyānantyād upādhibhedāt kṛtamaupacārikamānantyam śāstrātmano'pi srotobhedādadhyetṛbhedāt pravartayitṛbhedāt ||
children.translated_text: His one knowledge, whose nature is the illumination of things as they actually stand, has a merely figurative infinity, because knowables are infinite and because of distinctions in limiting conditions. Knowledge in the form of scripture too has such infinity because of differences in streams, students, and promulgators.

children.text: teṣāṃ ca parāparatvād gauṇamevānantyam ||
children.translated_text: And since these are higher and lower, the infinity is only secondary.

children.text: sarvajñānakriyārūpā śaktirekaivaśūlinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "The power of <s>Śūlin</s>, whose form is all knowledge and action, is one alone."

children.text: ityanayā dṛśā tasmāj jñānād abhinnatvāt kartṛtvamapi tathaivopacārādānantyaṃ pratipadyate ||
children.translated_text: From this perspective, therefore, since agency is not different from that knowledge, agency too attains infinity in just the same way, figuratively.

children.text: atha nirvarṇitopasaṃhārāya vyākhyeyopakṣepāya cāyaṃ ślokaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now this verse serves to summarize what has been described and to introduce what is to be explained.

children.text: Chapter 116
athopalabhya dehādi vastu kāryatvadharmakam
children.translated_text: "Then, having perceived an object such as the body, possessing the property of being an effect,

children.text: kartāramasya jānīmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: we know its maker."

children.text: ityādinā tāvadīśvarasya sattā sādhitā ||
children.translated_text: By this and the following, the existence of the Lord was first established.

children.text: nityaṃ kālānavacchedādvaitatyān na pradeśagam
children.translated_text: "Eternal, because it is not limited by time; because of pervasiveness, not confined to a place;

children.text: kramākramasamutpatteḥ kramādyutpattiśaktimat ||
children.translated_text: because sequential and non-sequential productions arise, endowed with the power of producing sequence and the rest."

children.text: iti tatsvarūpamuktam ||
children.translated_text: By this his nature was stated.

children.text: karaṇaṃ ca na śaktyanyacchaktir nācetanā citaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "And the instrument is not other than power; nor is the power of consciousness insentient."

children.text: ityanena karaṇaṃ kathitam ||
children.translated_text: By this the instrument was declared.

children.text: viniyogaphalaṃ muktirbhuktir apyanuṣaṅgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: "The fruit of its application is liberation, and enjoyment too, incidentally."

children.text: ityamunārthaḥ prayojanamupavarṇitam ||
children.translated_text: By this the purpose was described.

children.text: jagajjanmasthitidhvaṃsatirobhāvavimuktayaḥ
children.translated_text: "The birth, maintenance, destruction, concealment, and liberation of the world

children.text: kṛtyam ||
children.translated_text: are the task."

children.text: ityanena pañcavidhaṃ vidheyamuktam ||
children.translated_text: By this the fivefold thing to be accomplished was stated.

children.text: dṛkca asya jñānam
children.translated_text: "And his vision is knowledge;

children.text: nādhyakṣaṃ nāpi tallaiṅgam
children.translated_text: it is not perception, nor inferential."

children.text: ityādinā nirṇītamiti ||
children.translated_text: By this and the following, it has been determined.

children.text: etābhiḥ sattāsvarūpakaraṇārthavidheyadṛgbhiḥ saṃkṣepoktābhir īśatattvaṃ ye viduḥ jānanti te puruṣāḥ saṃsārakardamanimagnān saṃsāriṇo mocayanti na tu vistareṇa paśurūpaṃ pāśarūpaṃ vā īśvaraṃ ye viduḥ yathā ||
children.translated_text: Those persons who know, that is, understand the reality of <s>Īśa</s> through these briefly stated views concerning existence, nature, instrument, purpose, and what is subject to him, free embodied beings sunk in the mud of saṃsāra; but not those who know <s>Īśvara</s> in detail as being of the nature of the <s>paśu</s> or of the <s>pāśa</s>, as follows:

children.text: ātmaivedaṃ sarvam
children.translated_text: "The self alone is all this."

children.text: puruṣa evedaṃ sarvam ||
children.translated_text: "The Person alone is all this."

children.text: ityevaṃvidhapuruṣarūpeśvaravādinaḥ karmakālāvyaktādipāśarūpeśvaravādino vā paśūnāṃ svayam evānādyajñānanimagnatvenākiṃcitkaratvāt pāśānāṃ ca tatpāśana eva caritārthatvāt tattatsaṃyoge viyogādau vā nigalādivat parāpekṣatve satyanīśvaratvāt ||
children.translated_text: Those who teach <s>Īśvara</s> as a Person of this kind, or who teach <s>Īśvara</s> as a bond such as karma, time, or the unmanifest, cannot do so: for the <s>paśu</s>s themselves are useless because they are sunk in beginningless ignorance; the bonds have fulfilled their purpose simply in binding them; and, in conjunction and separation with each such thing, since they depend on another, like fetters and the like, they are not lords.

children.text: tathāvidheśvarāvabodhāt paramocanaṃ sakalalokopahāsāvahaṃ yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: For liberating another through awareness of such an <s>Īśvara</s> would bring the ridicule of the whole world.

children.text: paśuśabdaścātra samanantaraprakaraṇopakramyamāṇātmatattvopakṣepāyopahṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the word <s>paśu</s> is introduced here in order to bring in the topic of the reality of the self, which is begun in the immediately following section.

children.text: Chapter 117
athedānīṃ pāścātyapaṭalāntasūcitābhidhānasyātmano lakṣaṇamucyata iti pāṭalikaprākaraṇikau sambandhau jñeyau ||
children.translated_text: Now the definition of the self, whose designation was indicated at the end of the previous chapter, is stated; thus the chapter-connection and the topic-connection should be understood.

children.text: sautrādayastu prāgvadunneyāḥ pratipaṭalamucyamānā atipaunaruktyamāvahanti ||
children.translated_text: The connections with the <s>sūtra</s> and so on are to be inferred as before; if they were stated in every chapter, they would produce excessive repetition.

children.text: viśvasya jagato nimittaṃ pravartanaheturātmā tadbhogasādhanāya tanukaraṇabhuvanādīnāmutpatteḥ ||
children.translated_text: The self is the cause, the reason for the activity, of the whole world, because bodies, organs, worlds, and so on arise as means for its experience.

children.text: tasyātmano lakṣaṇamīśvaroktyanantaram avasaraprāptaṃ kathyate ||
children.translated_text: The definition of that self, which has become timely after the statement about <s>Īśvara</s>, is now given.

children.text: tac ca yadyapi
children.translated_text: And although that

children.text: tena svabhāvasiddhena bhavitavyaṃ jagatkṛtā ||
children.translated_text: "therefore there must be a maker of the world, established by his own nature,"

children.text: ityatra īśvarasiddhyanuṣaṅgeṇa ||
children.translated_text: in that place, in connection with the establishment of <s>Īśvara</s>,

children.text: caitanyaṃ dṛkkriyārūpaṃ tadastyātmani sarvadā
children.translated_text: "consciousness, whose form is seeing and acting, is always present in the self;

children.text: sarvataśca yato muktau śrūyate sarvatomukham ||
children.translated_text: and because, in liberation, it is heard to face everywhere and to have faces on all sides,"

children.text: ityādinoktaprāyaṃ kathitakalpaṃ tathāpyuddeśaḥ sopapattikatatsvarūpasaṃkṣepa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: and by such statements has almost already been stated, nevertheless an introductory account is given, a concise statement of its nature together with supporting reasoning.

children.text: Chapter 118
kāryatvaṃ tāvatkṣityādereva saṃniveśādimattvena prāk kathitam ||
children.translated_text: First, the fact that earth and the other elements are effects has already been stated, since they possess arrangement and the like.

children.text: tasya ca kartā prāguktābhiryuktibhirīśaḥ siddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And their maker has been established as <s>Īśa</s> by the arguments stated earlier.

children.text: tattu kāryaṃ tadupayogi vā syāt svopayogi anupayogi anyopayogi veti catvāraḥ pakṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But that effect, or what is useful for that effect, would have to be useful to him, useful to itself, useless, or useful to another: these are the four alternatives.

children.text: tatra na tāvadīśvaropayogi nahi pṛthivyādibhistasya svātmanyarthakriyā kācitkriyate nityaparipūrṇasvarūpatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Among these, it is certainly not useful to <s>Īśvara</s>, for earth and the rest perform no function at all for him with respect to his own self, since his nature is eternally complete.

children.text: na ca tat kṣityādi kāryaṃ kṣityādyarthameva kriyate teṣāmācaitanyāt karaṇīyasyābhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: Nor is that effect, earth and the rest, made for the sake of earth and the rest themselves, because they are insentient and have nothing to be done.

children.text: cetanasya hi dharmādicaturvargaprepsoḥ karaṇīyaṃ sambhavati na paṭādeḥ ||
children.translated_text: For something to be done is possible for a conscious being who desires the fourfold goal beginning with <s>dharma</s>, not for cloth and the like.

children.text: na caitat kāryamanarthakaṃ kartṛgauravāt ||
children.translated_text: Nor is this effect purposeless, because that would make the agent's activity needlessly heavy.

children.text: sāmānyenāpi kartrā yatkāryaṃ kriyate tan nānarthakaṃ bhavati kiṃ punaḥ parameśvaravyāpāritair jagatkartṛbhirbrahmādibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even a work done by an agent in general is not purposeless; how much less one done by <s>Brahmā</s> and the others, the world-makers employed by <s>Parameśvara</s>.

children.text: tatkāryakaraṇe ca na prayojanaṃ prāk pradarśitam ||
children.translated_text: And no purpose in producing that effect has been shown previously.

children.text: Chapter 119
tat kṣityādi kāryam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the effect, earth and the rest,

children.text: kaścātra para ityāha ||
children.translated_text: is for another. Who, then, is this other? He says:

children.text: Chapter 120
kartṛkāryayoḥ paro'nyaḥ prastutābhidhānaḥ kṣetrajño yaś cātmetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The other, distinct from the maker and the effect, whose designation is presently intended, is the knower of the field, that is, the self.

children.text: atra cārvākacchāyayā ātmanirāsāyedam āśaṅkyate ||
children.translated_text: Here, in the manner of a <s>Cārvāka</s>, the following objection is raised in order to deny the self.

children.text: Chapter 121
nanūpalabhyamānaprayojanānāṃ kṣityādīnāṃ parārthatvamastu sa tv atra paraḥ kāya eva yasyārambhakāś copayoginaśca pṛthivyaptejovāyavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let earth and the rest, whose purposes are perceived, be for the sake of another. But that other here is simply the body, for earth, water, fire, and air are both its constituents and what is useful to it.

children.text: tasmān na kṣityādīnāṃ parārthatvenātmanāmanumānam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the selves are not inferred from earth and the rest being for the sake of another.

children.text: atrottaraṃ ||
children.translated_text: To this the reply is:

children.text: Chapter 122
deho'pi parārtha eva ācaitanyāt pṛthivyādivaditi tasyāpy ānyārthyaṃ pārārthyaṃ sutarāmupapadyate ||
children.translated_text: The body too is for the sake of another, precisely because it is insentient, like earth and the rest; thus its being for another, its serving another, is all the more reasonable.

children.text: tataśca dehasya kṣityādīnāṃ ca parārthatvātpara ātmaivātra yuktyupapannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Consequently, since the body and earth and the rest are for the sake of another, the other here is rightly established by reasoning as the self alone.

children.text: nanu dehādanyatra yadi caitanyaṃ syāt syādetadevam ||
children.translated_text: One may object: if consciousness existed somewhere other than the body, this would indeed be so.

children.text: pṛthvyādicaturbhūtavikārake prāṇādikāraṇībhūte garbhādau saṃvidudbhavaḥ kiṇvādidravyavikāre bhavaśaktyutpattivat ||
children.translated_text: But consciousness arises in the embryo and the like, which are transformations of the four elements beginning with earth and become the causes of breath and the rest, just as a potency arises in a transformation of substances such as ferment.

children.text: tathāhi kṛśo'haṃ sthūlo'hamiti śarīra evāhaṃpratyayo dṛṣṭaḥ na ca tadvyatirikta ātmā upalabhyate dehe'styātmā ityasya aśve viṣāṇamityādivat pratyakṣanirākṛtatvāt ||
children.translated_text: For the cognition 'I am thin' or 'I am stout' is observed in the body alone, and no self distinct from it is perceived; the claim 'there is a self in the body' is refuted by perception, like the claim 'there is a horn on a horse.'

children.text: atha parārthāścakṣurādayaḥ saṃghātatvāt śayanādyaṅgavadityādinā karaṇādīnāṃ kartṛprayojyatvādinā vā anumānenātmā prasādhyate na tadyuktaṃ tasyātmāpalāpinaścārvākān pratyasiddheḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, if the self is to be established by an inference such as 'the eye and the other organs are for another because they are composites, like the parts of a bed,' or by saying that the organs and the rest are employed by an agent, that is not proper, because it is not established for the <s>Cārvāka</s>s, who deny the self.

children.text: nahy eṣāṃ pratyakṣād anyatkiṃcit pramāṇaṃ siddhāv api vā anumīyamānasyātmano devadattādivatparatvaṃ prasajyate ||
children.translated_text: For they do not accept any means of knowledge other than perception; and even if inference were accepted, the inferred self would turn out to be other, like <s>Devadatta</s> and the rest.

children.text: yatkila svayaṃ prakāśate sa evātmā tatprakāśyastu para iti viviktatayā ātmaparabhāvasya prakāśamānasyaiva saṃkaro'navasthānaṃ ca syāt ||
children.translated_text: What shines by itself alone is the self, while what is illuminated by it is other. Thus the clearly appearing distinction between self and other would become confused and unstable.

children.text: taduktam
children.translated_text: That has been said:

children.text: ātmā yadi bhavenmeyastasya mātā bhavetparaḥ
children.translated_text: "If the self were something measurable, its measurer would be another;

children.text: para ātmā tadānīṃ syātsa paro yastu mīyate ||
children.translated_text: then the other would be the self, and whatever is measured would be other."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tathā
children.translated_text: Likewise:

children.text: prakāśate saṃvidekā tadanyattu prakāśyate
children.translated_text: "A single consciousness shines; what is other than it is illuminated.

children.text: prakāśyaṃ ca bhavetkarma tac ca kartrā vinā katham ||
children.translated_text: And what is illuminated would be an object; how could that exist without an agent?"

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tasmān nānumānena dehavyatirikta ātmā upalabhyate apitu caitanyaviśiṣṭaḥ kāya eva vastusann ityāśaṅkayāha ||
children.translated_text: Therefore an <s>ātman</s> distinct from the body is not apprehended by inference; rather, the body itself, qualified by consciousness, is what exists as a real entity. With this objection, he says:

children.text: Chapter 123
atha manyase kāya eva cetanātmakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, if you think that the body itself is conscious in nature:

children.text: tathāhi yasminnupacite yasyopacayaḥ yadapacaye ca apacayaḥ tattadātmakaṃ yathā vahnyupacayāpacayayor upacayāpacayāv anugacchedauṣṇyam ||
