children.translated_text: For thus: when one thing increases, that whose increase occurs, and when that decreases, that whose decrease occurs, is of the nature of that thing; for example, heat follows the increase and decrease of fire through its own increase and decrease.

children.text: yauvanasthāvirabhojanalaṅghanādihetukau ca dehasambandhināv upacayāpacayāv anukurvadvijñānaṃ dehātmakameva ato deha eva cetana iti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And cognition, since it follows the increases and decreases connected with the body, caused by youth, old age, eating, fasting, and the like, is itself bodily in nature. Therefore the body itself is conscious. This is the prima facie position.

children.text: athaitatpratikṣepaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now comes the rejection of this.

children.text: Chapter 124
so 'pyevaṃ dehaścetanaḥ kadācin na bhavati bhogyatvādvikāritvāc ca ||
children.translated_text: Even that body, considered in this way, is never conscious, because it is an object of enjoyment and because it is subject to alteration.

children.text: ye ye kecana vikāriṇaḥ pariṇāmino bhogyāśca te te hy acetanā dṛṣṭāḥ yathā paṭādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whatever things are alterable, transformable, and objects of enjoyment are observed to be unconscious, such as cloths and the like.

children.text: sa deho'pyevaṃvidhaḥ tasmān na cetanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The body too is of this kind; therefore it is not conscious.

children.text: nanv aṅganādibhir bhogyatvamanaikāntikaṃ bhogyatve'pi tatrācaitanyābhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: But, one may object, being an object of enjoyment is inconclusive because of women and the like, since although they are objects of enjoyment, consciousness is not absent there.

children.text: nānaikāntikaṃ tadīyasya dehasyaiva bhogyatvāt ||
children.translated_text: It is not inconclusive, because only their body is the object of enjoyment.

children.text: yadyevaṃ nirjīvasya dehasya kathaṃ nopabhogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If this is so, why is there no enjoyment of a lifeless body?

children.text: bhavatyeva tadavasthocita upabhogaḥ kravyādādeḥ na punaḥ kāntādeḥ kāminyādyavasthāyā yenāvasthāntarāpatter vikāritvena bībhatsarasahetutvāt ||
children.translated_text: There is indeed enjoyment appropriate to that condition for flesh-eaters and the like, but not, for a lover and the like, the enjoyment of it in the condition of a beloved woman and so forth, because, through passing into another condition, it has altered and become a cause of the <s>bībhatsa-rasa</s>, the sentiment of disgust.

children.text: taduktir atraiva
children.translated_text: A statement of this occurs right here:

children.text: kva tadvaktraṃ kva tadadharamadhu kvāyatākṣyāḥ kaṭākṣaḥ
children.translated_text: "Where is that face? Where is the honey of that lip? Where is the sidelong glance of the wide-eyed woman?"

children.text: ityādi ||
children.translated_text: and so on.

children.text: evaṃ gajāśvādāv api jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: It should be understood in the same way also with elephants, horses, and the like.

children.text: tasmāt sthitametat vikāritvādbhogyatvāc ca dehasyācaitanyam ācaitanyāc ca pārārthyamiti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore this is established: because it is alterable and an object of enjoyment, the body is unconscious; and because it is unconscious, it exists for the sake of another.

children.text: punarapi paramatam āśaṅkate ||
children.translated_text: Again he raises the opposing view.

children.text: Chapter 125
yasminsati yasya bhāvo yadabhāve cābhāvastat tatkāryaṃ śītamiva himasya ||
children.translated_text: That whose being occurs when another exists, and whose non-being occurs when that is absent, is the effect of that, like cold of snow.

children.text: sati ca śukraśauṇitātmakadehārambhakabhūtaviśeṣapariṇāme sattvādasati ca pradhvaste tasminnasattvāc caitanyaṃ bhūtaviśeṣapariṇāmakṛtamiti vā yady aveṣi ||
children.translated_text: And if you understand consciousness as produced by a particular transformation of the elements that begin the body, which consists of semen and blood, because it exists when that exists and because it does not exist when that has been destroyed and is absent,

children.text: tadetadanupapannaṃ yasmāt ||
children.translated_text: then this is not tenable, because:

children.text: Chapter 126
yatsadbhāva eva yasya bhāvastattasya kāryamiti niyamo'trāvaśyaṃ pratijñātavyo'nyathā tadabhāve'pi bhavatas tatkāryatvāyogāt yathāgnisadbhāva eva sambhavan dhūmo'gnikāryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here one must necessarily assert the restriction, "Only that whose being occurs precisely when another exists is the effect of that." Otherwise, if it exists even in the absence of that, it cannot be its effect; for example, smoke, which occurs only when fire exists, is the effect of fire.

children.text: evaṃ ca śarīrārambhakabhūtasadbhāva eva bhāvaḥ tadabhāve cābhāva eva caitanyasya yadi syāt taddehasambandhitayā pratīyeta ||
children.translated_text: Accordingly, if consciousness had its being only when the body-originating elements exist, and only non-being when they are absent, then it would be apprehended as connected with the body.

children.text: yāvatā śarīrasadbhāve'pi garbhādāv uttarakālaṃ ca cetanāpagamo dṛṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But the absence of consciousness is observed even when the body exists, in the embryo and so on, and also at a later time.

children.text: tan na sati sattvaṃ dehārambhakacaitanyasādhakam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the fact that consciousness exists when they exist does not prove that consciousness is produced by the causes that begin the body.

children.text: nanu mṛtaśarīre'pi prāṇādyātmakasya vāyorūṣmarūpasya ca tejaso'pagamān na jīvāvasthāyāmiva śarīrārambhakabhūtasadbhāvas tasmād atrācetanatvam yac ca tat sati sattvam anaikāntikīkartum aśaktam ||
children.translated_text: But, one may object, even in a dead body, because the air that consists of breath and the like and the fire that has the form of warmth have departed, the body-originating elements do not exist as they do in the living state. Therefore unconsciousness in that case is unable to render the concomitance "existence when they exist" inconclusive.

children.text: maivam ||
children.translated_text: Not so.

children.text: gatāsavo'pi hi kecana calatsaṃdhayaḥ soṣmāṇaśca kiyantaṃ kālamupalabhyante ||
children.translated_text: For some whose life-breaths have departed are observed for a certain time with moving joints and with warmth.

children.text: teṣāṃ ca jīvadavasthāvad dehārambhakabhūtasadbhāve'pi na caitanyasambhavaḥ garbhāvasthāyāṃ ca sakalasāmagrīsadbhāve'pi kadācic caitanyāsaṃbhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And although, for them, the body-originating elements exist just as in the living state, consciousness does not arise; and in the embryonic state, even though the entire set of conditions exists, sometimes consciousness does not arise.

children.text: tasmātsati sattvamanaikāntikameva ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the concomitance "existence when they exist" is indeed inconclusive.

children.text: nanu jīvadavasthāyāṃ pariṇāmavaiśiṣṭyāc caitanyasambhavas tathāvidhapariṇāmābhāvāt gatāsudehe tadabhāva iti punarapi cārvākabhūmikayaivāśaṅkyate ||
children.translated_text: But, one may object, in the living state consciousness arises because of a distinctive transformation, and in a body whose life-breaths have departed it is absent because such a transformation is absent. Thus an objection is again raised from the standpoint of the <s>Cārvāka</s>s.

children.text: Chapter 127

kaumārayauvanādyavasthābhedād avāntaratattadavasthāviśeṣabhedena ca dehārambhakabhūtapariṇāmakṛtatattadvaiśiṣṭyāj jīvadavasthāyāṃ yac caitanyamasti tat tathāvidhabhūtapariṇāmakṛtatattadghaṭapaṭaśakaṭādyanekārthaprakāśakāni sakramāṇi hi vijñānāni pūrvapūrvanirodhe saty uttarottarāṇi pariṇāmavaiśiṣṭyādeva bhavanti nānyata iti na dehād anyac caitanyamiti codyam ||
children.translated_text: The objection is this: because of differences of state such as childhood and youth, and because of the subordinate distinctions within each particular state, the consciousness that exists in the living state has each of its particularities produced by transformations of the body-originating elements. The cognitions that illuminate many objects, such as pots, cloths, and carts, arise in sequence; when each previous one has ceased, each subsequent one comes about solely from a distinctive transformation, and not from anything else. Therefore consciousness is not something other than the body.

children.text: atra parihāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here is the reply.

children.text: Chapter 128
tadeti pratyarthaṃ sakramasaṃvedanaviśeṣasya pariṇāmitvābhyupagame sati smṛtir nāvakalpate ||
children.translated_text: In that case, if one admits that the particular cognitions that occur successively with respect to each object are transformations, memory cannot be accounted for.

children.text: pariṇāmaviśeṣāṇāṃ kramabhāvināṃ bhinnatvāt ||
children.translated_text: For the particular transformations that arise in sequence are distinct from one another.

children.text: asaṃviditasyānyaviditasya cānyenāsmaraṇāt ||
children.translated_text: And what has not been cognized, or what has been known by one, is not remembered by another.

children.text: nahy ananubhūtaṃ devadattānubhūtaṃ vā caitrādinā smartuṃ śakyam ||
children.translated_text: For something not experienced, or something experienced by <s>Devadatta</s>, cannot be remembered by <s>Caitra</s> and others.

children.text: evaṃ mā bhūt smṛtiḥ kiṃ naśchinnamiti cet tadapyayuktamityāha ||
children.translated_text: If it is said, "In that case let there be no memory; what is lost to us?" he says that too is improper.

children.text: Chapter 129

sakalalokaprasiddhasmṛtyapahnavas tāvan na śakyaḥ smṛtiś caivam upapadyate dehasyāsakṛtpariṇāmitve'pi ekasvabhāvas tadanyas tadarthasaṃnidhau tattajjñānasyānya evānubhavitā sa evānusaṃdhātā syāditi ||
children.translated_text: To begin with, it is not possible to deny memory, which is well known to all people. And memory is intelligible in this way: although the body is repeatedly transformed, there is something other than it, of a single nature; when the relevant object is present, that same other entity is the experiencer of each cognition, and that very same one is the one who connects it in recollection.

children.text: ata ityasmāt smṛtyanyathānupapattilakṣaṇādapi hetordehādanyaḥ smartāstīti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, from this reason also, characterized by the impossibility of otherwise accounting for memory, there exists a rememberer distinct from the body.

children.text: na ca vācyaṃ kimebhiḥ parānumānāsahiṣṇor vyarthair hetvādibhiriti yataś cārvākasyānicchorapi durgatasya daurgatyamiva balād evānumānaṃ khyātimanubadhnāti ||
children.translated_text: Nor should it be said, "What use are these useless reasons and the like for someone who cannot tolerate another's inference?" For inference, like wretchedness for a wretched man, forcibly attaches itself to the <s>Cārvāka</s>'s cognition even when he does not want it.

children.text: tathā hi tena pratyakṣaikapramāṇavādināpi caturmahābhūtavyatiriktatattvāntarānabhyupagame mṛtpāṣāṇādisthāvaralakṣaṇā pṛthivī jalādiś ca saraḥsaritsamudrādir nādṛṣṭasya guṇabhedena sarvaṃ pratyakṣeṇāvagāhituṃ śakyaṃ tasya pratiniyatavyaktihetutvenāśeṣajagadantargatapadārthaviṣayānvayagrahaṇākṣamatvāt ||
children.translated_text: For although he maintains that perception alone is a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) and does not admit any further reality apart from the four great elements, earth, characterized by stationary things such as clay and stone, and water and the rest, such as ponds, rivers, and oceans, cannot all be known through perception with their unseen differences of qualities; for perception, because it has fixed individuals as its causes, is incapable of grasping concomitance concerning objects contained in the whole world.

children.text: api ca yatra kāṭhinyaṃ sā pṛthivī sthalopalaparvatādivat pṛthivītvābhāve kāṭhinyasyābhāvaś cābādāv iva yac ca dravasvarūpaṃ taj jalaṃ tailaghṛtakṣīrāder apy udakatvād ityādyanvayagrahaṇam anumānāṅgaṃ kalpanīyam ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, one must posit an apprehension of positive concomitance, which is a limb of inference, such as: wherever there is hardness, that is earth, as in dry land, rocks, mountains, and the like; in the absence of earthhood, there is the absence of hardness, as in water and the like; and whatever has a fluid nature is water, since oil, ghee, milk, and so on also have aqueous nature.

children.text: dharmiṇi ca dehe pakṣīkṛte tadgatasya kāṭhinyādeḥ pṛthivyādidharmatvaniścayāt pṛthivyādibhūtacatuṣṭayārabdhatvamapi nānumānaṃ vināvagantuṃ śakyam ||
children.translated_text: And when the body is made the subject under discussion, because its hardness and the like are determined to be properties of earth and the other elements, its being produced from the four elements, earth and the rest, cannot be understood without inference either.

children.text: kiṃ ca pratyakṣameva pramāṇaṃ nānumānamiti pramāṇāpramāṇacintā nāsya pratyakṣaniśceyā ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, his deliberation about what is a <s>pramāṇa</s> and what is not, namely that perception alone is a <s>pramāṇa</s> and inference is not, cannot be decided by perception.

children.text: yathāha dharmakīrtiḥ
children.translated_text: As <s>Dharmakīrti</s> says:

children.text: pramāṇetarasāmānyasthiter anyaviyogataḥ
children.translated_text: Because the common status of <s>pramāṇa</s> and non-<s>pramāṇa</s> is established through exclusion of the other,

children.text: pramāṇāntarasadbhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the existence of another <s>pramāṇa</s> follows.

children.text: iti na paraṃ pratyasiddhatvam anumānasya ||
children.translated_text: Thus inference is not unestablished for the opponent.

children.text: tatpratyāyanārthaṃ ceha pariśeṣānumānaṃ prakaraṇārambhe darśitaṃ na tu svasaṃvedanasiddhatvenāparokṣasyātmanaḥ sādhanāya tatra pramāṇāntarasyānupayogāt ||
children.translated_text: And to make him understand that, a <s>pariśeṣānumāna</s> (inference from elimination) was shown here at the beginning of the topic, not to prove the self, which is immediate because established by self-awareness; for another <s>pramāṇa</s> is of no use there.

children.text: yad āhuḥ
children.translated_text: As they say:

children.text: anubhūtau pramāṇānāṃ pariniṣṭhā samāpyate
children.translated_text: In experience the final culmination of the <s>pramāṇa</s>s is reached;

children.text: svatas tayaiva yā jñaptiḥ kiṃ tatrānyaiḥ pramāntaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: when cognition is known by that very experience on its own, what need is there there for other <s>pramāṇa</s>s?

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: gatametat ||
children.translated_text: This point is settled.

children.text: yattu
children.translated_text: But as for the line:

children.text: pariṇāmasya vaiśiṣṭyādasti cen na smṛtistadā ||
children.translated_text: "If it exists because of a special transformation, then at that time there is no memory,"

children.text: ity akhaṇḍanameva ślokārdhaṃ tad etac chivāvasthāyāṃ sūkṣmatarasaṃvedanasambhave'pi pariṇāmasya vaiśiṣṭyāditi smṛtyabhāvapratipādakatvena paramatāśaṅkayā vyākhyāya samādhīyate yaduta nāpyevaṃ supratītatvāt na hy evaṃ kvacitprasiddhaṃ yadgatāsoḥ sūkṣmatarasaṃvedanamasti smṛtistu nāstītyapitu supratītametat yan nirjīve vapuṣi kāṣṭhādāv iva saṃvin nāstyeveti tasmād dehād anyaḥ smartāstītyevamapi vyākhyāyamāne na kaściddoṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: this half-verse is no refutation at all. It may be explained, as an objection expressing an opponent's view, as teaching the absence of memory because of a special transformation even though subtler awareness is possible in the corpse-state; then it is answered as follows: "Not even so, because the matter is well known." For nowhere is it established that, in one whose life-breath has departed, there is subtler awareness but no memory. Rather, this is well known: in a lifeless body, as in wood and the like, there is no consciousness at all. Therefore, if it is also interpreted in this way, that there is a rememberer other than the body, there is no fault.

children.text: evaṃ paśupadārthaṃ prasādhya tadviśeṣān vaktum āha ||
children.translated_text: Having thus established the <s>paśu</s> category, he says the following in order to state its particular features.

children.text: Chapter 130
sa cātmā nāvyāpakaḥ nāpi kṣaṇikaḥ deśakālābhyām anavacchinnatvāt ||
children.translated_text: And this self is not non-pervasive, nor is it momentary, because it is not delimited by space or time.

children.text: tadāhuḥ
children.translated_text: They say:

children.text: anavacchinnasadbhāvaṃ vastu yad deśakālataḥ
children.translated_text: The entity whose existence is not delimited with respect to space and time,

children.text: tan nityaṃ vibhu cecchantītyātmano vibhunityate ||
children.translated_text: that they hold to be eternal and all-pervasive; thus the self is all-pervasive and eternal.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: na cāsāv ekaḥ
children.translated_text: And that self is not one.

children.text: eko vaśī sarvabhūtāntarātmā
children.translated_text: "One, controlling, the inner self of all beings"

children.text: iti pratipannānāṃ brahmavidām iva janmamaraṇakaraṇādipratiniyamadarśanasya puruṣabahutvajñāpakasyāpahnotum aśakyatvāt ||
children.translated_text: is the view accepted by those who know <s>Brahman</s>; but the observed definite distribution of birth, death, faculties, and the like, which makes known the multiplicity of <s>puruṣa</s>s, cannot be denied.

children.text: na ca naiyāyikavaiśeṣikāṇāmiva jaḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nor is it insentient, as for the <s>Naiyāyika</s>-<s>Vaiśeṣika</s>s.

children.text: nāpi sāṃkhyānāmivākartā ||
children.translated_text: Nor is it a non-agent, as for the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>s.

children.text: na ca keṣāṃcidivāgantunā citā yuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nor is it joined with consciousness adventitiously, as some hold.

children.text: kutaḥ ityāha pāśānte śivatāśruteḥ pāśānāmavidyādīnām ante tatpratibandhakatvavyapagame yato 'syātmanaḥ śivatvavyaktiḥ śrūyate ||
children.translated_text: Why? He says: because scripture teaches its <s>Śiva</s>-state at the end of the bonds. That is, at the end of the bonds, ignorance and the rest, when their character as obstructions has ceased, the manifestation of <s>Śiva</s>-hood for this self is heard in scripture.

children.text: tathā coktam
children.translated_text: And so it has been said:

children.text: athātmamalamāyākhyakarmabandhavimuktaye
children.translated_text: Now, for release from the bondage called the impurity of the self, <s>māyā</s>, and <s>karma</s>,

children.text: vyaktaye ca śivatvasya śivāj jñānaṃ pravartate ||
children.translated_text: and for the manifestation of <s>Śivatva</s>, knowledge proceeds from <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: na ca tacchivatvam avyāpakatvādidharmayuktaṃ jñatvakartṛtvarahitaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: And that <s>Śivatva</s> is not endowed with properties such as non-pervasiveness, nor is it devoid of knowership or agency.

children.text: nityaṃ kālānavacchedād vaitatyān na pradeśagam ||
children.translated_text: It is eternal because it is not delimited by time; because it is extended, it does not occupy a limited place.

children.text: ityādinā pratyuta tadvilakṣaṇatvasyopapāditatvāt ||
children.translated_text: For by passages beginning in this way, its being of the opposite character has rather been established.

children.text: na ca vyāpakatvanityatvāder muktāv evodayāt saṃsāryavasthāyām abhāva iti mantavyam asadutpattyasambhavasyopapādayiṣyamāṇatvād iti ||
children.translated_text: Nor should it be thought that pervasiveness, eternality, and the rest arise only in liberation and are absent in the transmigratory state, because the impossibility of the origination of what is nonexistent will be established.

children.text: Chapter 131

atheti paśupadārthād anantaramavidyā ajñānamañjanamāṇavaḥ pāśa ādau yeṣāṃ te karmamāyārodhaśaktyākhyāḥ pāśāḥ adhunā idānīṃ leśataḥ saṃkṣepataḥ kathyante yeṣām apagame paśutvān muktvā aṇava ātmāno jagataḥ patayo bhavanti
children.translated_text: "Now" means after the topic of the <s>paśu</s>. The bonds beginning with the <s>āṇava pāśa</s> (atomic bond), called <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>ajñāna</s> (non-knowledge), and <s>añjana</s> (stain), namely the bonds called <s>karma</s>, <s>māyā</s>, and the power of obstruction, are now, at present, being described briefly. When these have disappeared, the atomic selves, released from <s>paśutva</s> (bound-soulhood), become lords of the world.

children.text: tatra śivavad anyānadhīnasvātantryābhivyaktir muktātmanāṃ patitvaṃ vidyeśvarādyadhikārabhājāṃ tu pañcavidhakṛtyakāritvam ||
children.translated_text: There, the lordship of liberated selves is the manifestation of independence that depends on no one else, like <s>Śiva</s>'s. But for those who possess offices such as <s>Vidyeśvara</s>, it is performing the fivefold act.

children.text: atha mukteḥ prāk kuto'vasīyate pāśitatvam aṇor iti cet jñānakriyayoḥ sarvārthatāvyāhateḥ
children.translated_text: Now, if it is asked, "Before liberation, from what is the bound condition of the atomic self ascertained?" the answer is: because its knowledge and action are obstructed from having all objects as their scope.

children.text: anyathā hi ||
children.translated_text: For otherwise:

children.text: Chapter 132
pāśarahitasya hipuṃso na baddhatvam abaddhasya ca kiṃkṛtaṃ pāratantryaṃ yad anicchato 'py asyāniṣṭaprāptir iṣṭavyāghātaśca bhavati
children.translated_text: For a person free from bonds has no boundness. And for one who is not bound, what could cause dependence, such that, even against his will, the attainment of what is unwanted and the obstruction of what is wanted occur for him?

children.text: atha manyase nāsya tatpāratantryaṃ pāśakṛtam api tu svābhāvikam iti tarhi muktāṇuṣu muktaśabdasya nivṛttiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, if you think that this dependence of the self is not caused by a <s>pāśa</s> (bond), but is natural, then the word "liberated" would cease to apply to liberated atomic selves.

children.text: vyapagatapāśe hi muktaśabdo loke prasiddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For in ordinary usage the word "liberated" is well known with regard to one whose bonds have departed.

children.text: etadeva ghaṭayann āha ||
children.translated_text: Making just this point fit, he says:

children.text: Chapter 133
iyadeva tadbaddhasya baddhatvaṃ yat pāśitatve satyapāśitavaśyatā svatantraparameśvarāyattatvam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This alone is the boundness of that bound being: when it is bound by a bond, it is subject to the unbound one, that is, dependent upon the independent <s>Parameśvara</s>.

children.text: muktasya caitāvadeva tanmuktatvaṃ yad baddhatvāpagamāt tadvaśitvaṃ svātantryābhivyaktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: And this much alone is that liberated one's liberation: because boundness has departed, there is mastery over that condition, the manifestation of independence.

children.text: tathā hi loke'pi bandharahito vaśī baddhaśca vaśya ityucyate ||
children.translated_text: For so too in ordinary life one free from fetters is called a master, and one who is bound is called subject to another.

children.text: kimata ityāha ||
children.translated_text: What follows from this? He says:

children.text: Chapter 134
tattasmāddhetor yad etadātmana iṣṭaprāptyādau pāratantryaṃ tadbaddhatvaṃ gamayati iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, for that reason, this dependence of the self in attaining what it desires and the like indicates its boundness; the word "indicates" is to be supplied.

children.text: nahy abaddhasya svātantryavyāghāto bhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: For there is no obstruction of independence for one who is not bound.

children.text: na ca tad ātmano 'nādikālīnatayājñānakriyāśaktivan nityam eṣṭavyam aniṣṭaprasaṅgāt ||
children.translated_text: Nor should that dependence of the self be accepted as eternal, on the ground that it is beginningless in time like the powers of knowledge and action, because an unwanted consequence would follow.

children.text: tathāhi ||
children.translated_text: For thus:

children.text: Chapter 135

tasminn ātmanaḥ pāratantrye nitye'bhyupagamyamāne kadācidapi tadanucchedān muktisādhanakalāpaḥ parair apīṣṭo jñānayogādir anarthakaḥ svātantryābhivyaktyabhāvāt sadaivātmano baddhatayāvasthiter ity alam anayā dhiyā nivāryatām īdṛśī saṃsārānucchittiheturmatiriti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If that dependence of the self is admitted to be eternal, then, since it is never cut off, the whole set of means to liberation accepted even by others, beginning with knowledge and yoga, would be useless, because independence would never become manifest and the self would always remain in a state of bondage. Thus the sense is: enough with this idea; let such a view, which causes the non-cessation of <s>saṃsāra</s>, be rejected.

children.text: tasmāt sthitam etatpāśakṛtaṃ pāratantryaṃ pāśāś cāñjanādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore this is established: dependence is caused by the <s>pāśa</s> (bond), and the bonds are <s>añjana</s> (stain) and the rest.

children.text: sa kilātmā ||
children.translated_text: That self, indeed,

children.text: Chapter 136

yadi hy aṇur anādyavidyoparuddhacicchaktir na bhavet tadānīṃ nityavyāpakacicchaktyāspadatve satyapi kathaṃ bhavāvasthāyāṃ bhogalakṣaṇasyārthasya niṣpattaye paśoridaṃ pāśavaṃ paśūcitaṃ kalādyuttejanaṃ svasāmarthyasyānviṣyaty apekṣate muktinimittaṃ ca kathaṃ śāmbhavaṃ balam anveṣate nānyathā balaṃ pratīkṣate pāśānabhyupagame sati svabhāvata evāmalacitsvarūpatvāt tadanveṣaṇasyānarthakyāt ||
children.translated_text: For if the atomic self were not one whose power of consciousness is obstructed by beginningless ignorance, then, even while it is the locus of an eternal, all-pervasive power of consciousness, how, in the state of worldly existence, would this <s>paśu</s> require the <s>paśava</s> stimulation of its own capacity through <s>kalā</s> and the rest, suited to a <s>paśu</s>, for the accomplishment of the object marked by experience? And, as the cause of liberation, how would it seek the power belonging to <s>Śambhu</s>? Otherwise it would not wait for power, since, if bonds were not admitted, by nature it would have a stainless form of consciousness, and the search for that power would be pointless.

children.text: yataś cāvasthādvaye 'pyayaṃ pāśavaṃ vā pārameśvaraṃ vā balottejanamapekṣate tasmāt kimapyasyāsti jñānakriyāsaṃnirodhakaṃ yatkṛtaḥ svātantryavyāghātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And since in both states this self requires an excitation of power, whether <s>paśava</s> or belonging to <s>Parameśvara</s>, therefore something exists that obstructs its knowledge and action, and because of that there is an obstruction of independence.

children.text: Chapter 137
asyātmanas tadāvaraṇam añjanaṃ pañcasrotasi śaive śāstre vakṣyamāṇair nāmabhir abhihitam ||
children.translated_text: That covering of this self is called <s>añjana</s> in the five-streamed Śaiva scripture by the names that will be stated.

children.text: tattu paśubhiḥ paśuśāstrapraṇetṛbhiḥ kadācidapi na buddham ||
children.translated_text: But that has never been understood by the <s>paśu</s>s, the propounders of the <s>paśu</s>-scriptures.

children.text: atha kair nāmabhis tacchāstreṣūktam ityāha ||
children.translated_text: Now, by what names is it stated in those scriptures? He says:

children.text: Chapter 138
na ca tadekaikasminnātmani bhinnam api tv ekam anekacidāvārakaśaktiyuktam ityāha ||
children.translated_text: And he says that it is not different in each individual self, but rather one, endowed with the power to cover many consciousnesses.

children.text: Chapter 139
tadāvaraṇaṃ caturdaśavidhasyāpi bhūtasargasyaikam eva ||
children.translated_text: That covering is one alone for even the fourteenfold creation of beings.

children.text: kasmād ityatraiva viśeṣaṇadvāreṇa hetumāha anādīti yasmād vakṣyamāṇayopapattyā tat sarvabhūtānām anādi na māyīyabandhanavad āgantukam ata evaikam ||
children.translated_text: In answer to "why?" he states the reason through the very qualifier "beginningless": because, by the reasoning to be stated, it is beginningless for all beings and not adventitious like the bond produced by <s>māyā</s>; for this very reason it is one.

children.text: anekatve hi tasyācetanatvāt kāraṇāntarapūrvakatvenānāditvānupapattiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For if it were many, then, since it is insentient, its beginninglessness would be impossible, because it would have to be preceded by another cause.

children.text: na ca kāraṇāntarapūrvakatve'pi kalādivat pāramparyeṇa bandhakatvād anāditvaṃ bhaviṣyatīti vācyaṃ yathoktaṃ śrīmatkiraṇe
children.translated_text: Nor should it be said that, even if preceded by another cause, it will be beginningless because it binds through succession, like <s>kalā</s> and the rest. As is said in the venerable <s>Kiraṇa</s>:

children.text: yathānādir malas tasya karmāpyevam anādikam
children.translated_text: "Just as <s>mala</s> is beginningless for him, so too his karma is beginningless.

children.text: yadyanādi na saṃsiddhaṃ vaicitryaṃ kena hetunā ||
children.translated_text: If it were not established as beginningless, by what cause would diversity exist?

children.text: tasmādanādikaṃ karma māyāpyevaṃ bhavettathā ||
children.translated_text: Therefore karma is beginningless; and <s>māyā</s> too would likewise be so."

children.text: iti tadvirahiṇaḥ śivasyeva punarbandhāsaṃbhavāt ||
children.translated_text: Thus, because for one devoid of that, as for <s>Śiva</s>, renewed bondage would be impossible.

children.text: tatsadbhāve vā na malarahitatvamiti vakṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or, if that were present, there would be no freedom from <s>mala</s>, as we shall say.

children.text: nibiḍaṃ ghanamabhedyamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Dense" means compact and impenetrable.

children.text: vyāpakānām ātmanām āvārakatvāt mahat ||
children.translated_text: It is great because it covers the all-pervasive selves.

children.text: pratyātmasthena svasvapariṇāmakālāpasāriṇā śaktivrātena yuktam ||
children.translated_text: It is endowed with a multitude of powers, each located in a particular self and accompanying its own series of transformations.

children.text: tathā coktaṃ tattvatrayanirṇaye
children.translated_text: And so it is said in the <s>Tattvatrayanirṇaya</s>:

children.text: malaśaktayo vibhinnāḥ pratyātmaṃ caiva tadguṇāvarikāḥ
children.translated_text: "The powers of <s>mala</s> are distinct, and for each self they cover that self's qualities."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tac cāñjanam ||
children.translated_text: And that <s>añjana</s>

children.text: Chapter 140
tatteṣām ātmanām anādau kāle sthitamanādisthaṃ na tv ādimattvena sthitam ||
children.translated_text: has stood in those selves in beginningless time, beginninglessly established, not established as having a beginning.

children.text: atraiva yuktimāha arvāgveti yadi hy ādimattvenātmasusthitaṃ tadabhyupagamyate tadā tadyoge hetuḥ vācyaḥ ityadhyāhāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here he gives the reasoning itself with the word "later": if it is accepted that it abides in the selves as having a beginning, then a cause for its conjunction with them must be stated; this is to be supplied.

children.text: tad ato'nyatheti yadi tu tadañjanamato 'nyatheti hetum anapekṣyaivātmānam āśliṣyati tadānīṃ muktān apyātmano ruṇaddhi uparuddhadṛkkriyān karotīti prasaktam ||
children.translated_text: But if that <s>añjana</s>, otherwise than this, attaches itself to the self without requiring a cause, then it would follow that it also blocks liberated selves, making their seeing and action obstructed.

children.text: ko doṣa iti cet mokṣe yatnastato mṛṣeti ||
children.translated_text: If one asks, "What is the fault?" he says: effort toward liberation would then be false.

children.text: muktātmāno'pi yadi punaḥpunar malena yujyante tato gajasnānaprāye 'smin mokṣe mithyaiva yatnaḥ bhūyo 'pi malayogataḥ saṃsāritāyāḥ sambhavāt ||
children.translated_text: If even liberated selves are joined again and again with <s>mala</s>, then effort for this liberation, which would be like an elephant's bath, is indeed vain, because saṃsāra would be possible again through renewed conjunction with <s>mala</s>.

children.text: tasmān nāgantukamātmanāṃ malaṃ kiṃ tarhi anādi ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the <s>mala</s> of selves is not adventitious. What, then? It is beginningless.

children.text: tathā coktaṃ śrīmatsvāyambhuvādau
children.translated_text: And so it is said in the venerable <s>Svāyambhuva</s> and other texts:

children.text: athānādir malaḥ puṃsāṃ paśutvaṃ parikīrtitam
children.translated_text: "Now the beginningless <s>mala</s> of persons is proclaimed to be <s>paśutva</s> (the condition of a bound soul).

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: athāsyaiva yuktyantaramāha ||
children.translated_text: Now he states another argument for this very point.

children.text: Chapter 141
tadañjanam ekam anekatve pramāṇābhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: That <s>añjana</s> is one, because there is no means of proof for plurality.

children.text: yato yasmāt tādṛgiti tathāvidham anekatvapariṇāmitvādiguṇayuktaṃ yad anekaṃ ghaṭādivad utpadyamānaṃ dṛṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: Since, that is, because, 'such' means 'of that kind': whatever is many, furnished with qualities such as plurality and transformability, is seen to arise, like pots and the like.

children.text: na caitad utpattimad anādyātmāvārakatvāt ata ekam anekatve hi kāraṇapūrvakatvād asyādimattvaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: And this is not something produced, because it covers the self beginninglessly. Therefore it is one; for if it were many, since multiplicity is preceded by a cause, it would have a beginning.

children.text: pratyātmasthasvakālāntāpāyiśaktisamūhavat
children.translated_text: like a collection of powers, situated in each self and ceasing at the end of their own time.

children.text: iti yaduktaṃ tad upapādayitum āha ||
children.translated_text: In order to justify what was stated in this way, he says:

children.text: Chapter 142
ekasyāpyasyānekāḥ pratyātmasthāś citkriyāsaṃnirodhikā nityāḥ śaktaya eṣṭavyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even though this is one, many eternal powers, situated in each self and obstructing cognition and action, must be accepted.

children.text: anyathaikatve sati ekasmāt puruṣādapasṛte tasmin sarveṣāṃ tulyakālaṃ muktiḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: Otherwise, if it were single, when that had departed from one <s>puruṣa</s>, liberation would occur for all at the same time.

children.text: yatastu na muktir yaugapadyenopalabhyate tasmāt kāraṇāt tacchaktibahutvābhyupagamo yuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But since liberation is not observed simultaneously, for that reason it is proper to accept the multiplicity of its powers.

children.text: na ca tās tacchaktayaḥ svātantryeṇa rundhanti apasaranti vā kiṃ tarhi ||
children.translated_text: And those powers do not obstruct or depart independently. Rather, what then?

children.text: Chapter 143
prāvṛtīśabale karma ||
children.translated_text: karma, variegated by the covering power of the Lord.

children.text: ityādinā prāk malena nāntarīyakatayoddiṣṭāṃ parameśvararodhaśaktiṃ vyāpāreṇa lakṣayati tāsāṃ malaśaktīnāṃ citkriyāsaṃnirodhakatvalakṣaṇasya dharmasyānuvartanāddhetoḥ śaivī śaktiḥ pāśatayopacaryate ||
children.translated_text: By the passage beginning in this way, he characterizes by its operation the obstructive power of <s>Parameśvara</s>, previously indicated as inseparably connected with <s>mala</s> (impurity). Because the property defined as obstruction of cognition and action continues in those powers of <s>mala</s>, the Śaiva power is figuratively treated as a <s>pāśa</s> (bond).

children.text: na ca tatra mukhyaṃ pāśatvam ||
children.translated_text: But in that case it is not a <s>pāśa</s> in the primary sense.

children.text: kuta iti viśeṣaṇadvāreṇātraiva hetuḥ sarvānugrāhikā śiveti ||
children.translated_text: Why? Through the qualifying phrase the reason is given right here: it is <s>Śiva</s>, gracious to all.

children.text: sā hi sakalajagadanugrahasvabhāvatvena tacchreyaḥprasādhikā ||
children.translated_text: For, because its nature is to bestow grace on the entire world, it accomplishes that world's welfare.

children.text: evaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: And so:

children.text: Chapter 144
pariṇāmaśabdāt prātipadikāddhātvarthe iti ṇici kṛte pariṇāmayatīti rūpam ||
children.translated_text: From the nominal stem <s>pariṇāma</s>, when the causative affix <s>ṇic</s> is applied in the sense of the verbal root, the form is <s>pariṇāmayati</s>, 'it causes to transform.'

children.text: etāśca sarvabhūtagatās tasya sambandhinī śaktiḥ rodhāntaṃ tadadhikārakālaṃ yāvat pariṇāmena yojayatī patiśaktiḥ kārkacittviṣā hetubhūtayonmīlanaṃ yadā karoti tadānugrāhiketyucyate ||
children.translated_text: And these powers, present in all beings, are the power belonging to him. The Lord's power connects them with transformation up to the end of obstruction, for as long as the period of their authority lasts; when, by the radiance of the consciousness-sun, it causes the opening that serves as the cause, then it is called gracious.

children.text: kaśabdena mūrdhā sadānugrahaikavyāpāra īśānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the word <s>ka</s> is meant the head, <s>Īśāna</s>, whose sole constant activity is grace.

children.text: īśānamūrdheti mantraliṅgam ||
children.translated_text: The mantra indication is, '<s>Īśāna</s> is the head.'

children.text: sa eva sakalajagadanugrahe nityodyuktatvād arkeṇopamitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He himself, because he is eternally intent on bestowing grace on the whole world, is compared to the sun.

children.text: tataḥ pravṛttayā paraśreyaḥprakāśikayā jñānabhāsā tayonmīlitasvarūpāṇām aṇuvargāṇāṃ yadonmīlanam āśayavikāsanaṃ karoti tadānugrāhikā bhaṇyate ||
children.translated_text: Then, when by the light of knowledge proceeding from him and revealing supreme welfare it produces an opening, the expansion of disposition, in the classes of <s>aṇu</s>s whose nature has been opened by that light, it is said to be gracious.

children.text: atra muniḥ praśnayati ||
children.translated_text: Here the sage asks:

children.text: Chapter 145
citaḥ sakalātmānaḥ ādigrahaṇād acito malakarmamāyātatkāryāṇi ||
children.translated_text: The conscious entities are the <s>sakala</s> selves; by the inclusion of 'and so on,' the insentient things are <s>mala</s>, karma, <s>māyā</s>, and their products.

children.text: tadetatsarvaṃ sarveśitvādeva kila parameśvarasyānugrāhyam ||
children.translated_text: All this, precisely because <s>Parameśvara</s> is lord of all, is surely something to be favored by him.

children.text: tac cānugrāhyatvam eṣāṃ cidacitāṃ pāśyapāśānāṃ tulyakālaṃ na ghaṭate ||
children.translated_text: But this being an object of grace, for these conscious and insentient things, the bound and the bonds, cannot occur at the same time.

children.text: tathā hy acitāṃ pāśānāmanugrahe pāśyasya pratyuta tiraskāraḥ syāt nānugrahaḥ citām anugrahe ca tadbandhānāṃ nyagbhāvanamiti parasparavirodhitvād yugapad eṣām anugrahānupapattiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For, if grace is shown to the insentient bonds, there would instead be suppression of the bound soul, not grace; and if grace is shown to the conscious beings, their bonds are subordinated. Thus, because these are mutually opposed, simultaneous grace toward them is impossible.

children.text: tatkathaṃ sarvānugrāhikā śaktiruktā ||
children.translated_text: How, then, has the power been called gracious to all?

children.text: kiṃ ca kṛpayā sarvabhūtānām anugrahapravṛttasya patyur upakārasyāpakārakaṃ duḥkhadam āṇavādipāśajālam anugṛhya āvṛtadṛkkriyāśaktitvād asvātantryādivyathitānāṃ paramātmanāṃ bandhakānugraheṇa vyathitavyathanaṃ na yuktamiti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, when the Lord, out of compassion, is engaged in benefiting all beings, it is not proper that he should favor the net of bonds beginning with <s>āṇava</s>, which counteracts that benefit and gives pain, and thereby torment the supreme selves already distressed by lack of freedom and the like because their powers of seeing and acting are covered; tormenting the tormented by favoring their binders is not reasonable. This is the prima facie objection.

children.text: siddhāntastu ||
children.translated_text: But the established conclusion is as follows:

children.text: Chapter 146
satyaṃ cidacitām anugrāhikā śaktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is true that the power is gracious toward the conscious and the insentient.

children.text: na cāsyās tulyakālamapi tadanugraho 'nupapannaḥ parasparavirodhābhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: Nor is its grace toward them impossible even at the same time, because there is no mutual opposition.

children.text: na tv aṇor vyathanārthaṃ malasya pariṇāmarūpamanugrahaṃ karoti api tv anugrahāyaiva ||
children.translated_text: It does not cause the grace consisting in the transformation of <s>mala</s> for the sake of tormenting the <s>aṇu</s>; rather, it does so precisely for the sake of grace.

children.text: tathā hi yat kiṃcidupāyena kartumucitaṃ tan nānupāyena ||
children.translated_text: For whatever is properly to be done by some means is not to be done without a means.

children.text: ayaṃ ca sādhūpāyaḥ yaduta ||
children.translated_text: And this is the proper means, namely:

children.text: Chapter 147
yāvatkila malasyādhikāras tāvan na muktiḥ kasyacidbhavati ||
children.translated_text: As long as the authority of <s>mala</s> lasts, no one attains liberation.

children.text: tannivṛttir eva muktiśabdābhidheyā ||
children.translated_text: Its cessation alone is denoted by the word 'liberation.'

children.text: yataḥ adhikāraśca tacchakteḥ pariṇāmāt samāpyate sa ca pariṇāmas tadarhasyāpi vastuno na svato bhavituṃ śaktaḥ sarvaprakāreṇa sarvakālaṃ cācetanasya cetanaprayuktasya tattatkāryadarśanāt ||
children.translated_text: For that authority is ended by the transformation of its power; and that transformation, even of a thing fit for it, cannot occur by itself, since in every way and at every time the respective effects of an insentient thing are observed to be prompted by something conscious.

children.text: tasmāc cidanugrahasya tadarthāñjanādipariṇāmasya ca parasparam avirodha iti prathamacodyanirāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore there is no mutual contradiction between grace toward the conscious being and the transformation, for that purpose, of things such as eye-salve; thus the first objection is refuted.

children.text: atha dvitīyasya parihāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now comes the answer to the second objection.

children.text: Chapter 148

pāśāvṛtadṛkkriyāvṛttiṣv aṇuṣu tattatpāśaśaktyanuvartanadvāreṇa janmadrāvaṇādiduḥkhadāyitvād vāmo 'pi parameśvaras tadabhyudayāyaiva pravṛttatvān na duḥkhahetur avagamyate yathā vaidyaḥ kṣāraśastrādinā rogiṇaṃ vyathayann api koṭau prānte abhimatasyārogyalakṣaṇasyārthasya sādhakatvāt vyathāheturapi na duḥkhadāyitvenaiva jñāyate ||
children.translated_text: With regard to the <s>aṇu</s>s whose functions of seeing and acting are covered by bonds, <s>Parameśvara</s>, even as <s>Vāma</s>, gives sufferings such as birth and dissolution by following the powers of each respective bond; yet, because he is active solely for their advancement, he is not understood as a cause of suffering. It is like a physician: although he hurts a patient with caustics, surgical instruments, and the like, since in the end he brings about the desired result, namely health, even though he is a cause of pain he is not known simply as one who gives suffering.

children.text: nanv atyantaśuddhasvarūpasya bhagavataḥ kiṃ pāśadharmānuvartanenety āha ||
children.translated_text: But one may object: for the Blessed Lord, whose nature is utterly pure, what is the point of conforming to the properties of the bonds? He says:

children.text: Chapter 149
acidadhiṣṭhānaṃ bhagavato na vihanyate sarvagatvān maheśatayā sarvakartṛtvāc ca ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed Lord's presiding over the insentient is not impaired, because he is all-pervasive and, as <s>Maheśa</s>, the maker of all.

children.text: yatra yatra kartavyaṃ kimapyasti tatra tatra ca tādarthyam etyāpi tattatkartur adhiṣṭhānena sarvadaiva sarvaṃ karotītyuktam īśvarasiddhau ||
children.translated_text: In the establishment of <s>Īśvara</s> it was stated that wherever there is anything to be done, in each such case he always does everything, even while entering into purposiveness for that end, through his superintendence of the particular agent.

children.text: udāsta ityudāsas tasya bhāva audāsyam akartṛtvam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Indifferent" means standing aside; the state of that is indifference, that is, non-agency.

children.text: tadevaṃ yugapat sarvānugrāhitvaṃ śakteḥ prasādhya tadeva ghaṭayann anugrahaśabdārtham āha ||
children.translated_text: Thus, having established that the Power benefits all simultaneously, he now explains precisely that while giving the meaning of the word "benefit."

children.text: Chapter 150
dharmiṇo 'nugrāhyasya dharmāṇāṃ yad anuvartanaṃ so 'nugrāhakasyānugrahaḥ kramavikasvarasvarūpāṇāṃ padmānāmiva vivasvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The following of the properties of a property-bearer that is to be benefited is the benefit conferred by the benefactor, just as the sun follows the lotuses whose nature unfolds successively.

children.text: sa iti tathāvidho dharmaḥ kasyacidapi dharmiṇo nāsti yaḥ parameśvareṇa nānuvartyate nādhiṣṭhīyate tasya sarvavyāpakatvāt ||
children.translated_text: That is, there is no such property belonging to any property-bearer which is not followed, not superintended, by <s>Parameśvara</s>, because he is all-pervasive.

children.text: evaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: And accordingly:

children.text: Chapter 151

gataḥ samāptaḥ kriyādṛkpratirodhakatvarūpo 'dhikāro yasya tadgatādhikāraṃ nīhārasya tamaso malasya sambandhi vīryaṃ sāmarthyaṃ yasya tasya tathāvidhasya sataḥ paśor baddhātmano 'nugraha edhate vardhate bahulībhavati nivṛttādhikārāyāṃ malaśaktāv iti yāvat ||
children.translated_text: When the potency belonging to the frost-like darkness, the impurity, whose function consists in obstructing action and knowledge has gone, that is, ended, then the benefit of the <s>paśu</s>, the bound self, who is in that condition, increases, grows, and becomes abundant; that is to say, when the power of impurity has ceased to have its function.

children.text: anyasya tu malādeḥ pāśajālasya yat karmaṇaḥ pariṇāmitādes tādarthyaṃ tatprayojakatvaṃ tasmād anugraho bhavati ||
children.translated_text: But with respect to the other net of bonds, such as impurity and the rest, benefit arises from their purposiveness, namely from their being made to bring about the transformability of karma and so on.

children.text: baddhātmavimuktyai yat pariṇāmitāprayojakatvaṃ sa eva pāśānām anugraha ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that precisely the being made to bring about transformability for the release of the bound self is the benefit of the bonds.

children.text: evaṃ ca prakṛte kiṃ vyavasthitam ityāha ||
children.translated_text: And in this way, he states what has been settled in the present context.

children.text: Chapter 152

malasya sādhikārasyety āṇavasyāñjanasyādhikāranivṛttes tadbhāvabhāvinyā anādikālīnāyāḥ parameśvararodhaśakter apagamonmukhyāḥ paricyutau kiṃcic chithilībhāve sati boddhṛtvadharmānuvartanam ātmano'nugrahaḥ pariṇāmitvadharmānuvartanaṃ pāśānāmiti ||
children.translated_text: When the impurity still possessed of function, that is, the atomic collyrium, undergoes some slipping away, some loosening, because its function has ceased, and because the beginningless power of obstruction toward <s>Parameśvara</s>, which exists when that impurity exists, is turned toward disappearance, then the following of the soul's property of being a knower is the benefit of the self; and the following of the property of transformability is the benefit of the bonds.

children.text: upasaṃharann āha ||
children.translated_text: Summing up, he says:

children.text: Chapter 153
ityevam uktayā yuktyā yaugapadyena cidacitor anugraho na viruddhaḥ kramāt sughaṭa eva na durupapādaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by the reasoning stated above, the simultaneous benefiting of the conscious and the insentient is not contradictory; in sequence, it is perfectly possible and not difficult to explain.

children.text: malavac ca māyāyāśca kalādikṣityantasvādhikārasahitāyāḥ kalādyāvirbhāvalakṣaṇas tadupasaṃhārātmakaśca karmaṇastu phaladānaunmukhyāpādanātmakaḥ so 'yamanugraho māyākarmaṇor anukto 'pyukta eva jñeyaḥ
children.translated_text: And just as in the case of impurity, this benefit, though not explicitly stated, should be understood as stated for <s>māyā</s> and karma: for <s>māyā</s>, together with its own function extending from <s>kalā</s> down to earth, it consists in the manifestation beginning with <s>kalā</s> and in the withdrawal of those principles; while for karma it consists in causing readiness to give its fruit.

children.text: sarvathā sarvadā yasmāc citprayojyam acetanam
children.translated_text: Because, in every way and always, the insentient is impelled by consciousness,

children.text: iti sāmānyena sarvasyaivoktatvād iti ||
children.translated_text: since by this general statement everything whatsoever has been stated.

children.text: Chapter 154

athetyāṇavarodhaśaktyākhyapāśadvayavicārānantaram indriyairantaḥkaraṇabahiṣkaraṇaiḥ śarīreṇa ca sthūlasūkṣmarūpeṇa arthaiś cendriyārthair viṣayair yo 'yaṃ cidātmano yogaḥ tasyāgāmibhāvād utpattimattvāt kāraṇaṃ nimittam anumīyate na hy utpattimaccāhetukaṃ kiṃcid bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Now, after the examination of the two bonds called the atomic power and the obstructing power, a cause, an occasion, is inferred for this conjunction of the conscious self with the senses, the inner and outer instruments, with the body in its gross and subtle forms, and with objects, the sense-objects that are objects of experience, because that conjunction is something that will arise in the future and therefore has origination; for nothing that has origination is without a cause.

children.text: itthaṃ sāmānyena kāraṇamātraṃ prasādhya tadviśeṣaṃ vaktum āha ||
children.translated_text: Having in this way established in general that there is some cause, he speaks of that specific cause.

children.text: Chapter 155
tasyendriyaśarīrārthaiś citāṃ yogasya yat suranaratiryagādiniyatasthānavartitvam
children.translated_text: Its conjunction of selves with senses, body, and objects consists in occupying fixed stations such as gods, humans, and animals.

children.text: yacca vailakṣaṇyaṃ vicitrāṇi hi prāṇināṃ śarīrāṇīndriyāṇi viṣayāś ca dṛśyante tatra jātidigdeśakālādivaicitryaṃ tāvat prasiddham ||
children.translated_text: And there is distinctness; indeed the bodies, senses, and objects of living beings are seen to be varied. First, variety of birth, direction, place, time, and so on is well known.

children.text: indriyavaicitryam api yathā parāvṛttajihvatvaṃ gajānāṃ cakṣuḥśravatvaṃ bhujaṃgamānām anālokālokitvam ulūkādīnāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ ca keṣāṃcid vipuladṛśām apyadarśanam andhaprāyāṇām api sūkṣmārthadarśitvam iti ||
children.translated_text: Variety among the senses too is seen, for example the turned-back tongue of elephants, the eye-like hearing of snakes, the seeing in darkness of owls and the like, and, among some humans, non-seeing even though they have large eyes, while others, though almost blind, perceive subtle things.

children.text: viṣayavaicitryaṃ tu yathājaladharanipatajjalakaṇopajīvitvaṃ cātakānāṃ mayūrāṇām avakarāhāratvaṃ kukkuṭādīnāṃ ca kamalakiñjalkarasāsvādanaṃ madhukarasārasānām ityādi
children.translated_text: Variety among objects is as follows: the cātakas live on drops of water falling from clouds; peacocks, chickens, and the like feed on refuse; and bees and sārasa birds taste the nectar of lotus filaments, and so on.

children.text: yataśca kṣaṇikatvam anityatā dehādeḥ ||
children.translated_text: And because there is momentariness, impermanence, of the body and the like.

children.text: yasmācca pratipuruṣanaiyatyam na hi śarīrendriyaviṣayāṇāṃ sādhāraṇyaṃ bhogasāmyaprasaṅgāt ||
children.translated_text: And because there is fixed allotment for each person; for bodies, senses, and objects cannot be common, since that would imply sameness of experience.

children.text: yataśca tat saṃtatatvaṃ tattatprāṇisaṃtatatvena kila janmāntare 'pi śarīrendriyādi sthitaṃ yathā jātyāyurbhogapradebhyaḥ karmabhyaḥ āyuḥpradasyopakṣīṇatvāt mṛtasyāpi tasyaiva jātibhogade karmaṇī saṃtatyā tv avatiṣṭhete na tv anyam upasarpataḥ tābhyāṃ ca tattajjātidehendriyayogaḥ kriyate ||
children.translated_text: And because that is continuous: since the body, senses, and so forth continue as the particular succession of each living being even in another birth. For example, when a man dies because the karma that gives lifespan has been exhausted, the same karmas that give birth and experience remain continuously and do not pass over to someone else; and by them the conjunction with the body and senses belonging to that particular birth is produced.

children.text: yata evaṃ tasmāt kāraṇāt tat tad api karma tādṛgguṇaṃ tattaddeśavartino vicitrān vinaśvarān pratyātmaniyatān bhavāntarabhāvinaś ca dehendriyārthān dātuṃ kṣamam ityevam anumīyate kāraṇāsambhavināṃ guṇānāṃ kāryeṣvanupalabdheḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since this is so, therefore from that cause it is inferred that each particular karma too possesses such a quality, being capable of giving bodies, senses, and objects that exist in particular places, are varied, perishable, fixed to each self, and occur in another existence; for qualities that cannot belong to the cause are not observed in the effects.

children.text: kiṃca ||
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: Chapter 156
īśaśabdanalakṣaṇayoktām aiśvarīṃ rodhaśaktim avidyāṃ ca malalakṣaṇām ādigrahaṇānmāyāṃ ca yasmād avaśyaṃ phaladāne 'pekṣate tasmāt sahakāritvam asya karmaṇaḥ na tu svātantryam ācaitanyādityuktam ||
children.translated_text: Because this karma necessarily depends, in the giving of its fruit, on the sovereign obstructing power stated by implication through the word <s>Īśa</s>, on ignorance characterized as impurity, and, through the inclusion of "and so on," on <s>māyā</s> as well, it has the status of an auxiliary cause, not independence, since it is insentient. This has been stated.

children.text: ata evāsyāpekṣaṇam aupacārikaṃ na tu kumbhakārasya sūtradaṇḍacakrādyapekṣaṇatulyam ||
children.translated_text: For this very reason its requiring this is figurative, not like a potter's requiring a cord, stick, wheel, and so on.

children.text: anyathā kumbhakārasyāpi sūtradaṇḍādyapekṣitvāt sahakāritvaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: Otherwise, because the potter too requires a cord, stick, and the like, he would have the status of an auxiliary cause.

children.text: kiṃca vyāpāreṇa yajjanyam ataḥ kriyata iti karma saukṣmyāccādṛṣṭam ityucyate ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, what is produced by activity is called <s>karman</s>, since it is 'done'; and because of its subtlety it is called the unseen.

children.text: tacca ||
children.translated_text: And that is:

children.text: Chapter 157
janakaṃ nimittatayā dehendriyabhuvanādeḥ yataḥ karmaphalopabhogāyaiva tattattanukaraṇādiyogotpādaḥ ||
children.translated_text: productive, as an efficient cause, of the body, the senses, the world, and so on, since the conjunction with each particular body, instrument, and the like arises solely for the experience of the fruit of karma.

children.text: dhārakatvaṃ ca tasyaiva pratiniyatakālasya mātṛtvena ||
children.translated_text: And its sustaining power belongs to that very thing, because it measures out a fixed time.

children.text: bhogyaṃ ca tatphaladvāreṇa ||
children.translated_text: And it is an object of experience through the mediation of its fruit.

children.text: kiṃcādhyātmādi trayaṃ sādhanaṃ yasya tat tathā ||
children.translated_text: Furthermore, that is so when the triad beginning with the inner/self-related is its means.

children.text: tatrādhyātmaśabdenāntaḥkaraṇatayā saṃnikarṣeṇātmānam adhikṛtya yadvartate tanmana ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Here, by the word <s>adhyātma</s>, the inner/self-related, what operates with respect to the self through close proximity as the internal organ is called mind.

children.text: ādigrahaṇād vākkāyau gṛhyete ||
children.translated_text: By the inclusion of 'and so on,' speech and body are understood as well.

children.text: evaṃ ca manovākkāyāḥ sādhanaṃ yasya tat yathākramam iṣṭadevatānudhyānanamaskārastotrapāṭhayajanādirūpadharmātmakaṃ karma parasvājihīrṣātatpravādatadupaghātādayo yathāsaṃkhyaṃ manovākkāyakarmakṛtāḥ sādhanaṃ yasya tad adharmātmakam ||
children.translated_text: Thus <s>dharma</s>-type karman has mind, speech, and body as its means in the forms, respectively, of meditation on the chosen deity, reverence, recitation of hymns, worship, and the like; and <s>adharma</s>-type karman has as its means the desire to seize another's property, slander of that person, injury to that person, and so on, produced respectively by actions of mind, speech, and body.

children.text: yad vādhyātmabhūtadaivāni hetutayādhikṛtyādhyātmam adhibhūtam adhidaivataṃ ca yat sukhaduḥkham utpadyate tasya trividhasyāpi sādhanam ||
children.translated_text: Or else, it is the means for the threefold pleasure and pain, inner, elemental, and divine, that arise by taking the inner, beings, and deities as causes.

children.text: karmavaśāddhi cetaḥprasādādyudvegādi cādhyātmikaṃ sukhaduḥkham udeti ādhibhautikaṃ cāṅganāsambhogagajasiṃhādyabhibhavarūpam ādhidaivikaṃ cābhimatānabhimatavātavarṣātapādikṛtam ||
children.translated_text: For, under the control of karma, inner pleasure and pain arise as serenity of mind and the like, or agitation and the like; elemental pleasure and pain take the form of union with women or overpowering by elephants, lions, and so forth; and divine pleasure and pain are caused by favorable or unfavorable wind, rain, heat, and the like.

children.text: Chapter 158
tacca karma dharmādharmasvarūpaṃ satyānṛtaprakṛtitvāt satyaprakṛti karma dharmarūpam anṛtaprakṛti adharmātmakaṃ svāpe ca sarvabhūtasaṃhārakāle vipākaṃ pariṇāmam abhitaḥ samantād eti ||
children.translated_text: And this karman is of the nature of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> because it has true and untrue forms: karman of true form is <s>dharma</s>, while karman of untrue form is <s>adharma</s>. And in cosmic sleep, at the time when all beings are withdrawn, it fully enters maturation, that is, transformation.

children.text: sṛṣṭāv iti sṛṣṭisamanantaram evāsya yathāsvaṃ bhogaḥ pravartate ante ca saṃhāre māyāyāṃ saṃskārarūpatayā vartate
children.translated_text: 'At creation' means that immediately after creation its appropriate experience begins; and at the end, at dissolution, it exists in <s>māyā</s> in the form of residual impressions.

children.text: na cābhuktaṃ tad vinaśyati ||
children.translated_text: And if it has not been experienced, it does not perish.

children.text: upasaṃhāram āha ||
children.translated_text: He states the summary.

children.text: Chapter 159
itthaṃpratipāditasvarūpam etat karma māyādikālāgnyantādhvavartidehendriyārthapravartakam ityatraivāsya prabhaviṣṇutā māyordhvaṃ praśamanāt ||
children.translated_text: This karman, whose nature has thus been explained, sets in motion the bodies, senses, and objects that exist in the path extending from <s>māyā</s> down to <s>Kālāgni</s>; its power extends only so far, because above <s>māyā</s> it becomes quiescent.

children.text: taccaitad yadyapi vyāpārajanyaṃ tathāpi pravāhanityatvād ādimattvaṃ nāsyopapadyata iti carcitaprāyam ||
children.translated_text: And although this karman is produced by activity, still, because its stream is eternal, beginning-ness is not possible for it; this has already been discussed for the most part.

children.text: kiṃca etat karma śubhasvarūpatvāt puṇyavyañjakam api sat rodhi rodhakaṃ saṃsārakāraṇam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, because this karman has an auspicious nature, even while it manifests merit, it is obstructive, a blocker, that is, a cause of saṃsāra.

children.text: kuta ityāha sadyanna muktaye yasmāt puṇyātmakam api karma sat vidyamānaṃ na muktaye nāpavargāya api tu tatpratibandhāyaiva kalpate yat karmakṣayāt tatsāmyād vā śaktipātānusārasamāsāditānugrahāṇām eva kaivalyam ||
children.translated_text: Why? He says, 'Though good, it is not for liberation.' Because even meritorious karman, while present, is not for liberation or release, but rather serves only as an obstacle to it; for <s>kaivalya</s> belongs only to those who have obtained grace in accordance with <s>śaktipāta</s>, through the exhaustion of karma or through its equilibrium.

children.text: nanu sadyanna muktaye ityayuktam uktaṃ satyapi karmaṇi tatsāmyānmukter āmnātatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Objection: the statement 'though good, it is not for liberation' is improper, since liberation is taught when karma still exists, because of its equilibrium.

children.text: yaduktaṃ śrīmatkiraṇe
children.translated_text: As is said in the venerable <s>Kiraṇa</s>:

children.text: same karmaṇi saṃjāte kālāntaravaśāttataḥ
children.translated_text: 'When karma has become equal, then, under the power of a later time,

children.text: tīvraśaktinipātena guruṇā dīkṣito yadā ||
children.translated_text: when he is initiated by a guru through an intense descent of power,

children.text: sarvajñaḥ sa śivo yadvat
children.translated_text: he is omniscient, just like <s>Śiva</s>.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: naiṣa doṣastathāvidhasya karmaṇaḥ sato 'pyasattvaṃ parasparapratibaddhaśaktitvenāphalatvāt dīkṣottarakālakṛtakarmavat ||
children.translated_text: This is not a fault, because karman of that sort, though existent, is as good as non-existent, since it does not bear fruit because its powers are mutually obstructed, like karman performed after <s>dīkṣā</s>.

children.text: yaduktaṃ kheṭakanandanena
children.translated_text: As <s>Kheṭakanandana</s> has said:

children.text: kṛtam api phalāya na syād dīkṣoparyūṣaroptabījam iva
children.translated_text: 'Even when performed, it is not for fruit, like a seed sown on barren ground after initiation,

children.text: balavadviśeṣaśāstravyatikarajātaṃ vihāya karmaikam ||
children.translated_text: except for the single karman that arises from transgressing a powerful and specific scriptural rule.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: Chapter 160
athaśabdaścānantarye pāśapadārthaparīkṣādhikāre karmapāśavicārānantaraṃ granthyātmano māyākhyasya pāśasya kiṃcit saṃkṣiptaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ kathyate ||
children.translated_text: And the word 'now' indicates immediate sequence: in the section examining the category of <s>pāśa</s>, after the discussion of the karmic bond, a somewhat concise definition is given of the bond called <s>māyā</s>, whose nature is a knot.

children.text: asya cānantaraprakaraṇopasaṃhāre māyāśabdopakṣepāt pāṭalikaḥ sambandho jñeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And because the word <s>māyā</s> is introduced in the conclusion of the immediately preceding section, its connection with this chapter should be understood.

children.text: padārthādisambandhacatuṣṭayaṃ tu prāg uktam ||
children.translated_text: But the fourfold connection beginning with that of the categories has been stated before.

children.text: sarvajñavākyena pratipannasyeti prāvṛtīśabale karma māyā ityādinoddeśasūtreṇa vaktum abhyupagatasya kiṃcid iti nahi sakalaṃ māyālakṣaṇaṃ saṃkṣepeṇāpyabhidhātuṃ śakyam ||
children.translated_text: The word 'somewhat' means that only a little is to be stated of what is established by the omniscient one's statement and was undertaken for explanation by the summary sūtra beginning 'prāvṛtīśabale karma māyā'; for the whole definition of <s>māyā</s> cannot be expressed even in brief.

children.text: tathā coktaṃ tatrabhavadbṛhaspatipādaiḥ
children.translated_text: And so the venerable <s>Bṛhaspatipāda</s> has said:

children.text: api sarvasiddhivācaḥ kṣīyeran dīrghakālam udgīrṇāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Even the words of all accomplished beings, poured forth for a long time, would be exhausted;

children.text: māyāyām ānantyān nocyeta srotasāṃ saṃkhyā ||
children.translated_text: because of the infinitude in <s>māyā</s>, the number of the streams could not be stated.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: yuktyāpi leśata iti nāgamamātreṇa kevalena api tu stokād anumānopapannam api tallakṣaṇam ucyata ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Also by reasoning, in a small measure' means that its definition is stated not solely by scripture alone, but also, to a small extent, as supported by inference.

children.text: Chapter 161

tat granthitattvam ekaṃ paramakāraṇatvād anekatve pramāṇābhāvācca aśivaṃ mohakatvāt bījaṃ jagata ityupādānakāraṇaṃ vividhaśaktiyuktaṃ ca sahakāriṇāṃ karmaṇām adhikārāntaṃ yāvat saṃruṇaddhi aṇūn badhnāti tacchīlamiti sahakāryadhikārāntasaṃrodhi karmābhāve granthitattvasyāpravṛtteḥ ||
children.translated_text: That knot-principle is one, because it is the supreme cause and because there is no means of proof for plurality; it is non-<s>Śiva</s> because it deludes; it is the seed of the world, that is, the material cause, and it is endowed with various powers. It shuts in, that is, binds, the <s>aṇu</s>s until the authority of the assisting karmas comes to an end; this is its character, so it is one that confines until the end of the authority of its assistants, because the knot-principle does not become active when karma is absent as an assistant.

children.text: vyāpi ca tat sarvagataṃ svakāryavyāpakatvena anaśvaraṃ nityatvāt mahāpralaye 'pi ātmavad īśvaravacca tasyāvasthānāt ||
children.translated_text: And it is pervasive, all-pervading through its pervasion of its own effects; it is imperishable because it is eternal, since it remains even at the great dissolution, like the self and like <s>Īśvara</s>.

children.text: tad uktaṃ tattvatrayanirṇaye
children.translated_text: This has been said in the <s>Tattvatrayanirṇaya</s>:

children.text: śambhuḥ puruṣo māyā nityaṃ vibhu kartṛśaktiyuktaṃ ca
children.translated_text: <s>Śambhu</s>, <s>puruṣa</s>, and <s>māyā</s> are eternal, pervasive, and endowed with the power of agency;

children.text: supte'pi vikṛtijāte tritayaṃ jāgarti tattvānām ||
children.translated_text: even when the class of evolutes is asleep, the triad of principles remains awake.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: yuktyāpi leśata ityuktam atas tāṃ yuktiṃ darśayati ||
children.translated_text: It was said, "by reasoning also, in brief"; therefore he shows that reasoning.

children.text: Chapter 162
saṃniveśādimattvād utpattimattvaṃ kila jagataḥ kartāram anumāpayati ||
children.translated_text: Because the world has arrangement and the like, its being produced indeed causes one to infer a maker.

children.text: tenaivotpattidharmakatvenopādānam apyanumīyate ||
children.translated_text: By that same property of being subject to production, a material cause too is inferred.

children.text: nahi utpattimatām upādānakāraṇaṃ vinotpattir dṛṣṭā yathā paṭādes tantvādyabhāve ||
children.translated_text: For the production of things that are produced is not observed without a material cause, as in the case of cloth and the like when threads and so on are absent.

children.text: kiṃca ||
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: Chapter 163

tacca granthitattvam acetanam acetanasyaiva tatkāryasya kalāder upalambhāt anyathetyacetanatatkāryopalambhe 'pi tasya cetanatvābhyupagame kāraṇāniyamalakṣaṇaḥ sarvahara iti sarvānumānocchedakaḥ sakalavyavahāraharaḥ ko 'pi doṣaḥ prāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And that <s>granthitattva</s> (knotted principle) is insentient, because its effect, <s>kalā</s> and the rest, is itself observed to be insentient. Otherwise, if, even when an insentient effect is observed, that cause were accepted as sentient, there would result some all-destroying fault, characterized by the absence of any fixed rule for causes, cutting off every inference and destroying all practical activity.

children.text: prāguddiṣṭam avinaśvaratvaṃ vyāpitvaṃ ca sādhayituṃ yuktim āha ||
children.translated_text: To establish the previously stated imperishability and pervasiveness, he states the reasoning.

children.text: Chapter 164
jagatsaṃhāre yadyupādānakāraṇasya māyākhyasyāpi nāśaḥ syāt tatpunaḥ sargādau kasmād upādānājjagad utpadyate ||
children.translated_text: If, at the dissolution of the world, even the material cause called <s>māyā</s> were destroyed, then from what material cause would the world arise again at the beginning of creation?

children.text: ato nāsyānityatvam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore it is not impermanent.

children.text: athocyate sargādāv upādānam api devaḥ srakṣyatīti
children.translated_text: If it is said, "At the beginning of creation, God will create the material cause too,"

children.text: naitad yuktam evaṃ hi sati tatkāryasyeva tasyāpyupādānaṃ vinānutpatter upādānāntaraṃ parikalpyaṃ tasyāpyanyad ityanavasthā syāt ||
children.translated_text: this is not reasonable. For if that were so, since it too, like its effect, could not arise without a material cause, another material cause would have to be imagined, and for that another; thus there would be an infinite regress.

children.text: vyāptyupasaṃhāreṇa śaktirūpatayā tv avasthāne na kaścid doṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But if it remains in the form of power when its pervasion is withdrawn, there is no fault.

children.text: evam asyāvyāpitve sarvatomukhasya kāryasyānutpādaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, if it were not pervasive, the effect that faces every direction would not arise.

children.text: ato vyāpakatvam avaśyam abhyupeyam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore pervasiveness must necessarily be accepted.

children.text: tathaikatve yuktyupanyāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, the presentation of reasoning concerning its oneness is as follows.

children.text: Chapter 165
yad yad anekam acetanaṃ tat tat ghaṭapaṭādivad utpattimad dṛṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: Whatever is many and insentient is seen to be produced, like pots, cloths, and the like.

children.text: idaṃ tu notpattimanna kāraṇajanyaṃ paramakāraṇatvāt ata ekam ||
children.translated_text: But this is not produced, not generated by a cause, because it is the ultimate cause; therefore it is one.

children.text: nahi paramakāraṇāni bahulībhavantīti ||
children.translated_text: For ultimate causes do not become numerous.

children.text: nanu jagadutpattau paraparikalpitaparamāṇvādivad upādānakāraṇabahulatvaṃ yadi syāt tataḥ ko doṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Objection: if, in the production of the world, there were a plurality of material causes, as with the atoms and the like imagined by others, what fault would follow?

children.text: tathāhi ||
children.translated_text: For example:

children.text: Chapter 166
bahubhyo'pi hi tantubhyaḥ paṭasyaikasyotpattir dṛṣṭā ||
children.translated_text: Even from many threads, the production of a single cloth is observed.

children.text: tadvacca jagat sarvam anekasmāt kāraṇād utpadyatāṃ kiṃ granthyātmakaparamakāraṇakalpanayeti codyam ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, let the whole world arise from many causes. What need is there to posit an ultimate cause in the form of the <s>granthi</s> (knot)? This is the objection.

children.text: atra parihāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here is the reply.

children.text: Chapter 167
yat tadbhavatānekatantvātmakaṃ kāraṇaṃ paṭasyoktaṃ tad anekam apyekasmāt tūlakārpāsādidravyād utpannatvād ekam ||
children.translated_text: That cause in the form of many threads, which you stated for a cloth, though multiple, is one because it has arisen from one substance, such as cotton fiber or cotton.

children.text: yathā caikasmāt tūlakārpāsādidravyād anekākārapaṭādyutpattiḥ evaṃ paramakāraṇāt sargasthitilayādhārākhyāt sargādau māyātattvājjagadutpattir iti na kaścid doṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And just as cloth and the like in many forms arise from one substance such as cotton fiber or cotton, so the world arises at the beginning of creation from the ultimate cause called the support of creation, maintenance, and dissolution, namely the <s>māyātattva</s>. Thus there is no fault.

children.text: paramātmana eva sakāśāccidacidāvirbhāvatirobhāvāv iti yeṣāṃ pakṣas tān pratikṣipati ||
children.translated_text: He rejects those whose position is that the manifestation and disappearance of the sentient and the insentient occur from the <s>Paramātman</s> alone.

children.text: Chapter 168
citsvabhāvakāddhetor yair acitām apyudbhavo 'bhyupagataḥ tair dhūmājjalānumānaṃ kiṃ na kriyate kāryakāraṇapratītiniyamāsaṃbhave saty atatsvabhāvād api tatsvabhāvasyotpattiprāpteḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those by whom the arising even of insentient things is accepted from a cause whose nature is consciousness: why do they not infer water from smoke? For if the fixed rule in the cognition of effect and cause is impossible, something of one nature would be able to arise even from what is not of that nature.

children.text: yathā na dṛṣṭā dhūmālliṅgāt kadācid api jalaprāptiḥ tathā hy acitsvabhāvasya svaviruddhāccitsvabhāvānnotpattir dṛṣṭā ||
children.translated_text: Just as the obtaining of water from the sign smoke has never been seen, so the production of what has an insentient nature from what has the nature of consciousness, its own opposite, is not seen.

children.text: atatsvabhāvāt tatsvabhāvasyotpattau sarvaṃ sarvasmād utpadyeta ||
children.translated_text: If something of one nature arose from what does not have that nature, everything would arise from everything.

children.text: paramāṇukāraṇaṃ jagad iti yeṣām abhyupagamas tān pratyāha ||
children.translated_text: Against those whose accepted view is that the world has atoms as its cause, he says:

children.text: Chapter 169
yeṣāṃ bhūtāvadhi pṛthivyādisthityantaṃ pāramāṇavaṃ jagat teṣāṃ pūrvoditāt dravyādiṣaṭpadārthajñānāt ṣoḍaśapadārthāvabodhād vā niḥśreyasāvāpter hetor jñānasūkṣmatā prabodhataikṣṇyaṃ jñātam ||
children.translated_text: For those whose atomic world is limited by the elements, ending with the condition of earth and the rest, the subtlety of their knowledge, the sharpness of their awakening, concerning the means to the attainment of the highest good is already known from the previously stated knowledge of the six categories beginning with substance, or from the understanding of the sixteen categories.

children.text: tādṛgvidhasūkṣmadarśinyā buddhyā paramāṇukāraṇatām abhidadhānā na te vācyatām arhanti ||
children.translated_text: When they declare atoms to be the cause with an intellect capable of such subtle seeing, they do not deserve to be addressed.

children.text: paramāṇūnāṃ kaiścit paramāṇukataiva niṣiddhā ṣaṭke yugapad yogāt ṣaḍaṃśatvasyāparihāryatvāt ||
children.translated_text: The very atomicity of atoms has been denied by some, because when a group of six is in simultaneous conjunction, the possession of six parts is unavoidable.

children.text: kiṃca ācaitanye sati anekatvāt ghaṭapaṭādivat teṣām api kāraṇapūrvakatvena bhāvyam iti ca kutaḥ paramakāraṇatā ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, since they are insentient and many, they too must be preceded by a cause, like pots and cloths. How then could they be the ultimate cause?

children.text: tataśca na tatprakṛtikatvaṃ jagataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Consequently, the world does not have them as its <s>prakṛti</s> (material source).

children.text: nanu yatas tāvanmātāpitṛsambandhibhyo dehendriyādibhyas tattatsvasadṛśaśarīrakaraṇādi utpadyamānam upalabhyate tataḥ kim adṛṣṭena māyādinā kāraṇena kﾱptenetyāśaṅkyāha ||
children.translated_text: Now, since bodies, senses, and the like corresponding to each particular case are observed to arise from bodies, senses, and so on connected with mother and father, why posit an unseen cause such as <s>māyā</s>? Anticipating this objection, he says:

children.text: Chapter 170

mātāpitṛsaṃśleṣaśarīrendriyādikāraṇakaṃ jantūnāṃ śarīrendriyādi tadbhāve bhāvāttadabhāve cābhāvāditi yadyabhimataṃ tadastu kiṃtvetatpraṣṭavyo bhavān tannikhilātyaye sarvasaṃhāre dehendriyādyutpatteḥ kīdṛśī gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: If it is accepted that the bodies, senses, and so on of living beings are caused by the conjunction of mother and father, and by body, senses, and the like, because they exist when those exist and are absent when those are absent, let that be so. But you must be asked this: when all of that has completely perished, at the universal dissolution, what possibility is there for the production of bodies, senses, and the like?

children.text: atha sakrama eva sarvabhāvānāṃ nāśaḥ natu yugapatsarvasaṃhāra ityucyate ||
children.translated_text: Now, if it is said that the destruction of all entities is certainly successive, but that there is not a simultaneous dissolution of all,

children.text: tad ayuktaṃ śrutismṛtītihāsapurāṇādisadāgamagīyamānasya saṃhārasyāpahnotum aśakyatvāt ||
children.translated_text: that is not correct, because it is impossible to deny the dissolution proclaimed in the true scriptures such as śruti, smṛti, itihāsa, purāṇa, and the rest.

children.text: tadapahnave ca prathamasṛṣṭir api neṣṭā ||
children.translated_text: And if that is denied, an initial creation too is not accepted.

children.text: tataś ca sṛṣṭisaṃhārau jagato na sambhavata iti bruvāṇaḥ sarvajñatām eva jahyāt ||
children.translated_text: Consequently, one who says that the creation and dissolution of the world are impossible would abandon omniscience itself.

children.text: atha kathaṃ saṃhārābhāvam abhidadhato mithyāvāditvam ityāha ||
children.translated_text: Now he says how one who states the absence of dissolution would be speaking falsely.

children.text: Chapter 171
sarvajñena hi svasya vacasaḥ pramāṇopapannatayā parīkṣaṇaṃ pratijñātam ||
children.translated_text: For the omniscient one has declared that his own word is to be examined as being supported by valid means of knowledge.

children.text: yadāha
children.translated_text: As he says:

children.text: tāpācchedānnikarṣācca suvarṇamiva sarvataḥ
children.translated_text: Just as gold is tested in every way by heating, cutting, and rubbing,

children.text: parīkṣya bhikṣavo grāhyaṃ madvaco natu gauravāt ||
children.translated_text: so, monks, my word should be accepted after examination, not out of reverence.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.
