children.text: iyaṃ tu saṃhārasambhave nirbādhā tāvad upapattir yaduta yasya dharmiṇo vahnyādeḥ kvāpyekadeśe dhūmaprakāśadāhādidharmo dṛṣṭaḥ sa tasya sarvatrotpadyamānaḥ kena niṣidhyate tataśca durbhikṣamārīkṛtabhaṅgādinā ekadeśe jantusaṃghātasya kramikāṃ koṭiśo vipattim upalabhya kṛtsnajagatsaṃhārakālaḥ sadāgamodito 'pi anumānenolliṅgyate ||
children.translated_text: But, once dissolution is possible, this much is an unobstructed reasoning: namely, when a property such as smoke, light, or burning has been seen somewhere in one part of a property-bearer such as fire, who can prevent it from arising everywhere in that same thing? Therefore, after observing in one region the successive destruction of hosts of living beings by the tens of millions through famine, pestilence, destructive calamity, and the like, the time of the dissolution of the whole world, also taught by the true scriptures, is indicated by inference.

children.text: tadānīṃ ca māyāyāmupasaṃhṛtāni sarvakāryāṇyāsannityāha ||
children.translated_text: And he says that at that time all effects are withdrawn into <s>māyā</s>.

children.text: Chapter 172
prāguktābhir upapattibhir nityatvavyāpakatvādiguṇayuktaṃ yattu māyākhyaṃ kāraṇam upapāditaṃ tadāśrayāṇi tanukaraṇabhuvanādīni saṃhārakāle śaktirūpāṇyavatiṣṭhante ||
children.translated_text: The cause called <s>māyā</s>, endowed with qualities such as permanence and pervasiveness, was established by the arguments stated earlier; things based on it, such as bodies, instruments, and worlds, remain at the time of dissolution in the form of powers.

children.text: sṛṣṭau tu vyaktisvarūpāṇi svasvaprayojananiṣpattaye savyāpārāṇi bhavantīti sarvaṃ sustham ||
children.translated_text: But at creation they have the nature of manifestation and become active for the accomplishment of their respective purposes; thus everything is coherent.

children.text: atra muniḥ satkāryavādam asahamānaḥ praśnayati ||
children.translated_text: Here the sage, unable to accept <s>satkāryavāda</s> (the doctrine that the effect exists in the cause), asks:

children.text: Chapter 173
yad etacchaktirūpatayā māyākhye paramakāraṇe jagato 'vasthānakāraṇam uktaṃ tannopapadyate ||
children.translated_text: What was stated as the reason for the world's abiding in the supreme cause called <s>māyā</s> in the form of powers is not tenable.

children.text: tathāhi dṛṣṭavadadṛṣṭakalpanā kartavyā dṛśyate ca tantuturīvemādikārakagrahaṇam avidyamānapaṭasyārthinaḥ natu paṭasadbhāve sati ||
children.translated_text: For this is so: what is unseen should be postulated in conformity with what is seen, and we observe one who wants a cloth that does not yet exist taking up causal factors such as thread, shuttle, and loom, but not when the cloth already exists.

children.text: paṭasya hi sattve sati kārakaśabdo 'pi tantvāder nopapannaḥ vidyamānatvād eva ||
children.translated_text: For when the cloth exists, even the term 'causal factor' is not appropriate for the threads and the like, precisely because the cloth is already present.

children.text: asadutpattau hi kārakavastunaḥ sāphalyaṃ nānyatheti ||
children.translated_text: For only if a nonexistent effect is produced do the causal objects have a purpose, and not otherwise.

children.text: atra parihāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here is the reply:

children.text: Chapter 174
āstāṃ tāvat sadutpattiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let the production of an existent thing stand aside for the moment.

children.text: asadutpattau kārakavastunaḥ turītantuvemādeḥ sāphalyābhyupagame sarvebhyo bhāvebhyaḥ sarvaḥ sarvam abhīpsitaṃ kim iti notpādayati ||
children.translated_text: If, in the production of a nonexistent thing, the usefulness of causal objects such as shuttle, thread, and loom is accepted, why does everyone not produce every desired thing from all entities?

children.text: atha na śakyaṃ sarvasmāt sarvam utpādayituṃ kutaścit kasyacit kāryasyotpattidarśanāt ||
children.translated_text: If it is said that everything cannot be produced from everything, because the production of a particular effect is observed from some particular thing,

children.text: evaṃ tarhi yasmādeva kāraṇād yad utpadyate tasmād eva tat nānyasmāt ||
children.translated_text: then, in that case, whatever arises from a particular cause arises from that alone, and not from another.

children.text: tatra kiṃ niyāmakaṃ bhavatāṃ nahi tasminkāraṇe kim apyanyanniyāmakam utpaśyāmo yenābhijñātenānyad anādṛtya tadeva tadutpattyarthino gṛhṇīmahi ||
children.translated_text: What, on your view, is the regulator there? For we do not see anything else in that cause as a regulator, by recognizing which we would disregard another thing and take that very cause for the sake of producing that effect.

children.text: atha sarvasmāt sarvotpattiprasaṅgabhayāt tasyaiva kāraṇasya tatkāryajanikā śaktir nānyasyeti ||
children.translated_text: If, then, out of fear of the consequence that everything would arise from everything, you say that only that cause, and not another, has the power that produces that effect,

children.text: tad etat siddhaṃ sādhyata ityāha ||
children.translated_text: then he says that this proves what is already established.

children.text: Chapter 175
kimanyena kāryapratiniyatakāraṇeneti tattatkāryajanikā śaktireva niyāmikā bhaviṣyati atacchaktimatas tajjananāyogāt yathā na putrajananaṃ ṣaṇḍhasyopapadyate ||
children.translated_text: What need is there for any other cause fixed to an effect? The power that produces each particular effect itself will be the regulator, because one lacking that power cannot produce that effect, just as the generation of a son is not possible for a eunuch.

children.text: yadyevaṃ tasminneva kāraṇe tatkāryajananaśaktimattvaṃ nānyatreti śaktirūpatayā tatra tatkāryam avasthitam ityāsmākīnapakṣānupraveśāt siddhaṃ sādhyate bhavadbhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: If this is so, then, since the possession of the power to produce that effect is in that very cause and nowhere else, that effect exists there in the form of a power; because you have entered our position, what you are proving is already established.

children.text: upacayadūṣaṇam āha ||
children.translated_text: He states the objection concerning accretion.

children.text: Chapter 176
satyasadutpattyabhyupagame kārakavrātasyaiva pravṛttir nopapadyate ||
children.translated_text: If the production of a nonexistent thing is accepted, the activity of the whole group of causal factors itself is not tenable.

children.text: asato hi kāryasya vandhyāsutāder ivotpattaye kiṃ kila kārakāṇi kuryuḥ ||
children.translated_text: For what, indeed, could causal factors do for the production of a nonexistent effect, such as the son of a barren woman?

children.text: kārakapravṛttyanupapatteś ca ghaṭādicikīrṣor mṛtpiṇḍādy ānayetyādikā śrutiḥ teṣāṃ ca kārakāṇāmādānaṃ grahaṇam arthaśca tadvyāpāralakṣaṇā kriyā vyapaiti vighaṭate ||
children.translated_text: And because the operation of causal factors is untenable, the instruction of one who wishes to make a pot, such as 'Bring clay lumps,' together with the taking up of those causal factors, their purpose, and the activity characterized by their operation, disappears and collapses.

children.text: tasmiṃśca vyapete sarvaceṣṭāvyāghātaḥ pratyuta yuṣmatpakṣe jagadvyāhataṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: And when that has disappeared, there is obstruction of every effort; on the contrary, on your view the world itself would be obstructed.

children.text: nanu śaktyātmanā kāraṇe kāryaṃ nāvasthitam apitu tadutpādikā śaktis tatrāstītyatacchaktimatas tajjananāyogāt kāryakāraṇapratiniyamasiddhau na kācit kṣatiriti parābhiprāyam āśaṅkya taṃ parākaroti ||
children.translated_text: Now, anticipating the opponent's intention, namely, 'The effect is not situated in the cause as the self of the power; rather, the power that produces it exists there, and therefore there is no damage when the fixed relation of effect and cause is established on the ground that one lacking that power cannot produce it,' he refutes it.

children.text: Chapter 177
atha mataṃ pratiniyatakāryajanikā kāraṇe śaktirasti natu śaktyātmanā kāryam avasthitam iti ||
children.translated_text: If the view is this: in the cause there exists a power that produces a determinate effect, but the effect is not situated there as the self of that power,

children.text: tad etacchabdamātreṇa bhinnaṃ nārthena ||
children.translated_text: then this differs only in word, not in meaning.

children.text: vaktavyaṃ hy atra viśeṣaṇaṃ bhavatā ||
children.translated_text: For you must state a distinguishing feature here.

children.text: yaduta tattatkāryajanikā śaktiḥ kāraṇe 'sti śaktyātmanā vā tattatkāryaṃ kāraṇe sthitamityatra nahi kiṃcid viśeṣaṇam utpaśyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Namely, in saying 'the power that produces each particular effect exists in the cause' or 'each particular effect is situated in the cause in the form of a power,' we do not see any distinction at all.

children.text: yata eva ||
children.translated_text: For precisely because of this...

children.text: Chapter 178
tasmātsthitam etad yaduta janyaśaktiḥ kārakavastuno niyāmikā idam asmād evotpadyata iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore this is established: the generative power of a causal entity determines that this arises only from this.

children.text: sā ca janyaśaktir anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ prasiddhyā vāvagamyate ||
children.translated_text: And that generative power is understood from positive and negative concomitance, or from common recognition.

children.text: satyeva mṛtpiṇḍe ghaṭādyutpattir asatyanutpattir evetyanvayavyatirekau ||
children.translated_text: The positive and negative concomitance is this: when a lump of clay exists, a pot and the like are produced; when it does not exist, they are simply not produced.

children.text: rūḍhiś ceyam ā bālabāliśāṅganaṃ sthitā yad ghaṭotpattyarthino na mṛtpiṇḍavyatiriktam upādānaṃ kulālasyopāharantīti ||
children.translated_text: And this convention is established even among children, the simple-minded, and women: those who want a pot produced do not bring the potter a material cause other than a lump of clay.

children.text: nanu mṛtpiṇḍe yadi ghaṭaḥ syāt tatkumbhakāravyāpāraṃ vināpyupalabhyeta na copalabhyate tasmānna mṛtpiṇḍe ghaṭo'sti apitu tataḥ kumbhakāreṇa kriyate yatastadvyāpārānantaram utpadyamānasya ghaṭasyopalambhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But, one may object, if the pot existed in the lump of clay, it would be perceived even without the potter's activity; and it is not perceived. Therefore the pot does not exist in the lump of clay, but rather is made from it by the potter, since the pot is perceived as arising after that activity.

children.text: naitat ||
children.translated_text: This is not so.

children.text: upalabdhikāraṇābhāvāt tatra ghaṭasyānupalambhaḥ na tv asattvāt ||
children.translated_text: The pot is not perceived there because the causes of perception are absent, not because it is nonexistent.

children.text: yadā punaḥ kulālād asyābhivyañjanakriyayopalabdhiyogyatā bhavati tadopalabhyata eva yathā khananādinā kīlamūlodakādi ||
children.translated_text: But when, through the potter's manifesting operation, it becomes fit for perception, then it is indeed perceived, just like a peg, a root, water, and the like through digging and so on.

children.text: nanu kīlamūlādeḥ prāksattve pramāṇam asti na tu mṛtpiṇḍe ghaṭasya tasmād ghaṭas tato bhavati na tv abhivyajyata iti yuktam uktam ||
children.translated_text: But, one may object, there is a valid means of knowledge for the prior existence of a peg, root, and the like, but not for the existence of a pot in the lump of clay. Therefore it is reasonable to say that the pot comes from that, not that it is manifested.

children.text: evaṃ cet tadatrāpi sattve pramāṇam asadakaraṇād upādānagrahaṇāt ityādi sambhavet ityabhivyaktivāda evam uktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If this is said, then here too there can be a valid proof of its existence, such as 'because what is nonexistent cannot be produced' and 'because the material cause is taken up.' Thus the doctrine of manifestation has been stated in this way.

children.text: yadyevaṃ tarhi sato bhāvasya sattvādeva jananaṃ nopapadyate dṛśyamānasya ghaṭāder iveti punaḥ sa doṣastadavastha evetyāha ||
children.translated_text: If so, then the production of an existent entity is not possible precisely because it exists, just as in the case of a pot and the like that is already being seen; so the same fault remains as before. He says this:

children.text: Chapter 179
tadetat paṭāder bhāvasya jananam abhimataṃ yat turītantuvemādisamāśrayācchaktyātmanāvasthitasya tasyābhivyaktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The production that is accepted for an entity such as a cloth is the manifestation of that entity, which abides in the form of a power while depending on the shuttle, threads, loom, and the like.

children.text: yataḥ paṭākārapratibandhakaṃ tantugatamākāraṃ vemādikārakavrātenāpāsya anantaraṃ paṭasya vyaktiḥ prakāśyate na tūpalabhyamānapaṭāntaravat sadeva tantvādibhyaḥ paṭādyutpadyate iti ||
children.translated_text: For the form residing in the threads, which obstructs the cloth-form, is removed by the collection of causes such as the loom, and immediately the manifestation of the cloth is revealed. It is not that a cloth and the like, already existent in the manner of another perceptible cloth, are produced from threads and so on.

children.text: abhivyaktir api kim asatkāryam uta netyevam ādikutārkikakuvikalpaparihāro granthavistarabhīrutvānna likhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The refutation of the bad conjectures of sophists, such as whether manifestation too is an effect of the nonexistent or not, has not been written down, because of fear of making the work too extensive.

children.text: vyaktisvarūpatvādabhivyakter abhivyaṅgyatā na vetyādayaḥ kila vitarkā dūrāpetā eva prakāśavat ||
children.translated_text: Speculations such as whether manifestation, because it has the nature of manifestation, is itself something to be manifested or not, are indeed very far removed, as in the case of light.

children.text: yathāhi prakāśaḥ prakāśātmakatvānna prakāśāntaraprakāśyaḥ evam abhivyaktir vyaktisvabhāvatvānnābhivyaktyantaram apekṣata iti ||
children.translated_text: For just as light, because it is of the nature of illumination, is not illuminated by another light, so manifestation, because its own nature is manifestation, does not depend on another manifestation.

children.text: tadevaṃ prakṛte kiṃ siddham ityāha ||
children.translated_text: Thus what has been established in the present topic? He says:

children.text: Chapter 180

yadvat kaṭādyācchannasya paṭāder vastunas tadācchādakāpanayān nāvidyamānasya vyaktiḥ kriyate api tu sadeva paṭādi vyajyate evam upasaṃhārakāle śaktyātmanā līnaṃ kalādi kāryam aharmukhe granthitaḥ granthitattvād ananteśavyāpāreṇābhivyajyata iti māyākhyaparamakāraṇasiddhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Just as, when the covering is removed, the manifestation of an object such as a cloth covered by a mat and the like is not produced when that object is nonexistent, but rather the already existent cloth and the like is manifested, so at the time of withdrawal the effects such as <s>kalā</s>, dissolved in the form of powers, are manifested at the beginning of the day of creation from the compacted condition through the activity of <s>Ananteśa</s>. Thus the supreme cause called <s>māyā</s> is established.

children.text: Chapter 181

māyātattvātprathamataḥ kalābhidheyayoḥ kalāniyatyoḥ kālasya nṛśabdenoktasya puṃsaśca puṃspratyayahetos tattvaviśeṣasyābhivyaktiḥ kalātattvāt tu vidyārāgāvyaktānāṃ mātṛśabdena ca prakṛtir avyaktākhyā tatsakāśād guṇāḥ tebhyo buddhiḥ tasyā ahaṃkāraḥ tasmāttaijasādbuddhīndriyāṇi manaśca vaikārikāt karmendriyāṇi bhūtādisaṃjñāt mātrāśabdenoddiṣṭāni tanmātrāṇi tebhyo bhūtānītyasmād anukramād etad granthitattvato 'bhivyaṅgyam ||
children.translated_text: From the <s>māyā</s>-principle there is first the manifestation of the special principles <s>kalā</s> and <s>niyati</s>, called by the name <s>kalā</s>, of <s>kāla</s>, and of the <s>puruṣa</s>, indicated by the word <s>nṛ</s> and causing the cognition of a person. From the <s>kalā</s>-principle there are <s>vidyā</s>, <s>rāga</s>, and the unmanifest; and by the word <s>mātṛ</s> is meant <s>prakṛti</s>, called the unmanifest. From that come the <s>guṇa</s>s; from them, <s>buddhi</s>; from it, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>; from that, in its <s>taijasa</s> form, the cognitive senses and the mind; from its <s>vaikārika</s> form, the organs of action; from what is called <s>bhūtādi</s>, the subtle elements indicated by the word <s>mātrā</s>; and from those, the gross elements. According to this sequence, all this is to be manifested from the compacted condition.

children.text: Chapter 182

aśuddhādhvanyadhikṛto 'nanteśanātha ātmanāṃ dehādikﾱptyai granthitattvāt yat sākṣād avyavadhānena kalādikāryaṃ vyanakti yacca padāntarāt sthānāntarāt kalāder vidyārāgādi vyanakti tad yasmāt kāraṇād abhivyaktaṃ padārthaṃ yena vā prakāreṇa yunakti dehādisiddhau yojayati tattādṛg idānīṃ kathyate ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ananteśa</s>, the lord appointed over the impure path, for the arrangement of bodies and the like for the selves, directly and without mediation manifests from the compacted condition the effect beginning with <s>kalā</s>; and from another station, another level, beginning with <s>kalā</s>, he manifests <s>vidyā</s>, <s>rāga</s>, and the rest. Now it is stated from what cause, or in what manner, he joins the manifested entity of that kind to the accomplishment of bodies and the like.

children.text: Chapter 183
aṇor ātmanaḥ śivaśaktivadyadyapi nityā vyāpikā ca kartṛśaktir muktau tathāvidhatvasaṃśravaṇāt tathāpyanādimalāvṛtatvāt karaṇīyeṣvartheṣu na niranugrahā sā ābhāti ||
children.translated_text: Although the power of agency belonging to the atomic self is eternal and pervasive like the power of <s>Śiva</s>, since it is taught to be such in liberation, nevertheless, because it is covered by beginningless <s>mala</s>, it does not shine forth, without assistance, in the things to be done.

children.text: tasyā anugrāhakaṃ samarthakaṃ kalākhyaṃ tattvaṃ harati bhogamuktyartham adhovartino 'ṇūn iti haro 'nanteśaḥ māyāṃ vikṣobhya prasavonmukhīṃ kṛtvā kurute abhivyanaktītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The principle called <s>kalā</s> assists and empowers that power. <s>Ananteśa</s> is <s>Hara</s> because he carries the lower <s>aṇu</s>s for the sake of enjoyment and liberation; having stirred <s>māyā</s> and made it ready for generation, he makes it act, that is, he manifests it.

children.text: yasmāt kalākhyaṃ tattvaṃ paraṃ pravṛttyaṅgam ātmanaḥ kartṛsvarūpasamarthanaṃ tenaiva vyāpṛtatvāt ||
children.translated_text: For the principle called <s>kalā</s> is the chief limb of activity, the empowering of the self's nature as agent, since the self acts only through it.

children.text: nahyasau tenānuttejitakartṛbhāvaḥ pravartituṃ śaktaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: For that self, if its state of agency were not stimulated by that principle, would not be able to act.

children.text: taijasatvaṃ cāsya sahajamalatiraskaraṇenāṇor ekadeśena prakāśanahetutvāt ||
children.translated_text: And its <s>taijasa</s> character consists in being the cause of illuminating the <s>aṇu</s> in one part by removing its innate <s>mala</s>.

children.text: etad evāha ||
children.translated_text: He states this very point:

children.text: Chapter 184

sa eṣa prāgukto maheśvaras tadā tasmin māyāprasavābhimukhyakāle 'timalinacicchakter ātmanastena taijasena kalākhyena tattvena kiṃcit prakāśakāritvād dīpaprāyeṇa nibiḍaṃ tamo nirbhidyaikadeśaṃ prakaṭayati malāvacchinnāṃ kartṛtāṃ samupodbalayatīti yāvat ||
children.translated_text: That same <s>Maheśvara</s> mentioned before, then, at the time when <s>māyā</s> is turned toward production, through that radiant principle called <s>kalā</s>, because it causes some illumination for the self whose power of consciousness is extremely obscured, like a lamp, pierces the dense darkness and reveals one region; that is, he strengthens the agency limited by <s>mala</s>.

children.text: kalāśabdenoddeśasūtre niyatirapi lāghavādupakṣiptā ||
children.translated_text: In the introductory sūtra, <s>niyati</s> too is included by the word <s>kalā</s>, for the sake of brevity.

children.text: tayośca kalāniyatyoranvarthakalāśabdābhidheyatāṃ vaktumāha ||
children.translated_text: And to state that both of them, <s>kalā</s> and <s>niyati</s>, are denoted by the word <s>kalā</s> in an etymologically meaningful way, he says:

children.text: Chapter 185
kala ityeṣa saṃkhyānārthavṛttireko dhātuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The root 'kal' is one root whose function is in the sense of counting.

children.text: kala kṣepa iti protsāraṇārthavṛttiranyo dhātuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The root 'kal,' in the sense of casting, is another root whose function is in the sense of throwing aside.

children.text: tatraikadeśe tamaso malasya kṣepaṇaṃ protsāraṇaṃ kurvāṇāyāḥ kalāyāḥ kṣepārthavṛttiprakṛtibhūtaḥ prathamaḥ dvitīyas tu saṃkhyānārthavṛttiḥ kalanādiyattayā niyamanāt kalāśabdāparaparyāyā niyateḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among these, for <s>kalā</s>, which casts away, pushes aside, one portion of the darkness, namely <s>mala</s>, the underlying root is the one functioning in the sense of casting away; but for <s>niyati</s>, which is synonymous with the word <s>kalā</s>, the root is the one functioning in the sense of counting, because it restricts by measuring and determining.

children.text: idānīm ātmanaḥ kalāyāśca kartṛkārakatām abhidhātum āha ||
children.translated_text: Now, to state the agent-instrumentality of the self and of <s>kalā</s>, he says:

children.text: Chapter 186
jantoranāsāditabhogasyāṇoryo bhogakriyāvidhis tasminnutpādye iti anena prāguktena prakāreṇa etat ātmakalākhyaṃ kartṛkārakaṃ nijagur upadidiśur guravaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The teachers, intending to teach, declared this agent-instrument called the self and <s>kalā</s>, with respect to the production of the procedure of the act of experience for the living being, the <s>aṇu</s>, who has not yet attained experience, in the manner previously stated by the words 'to be produced.'

children.text: tair hi bhoktṛtayā kartṛtvenātmoktaḥ tasya kartṛśakter upodbalakatvāt kārakaṃ hetuḥ kartrī kalā prayoktryādi mahīprāntam ||
children.translated_text: For by them the self was said to be the experiencer as agent; since <s>kalā</s> strengthens that self's power of agency, it is the instrument, the cause, the acting factor, called the impeller and so on down to earth.

children.text: ityādinā tasyā eva prayoktṛśabdena vakṣyamāṇatvāt ||
children.translated_text: For that very same one is later to be spoken of by the word 'impeller' and the like.

children.text: kathaṃ caitaddvayaṃ sthitam ityāha sambhūyānanyavat ekībhūyālakṣitavyatirekam iti yāvat ||
children.translated_text: How are these two situated? He says, 'together, like what is not other': that is, having become one, with no distinction perceptible.

children.text: uktaṃ ca bṛhaspatipādaiḥ
children.translated_text: And <s>Bṛhaspatipāda</s> has said:

children.text: jantor vibhātyatiśleṣāt sā dvitīyeva cetanā
children.translated_text: Because of her extreme closeness to the living being, she appears like a second consciousness.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: vipretyāmantraṇena vaktā śrotāraṃ munim avahitaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: By the address 'O brahmin,' the speaker makes the listening sage attentive.

children.text: vidyātattvasya vyāpāraṃ vaktum āha ||
children.translated_text: To state the operation of the <s>vidyā</s>-principle, he says:

children.text: Chapter 187
uktena prakāreṇa vyaktā kriyāśaktir yasya sa tathāvidho 'ṇur gocaraṃ pratibimbitaviṣayaṃ buddhyākhyaṃ draṣṭumicchurdṛśo jñānasyānugrahāpekṣāṃ bhajate jñānaśaktyanugraham apekṣata iti tātparyam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>aṇu</s> whose power of action has been made manifest in the stated manner, wishing to see the object, the reflected object called <s>buddhi</s>, resorts to dependence on the favor of sight, that is, of knowledge; the purport is that he depends on the favor of the power of knowledge.

children.text: svayaṃ draṣṭum aśaknuvanniti viśeṣaṇabhāvena hetūpanyāsaḥ svayaṃ boddhum asamarthatvād ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The phrase 'being unable to see by himself' gives the reason in the form of a qualifier: it means, because he is unable to know by himself.

children.text: tadartham ananteśaḥ kalāṃ tattvāvirbhāvanasahāṃ prakṣobhya janyajananābhimukhīṃ kṛtvā ātmanaḥ paraṃ prakṛṣṭaṃ karaṇaṃ vidyākhyaṃ sṛṣṭavān ||
children.translated_text: For that purpose <s>Ananteśa</s> stirred <s>kalā</s>, which assists the manifestation of the principles, made it face toward generating what was to be generated, and created for the self a higher, eminent instrument called <s>vidyā</s>.

children.text: paratvaṃ cāsya sākṣāt sādhyasyaivopakārakatvāt taduttejitajñānaśakter antaḥkaraṇabahiṣkaraṇair yoga iti teṣām aparatvam ||
children.translated_text: Its superiority consists in the fact that it directly assists the very thing to be accomplished; the connection of the power of knowledge stimulated by it with the inner and outer instruments is the reason for those instruments' inferiority.

children.text: yaduta ||
children.translated_text: That is to say:

children.text: Chapter 188

tena vidyākhyena tattvena prakāśakatvāt jñānaśaktyabhivyañjakena sarvair buddhīndriyaiḥ karmendriyair yathāsvaṃ nirvartyaṃ paraṃ kartṛviṣayāt kāryātmakaviṣayād anyat jñeyākhyaṃ yadvā param iti avyavahitaṃ viṣayaṃ pratibimbitabāhyaviṣayatvena saṃnikṛṣṭaṃ buddhitattvam avaiti jānāti ||
children.translated_text: Through that principle called <s>vidyā</s>, because it illuminates and manifests the power of knowledge, he knows, by all the cognitive senses and active senses according to what each performs, the object called the knowable, which is different from the object belonging to the agent, the object constituted as an effect; or, taking 'higher' to mean immediate, he knows the proximate <s>buddhi</s>-principle, since external objects are reflected in it.

children.text: vidyākhyena karaṇena kila pratibimbitasrakcandanādibāhyaviṣayā bhogyarūpā buddhir gṛhyate ||
children.translated_text: For by the instrument called <s>vidyā</s>, <s>buddhi</s>, which has the form of what is to be enjoyed and contains reflected external objects such as garlands and sandal paste, is grasped.

children.text: yadāha kheṭakanandanaḥ
children.translated_text: As <s>Kheṭakanandana</s> says:

children.text: buddhir viṣayākārā sukhādirūpā samāsato bhogyā ||
children.translated_text: In brief, <s>buddhi</s>, having the form of objects and the form of pleasure and the like, is what is to be enjoyed.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tathā
children.translated_text: Likewise:

children.text: ravivatprakāśarūpo yadi nāma mahāṃstathāpi karmatvāt
children.translated_text: Even if the great one is indeed of the nature of light like the sun, still, because he is an object of action,

children.text: karaṇāntarasāpekṣaḥ śakto grāhayitum ātmānam ||
children.translated_text: he is capable of making himself grasped only in dependence on another instrument.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: rāgatattvābhivyaktim āha ||
children.translated_text: He states the manifestation of the <s>rāga</s>-principle:

children.text: Chapter 189
tena vidyākhyena tattvenābhivyaktajñānaśaktitvād dṛṣṭārtho 'pyaṇur apipāsito 'saṃjātābhilāṣaḥ sannaiti na bhogyāharaṇāya gacchati ||
children.translated_text: Because by that principle called <s>vidyā</s> his power of knowledge has been manifested, the <s>aṇu</s>, although he has seen the object, still, being unthirsting and without desire having arisen, does not go, does not proceed, to fetch the object of enjoyment.

children.text: atas tasyābhilāṣasya janakaṃ rāgaṃ tata eva kalātattvāt prabhavanaśīlo 'nanteśanāthaḥ sasarja ||
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>Ananteśanātha</s>, whose nature is to bring things forth from that very <s>kalā</s>-principle, created <s>rāga</s>, the producer of that desire.

children.text: Chapter 190
tena rāgeṇa rañjito janitābhiṣvaṅgaḥ so 'ṇur malinatamam api māyīyabhogyam abhilaṣannupāharati na caivam upabhuñjāno virajyate ||
children.translated_text: Colored by that <s>rāga</s>, with attachment produced, that <s>aṇu</s>, desiring even the very impure object of enjoyment belonging to <s>māyā</s>, brings it near; and even while enjoying it in this way he does not become dispassionate.

children.text: curādīnām aṇijantatvāc ca spṛhannityaduṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: And because roots such as those of the cur-class are not necessarily treated as ending in ṇic, the form 'spṛhan' is not faulty.

children.text: kālatattvanirūpaṇāyāha ||
children.translated_text: For the explanation of the <s>kāla</s>-principle, he says:

children.text: Chapter 191
ityevam uktanītyā kalottejitakartṛtvaḥ san pravṛtto bhogodyuktaḥ nā puruṣaḥ kālenānuvartinas tāsu tāsu bhogabhūmiṣu sukhaduḥkhādirūpān bhogān bhuṅkte ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by the method just stated, the person, with his agency stimulated by <s>kalā</s>, having become active and intent on experience, enjoys experiences in the form of pleasure, pain, and so forth in those various planes of enjoyment, attended by <s>kāla</s>.

children.text: kair bhuṅkte ityāha bhauvanadehasahitaiḥ karaṇairbuddhīndriyaiḥ karmendriyais trividhenāntaḥkaraṇena ||
children.translated_text: With what does he enjoy them? He says: with the instruments together with the worldly body, namely the cognitive senses, the active senses, and the threefold inner instrument.

children.text: malinatvāt kriyājñānaśaktyoḥ karmendriyabuddhīndriyāṇām apekṣā ||
children.translated_text: Because his powers of action and knowledge are impure, there is dependence on the active senses and cognitive senses.

children.text: kīdṛśaiḥ karaṇairityāha kāryarūḍhair avibhutvato nirāśrayāṇāmeṣāṃ ceṣṭādyayogād bhūtatanmātrātmakakāryāśrayasthaiḥ sadbhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: What sort of instruments? He says: established in effects; since, because they are not all-pervasive, activity and the like would be impossible for them if they had no support, they exist located in supports that are effects made of the elements and subtle elements.

children.text: uktaṃ ca kheṭakanandanena
children.translated_text: And <s>Kheṭakanandana</s> has said:

children.text: etatkāryaṃ daśadhā karaṇairāviśya kāryate ceṣṭām
children.translated_text: Having entered this effect, which is tenfold, by means of the instruments, he causes activity.

children.text: avibhutvātkaraṇāni tu kāryam adhiṣṭhāya ceṣṭante ||
children.translated_text: But the instruments, because they are not all-pervasive, act after taking an effect as their basis.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: atha ko 'sau kālo nāma kuta utpannaḥ kiṃ vā karotīti ||
children.translated_text: Now, what is that thing called <s>kāla</s> (time), from where has it arisen, and what does it do?

children.text: atrocyate ||
children.translated_text: On this, the reply is:

children.text: Chapter 192
truṭilavanimeṣamuhūrtādeḥ pratyayasya jñānasyārtho nimittaṃ yaḥ sa kālaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That which is the object and occasion of the cognition expressed by <s>truṭi</s>, <s>lava</s>, <s>nimeṣa</s>, <s>muhūrta</s>, and the like is <s>kāla</s>.

children.text: sa muhūrtamāste praharaṃ bhrāmyati ityādipratītir ajasraparivartino yasmād bhavati sa māyāta utpannaḥ paśutvena malena yuktam ātmānaṃ kalayan kāla ityucyate ||
children.translated_text: Because from it arises the cognition, 'he sits for a <s>muhūrta</s>,' 'he wanders for a watch,' and so on, while it is ceaselessly changing, it is called <s>kāla</s>: arisen from <s>māyā</s>, it measures the self that is joined with impurity in the condition of a <s>paśu</s>.

children.text: yad āhuḥ
children.translated_text: As they say:

children.text: jalayantrabhramāvegasadṛśībhiḥ pravṛttibhiḥ
children.translated_text: Through activities like the speed of the turning of a water-wheel,

children.text: sa kālaḥ kalayaṃstāvatkālākhyāṃ labhate tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: that is <s>kāla</s>; as long as it measures, it then receives the name <s>kāla</s>.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: kīdṛśaṃ paśuṃ kalayannityāha ā samutthānānniyatyā niyataṃ niyateḥ samutthānaṃ svakāraṇād abhivyaktiḥ tata ārabhya yāvat saṃhāramasau paśuṃ karmajanite sukhaduḥkhopabhoge niyacchati ||
children.translated_text: Asking what kind of <s>paśu</s> it measures, he says, 'from its arising onward, fixed by <s>niyati</s>.' The arising of <s>niyati</s> is its manifestation from its own cause. From then until dissolution, that <s>niyati</s> confines the <s>paśu</s> with respect to the experience of pleasure and pain produced by karma.

children.text: na cāyaṃ kālasya vyāpārastasya kalanamātra eva caritārthatvāt ||
children.translated_text: And this is not the operation of <s>kāla</s>, since <s>kāla</s> is fulfilled by mere measuring.

children.text: atra parā śaṅkā ||
children.translated_text: Here there is an objection from the opponent:

children.text: Chapter 193
avaśyaṃ tāvad bhogas tatsādhanāni ca bhoktuḥ karmādhīnāni tadapekṣāṃ vinā bhogavaicitryasyānupapatter ityuktam ||
children.translated_text: Experience and the means to it must necessarily depend on the enjoyer's karma, because the variety of experience cannot be explained without regard to that; this has been stated.

children.text: tanniyāmakatvaṃ ca tasyaiva bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: And the function of regulating them will belong to that alone.

children.text: tataś ca yad anyanniyatyākhyaṃ tattvaṃ kalpyate tadatiricyate niṣprayojanatvāt tad adhikībhavati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the other principle that is imagined under the name <s>niyati</s> is excessive, because it has no purpose; it becomes superfluous.

children.text: tathā coktam
children.translated_text: And so it has been said:

children.text: yasmācca yena ca yathā ca yadā ca yacca yāvacca yatra ca śubhāśubham ātmakarma
children.translated_text: From what, by what, in what way, when, what, how much, and where one's own good or bad karma is,

children.text: tasmācca tena ca tathā ca tadā ca tacca tāvacca tatra ca vidhātṛvaśādupaiti ||
children.translated_text: from that, by that, in that way, then, that very thing, so much, and there it comes to him under the power of <s>Vidhātṛ</s>.

children.text: atra parihāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here is the reply:

children.text: Chapter 194
mā bhūn niyatitattvaṃ tadanyānyapi bhogasādhanāni tattvāni karmanibandhanānyeva teṣāṃ cāvaśyaṃ karmāpekṣitvāt karmaiva kevalaṃ bhogasādhanam astu yadvinā anyāni akiṃcitkārīṇi ||
children.translated_text: Let there be no <s>niyatitattva</s>. Then the other <s>tattva</s>s too, which serve as means of experience, are bound to karma alone, since they must necessarily depend on karma. Let karma alone be the means of experience, since without it the others do nothing.

children.text: tathāca sati śarīrendriyaviṣayādeḥ sarvasyānarthakyam ||
children.translated_text: If that is so, everything such as body, senses, and objects becomes pointless.

children.text: Chapter 195
nanu dehādisavyapekṣaṃ karma puruṣārthasādhanasamarthaṃ na kevalam ||
children.translated_text: Objection: karma, when dependent on the body and the rest, is capable of accomplishing the soul's purpose; it is not capable by itself alone.

children.text: nahyekaṃ janakaṃ kiṃ tarhi sāmagryeva kāryajaniketi ||
children.translated_text: For one thing alone does not produce; rather, only the complete assemblage produces an effect.

children.text: atrocyate ||
children.translated_text: The answer is:

children.text: Chapter 196
eva tarhi yathā dehendriyādibhiḥ svasvavyāpārapravṛttaiḥ saha karma puruṣārthasādhanakṣamam evaṃ svakāryaniṣpādakaniyatitattvasāpekṣaṃ tat niyāmakam astviti na kaścid doṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, just as karma together with body, senses, and the rest, each engaged in its own function, is capable of serving the soul's purpose, so let that karma be the regulator while depending on the <s>niyatitattva</s> that accomplishes its own effect; there is no fault at all.

children.text: Chapter 197
saṃhārasamaye yadananteśanāthena viśrāmitaṃ tataḥ tasmād eva māyātattvāt puṃstattvam āvirabhūd ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that the <s>puṃstattva</s> emerged from that very <s>māyātattva</s> which, at the time of dissolution, had been brought to rest by lord <s>Ananteśa</s>.

children.text: puṃspratyayanibandhanamiti puṃspratīter hetuḥ anena māyāgarbhasthebhyo 'dhikārirudrāṇubhyas tattadbhuvananivāsibhyaś ca vailakṣaṇyam uktaṃ teṣāṃ puṃspratyayāyogāt ||
children.translated_text: 'The basis for the cognition of <s>puṃs</s>' means the cause of the awareness of <s>puṃs</s>. By this its difference is stated from the authority-bearing <s>Rudra-aṇu</s>s situated in the womb of <s>māyā</s> and from those dwelling in their respective worlds, because the cognition of <s>puṃs</s> does not apply to them.

children.text: tacca puṃstattvaṃ pradhānādes tattvavrātasyāpūrakaṃ puruṣārthatvena kāryasahitasya pradhānasyeṣṭatvāt ||
children.translated_text: And that <s>puṃstattva</s> is what completes the mass of <s>tattva</s>s beginning with <s>pradhāna</s>, because <s>pradhāna</s> together with its effects is intended as serving the <s>puruṣa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ chāttrahetukatvād adhyayanasya chāttrā adhyāpakāḥ ityādivad āpūrakaśabdo jñeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus the word 'completer' should be understood as in usages such as calling teachers student-based, because instruction depends on students.

children.text: bhauvane cādhvani tat puṃstattvaṃ rudrasaṃśrayam ||
children.translated_text: And in the cosmic path of the worlds, that <s>puṃstattva</s> is the support of <s>Rudra</s>s.

children.text: tathā coktaṃ śrīmatsvatantre
children.translated_text: And so it is said in the venerable <s>Svatantra</s>:

children.text: ataḥ puruṣatattve tu bhuvanāni nibodha me
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, in the <s>puruṣatattva</s>, learn from me the worlds

children.text: divyāmbhaḥ salilaughe ca ||
children.translated_text: in the stream of divine waters and in the mass of waters ...'

children.text: ityādi ||
children.translated_text: and so on.

children.text: puṃrāgasaṃpuṭitarūpaṃ ca etatpuruṣatattvaṃ rudrāṇām āśrayatveneṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: This <s>puruṣatattva</s>, whose form is enclosed by <s>puṃs</s> and <s>rāga</s>, is accepted as the support of <s>Rudra</s>s.

children.text: yathoktaṃ śrīmatkiraṇe
children.translated_text: As stated in the venerable <s>Kiraṇa</s>:

children.text: vāmadevo'tha bhīmaś cāpyugraśca bhavasaṃjñakaḥ
children.translated_text: '<s>Vāmadeva</s>, then <s>Bhīma</s>, also <s>Ugra</s>, and the one named <s>Bhava</s>,

children.text: sarveśānaikavīrau ca pracaṇḍaś ceśvaraḥ pumān ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sarveśāna</s> and <s>Ekavīra</s>, <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>, and <s>Pumān</s>,

children.text: umābhartā hy ajo 'nanta ekaścaiva śivastataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Umābhartṛ</s>, <s>Aja</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Eka</s>, and then <s>Śiva</s>:

children.text: rāgatattve sthitā hy ete rudrāstīvrabalotkaṭāḥ ||
children.translated_text: these <s>Rudra</s>s, fierce and mighty in strength, are situated in the <s>rāgatattva</s>.'

children.text: atraiva puruṣo jñeyaḥ pradhānagṛhapālakaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Here the <s>puruṣa</s> is to be known as the guardian of the house of <s>pradhāna</s>,'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: thus.

children.text: Chapter 198
tato māyātaḥ puṃstattvaprasavādanantaraṃ kalātattvād avyaktaṃ tattvam udapadyata ||
children.translated_text: Then, after the production of the <s>puṃstattva</s> from <s>māyā</s>, the unmanifest <s>tattva</s> arose from the <s>kalātattva</s>.

children.text: kīdṛgityāha saptagranthinidānasya ityādi yatpradhānaṃ mahadahaṃkārayos tanmātrapañcakasyetyevaṃ saptānāṃ granthīnāṃ kāryayonīnām udbhavahetor gauṇasya tattvasya kāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: Of what kind? He says, 'of the source of the seven knots,' and so on. It is <s>pradhāna</s>, the cause of the derivative <s>tattva</s> that is the source for the arising of the seven knots, the wombs of effects, namely <s>mahat</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, and the five <s>tanmātra</s>s.

children.text: yathāhi tasya tasya kāñcanaratnāder uttarakālabhāvinyaḥ karipuruṣaturaṃgādirūpāḥ kaṭakakuṇḍalādyā bharaṇātmikā vā arthakriyāḥ śaktirūpatayā sthitāḥ evaṃ śaktyātmanā sthitasvasvakāryajanakatanmātrādigrānthasaptakakāraṇasya guṇatattvasyāvyaktād udbhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For just as in gold, jewels, and the like there remain, in the form of powers, later functions such as figures of elephants, men, and horses, or ornaments such as bracelets and earrings, so the <s>guṇatattva</s> arises from the unmanifest: it is the cause of the sevenfold complex of knots beginning with the <s>tanmātra</s>s, each established in the form of power and productive of its own effect.

children.text: Chapter 199
tata iti tasmāt prādhānikāt tattvād vakṣyamāṇabhāvapratyayasahitāyā buddher udbhavahetur gauṇaṃ tattvaṃ sattvarajastamorūpamajījanaditi pūrveṇa sambandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'From that' means from that principle belonging to <s>pradhāna</s>. The construction is with the preceding statement: it produced the <s>guṇatattva</s>, consisting of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>, which is the cause of the arising of <s>buddhi</s> together with the disposition-cognitions to be mentioned later.

children.text: teṣāṃ ca sattvādīnāṃ prakāśapravṛttiniyamātmikās tisro vṛttayo bāhulyena prathitā itīha noktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And among these, the three functions of <s>sattva</s> and the others, consisting respectively of illumination, activity, and restraint, are widely known, so they are not stated here.

children.text: Chapter 200
tritve'pi parasparāviyogād guṇatattvam ekaṃ jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: Although they are three, because they are mutually inseparable the <s>guṇatattva</s> should be understood as one.

children.text: nanu
children.translated_text: Objection:

children.text: ye caike sāttvikā bhāvā rājasā ye ca tāmasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'And those states that are sāttvika, and those that are rājasika and tāmasika ...'

children.text: ityādau bhinnameṣāṃ sattvādīnāṃ kāryaṃ śrūyate na tv aviyogād ekam etat tattvam ityāha ekaikaśrutir ityādi eṣāṃ guṇānām idaṃ sāttvikam idaṃ rājasam idaṃ tāmasamityādikā ekaikaśrutir vṛttyādhikyahetukī ||
children.translated_text: In such passages, the effects of these, <s>sattva</s> and the others, are heard of as distinct; but it is not the case that, because they are inseparable, this is a single principle. Therefore he says, 'the mention of each one,' and so on. The separate mention of these <s>guṇa</s>s, as in 'this is <s>sāttvika</s>, this is <s>rājasa</s>, this is <s>tāmasa</s>,' has the predominance of a mode of activity as its cause.

children.text: adhikavṛtti sattvaṃ yasya sa sāttvikaḥ padārthaḥ evaṃ rājasatāmasau vijñeyau ||
children.translated_text: A thing in which <s>sattva</s> has the predominant activity is <s>sāttvika</s>; in the same way the <s>rājasa</s> and <s>tāmasa</s> are to be understood.

children.text: Chapter 201
asmin jagati tādṛg acetanaṃ vastu na kiṃcid apyasti yad guṇair na vyāptaṃ yatra vāmiśrako 'nyāsaṃpṛkta eka eva sattvādir guṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this world there is no insentient thing of such a kind that it is not pervaded by the <s>guṇa</s>s, or in which there is only one <s>guṇa</s>, such as <s>sattva</s>, unmixed and unconnected with the others.

children.text: unmagnanimagnādivṛttisattvādiguṇatrayānvitaṃ sarvaṃ jagad iti tātparyam ||
children.translated_text: The purport is that the whole world is endowed with the triad of <s>guṇa</s>s, <s>sattva</s> and the rest, whose activities rise to the surface and sink down in turn.

children.text: evaṃ guṇatattvam uktvā buddhitattvaṃ vaktum āha ||
children.translated_text: Having thus stated the <s>guṇa</s>-principle, he speaks in order to state the <s>buddhi</s>-principle.

children.text: Chapter 202

vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇā dharmādayo bhāvāstathā viparyayāśaktyādayaḥ pratyayāḥ ta eva liṅgaṃ sattāgamakaṃ yasya tat abhidhāsyamānair arthair viṣayaiḥ saṃskṛtam uparaktaṃ buddhitattvaṃ paraṃ prakṛṣṭam avyavahitam ātmano bhogyaṃ viṣayāṇāṃ bhogyatve 'pi tatpratibimbitatvenāsaṃnikṛṣṭatvād apakṛṣṭatvaṃ yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The states beginning with <s>dharma</s>, whose definitions will be stated, and the cognitions beginning with error and incapacity are the very marks by which its existence is known. The <s>buddhi</s>-principle, colored and conditioned by the objects that will be described, is the supreme, excellent, immediate object of enjoyment for the self. Although sense-objects too are objects of enjoyment, they are inferior because, being enjoyed only as reflected in it, they are not directly near.

children.text: uktaṃ ca tatrabhavatsadyojyotiḥpādaiḥ
children.translated_text: And this was said by the venerable <s>Sadyojyotis</s>:

children.text: buddhirviṣayākārā sukhādirūpā samāsato bhogyā
children.translated_text: '<s>Buddhi</s>, taking the form of objects and consisting of pleasure and the like, is, in brief, the object of enjoyment.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: bhāvān vaktum āha ||
children.translated_text: To state the <s>bhāva</s>s, he says:

children.text: Chapter 203
dharmajñānavairāgyaiśvaryākhyā buddhiguṇā bhāvasaṃjñayā vijñeyāḥ
children.translated_text: The qualities of <s>buddhi</s> called <s>dharma</s>, knowledge, dispassion, and lordly power are to be understood under the designation <s>bhāva</s>.

children.text: bhāvayanti yato liṅgaṃ tena bhāvā iti smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because they bring the <s>liṅga</s> into being, they are remembered as <s>bhāva</s>s.

children.text: ete ca sāttvikā boddhavyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And these are to be understood as <s>sāttvika</s>.

children.text: vyatyayena viparyayeṇaite rāgam utsṛjya vairāgyavivarjitās tāmasāḥ adharmājñānānaiśvaryarūpāḥ ||
children.translated_text: By reversal, as their opposites, these, leaving aside attachment and being devoid of dispassion, are <s>tāmasa</s>, consisting of <s>adharma</s>, ignorance, and lack of lordly power.

children.text: avairāgyalakṣaṇas tu bhāvo rājasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But the <s>bhāva</s> characterized by absence of dispassion is <s>rājasa</s>.

children.text: pratyayān saṃcaṣṭe ||
children.translated_text: He explains the <s>pratyaya</s>s.

children.text: Chapter 204
te dharmādaya upādānam utpattihetur yeṣāṃ te saṃsāryaṇoḥ pratyāyanātpratyayā iṣṭāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those whose material cause, whose cause of arising, is <s>dharma</s> and the rest, and which make the transmigrating <s>aṇu</s> cognize, are accepted as <s>pratyaya</s>s.

children.text: kiyanta ityāha aṣṭau navetyādi aṣṭavidhā siddhirnavavidhā tuṣṭir vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇā ||
children.translated_text: How many are they? He says, 'eight, nine,' and so on. The <s>siddhi</s>s are eightfold, and the <s>tuṣṭi</s>s are ninefold, with definitions to be stated below.

children.text: uktaṃ ca sāṃkhyaiḥ
children.translated_text: And the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>s have said:

children.text: ūhaḥ śabdo'dhyayanaṃ duḥkhavighātatrayaṃ suhṛtprāptiḥ
children.translated_text: 'Reasoning, verbal instruction, study, the threefold removal of suffering, and the obtaining of a friend,

children.text: dānaṃ ca siddhayo'ṣṭau ||
children.translated_text: and giving: these are the eight <s>siddhi</s>s.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tathā
children.translated_text: Likewise:

children.text: ādhyātmikyaś catasraḥ prakṛtyupādānakālabhāgyākhyāḥ
children.translated_text: 'The internal ones are four, called <s>prakṛti</s>, means, time, and fortune;

children.text: bāhyā viṣayoparamāt pañca ca nava tuṣṭayo 'bhihitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the external ones, from cessation with regard to objects, are five. Thus nine <s>tuṣṭi</s>s are stated.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: caturguṇāḥ sapta aṣṭāviṃśatisaṃkhyā bhavanti tāvatsaṃkhyasaṃkhyātā śaktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seven taken fourfold amount to the number twenty-eight; <s>aśakti</s> (incapacity) is reckoned as having that number.

children.text: karmendriyabuddhīndriyamanasāṃ vighātā ekādaśa
children.translated_text: The impairments of the organs of action, the organs of cognition, and the mind are eleven:

children.text: bādhiryam āndhyam aghratvaṃ mūkatā jaḍatā ca yā
children.translated_text: deafness, blindness, lack of smell, muteness, and dullness,

children.text: unmādakauṣṭhyakauṇyāni klaibyodāvartapaṅgutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: madness, leprosy, maimedness, impotence, retention, and lameness.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: buddhivadhāśca prāguktānāṃ tuṣṭisiddhīnāṃ viparyayāḥ saptadaśetyaṣṭāviṃśatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the impairments of <s>buddhi</s> are the opposites of the previously mentioned <s>tuṣṭi</s>s and <s>siddhi</s>s; these are seventeen. Thus there are twenty-eight.

children.text: tathā cāhuḥ kāpilāḥ
children.translated_text: And so the <s>Kāpila</s>s say:

children.text: ekādaśendriyavadhāḥ saha buddhivadhair aśaktir uddiṣṭā
children.translated_text: 'The eleven impairments of the senses, together with the impairments of <s>buddhi</s>, are specified as incapacity;

children.text: saptadaśa vadhā buddherviparyayāt tuṣṭisiddhīnām ||
children.translated_text: the impairments of <s>buddhi</s> are seventeen, because they are the reverses of the <s>tuṣṭi</s>s and <s>siddhi</s>s.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: pañca ca vikhyātā iti viparyayabhedās tamomohamahāmohatāmisrāndhatāmisrākhyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the five well-known ones are the divisions of error called <s>tamas</s>, <s>moha</s>, <s>mahāmoha</s>, <s>tāmisra</s>, and <s>andhatāmisra</s>.

children.text: ete pañca siddhayo 'ṣṭau tuṣṭayo nava aśaktayo 'ṣṭāviṃśatir ityevaṃ vargaśaḥ vargakrameṇa pañcāśat pratyayāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These five errors, the eight <s>siddhi</s>s, the nine <s>tuṣṭi</s>s, and the twenty-eight <s>aśakti</s>s: in this way, by classes and in class order, there are fifty <s>pratyaya</s>s.

children.text: ye caivaṃ saṃkhyātaḥ pratipāditāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And these have thus been enumerated and explained.

children.text: Chapter 205
kiṃ tadityāha ||
children.translated_text: What is that? He says:

children.text: Chapter 206
ete bhāvāḥ sāṃsiddhikādibhedāttridhā saṃsāryaṇorbhavanti ||
children.translated_text: These <s>bhāva</s>s become threefold for the transmigrating <s>aṇu</s>, because of distinctions such as the innate.

children.text: atha teṣāṃ sāṃsiddhikādīnāṃ svarūpam abhidhatte ||
children.translated_text: Now he states the nature of those, the innate and the others.

children.text: Chapter 207
viśiṣṭeneṣṭāpūrtādidharmasaṃskāreṇa samyag uddīpitaṃ ceto yeṣāṃ teṣāṃ na paraṃ dehasaṃyoge yāvad dehābhāve 'pi prāgvadyo guṇaḥ prakāśate sa sāṃsiddhiko nāma boddhavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For those whose mind has been properly kindled by a specific impression of <s>dharma</s>, such as sacrificial and charitable merit, the quality that shines forth not only in conjunction with a body, but even in the absence of a body as before, is to be understood as called <s>sāṃsiddhika</s> (innate).

children.text: Chapter 208
yastu sadyathāvaddhitalokabuddher gurutaḥ śāstrādvā samarjitaḥ sa vainayiko bhāti prakāśate ||
children.translated_text: But that which has been properly acquired from a teacher or from scripture, by an understanding directed toward what is beneficial, shines forth as <s>vainayika</s> (produced by discipline).

children.text: Chapter 209
yo manovāktanuceṣṭayā śuddhavyāpāreṇārjitaḥ sa vainayiko boddhavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That which is acquired through pure activity of mind, speech, and body is to be understood as <s>vainayika</s>.

children.text: Chapter 210
yaḥ punaḥ svapnamadamūrchāprabuddhasya yathāprastutasaṃskāra iva dehasaṃyoga eva vyajyate na dehāpāye'pi sa prākṛto nāma guṇo vijñeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, the quality which, like the relevant latent impression in someone awakened from dream, intoxication, or fainting, becomes manifest only in conjunction with the body and not also when the body has passed away, is to be known as <s>prākṛta</s> (natural).

children.text: athaitebhyaḥ sāṃsiddhikādibhyo dharmebhyaḥ phalaviśeṣān vaktumāha ||
children.translated_text: Now, in order to state the specific fruits arising from these <s>dharma</s>s, the innate and the others, he says:

children.text: Chapter 211
tatra tāvadvainayikeṣu rūpeṣu krameṇārthāḥ sampadyante sphītim upayānti ||
children.translated_text: There, first, in the <s>vainayika</s> forms, the aims are accomplished in order; they attain increase.

children.text: ke ta ityāha svarga ityādi dharmātsvargaḥ jñānānmuktiḥ vairāgyāt prakṛtilayaḥ aiśvaryādavighātaḥ yatheṣṭasiddhir ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What are they? He says, 'heaven,' and so on. From <s>dharma</s> comes heaven; from knowledge, liberation; from dispassion, dissolution into <s>prakṛti</s>; from lordly power, freedom from obstruction, that is, the accomplishment of what one desires.

children.text: athādharmāt tiryagādiyonikrāntiḥ ajñānānnirayāvāptiḥ avairāgyādbandhaḥ anaiśvaryād vighātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then from <s>adharma</s> comes passage into animal and other wombs; from ignorance, attainment of hell; from absence of dispassion, bondage; and from lack of lordly power, obstruction.

children.text: atha sāṃsiddhikeṣūcyante ||
children.translated_text: Now the results among the innate forms are stated.

children.text: Chapter 212
dharmādiṣu sāṃsiddhikeṣu satsvidam idaṃ sampadyata iti pūrveṇa sambandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the innate forms of <s>dharma</s> and the rest exist, 'this and this is accomplished': this is to be connected with the preceding statement.

children.text: kiṃ kimityatrāha vaśyākrāntirityādi vaśyākrāntiḥ sāṃsiddhikād dharmāt tatparijñānayogas tādṛgvidhājjñānāt bhogeṣvanabhilāṣo vairāgyāt vighnasamūhāpagama aiśvaryāt bhogeṣvāsaktiḥ sāṃsiddhikād adharmāt nyakkṛtir nyakkāras tathāvidhād ajñānāt dehalabdhir avairāgyāt kāryeṣu vighno'naiśvaryāditi ||
children.translated_text: What are these several things? He says, 'subjugating mastery,' and so on. Subjugating mastery arises from innate <s>dharma</s>; conjunction with knowledge of that arises from knowledge of that same kind; lack of desire for enjoyments arises from dispassion; the disappearance of a mass of obstacles arises from lordly power; attachment to enjoyments arises from innate <s>adharma</s>; humiliation, that is, being put down, arises from ignorance of that kind; acquisition of a body arises from lack of dispassion; and obstruction in actions arises from lack of lordly power.

children.text: Chapter 213
atheti bhāvoktyanantaraṃ pratyayasambandhināṃ siddhituṣṭyādivargāṇāṃ saṃkṣepātsādhāraṇaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ kathyate ||
children.translated_text: With 'now,' after the statement of the <s>bhāva</s>s, a concise common definition is given for the classes such as <s>siddhi</s> and <s>tuṣṭi</s>, which belong to the <s>pratyaya</s>s.

children.text: kimarthamityāha viplavo mā bhūd iti prabhedaśaḥ pravibhāgaśaḥ vargaśaḥ yā saṃkṣepoktiḥ kṛtā tasyāḥ sakāśādviplavo matisammoho mā bhūt ||
children.translated_text: Why? He says, 'so that there may be no confusion.' The summary that was made by divisions, by subdivisions, and by classes should not produce confusion, that is, bewilderment of the mind.

children.text: te 'ṣṭau nava caturguṇāḥ sapta pañca cetyetāvatā saṃkṣiptaprabhedakathanena buddhiviplavo yaḥ śaṅkyate sa evaṃvidhā tuṣṭiritthaṃvidhā siddhir ityevaṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇe saṃkṣipte kṛte na bhavatītyetadartham idam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The confusion of <s>buddhi</s> that might be suspected from the abbreviated statement of divisions as 'eight, nine, four times seven, and five' does not arise when a general definition has been given in summary: 'such is <s>tuṣṭi</s>, such is <s>siddhi</s>.' This is the purpose of the present statement.

children.text: atha taducyate ||
children.translated_text: Now that is stated.

children.text: Chapter 214
puṃsyātmani prakṛtāv avyakte ādigrahaṇād vyakte ca yā buddhir vijñānaṃ sā siddhir ityucyate ||
children.translated_text: The cognition, the discriminative knowledge, concerning the <s>puruṣa</s>, the self, concerning <s>prakṛti</s>, the unmanifest, and, by the word 'and so on,' concerning the manifest as well, is called <s>siddhi</s>.

children.text: yā tv akṛtārthasya nuḥ puṃsaḥ kṛtārtho 'smīti buddhiḥ sā tuṣṭiḥ ||
children.translated_text: But the cognition of a person who has not accomplished his aim, 'I have accomplished my aim,' is <s>tuṣṭi</s>.

children.text: Chapter 215
kārakāṇām antaḥkaraṇabahiṣkaraṇānām apāye vināśe sati vidyamāne 'pyarthe aprabhavaṇaśīlatvam aśaktir andhabadhirāder iva rūpaśabdādau ||
children.translated_text: When the instruments, the inner organ and the outer organs, have lapsed or been destroyed, the inability to function even though the object is present is <s>aśakti</s> (incapacity), as in the case of a blind or deaf person with regard to form or sound.

children.text: kiṃcit sādhāraṇyād anyasminnanyādṛśī buddhirviparyayaḥ marumarīcikāsviva jalāvagatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because of some common feature, cognition of one thing as another of a different kind is <s>viparyaya</s> (error), as when water is apprehended in desert mirages.

children.text: Chapter 216
saiṣā siddhirvyaktyādiprakāśakatvāt sāttvikī sattvasya prakāśasvarūpatvāt ||
children.translated_text: This <s>siddhi</s> is <s>sāttvika</s>, because it illuminates the manifest and the rest, since <s>sattva</s> has illumination as its nature.

children.text: kiṃca prakāśārthapravṛttatayā hetubhūtayā rajo'ṃśaprabhavāpyasau siddhir jñeyā ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, because its activity is directed toward illumination and has a causal basis, this <s>siddhi</s> too should be understood as arising from a portion of <s>rajas</s>.

children.text: na hy amiśrā guṇā janakā ityuktam ||
children.translated_text: For unmixed <s>guṇa</s>s are not producers, as has been stated.

children.text: yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: For this reason:

children.text: Chapter 217
akṛtārthasya kṛtārtho'smīti buddhis tuṣṭir yoktā seyaṃ mithyārūpatvāt tamoguṇalakṣaṇā sukharūpatayā sāttvikyapyavagamyate ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tuṣṭi</s> has been stated as the cognition, 'I have accomplished my aim,' in one whose aim has not been accomplished. Since it is false in nature, it is characterized by the <s>tamo-guṇa</s>; yet because it has the form of pleasure, it is also understood to be <s>sāttvika</s>.

children.text: Chapter 218
apravṛttirūpā aśaktir uktā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aśakti</s> has been stated as consisting in non-activity.

children.text: ataścāsau tāmasī duḥkhahetutvācca rājasyapi vijñeyā ||
children.translated_text: Therefore it is <s>tāmasī</s>; and because it is a cause of suffering, it should also be known as <s>rājasī</s>.

children.text: yo hi kārye 'śaktyākhye duḥkharūpo 'prabhaviṣṇutārūpo vā guṇo'sti so 'vaśyaṃ kāraṇāśrayaḥ rajastamolakṣaṇakāraṇajanita ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For whatever quality exists in the effect called <s>aśakti</s>, whether it has the form of suffering or the form of inability to function, must necessarily rest on its cause. The meaning is that it is produced by a cause characterized by <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>.

children.text: Chapter 219
viparyayasya mithyārūpatvāt tamaḥprabhavatvam ||
children.translated_text: Because <s>viparyaya</s> is false in nature, it arises from <s>tamas</s>.

children.text: sa ca viparyayaḥ sādhāraṇyamātraprathanāt prakāśarūpaḥ sattvātmako'pi niścitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And that <s>viparyaya</s>, because it manifests only a bare commonality, is also determined to be luminous and of the nature of <s>sattva</s>.

children.text: upasaṃharannāha ||
children.translated_text: Summing up, he says:

children.text: Chapter 220
iti evaṃpratipādito bhāvapratyayalakṣaṇo buddhiprakāśaḥ paśoḥ saṃsāryaṇoḥ bodhavyaktyāśrayatvād bodhasaṃjñayocyate ||
children.translated_text: Thus the illumination of <s>buddhi</s>, defined by the <s>bhāva</s>s and <s>pratyaya</s>s and explained in this way, is called <s>bodha</s> (cognition), because it is the locus for the manifestation of cognition in the <s>paśu</s>, the transmigrating atomic self.

children.text: athātra muniḥ sāṃkhyacchāyayā praśnayati ||
children.translated_text: Now here the sage raises a question in a <s>Sāṃkhya</s>-like manner.

children.text: Chapter 221
uktayā nītyā bodhanimittatvaṃ buddher yaducyate tadvidyāyā ānarthakyaṃ tasyā api bodhahetutvenābhyupagamāt ||
children.translated_text: By the reasoning already stated, if <s>buddhi</s> is said to be the cause of cognition, then <s>vidyā</s> is purposeless, since it too is accepted as a cause of cognition.

children.text: yadi ca sāmānyavyāpāratve 'pi tadabhyupagamaḥ tadānavasthā ||
children.translated_text: And if that is accepted even though its operation is general, then there is an infinite regress.

children.text: kiṃca avairāgyalakṣaṇe buddhidharme rāgarūpe satyapi kalājanmā rāgaḥ kiṃ karoti na kiṃcidapyasya kāryam avairāgyeṇaivātiśayavatā tatprayojanasya sampatteḥ ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, even when the <s>buddhi</s>-quality characterized by lack of dispassion exists as attachment, what does the attachment born of <s>kalā</s> do? Nothing at all, since its purpose is already accomplished by lack of dispassion itself, which is stronger.

children.text: athaitatpratikṣepaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now comes the refutation of this.

children.text: Chapter 222
bodhavyañjakavidyākhyaṃ tattvaṃ buddhyātmakavyañjakāntarasadbhāve sati yadyanarthakaṃ tarhi bhavato 'pi kāpilasya manaindriyalakṣaṇārthasadbhāve buddhir apyanarthikā ||
children.translated_text: If the principle called <s>vidyā</s>, the revealer of cognition, is purposeless when another revealer in the form of <s>buddhi</s> exists, then for you too, a <s>Kāpila</s>, <s>buddhi</s> would also be purposeless when there exists an entity characterized as mind and senses.

children.text: tathāhi rūpādigrāhakacakṣurādikaraṇāvadhātari manasi vyañjakāntareṇa buddhyākhyena kiṃ prayojanaṃ mano'dhiṣṭhitair indriyair eva tattatkāryasiddheḥ ||
children.translated_text: For, when the mind attends to the instruments such as the eye that apprehend form and the like, what purpose is served by another revealer called <s>buddhi</s>, since the corresponding tasks are accomplished solely by the senses governed by the mind?

children.text: Chapter 223

atha proktavadbuddher apyānarthakyaprasaṅgatayā vyañjakāntarasadbhāve vyañjakasyānarthakyaṃ prasajyata ityevaṃ na paryanuyujyate kiṃtu karaṇatvavivakṣayaivaṃ kecidbruvate codyaṃ kurvanti yaduta buddhyākhye karaṇe satyapi kiṃ vidyābhidhānena karaṇena ||
children.translated_text: Now, because the uselessness of <s>buddhi</s> would follow in the way just stated, the objection is not framed simply as, 'When another revealer exists, a revealer becomes purposeless.' Rather, with instrumentality in view, some state the objection as follows: even when an instrument called <s>buddhi</s> exists, what need is there for an instrument called <s>vidyā</s>?

children.text: yathoktam
children.translated_text: As has been said:

children.text: sā vidyā tatparaṃ karaṇam ||
children.translated_text: 'That <s>vidyā</s> is the supreme instrument.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: ihāpyuktam
children.translated_text: Here too it has been said:

children.text: tattvaṃ vidyākhyam asṛjat karaṇaṃ paramātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'He created the principle called <s>vidyā</s>, the supreme instrument of the Supreme Self.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: so 'pyayaṃ pakṣo manaḥṣaṣṭhair buddhīndriyair anaikāntikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That position too is inconclusive in view of the cognitive senses together with the mind as the sixth.

children.text: tathāhi buddhīndriyapañcakasya svasvaviṣayagrahaṇakriyāyāṃ karaṇasya sataḥ ṣaṣṭhena manasā karaṇāntareṇāṅgīkriyamāṇenānaikāntikīkṛtam etat yatkaraṇāntarasadbhāve karaṇānarthakyam iti ||
children.translated_text: For the claim that an instrument is useless when another instrument exists is made inconclusive by the five cognitive senses: in their acts of apprehending their respective objects, another instrument, the sixth, namely the mind, is accepted.

children.text: pratyuta karaṇāntarāpekṣasya kāsucitkriyāsūpalambhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: On the contrary, in some actions an instrument is observed to depend on another instrument.

children.text: uktaṃ ca śrīmatparākhye
children.translated_text: And it is said in the venerable <s>Parākhya</s>:

children.text: karaṇaṃ karaṇāpekṣam ājāvibhakarāstravat ||
children.translated_text: 'An instrument depends on an instrument, like a hand and a weapon in battle.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: yathā caiṣāṃ śrotrādīnāṃ pañcānāṃ manaḥṣaṣṭhatvaṃ karaṇatve sāmānye 'pyātmavādibhir iṣṭaṃ tathā buddhau satyāmapi tadgrāhikā vidyā setsyatīti na kaścid doṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And just as, even though the five beginning with hearing have the common status of instruments, those who affirm a self accept them as having the mind as a sixth, so too, even when <s>buddhi</s> exists, a <s>vidyā</s> that apprehends it will be established; there is no fault.

children.text: evaṃ ca pakṣadvayenāśaṅkitaṃ codyaṃ samarthya pakṣāntareṇāpyāśaṅkamānas taddūṣaṇāyāha ||
children.translated_text: And thus, having presented the objection suspected under two alternatives, and now suspecting it under another alternative as well, he speaks in order to refute it.

children.text: Chapter 224
nanvekasmin viṣaye viniyogo'sti yasya sa padārtha eko'nyasya ekaviniyogitve satyatiricyate adhikībhavati dhvāntadhvaṃsakṣamamaṇyālokasambhava iva dīpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Objection: when one entity has an application with respect to one object, then, if another has the same application, that other is superfluous and excessive, like a lamp when there is light from a gem capable of destroying darkness.

children.text: tataśca sukhaduḥkhamohātmakapuṃbhogasādhanatvaṃ buddher eva paryāptam atas tadartham iṣyamāṇāyāḥ punar api vidyāyā ānarthakyam ityāśaṅkyaitannirāsaḥ śrotradṛkpāṇipādādīti tata iti evam abhyupagamāt ekaviniyogitve satyekasyātirekatvāṅgīkaraṇe satītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>buddhi</s> alone is sufficient as the means for the enjoyment of the <s>puṃs</s>, whose experience consists of pleasure, pain, and delusion; hence the <s>vidyā</s> accepted again for that purpose would be useless. Suspecting this, he gives the refutation with the words beginning 'hearing, sight, hands, feet, and so on.' The word 'therefore' means: because this is admitted, namely because, when there is one application, one accepts the excessiveness of one of the two.

children.text: nur iti paśutvayogino bhoktuḥ puṃsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The word 'nuḥ' means the enjoying <s>puṃs</s>, who is connected with the condition of a bound soul.

children.text: yaduktaṃ prāk
children.translated_text: As was said earlier:

children.text: bhogabhūmiṣu nā bhuṅkte bhogān kālānuvartinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the grounds of enjoyment, the person enjoys enjoyments that follow upon time.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tasya nuḥ puṃsaḥ śrotradṛgādi pāṇipādādi ca bhavatpakṣe bhinnārtham astu ekaviṣayaṃ mā bhūt ||
children.translated_text: For that 'nuḥ,' the <s>puṃs</s>, let hearing and sight and so on, and hands and feet and so on, in your view have distinct purposes; let them not have one object.

children.text: nanu kenoktaṃ śrotradṛgāder ekaviṣayatvaṃ nahi śrotragrāhyamarthaṃ dṛk gṛhṇāti pāṇikāryaṃ vā pādaḥ karoti pṛthagarthatvenaiṣāṃ prātisvikasvarūpatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Objection: Who has said that hearing, sight, and the rest have one object? The eye does not grasp an object graspable by hearing, nor does the foot perform the work of the hand, since each has its own specific nature through having a distinct purpose.

children.text: satyaṃ kiṃtu bhogaikasādhanatvavivakṣayaivam uktam ||
children.translated_text: True; but this has been said with the intention that they are means to one enjoyment.

children.text: tathāhi bhoktuḥ puṃsaḥ āmrādisaurabhānubhavatas tadanveṣaṇodyamaḥ tataścāmrāḥ santīti śravaṇāt tatra pravartanaṃ dṛśā taddarśanaṃ rasanena cāsvādanam ityekaviniyogitvam indriyāṇām anumānam api bhavatpakṣe na yuktam abhyupagantum ānarthakyabhayāt ||
children.translated_text: For example, when the enjoying <s>puṃs</s> experiences the fragrance of mangoes and the like, there is an effort to seek them out; then, on hearing that mangoes are there, he proceeds to that place, sees them with sight, and tastes them with the sense of taste. In this way the senses have one application. In your view, even inference is not properly admitted, for fear of uselessness.

children.text: tataśca bhinnārthameva śrotradṛgādi pāṇipādādi ca yuṣmaddṛśā bhavatu puṃbhogakāryahetutve nābhinnaviṣayamapi bhinnaphalam astvityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the sense is this: in the view of people like you, hearing and sight and so on, and hands and feet and so on, may indeed have distinct purposes; yet, as causes of the act of the <s>puṃs</s>'s enjoyment, even things with a common object may have distinct results.

children.text: na caivam ittham ||
children.translated_text: And it is not so in this way.

children.text: tṛtīyam api parāśaṅkāprakāraṃ parihṛtya parābhimatam ekaviniyogitvaṃ vidyābuddhyor nirākartum āha ||
children.translated_text: Having also disposed of the third form of the opponent's suspicion, he speaks in order to reject the single application of <s>vidyā</s> and <s>buddhi</s> accepted by the opponent.

children.text: Chapter 225
naca vidyāyā buddheścaikārthaviniyogitvaṃ bhinnaviṣayatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Nor do <s>vidyā</s> and <s>buddhi</s> have one and the same application, because their objects are different.

children.text: viniyogāntaraṃ ca tad dvāraṃ mukhaṃ yasyāḥ sā mukhāntareṇānyena viniyogena pravṛttā anekasādhyatā na duṣṭā yathā indhanodakadarvyādyanekasādhanasādhyāyāḥ pākakriyāyāḥ pṛthakprayojanatve sati bhinnakārakābhyupagame na kiṃcid apakṛṣyate ||
children.translated_text: That which has another application as its doorway or opening proceeds through another opening, that is, through another application. Being accomplished by many means is not faulty. Just as, when the act of cooking is accomplished by many means such as fuel, water, and a ladle, nothing is diminished by accepting distinct factors when their purposes are separate.

children.text: atha kiṃ tadbhinnaviṣayatvaṃ vidyābuddhyorityāha ||
children.translated_text: Now he asks, 'What is that difference of object between <s>vidyā</s> and <s>buddhi</s>?' He says:

children.text: Chapter 226
vidyā tāvat vyaktāṇucicchaktiḥ vyaktā uddīpitā aṇoś cicchaktir yayā etāvadevāsyāḥ karaṇīyam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vidyā</s>, first, is that by which the conscious power of the <s>aṇu</s> is made manifest: by it the <s>aṇu</s>'s power of consciousness is manifested and kindled. This alone is what it has to do.

children.text: tatastu nunnaṃ preritamavadhānena niyojitam akṣeśaṃ mano yeṣāṃ tāni tathāvidhāni yānyakṣāṇīndriyāṇi tadgocarāṃs tadviṣayān svīkṛtya puṃsprayuktasyeti puṃsā prakarṣeṇa yuktasya sākṣātsvātmanyevopakārakatvena sthitasyāsyaiva vidyākhyasya karaṇasya buddhiryataḥ karmatāmeti grāhyatvam āgacchati tenetarā vidyā ato dūraṃ bhinnā ||
children.translated_text: Then the senses, whose lord, the mind, has been driven, impelled, and directed by attention, take up the objects within their range. And since <s>buddhi</s> becomes the object, that is, comes to be graspable, for this very instrument called <s>vidyā</s>, which is employed by the <s>puṃs</s>, meaning fully joined to the <s>puṃs</s> and standing directly as a helper in its own self, that other <s>vidyā</s> is therefore far different from <s>buddhi</s>.

children.text: tadiyatā vidyāvaidharmyaṃ nirākṛtya atha dvitīyacodyasya nirāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having thus disposed of the matter of <s>vidyā</s>'s difference, there is now the refutation of the second objection.

children.text: Chapter 227
rāgo na buddhiguṇo'vairāgyalakṣaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāga</s> is not a quality of <s>buddhi</s> characterized by absence of dispassion.

children.text: kuta ityāha tadvidharmataḥ tasmādāgamoktādrāgāt gauṇasya vaidharmyaṃ yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Why? He says, 'because it is different from that': because the secondary usage differs from that <s>rāga</s> taught in scripture.

children.text: luptabhāvapratyayo vidharmaśabdaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the word 'different-in-nature,' the abstract suffix has been elided.

children.text: kiṃ tadvaidharmyamityāha tacca bhogyatvamiti avairāgyalakṣaṇo buddhidharmaḥ srakcandanavanitādirvā viṣaya evaṃ bahiṣṭho yaḥ pareṣāṃ rāgatveneṣṭaḥ tasyaitadeva vaidharmyaṃ yadbhogyatvam ||
children.translated_text: What is that difference? He says, 'and that is being an object of enjoyment.' A quality of <s>buddhi</s> characterized by absence of dispassion, or an external object such as a garland, sandalwood, or a woman, which others accept as <s>rāga</s>, has precisely this difference, namely that it is enjoyable.

children.text: bhogābhiṣvaṅgahetunā rāgeṇa bhojakena ca bhāvyam ||
children.translated_text: There must be <s>rāga</s>, the cause of clinging to enjoyment, and there must also be an enjoyer.

children.text: na ca bhogyasya bhogahetoścābhedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the enjoyed object and the cause of enjoyment are not identical.

children.text: etadvā bhogyatvaṃ rāgasyāṅgīkriyate tarhi vītarāgastato hataḥ tata iti evamabhyupagamādvītarāgābhāvadoṣaḥ prasajyate ||
children.translated_text: Or, if this enjoyability is accepted for <s>rāga</s>, then the category of the dispassionate person is destroyed by that; from such an admission the fault follows that there would be no one free from <s>rāga</s>.

children.text: bhoktṛgatarāgānabhyupagame bahiṣṭhavarāṅganādibhogyaviśeṣarūparāgopagame ca sati sarāgavītarāgasaṃnikarṣasthasragādau bhogyaviṣaye sarveṣāṃ sarāgatā prāpnoti nahi kaścidatra vītarāgo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: If one does not accept <s>rāga</s> as located in the enjoyer, and instead accepts <s>rāga</s> as a particular external enjoyable object such as a beautiful woman, then, when an enjoyable object such as a garland stands in proximity to both the attached and the dispassionate, everyone would become attached; no one here would be free from <s>rāga</s>.

children.text: vastuto vītarāgāṇāmapi bhogyaviśeṣasaṃnidhimātrādeva sarāgatāyā dṛṣṭatvāt ||
children.translated_text: For, in fact, even dispassionate persons would be seen as attached merely because of the presence of a particular enjoyable object.

children.text: uktaṃ ca sadyojyotiḥpādaiḥ bhogyaviśeṣe rāge nahi kaścidvītarāgaḥ syāt
children.translated_text: And the venerable <s>Sadyojyotis</s> has said: 'If <s>rāga</s> were a particular enjoyable object, no one would be free from <s>rāga</s>.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tasmādbhoktṛgata eva rāgopagamo na bhogyaviśeṣarūpaḥ sragādiḥ avairāgyalakṣaṇabuddhidharmātmako vā ||
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>rāga</s> is to be accepted only as located in the enjoyer, not as a particular enjoyable object such as a garland, nor as consisting in a property of <s>buddhi</s> characterized by absence of dispassion.

children.text: ataśca ||
children.translated_text: And therefore:

children.text: Chapter 228

uktavadbhoktṛgato rāgo yo'rtheṣu sragādiṣvabhilāṣa ityabhilāṣaheturevābhilāṣaśabdenoktaḥ kāraṇe kāryasyābhedopacārāt āyurghṛtamitivat sa ca rāgākhyo'rtheṣu abhilāṣarūpatvādabhilāṣaheturviṣayadvaye ekasminbāhye srakcandanādau vītarāgābhāvaprasaṅgatayā nāstītyabhyupagantavyaḥ dvitīyasmiṃstu avairāgyalakṣaṇe buddhidharme bhogyarūpatvād abhilāṣahetutvaṃ nāsti ||
children.translated_text: As stated, the <s>rāga</s> (attachment) that belongs to the enjoyer, namely desire for objects such as garlands and the like, is called by the word 'desire' only as the cause of desire, because the effect is figuratively identified with the cause, as in the expression 'ghee is life.' And this so-called <s>rāga</s>, as the cause of desire toward objects because it has the form of desire, must be admitted not to exist in one of the two domains, namely in external things such as garlands and sandalwood, since otherwise there would be no one free from attachment. But in the second domain, the property of <s>buddhi</s> characterized as absence of dispassion, there is no status as cause of desire, because it has the form of something to be enjoyed.

children.text: tasmādabhilāṣahetunā rāgeṇa janyate asau buddhigataspṛhātmakaḥ kriyārūpo bhogyatvasaṃpādaka ityalam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore that state, whose nature is longing located in <s>buddhi</s>, which has the form of activity and which produces enjoyability, is generated by <s>rāga</s>, the cause of desire. Enough on this.

children.text: nanu karmaiva sukhaduḥkhādirūpabhogye'bhilāṣa hetutvena bhaviṣyatītyāha ||
children.translated_text: But, one might object, <s>karma</s> itself may be the cause of desire for what is to be enjoyed in the form of pleasure, pain, and the like. He replies:

children.text: Chapter 229
prāgukte'smin viṣayadvaye sarāgavītarāgātmakasthitivyavasthāpakatvena vyāpakaṃ karmāstu yat itaratreti rāge parikalpite'pi kalpyaṃ kilāvaśyam abhyupagantavyam ||
children.translated_text: Let <s>karma</s> be pervasive insofar as it establishes the condition consisting of attachment and freedom from attachment in the two domains just mentioned; even if <s>rāga</s> is postulated as something other, surely it too must necessarily be accepted.

children.text: taddhetorapi karmaiṣṭavyam ||
children.translated_text: For <s>karma</s> must be accepted even as the cause of that.

children.text: tadeva tattadvastuvaicitryāt sarāgavītarāgatākāraṇatvenāstviti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The prima facie view is this: let that very <s>karma</s>, because of the diversity of the various things, be the cause of states of attachment and freedom from attachment.

children.text: siddhāntastu ||
children.translated_text: But the established conclusion is as follows:

children.text: Chapter 230
kevalasya karmaṇo niyatisiddhāveva dūṣaṇaṃ darśitam ||
children.translated_text: The fault in positing <s>karma</s> alone has already been shown in the establishment of <s>niyati</s> itself.

children.text: tathā coktam
children.translated_text: And so it has been said:

children.text: bhogo'rthaḥ sarvatattvānāṃ so'pi karmanibandhanaḥ
