children.translated_text: Enjoyment is the purpose of all the principles; and that too is dependent on <s>karma</s>.

children.text: karmaivāstu śarīrādi tataḥ sarvamapārthakam ||
children.translated_text: Let <s>karma</s> alone account for the body and so forth; then everything else is purposeless.

children.text: atha dehādisāpekṣaṃ tatpumarthaprasādhakam
children.translated_text: But if, depending on the body and the like, it accomplishes the aim of the person,

children.text: tato niyatisāpekṣamastu karma niyāmakam ||
children.translated_text: then let <s>karma</s>, depending on <s>niyati</s>, be the regulator.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tasmāt tanukaraṇabhogādivaicitryamātra eva caritārthatvāt kāryāntare pramāṇābhāvācca na karmaṇo rāgakāryasaṃpādakatvam api tu uktaprayojanaḥ kalājanyo rāgaḥ siddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, since <s>karma</s> has fulfilled its purpose merely in the diversity of body, instruments, enjoyments, and the like, and since there is no proof for any further effect, <s>karma</s> does not accomplish the effect of <s>rāga</s>. Rather, <s>rāga</s>, produced by <s>kalā</s> and serving the purpose already stated, is established.

children.text: naca rāgavaddveṣasyāpi tattvāntaratvaṃ dveṣādīnāṃ rāgajanitapravṛttiviśeṣātmakatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Nor is <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), like <s>rāga</s>, a separate principle, because aversion and the other such states consist of particular activities generated by <s>rāga</s>.

children.text: kasmiṃścidabhilaṣaṇīye vastuni kila vyāhanyamāne'sya dveṣādayaḥ saṃjāyante ||
children.translated_text: For when some desirable object is obstructed, aversion and the like arise in him.

children.text: nanvitaretaropamardena rāgadveṣayoryato'vasthitistasmādekasminpuṃsi sahānavasthānadoṣaḥ prāpnotītyāha ||
children.translated_text: But, one might object, since <s>rāga</s> and <s>dveṣa</s> exist by mutually suppressing one another, the fault would follow that they cannot abide together in one person. He replies:

children.text: Chapter 231
kastāvadayaṃ sahānavasthānadoṣaḥ yadyekakālatayā tadetanna dūṣaṇam apitu dūṣaṇameva ||
children.translated_text: First, what is this alleged fault of not abiding together? If it is simultaneity that is meant, then that is not a fault for us; rather, that itself would indeed be the fault.

children.text: nahi yadaiva yatra rāgastadānīmeva tatra dveṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For wherever there is attachment at a given time, there is not aversion toward that very thing at that very time.

children.text: atha yasminneva bhoktari rāgastatra dveṣa ityetannopapannaṃ tadapyayuktam ||
children.translated_text: If, however, the claim is that where there is attachment in the very same enjoyer, there cannot be aversion there too, that also is incorrect.

children.text: nahi anayorāśraye virodhaḥ kiṃtu viṣaye ||
children.translated_text: For the opposition between these two is not in their substrate, but in their object.

children.text: tulyabalatvena rāgadveṣayoḥ kramikatayā ekasminnāśraye viṣayavyāvṛttau na kaściddoṣo bhavadbhirudbhāvitasya sahānavasthānasyeṣṭatvāt ||
children.translated_text: When <s>rāga</s> and <s>dveṣa</s> are equal in strength, there is no fault if, with their objects kept distinct, they occur successively in one substrate; for the non-coexistence brought forward by you is accepted.

children.text: tathāhi sarvasya vyavahartuḥ sarvā vyavahṛtiḥ sukhaduḥkhabuddhisaṃbhavā ||
children.translated_text: For all ordinary activity of every agent arises from cognitions of pleasure and pain.

children.text: pravṛttasya cāsya sukhaṃ vā duḥkhaṃ vā moho vā jāyate ||
children.translated_text: And when this person has engaged in action, pleasure, pain, or delusion arises for him.

children.text: bhojanādipravṛttyanantaraṃ ca tatraiva dveṣaḥ tatpūrvakālatastu rāgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After the activity of eating and the like there is aversion toward that very thing, while before that time there was attachment.

children.text: punaśca dveṣānte kasmiṃścitkāle tadabhilāṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And again, at some time after the aversion has ended, desire for that thing arises.

children.text: yasmādyadeva vīryavadbalīyastadeva yogasyābhiṣvaṅgajanitasya saṃśleṣasya kāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: For whatever has potency and is stronger is the cause of <s>yoga</s>, that is, conjunction or adhesion produced by clinging.

children.text: yata evaṃ tasmādrāgasya dveṣād balīyastvāt sahānavasthānadoṣo na doṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since this is so, because <s>rāga</s> is stronger than <s>dveṣa</s>, the alleged fault of non-coexistence is no fault.

children.text: itthaṃ prāsaṅgikīṃ rāgatattvopapattimuktvā ahaṅkāratattvavyāpāramāha ||
children.translated_text: Having in this way stated the incidental proof of the <s>rāga</s>-principle, he states the operation of the <s>ahaṃkāra</s>-principle.

children.text: Chapter 232

avyaktādvyaktaṃ guṇatattvaṃ vyaktāntaraṃ tatkāryaṃ buddhiḥ tasyāḥ sakāśādahaṅkāraḥ cita ātmanaḥ saṃrambhavṛttyantaḥkaraṇamupapadyate yadvyāpārācchārīrāḥ śarīrāntaścarāḥ pañca vāyavaśceṣṭante svaṃ svaṃ vyāpāraṃ vidadhati ||
children.translated_text: From the unmanifest arises the manifest <s>guṇa</s>-principle; another manifest principle, its effect, is <s>buddhi</s>. From that comes <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, the inner organ whose mode is the aroused activity of the conscious self; through its operation the five bodily winds that move within the body act, each carrying out its own function.

children.text: ke ta ityāha ||
children.translated_text: Which are they? He says:

children.text: Chapter 233
prāṇāpānādayo ye pañca vāyavaste vṛttervyāpārabhedādbhinnāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The five winds, <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, and the others, are distinct because of differences in the operations of their activity.

children.text: natveṣāṃ vāstavo bhedaḥ vāyurūpatvāviśeṣāt ||
children.translated_text: But there is no real difference among them, since they are not different in being forms of wind.

children.text: athaiṣāmeva vyāpārabhedaṃ vakti ||
children.translated_text: Now he states the difference in their operations.

children.text: Chapter 234
tatra kā prāṇasya vṛttirityāha ||
children.translated_text: There, what is the activity of <s>prāṇa</s>? He says:

children.text: Chapter 235
prakarṣeṇa nayanaṃ praṇayanam
children.translated_text: Leading forth in a special way is <s>praṇayana</s>.

children.text: koṣṭhasthasya vāyorbāhyadvādaśāntaṃ yāvad yatprāpaṇaṃ saiṣā prāṇasya vṛttirvyāpāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The carrying of the wind located in the abdomen as far as the external twelve-finger limit: this is the activity, the operation, of <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: etacca vyāpārato nirvacanam ||
children.translated_text: And this is an explanation in terms of operation.

children.text: phalatastūcyate yattajjīvanaṃ nāma sā prāṇasyaiva vṛttiḥ ayamāśayaḥ praṇayanāt prāṇa iti niruktadṛśā vyāpāreṇa prāṇaśabdo lakṣitaḥ prakarṣeṇa ananaṃ prāṇanaṃ jīvanaṃ tato'pi prāṇa ityucyata iti phalaviṣayamasya nirvacanam ||
children.translated_text: But in terms of result, what is called living is precisely the activity of <s>prāṇa</s>. The intention is this: by the etymological view, the word <s>prāṇa</s> is indicated through the activity, because it performs <s>praṇayana</s>, leading forth; and it is also called <s>prāṇa</s> from <s>prāṇana</s>, living or breathing in an eminent way. Thus this explanation concerns its result.

children.text: phalatastūcyate yattatpuruṣāṇāmūhaṃ mārgayamāṇā andheva matirbhramati sa prāṇasyaiva vyāpāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: But in terms of result it is said that the reasoning of persons, while seeking a path, in which the mind wanders like a blind person, is also the operation of <s>prāṇa</s> itself.

children.text: ūho vimarśātmakastarkaḥ tatrāsyā dhiyaḥ prāṇe naiva preraṇaṃ kriyate ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ūha</s> is reasoning, a reflection in the form of deliberation; in that process this intellect is impelled by <s>prāṇa</s> alone.

children.text: prāṇarathādhirūḍhā hi sā saṃvid vimṛśati ||
children.translated_text: For mounted on the chariot of <s>prāṇa</s>, that consciousness reflects.

children.text: prāṇo vā balaṃ tadyogātprāṇa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Or else <s>prāṇa</s> is strength; because of connection with that, it is called <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: tasmācciti caitanye ātivāhike kalādikṣityante tattvaśarīre śaktau ca balātmikāyāṃ kalāsu ca somasūryādyātmikāsu prāṇaśabdo jñeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the word <s>prāṇa</s> should be understood with reference to <s>citi</s>, consciousness, to the <s>ātivāhika</s> body, to the body made of the <s>tattva</s>s from <s>kalā</s> down to earth, to <s>śakti</s> whose nature is strength, and to the <s>kalā</s>s whose nature is the moon, sun, and the like.

children.text: apānasya vṛttimāha ||
children.translated_text: He states the activity of <s>apāna</s>.

children.text: Chapter 236
apanayanamadhaḥprāpaṇaṃ bhuktapītaviṇmūtraretasāṃ yat karoti atastattvajñairapānākhyayoktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because it performs the carrying away, the downward conveyance, of what has been eaten and drunk, of feces, urine, and semen, it is therefore called <s>apāna</s> by those who know the <s>tattva</s>s.

children.text: atha samānavyānayor vyāpāroktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now there is a statement of the operations of <s>samāna</s> and <s>vyāna</s>.

children.text: Chapter 237
annapānasya sarvatra sāmyena niyamanātsamānasya samānatvaṃ dehasya vinamanādvyānasya vyānatā ||
children.translated_text: The sameness of <s>samāna</s> comes from its regulating food and drink everywhere evenly; the diffusiveness of <s>vyāna</s> comes from its causing the body to bend.

children.text: udānasya vṛttirucyate ||
children.translated_text: The activity of <s>udāna</s> is stated.

children.text: Chapter 238
vaktumicchā vivakṣā yatnaḥ saṃrambhaḥ tau pūrvau yasya tena
children.translated_text: By that for which the two preceding factors are the desire to speak, called <s>vivakṣā</s>, and effort, namely exertion,

children.text: koṣṭhasya vyomna āntarasyākāśasya guṇarūpo yaḥ śabdastasya yena vāgindriyasacivena vivakṣāyatnapūrveṇa vibhajya vaicitryaṃ kriyate so 'smindehe udānaśabdāt jñeyaḥ
children.translated_text: the sound that is the quality-form of the inner ether, the space within the bodily cavity, is differentiated and made varied, with the organ of speech as assistant and preceded by the desire to speak and effort; that is to be understood in this body by the word <s>udāna</s>.

children.text: yasya ca vāyoḥ prāṇāderyatsthānaṃ dhāraṇe sati jayaśca tajjayāt phalaṃ tadetadvaktavyaśeṣabhūtaṃ bhagavatā prakaraṇāntareṇa yogapādākhyenādiṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: For each wind, beginning with <s>prāṇa</s>, its particular location, its conquest when it is held, and the fruit resulting from conquering it, all this, being something still to be stated, has been taught by the Lord in another section called the <s>Yogapāda</s>.

children.text: Chapter 239

athānantaraṃ śeṣabhūtasyārthasya tanmātrendriyādeḥ siddhyarthamasyāhaṅkārasya ata eveti ahaṅkārādeva sa bhagavān anantaraprakaraṇānte patiśabdenokto yaḥ sa māyāgarbhādhikāriṇām anantādīnāmīśānāṃ śaktigastadabhivyaktaśaktiḥ sattvarajastamobahulān trīn skandhānniścakarṣa niṣkṛṣṭavān avibhinnamahaṅkāramāvirbhāvya tridhā vyabhajadityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Next, for the accomplishment of the remaining topic, namely the <s>tanmātra</s>s, senses, and so on, from this <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, the phrase "from this very" means from <s>ahaṅkāra</s> alone. That Lord, who was mentioned by the word <s>pati</s> at the end of the immediately preceding section, whose power abides in the lords beginning with <s>Ananta</s> who have authority over <s>Māyāgarbha</s>, and whose power is manifested through them, drew out three masses predominated by <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>; that is, having manifested undivided <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, he divided it threefold.

children.text: tadeva traividhyamāha ||
children.translated_text: He states that very threefoldness.

children.text: Chapter 240
taijasavaikārikabhūtādikasaṃjñakebhyas tebhyo'haṅkāraskandhebhyo devā buddhīndriyakarmendriyākhyāḥ samātrakās tanmātrasahitāḥ tanmātrebhyaśca bhūtapañcakamabhivyaktamiti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From those masses of <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, named <s>taijasa</s>, <s>vaikārika</s>, and <s>bhūtādika</s>, the gods called organs of cognition and organs of action, together with the <s>tanmātra</s>s, became manifest; and from the <s>tanmātra</s>s the set of five gross elements became manifest. This is the remaining sense.

children.text: atha kutaḥ kimabhivyaktam ||
children.translated_text: Now, from what was what manifested?

children.text: āha ||
children.translated_text: He says:

children.text: Chapter 241
śrotrādibuddhīndriyapañcakasya manasaśca prabodhavattvāt prakāśānvayo'sti ataḥ sāttvikā ete devāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because the five organs of cognition beginning with hearing, and the mind, have a connection with illumination, since they possess awakening, these gods are <s>sāttvika</s>.

children.text: sa ca sāttvika eva ||
children.translated_text: And that is precisely <s>sāttvika</s>.

children.text: tatprakṛtirahaṅkāraskandhastaijaso nāma jñeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The mass of <s>ahaṅkāra</s> that is their source is to be known by the name <s>taijasa</s>.

children.text: Chapter 242
vākpāṇipādapāyūpasthāḥ pañca rājasā devāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Speech, hands, feet, anus, and genitals are the five <s>rājasa</s> gods.

children.text: teṣāṃ karmānvayāt karmendriyatvāt rajobahulo vaikārikākhyo'haṅkāraskandhaḥ prakṛtibhūtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because they are connected with action, being organs of action, the mass of <s>ahaṅkāra</s> called <s>vaikārika</s>, which is predominated by <s>rajas</s>, is their material source.

children.text: Chapter 243
śabdasparśarūparasagandhā aviśiṣṭaguṇā anabhivyaktaviśeṣatvena tāvanmātrapade bhūtaprakṛtitvarūpe yojitāstanmātrāśabdena jñeyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell are undifferentiated qualities; since their specific distinctions are not yet manifest, they are connected with the word "so-much-only" in the sense of being the material causes of the elements, and are to be understood by the term <s>tanmātra</s>.

children.text: tāvatyaśca mātrāstanmātrā iti strīliṅgo'yamiha tanmātrāśabdaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And measures of just that extent are <s>tanmātra</s>s; here this word <s>tanmātrā</s> is feminine.

children.text: guṇāviśiṣṭatvaṃ caitāsāmittham yathā pṛthivyāṃ khaṭakhaṭādirūpaḥ śabdaḥ sparśaśca śītoṣṇaḥ rūpamapi anekavidhaṃ śuklādi ṣaḍvidhaśca raso gandhaśca surabhyasurabhirūpo'sti ||
children.translated_text: Their undifferentiatedness as qualities is as follows: in earth there is sound of the clacking and similar sort, touch as cold and hot, form of many kinds such as white, taste in six varieties, and smell in the form of fragrance and non-fragrance.

children.text: naivaṃ tatkāraṇabhūtapṛthivītanmātrāvasthitā viśeṣā upalabhyante apitu aviśiṣṭaguṇapañcakamātraṃ pṛthivītanmātrameva manyate ||
children.translated_text: But such specific distinctions are not perceived as present in the earth-<s>tanmātra</s> that is its cause; rather, the earth-<s>tanmātra</s> is regarded as merely the set of five undifferentiated qualities.

children.text: etāśca tanmātrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And these are the <s>tanmātra</s>s.

children.text: Chapter 244

prakāśakṛt sāttviko buddhīndriyamanolakṣaṇo yo vargaḥ yaśca karmakṛt rājasattvādvyāpārapravṛttaḥ karmendriyavargaḥ tābhyāṃ vargābhyāṃ vailakṣaṇyaṃ vaisādṛśyaṃ yasmādetāsāṃ tanmātrāṇāmatastamobhavā etāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because these <s>tanmātra</s>s are distinct and dissimilar from the two groups, namely the <s>sāttvika</s> group characterized by the organs of cognition and the mind, which produces illumination, and the group of organs of action, which performs action and is engaged in activity because it is <s>rājasa</s>, they are therefore born of <s>tamas</s>.

children.text: Chapter 245
eṣu cāhaṅkāraskandheṣu madhyādyo'yaṃ bhūtādirahaṅkāraskandhaḥ sa yasmātprakāśyaḥ tatkāryasya tanmātrātmano manobuddhibhyāṃ buddhīndriyaiśca yogibhir upalabhyatvāt tato'yaṃ tāmaso vijñeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And among these masses of <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, this present mass of <s>ahaṅkāra</s> called <s>bhūtādi</s> is something to be illuminated, because its effect, whose nature is the <s>tanmātra</s>s, is apprehended by yogins through mind, intellect, and the organs of cognition; therefore this is to be known as <s>tāmasa</s>.

children.text: uktaṃ ca sāṃkhyaiḥ
children.translated_text: And it has been said by the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>s:

children.text: bhūtādestānmātraḥ sa tāmasaḥ
children.translated_text: "The <s>tanmātra</s> is from <s>bhūtādi</s>; that is <s>tāmasa</s>."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: atha manaso vyāpāra ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Now the operation of the mind is stated.

children.text: Chapter 246
devanāt dyotanādvā devā indriyāṇi teṣāṃ pravartakamudyojakam āśusaṃcaraṇaśīlaṃ saṃkalpaguṇaṃ ca mano boddhavyam ||
children.translated_text: The senses are gods because of their play, or because of their illumination; the mind is to be understood as what sets those senses in motion and instigates them, as having the habit of moving swiftly, and as having conception as its quality.

children.text: śrotrādayastu devā yathāsvaṃ śabdādiviṣayagrāhakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But the gods beginning with hearing grasp their respective objects, sound and so on.

children.text: Chapter 247
vacanaṃ bhāṣaṇam ādānaṃ grahaṇaṃ saṃhlādaḥ ānandaḥ visargo malaviyogaḥ vihṛtiḥ sañcāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Speech is speaking; taking is grasping; <s>saṃhlāda</s> is pleasure; emission is separation from waste; wandering is movement.

children.text: etāḥ kriyāḥ krameṇa vāgādīnāṃ jñeyāḥ kākākṣinyāyena vāgādīnāmiti yojyam ||
children.translated_text: These actions are to be known, in order, as belonging to speech and the rest; by the crow's-eye rule, the phrase "of speech and the rest" should be construed with them.

children.text: tataśca vāgādīnāṃ padānyatvamiti yat tasyāśrayabhūtaṃ sthānaṃ tato'nyadevendriyam ||
children.translated_text: Consequently, as for the fact that the seats of speech and the rest are different: the organ is indeed something other than the place that serves as its support.

children.text: nahi karṇaśaṣkulyādereva śravaṇāditvam apitu tatsthānasthāyā indriyaśakteḥ ||
children.translated_text: For hearing and the like do not belong to the shell of the ear and so on itself, but rather to the power of the organ that abides in that place.

children.text: kuta ityāha pade satyapyatadguṇāḥ tacchaktivirahiṇo janā dṛśyante ||
children.translated_text: Why? He says: even when the seat exists, people are seen who do not have that quality, being devoid of that power.

children.text: na caiṣāṃ tāni sthānāni na santi ||
children.translated_text: And it is not the case that those seats do not exist in them.

children.text: mānasatve yuktimāha ||
children.translated_text: He states the reasoning for the existence of mind.

children.text: Chapter 248

ātmano bhokturindriyair bhogasādhanairarthaiśca śabdādibhirbhogyaiḥ saṃnikarṣe satyapi sarveṣāṃ devānāmindriyāṇāṃ yasmānna pravṛttiḥ apitu kasyacideva ato yattadindriyaṃ pravṛttaṃ tasya pravṛttau kārakamastīti yuktito'numānādavasīyate ||
children.translated_text: Although there is proximity between the self, the experiencer, the senses, which are instruments of experience, and objects such as sound, which are to be enjoyed, not all the gods, the senses, enter into activity, but only some one of them. Therefore it is ascertained by reasoning, by inference, that there is a causal factor in the activity of whichever sense has become active.

children.text: yadāhuḥ
children.translated_text: As they have said:

children.text: yugapaj jñānānutpattir manaso liṅgam
children.translated_text: The non-arising of cognitions simultaneously is the mark of <s>manas</s> (mind).

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: sarvadaiveti pāṭhe indriyārthasaṃnikarṣe satyapi kadācidevendriyāṇi arthagrahe pravartante na sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: On the reading 'always', the sense is: even when there is contact between a sense-organ and its object, the sense-organs engage in grasping objects only at some time, not always.

children.text: tato nūnameṣāṃ pravartakaṃ kimapyasti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore there must surely be some activator of them.

children.text: yadvinā na pravartante iti vyākhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: It should be explained as 'that without which they do not function.'

children.text: apiḥ samuccaye ||
children.translated_text: The word <s>api</s> has the sense of addition.

children.text: na paramāgamo manaḥsattāvedakaḥ yāvadyuktirapītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that not only scripture is a revealer of the existence of <s>manas</s>; reasoning too is.

children.text: evaṃca sati ||
children.translated_text: And when this is so,

children.text: Chapter 249
tattvāntarāṇāṃ kalārāgavidyādīnāmuktā yā vṛttayo vyāpārāḥ tābhyastāvadvailakṣaṇyaṃ saṃkalpanākhyasya karmaṇo'sti ||
children.translated_text: as against the stated functions, the operations, of other principles such as <s>kalā</s>, <s>rāga</s>, and <s>vidyā</s>, there is a distinctness of the action called <s>saṃkalpana</s> (conceptual construction).

children.text: vilakṣaṇaścāyaṃ saṃkalpo bījamudbhavahetuṃ gamayati jñāpayati ||
children.translated_text: And this distinct <s>saṃkalpa</s> (conceptual determination) points to, that is, makes known, a seed, a cause of its arising.

children.text: pāriśeṣyācca manastadvijñeyam ||
children.translated_text: And by elimination that should be known as <s>manas</s>.

children.text: Chapter 250
tasya manaso'kṣairyogāt jñānam utpadyate ||
children.translated_text: From the conjunction of that <s>manas</s> with the sense-organs, cognition arises.

children.text: tacca kramayogitayā kramikaṃ yathā rūpānubhavakāle na sparśānubhavaḥ rasādyanubhavo vā ||
children.translated_text: And because it is connected with sequence, that cognition is sequential: for example, at the time of the experience of color/form there is no experience of touch, or of taste and the rest.

children.text: yadyapi svādusurabhyabhijātamarmaraśabdavadabhirūpaṃ ca drāghiṣṭhaśaṣkulyādikam āsvādyamānaṃ yugapat pañcajñānotpādahetuḥ tathāpi utpalapatraśatavyaktibhedavadalakṣyasūkṣmakramāṇi kramikāṇyeva tāni rasādijñānāni ||
children.translated_text: Although a very long <s>śaṣkulī</s> and the like - sweet, fragrant, refined, making a crisp rustling sound, and beautiful - while being tasted, is a cause for the arising of five cognitions at once, nevertheless those cognitions of taste and the rest are indeed sequential, with a subtle sequence that is not perceived, like the distinct manifestation of a hundred lotus petals.

children.text: etacca śīghrasaṃcāritāṃ vinā yugapanmanasaḥ pañcajñānotpādanaṃ nābhāti na prakāśate ||
children.translated_text: And this does not appear as the mind producing five cognitions simultaneously, except through its very rapid movement.

children.text: bhautikendriyavādyabhiprāyeṇāhaṅkārikatvam indriyāṇām ākṣeptum āha ||
children.translated_text: To challenge the claim that the sense-organs are <s>āhaṃkārika</s> (derived from ahaṃkāra) from the standpoint of those who hold the senses to be material, he says:

children.text: Chapter 251
anyānyapi niyatārthatayā hetubhūtayā kasyacid vādinaḥ pakṣe'kṣāṇi indriyāṇi bhinnakāraṇāni ||
children.translated_text: According to a certain disputant, the other organs also, the senses, have distinct causes, because their restriction to definite objects is taken as the reason.

children.text: āhaṅkārikatve hi naiṣāṃ niyatārthatvaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: For if they were <s>āhaṃkārika</s>, they would not have this restriction to definite objects.

children.text: gandhādivyañjakatvācca hetosteṣāṃ gandhādīnāmādhārā āśrayāḥ pṛthivyādayas tadādhārāḥ tadātmakāni ||
children.translated_text: And because they manifest smell and the rest, their bases are the supports, the substrata, of smell and the rest, namely earth and the other elements; they rest on those and consist of those.

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ hi pārthivameva dravyaṃ gandhavyañjakaṃ ghrāṇaṃ ca gandhasya grāhakam ||
children.translated_text: For it is seen that only an earthy substance manifests smell, and the <s>ghrāṇa</s> (organ of smell) grasps smell.

children.text: tasmātpārthivaṃ ghrāṇam āpyaṃ rasanaṃ taijasaṃ cakṣuriti evam anyat ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the organ of smell is earthy, the organ of taste watery, the eye fiery, and similarly with the others.

children.text: tatkiṃ yuktaṃ navetyāha ||
children.translated_text: He asks: Is that reasonable or not?

children.text: Chapter 252
ekaikamindriyaṃ svakāraṇād anyat kāraṇāntaraṃ guṇasahitaṃ yadi nādatte na gṛhṇāti tattathāstu ||
children.translated_text: If each sense-organ does not take up, does not grasp, another cause different from its own cause together with its quality, then let it be so.

children.text: ayamarthaḥ yadi indriyaṃ svakāraṇasamānajātīyaṃ dravyaṃ tadguṇaṃ ca gṛhṇīyāt tadānīṃ viṣayaniyamaḥ prakṛtiniyamagamaka iṣyeta ||
children.translated_text: This is the meaning: if a sense-organ were to grasp a substance of the same class as its own cause and also that substance's quality, then restriction of object would be accepted as indicating restriction of material source.

children.text: yāvatā dravyāntarāṇi tadguṇāṃśca gṛhṇāti tasmānna niyatārthatayā prakṛtigamakatvam akṣāṇām upapannam ||
children.translated_text: But since it grasps other substances and their qualities, it is not established that the senses, through being restricted to definite objects, indicate their material source.

children.text: atha kiṃ tadanaiyatyamityāha tvagindriyam ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Now he asks, 'What is that absence of restriction?' with 'the tactile sense,' and so forth.

children.text: tathāhi tvagindriyaṃ yuktasya svakāraṇatvāt grahītumupapannasya parāṅmukhaṃ na syāt tadā tadeva tatparatvena gṛhṇīyāt na ca svakāraṇād anyatvena ayuktagrahaṇānāṃ pṛthivyaptejasāmarthānāṃ gṛhītṛ ||
children.translated_text: For example, if the tactile sense were not turned away from what is fit to be grasped because it is its own cause, then it would grasp that alone as its proper object, and it would not grasp earth, water, and fire objects, whose grasping is improper because they are different from its own cause.

children.text: tatkathaṃ viṣayaniyamasiddhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: How, then, could restriction of objects be established?

children.text: tathā dṛgdṛṣṭiḥ tejodravyaṃ pṛthivīdravyaṃ ca bhinnarūpaṃ gṛhṇāti ||
children.translated_text: Likewise the eye, the visual faculty, grasps fiery substance and earthly substance that possess different forms/colors.

children.text: ataśca sā dṛk tridravyajā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Therefore that visual faculty would be born from three substances.

children.text: na cāsyās tridravyajatvaṃ pareṇeṣyate taijasatvenābhyupagamāt ||
children.translated_text: But the opponent does not accept that it is born from three substances, since he admits it to be fiery.

children.text: Chapter 253
bhavatpakṣe yenendriyeṇa yo gandhādyāśrayaḥ pṛthivyādirupalabhyate sa pṛthivyādistasya kāraṇam ityabhyupagamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: On your view, it is accepted that whichever earth and so on, as the substrate of smell and the rest, is apprehended by a given sense-organ, that earth and so on is the cause of that organ.

children.text: tathāca sati bhūteṣu tadguṇeṣveva cendriyebhyaḥ pratītayaḥ syuḥ ||
children.translated_text: And if this is so, cognitions from the senses would occur only with regard to the elements and their own qualities.

children.text: karmasāmānyasamavāyādi tat dravyebhyo guṇebhyaśca padārthāntaram ||
children.translated_text: <s>Karman</s> (action), <s>sāmānya</s> (universal), <s>samavāya</s> (inherence), and the like are categories different from those substances and qualities.

children.text: na ca tadātmakānyakṣāṇi ||
children.translated_text: And the senses are not made of those.

children.text: tasmātkarmāder akṣairgrahaṇaṃ na prāptam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the grasping of action and the like by the senses would not follow.

children.text: uktaṃ ca kheṭakanandanena
children.translated_text: And this has been said by <s>Kheṭakanandana</s>:

children.text: bhautikatvācca niyame karmasāmānyayoḥ sphuṭam
children.translated_text: Because they are material, if there is restriction, then plainly with regard to action and universal,

children.text: devebhyo buddhayo na syuḥ samavāye ca dehinām ||
children.translated_text: there would be no cognitions from the <s>deva</s>s, nor, for embodied beings, with regard to inherence.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: seyaṃ prakṛtiniyamagamake viṣayaniyame 'ṅgīkriyamāṇe niṣphalā kleśaparamparā prasajyate ||
children.translated_text: This is the useless chain of troubles that follows when restriction of objects is accepted as indicating restriction of material source.

children.text: tasmādviṣayāṇāmindriyāṇāṃ ca bhavadabhimatagrāhyagrāhakaniyamāsaṃbhavāt na kṣityādiprakṛtiniyamasiddhir ityāhaṅkārikāṇyevendriyāṇīti siddham ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, because the fixed relation of graspable and grasper between objects and senses, as admitted by you, is impossible, no restriction of an elemental source such as earth is established; hence the sense-organs are indeed <s>āhaṃkārika</s>.

children.text: abhyupagamyāpi brūmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even while granting the point, we say:

children.text: Chapter 254
niyataviṣayatve'pyakṣāṇāmidaṃ tāvadbhavān pṛṣṭo vyācaṣṭāṃ yadi karṇarandhraviśiṣṭo nabhobhāgaḥ śabdavargasyetyanekavidhasya śabdasya dyotakaḥ tat nāsārandhrādicchidrāntaraṃ tathāvidhatvāducyatām ||
children.translated_text: Even if the senses have fixed objects, let Your Honor first explain this when asked: if the portion of space distinguished by the aperture of the ear illuminates the class of sounds, that is, manifold sound, then let another opening, such as the nostril-aperture, be said to do so, since it is of the same kind.

children.text: kena tadgrahaṇaṃ nivāryate ||
children.translated_text: By what is its grasping prevented?

children.text: athātrādṛṣṭaṃ puruṣārthapradaṃ karmākhyamasti yena śrotranabhobhāga eva śabdavargāvabhāsako na nāsārandhrādiriti niyamaḥ tarhi tadapīti tathāpi anyatretyasmatpakṣe'pi tathātvābhyupagamasya kā kṣatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: If, here, there is an unseen factor called <s>karman</s>, which bestows the aims of a person, by which there is the rule that only the ear-space portion reveals the class of sounds and not the nostril-aperture and the like, then, even so, what loss is there for our position in accepting the same condition elsewhere as well?

children.text: tatra hi kiṃ kṛtaṃ ko bādhako jātaḥ āhaṃkārikatve satyapyadṛṣṭāvaruddhatvasya ko doṣa ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For what has been done there? What defeater has arisen? The meaning is: even when the senses are <s>āhaṃkārika</s>, what fault is there in their being restrained by <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen karmic force)?

children.text: anyathāhi ātodye tantrīvaṃśamurajādivādye prāptamapi āsyanāsārandhrasaṃnikarṣastham api śabdaṃ tadāstharandhraṃ ghrāṇacchidraṃ vā kiṃ kenāpi dasyunā durācāreṇa śaptatvāt śabdaṃ na gṛhṇātīti kākvā vyākhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: For otherwise, in the case of a musical instrument, such as an instrument with strings, a flute, or a drum, even though sound has arrived and is situated close to the openings of the mouth and nose, one would have to explain sarcastically: "Does the mouth-opening or nostril not grasp sound because it has been cursed by some wicked bandit?"

children.text: etacca proktavadyuktyupapannam ||
children.translated_text: And this is supported by reasoning in the way already stated.

children.text: yatrāpi ca yuktirgamikā na sambhavati tatra ||
children.translated_text: And even where no reasoning that leads to knowledge is possible, there:

children.text: Chapter 255
asaṃbhavadyuktike'pi vastuni sadāgamokteḥ pratītiḥ avagamo nirbādhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even with respect to a thing for which reasoning is impossible, cognition, that is understanding, from the statement of a reliable <s>āgama</s> is unobstructed.

children.text: kuta ityāha mitārthāditi ||
children.translated_text: Why? He says, "because its object is limited."

children.text: yasmālliṅgasāpekṣatvena parimitārthādanumānān sarvadarśijñānasyāgamarūpasyāparimitārthatvena jyāyastvamityāgamādiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For, since <s>anumāna</s> (inference), because it depends on a <s>liṅga</s> (sign), has a restricted object, the knowledge of the all-seer in the form of <s>āgama</s> is superior because its object is unrestricted; this is the sense of the passage beginning with "<s>āgama</s>."

children.text: mātrebhyo bhūtapañcakam iti yadupakrāntaṃ tadviśeṣayitumāha ||
children.translated_text: In order to specify what was introduced by the statement, "from the <s>mātrā</s>s comes the fivefold set of elements," he says:
